This is the first truth on which Islam's conceptual foundations rest: the Oneness of Allah (tawhid al-i'tiqad), the Oneness of Divinity (tawhid al-uluhiyyah), and the Oneness of Self-Subsistence (tawhid al-qayyumiyyah), and that the entire governance of this universe is being carried out by Allah in accordance with the principles of justice and equity. The discourse of this surah began with this first truth: ﴿Allah, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence.﴾ This beginning was intended, on the one hand, to express and clarify the Islamic belief, and on the other hand, to refute the doubts spread by the People of the Book. On the one hand, it was intended to explain and clarify to the People of the Book their inherited belief in the Oneness of Allah; on the other hand, it was intended to clarify the effect that the doubts they had spread were having upon the Muslims, because at times Muslims too were influenced by them.

The testimony of Allah, that there is no god but Allah, is a sufficient and healing belief for everyone who has already believed. Here the question arises: the testimony of Allah can be sufficient and healing only for those who believe in Allah and who have accepted faith. Then what need remains for them for testimony? The reality is that the People of the Book did believe in Allah, but alongside this they also ascribed offspring to Allah and ascribed partners to Him. Indeed, the polytheists of Makkah also believed in God, but they went astray in that they set up many partners with Allah, equated many with Allah, and believed in sons and daughters for Allah. Therefore, when the Noble Qur'an confirmed that the God whom they themselves acknowledge testifies that He has no partner, this testimony was an effective testimony for purifying their thoughts.

Moreover, this matter, as we have examined in our commentary before this section, is a very profound and subtle matter. Here, testimony to the doctrine of Oneness is given by Allah, because with the testimony of Oneness are attached its requirements, and the mention of these requirements comes later. And that belief in Oneness expects from its bearers worship and obedience to that One without partner alone. And that worship and obedience is also in the form of Islam. And Islam is required in the sense of surrendering oneself completely and total submission. By Islam is not meant merely awareness, conception and belief, but it means action, obedience and complete submission as well. And this submission is also in accordance with the form of the Islamic system of life derived from the Qur'an and Sunnah. From this aspect we see that in every age and every era the majority of people claim that they have believed, yet they also set up countless others as partners with that Allah, in the case when they get their judgments made according to laws that are not based on the Shari'ah, and they obey those people who do not obey Allah and His Messenger; along with this, they take their morals and values, their thoughts and ideas, and their standards of good and bad from other than Allah. All these matters contradict their statement that we have believed, and furthermore, this conduct of theirs is also contrary to the testimony of Allah that there is no god but Allah.

Now the question remains regarding the testimony of the angels and the scholars. Its meaning is that the angels and the scholars completely obey Allah and His commands and prohibitions; they take guidance only from Allah, and follow whatever is revealed from Allah. They neither dispute about it nor do they doubt it in any way, provided it is established that this matter is from Allah. In this surah, while describing the state of those firm in knowledge (ulu al-'ilm), it was stated: ﴿And those firm in knowledge say: "We believe in it; all of it is from our Lord."﴾ This is the testimony, that is, the affirmation, obedience, following and submission of the people of knowledge and the angels. The essence of the testimony of the angels and the people of knowledge is that there is no god but Allah, and that He is established with justice and equity. That is, justice and equity is an attribute which is established and necessary along with His glory of Divinity.

﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god but He, and the angels and those of knowledge also bear witness that He is maintaining justice.﴾ As the text of the verse makes clear, "qa'iman bil-qist" (maintaining justice) is a state that is necessary to the glory of Divinity. And this is an explanation of what was said earlier in the surah, that Allah is the Sustainer and Guardian; the meaning is that His guardianship is established upon justice.

The measures Allah has adopted to run this world, or the measures He has adopted for the establishment and continuance of people's lives here, are based upon the principles of justice and equity. Therefore justice can be established in people's lives only when their lives are founded upon the Shari'ah of the Book of Allah, just as this universe has been established upon the just principles of the laws of nature, and it stands firm. Only in this way can humanity and nature move in harmony. The Shari'ah is the system which Allah has set out in His Book. If it is not so, then justice will not prevail in this world, and balance and moderation will not be established here. There will be no harmony and conformity between the course of the universe and the course of humanity. The result will emerge in the form of oppression, division and the wastage of powers.

Human history bears witness that humanity tasted justice and equity only in those eras in which the rule of the Book of Allah alone prevailed, and their lives were organized and firmly established in the same manner as the orbit of this earth is organized and firm, to the extent that is possible for human nature; that is, there is balance between the inclinations of human nature toward obedience and its inclinations toward disobedience, and balance between these two pans, and the human being inclines toward the obedience of Allah in the form of establishing the Islamic system of life and the rule of the Book of Allah. If over human life there rules a system which man himself has made, then human ignorance will necessarily have a role in it; the deficiency of human conception and perception will be included in it, and as a result this system will fall, in some form or other, into oppression and contradiction. Sometimes one individual will inflict oppression upon the whole society, and sometimes a society will be oppressing an individual, or sometimes one class will be oppressing another class, or one nation oppressing other nations, or one generation oppressing another generation. As for the Islamic system of life, it is free from all these tendencies and inclinations, because Allah is the God of all, and there is no hidden secret in this earth and heaven.

﴿There is no god but He, the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ Here, in this part of the verse, the Oneness of Divinity is stated again with two important attributes: one attribute is that He is Mighty, the possessor of power, and the other is that He is Wise. Both power and wisdom are attributes whose existence is necessary for the glory of Allah's justice and guardianship. This is because the meaning of justice is that the one who has a right receives it, and it can be secured for him. And the concept of Allah's attributes gives the awareness of positive action. For in the Islamic concept of God there is no negativity; there is affirmation upon affirmation, and this concept is the most complete concept of Allah, the truest concept, and this concept has been presented by Allah Himself with reference to Himself. And the effect of this positive and affirmative activity upon a human being is that the human heart becomes connected with the will of Allah. Therefore a person's belief becomes a living and effective belief; it is not merely a dry concept, but within it there is activity and freshness.

Now, building on the truth repeated twice in this one verse, the natural conclusion is drawn: if Godhead is one, then worship and submission belong to that One God alone.

The essential idea is that there is one Deity; therefore there is one system, and before that Deity one must bow in submission. Their conception should contain nothing other than this, and no part of their life should be free from this system... When Allah is one, worship and submission are also for Him alone. And this same Allah is entitled to have people obey Him: the Shari'ah should be enforced in their legal system, the Shari'ah should be the criterion in their values of life and in their measures of good and evil, and their entire practical life should be founded upon this Shari'ah.

If there is one Allah, then the conception of life will also be one. And that conception and ideology will be the one that this Deity has chosen for His servants, namely the pure belief in the Tawhid, shining and clean.

As we have stated repeatedly, the first requirement of the belief in Tawhid is: ﴿Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam﴾ (3:19)... With Allah, the system of life is only the religion of Islam. And Islam is not merely a claim; it is not merely the name of a flag; it is not merely the name of a slogan; it is not merely the name of an idea or a vain fancy where the heart is at ease; and it is not merely the name of individual acts of worship that a person performs as an individual, such as prayer, Hajj and fasting. Such is by no means the case. Those matters alone are not the Islam regarding which Allah the Exalted says that He accepts no other religion besides it. Rather, Islam is the name of complete submission. Islam is the name of complete worship. It is complete following. Islam means that judgments in the courts are being made according to the Book of Allah, the details of which will come shortly.

Islam means that Allah is regarded as One without partner. The belief should be firm that He alone sustains this universe. Whereas the People of the Book mixed up the Essence of the Divine with the person of the Messiah. Rather, they also mixed up the will of Allah with the will of the Messiah. On this subject there were several sects among them themselves, and each sect had its own belief. And these differences sometimes became so severe that they resulted in killing and plunder. Therefore, here Allah informs the People of the Book and the Muslim community what the real cause of these differences and intellectual confusion was.

﴿And those who were given the Scripture did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of jealousy among themselves﴾ (3:19)

"And the various ways that those who were given the Scripture adopted, departing from this religion, had no cause other than that, after knowledge had come to them, they did so out of transgression against one another."

These differences did not exist because they did not know the reality of the matter, for knowledge decisive regarding the Oneness of Allah had come to them: that Allah is One, and that the nature of man is that he is only a servant, not a deity. The severe differences they created were merely for the sake of transgressing against one another. A pretext for oppression and aggression against one another was created. In the system of Allah's justice and equity there was no justification for them; in the Islamic ideology of life and in the heavenly Shari'ah, or the heavenly Scriptures, there was no justification for such differences.

Earlier we have already cited a Christian historian, in which we showed how political movements among the Christians deliberately created religious differences, and that the differences between Jewish and Christian thought were also of this kind. We have read how this religious hatred spread between Egypt and Syria. Since the Roman Empire ruled Syria, the Egyptians, because of this political hatred, abandoned the Roman Catholic school and adopted another school of thought. Or, as some of the Caesars of Rome attempted, that all these Christian schools of thought should agree upon a middle school of thought, so that intellectual unity would arise among their subject subjects; they thought that by such a religion everyone's aims would be fulfilled. In effect, belief was a game, and it could easily be changed for political and national aims. Yet in reality this was a great injustice, and this oppression and transgression they carried out under a deliberately planned scheme.

For this very reason, Allah sharply rebukes this very conduct, and at the appropriate time: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in the signs of Allah, then indeed Allah is swift in reckoning﴾ (3:19)... "And whoever refuses obedience to Allah's guidance and commands, Allah is not slow in taking account of him." Here Allah has described disagreement regarding the belief in Tawhid as disbelief, and warned the disbelievers and frightened them that I am very swift in reckoning. Therefore, if I give them more respite, these people would remain further bewildered in differences and disbelief and atheism. After this, Allah commands His Prophet to speak a decisive word to these people, that is, to both the People of the Book and others, so that the dialogue with them enters a decisive stage, and after that it is brought to an end, and you proceed alone on your clear path.

Now there is no need for further clarification; much has been said. So either you acknowledge the divinity of Allah alone, acknowledge His guardianship, and consequently follow and submit to Him; otherwise you will find no solution to your problem, this debate will continue in the same way, and you will remain deprived of tawhid and Islam. Accordingly, Allah instructs His Messenger to say just one word which simultaneously reflects both a worldview (nazariyah-i-hayat) and a system of life (nizam-i-zindagi): that if these people still argue with you, you should plainly say: "I have submitted my face (to Allah)..." ﴿أَسْلَمْتُ وَجْهِيَ﴾ "I have submitted, and so have those who follow me." Here, by calling the believers "those who follow" (mutabi'in), the indication intended is that Islam is not merely affirmation (tasdiq); after it, following (ittiba') is also necessary. Likewise, the expression "my face has bowed before Allah" is used because Islam is not merely the name of verbal declaration and agreement, nor only the name of belief and concept. Its meaning includes submission (inqiyad), and also obedience and following. The face being obedient is the goal, meaning complete submission and following, because in the human body the face holds an elevated status. It is from the face that one can tell how obedient, compliant, humble and always ready and alert for action a person is.

This is the belief of Hazrat Muhammad (ﷺ) himself and his system of life, the Nizam-i-Mustafa; and the Muslims are indeed those who follow and emulate him, both in belief and in action. Therefore, now let this question be put to the People of the Book and to those who are not People of the Book. Let this question be asked which clearly demarcates the two camps, establishes a dividing line between the two, leaves no ambiguity, and leaves no intellectual confusion or mixing between them.

﴿وَقُلْ لِلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ وَالأُمِّيِّينَ أَأَسْلَمْتُمْ﴾ "Say to those who were given the Book and to the unlettered: Have you submitted?" Here the distinction between the People of the Book and the non-People of the Book is now set aside. Now both stand on the same footing. Both the People of the Book and the polytheists are invited to Islam, and this invitation is with the meaning explained by us: they are invited to accept the belief in Tawhid, in Allah's Being and His self-subsistence and guardianship; then, after adopting this belief, they are invited to become obedient to His command, and obedience means that in their whole life they decide matters according to the Book of Allah, and adopt the Islamic system of life. ﴿فَإِنْ أَسْلَمُوا فَقَدِ اهْتَدَوْا﴾ "If they submit, then they have been guided."

It becomes clear that the manifestation of guidance takes only one form, namely Islam, in accordance with its nature and disposition; there is no other form, no other concept, no other method, and no other path through which guidance may be attained. All other paths are crooked; they are all paths of bewilderment and confusion, all paths of deviation and misguidance.

﴿وَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْكَ الْبَلاغُ وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِالْعِبَادِ﴾ "But if they turn away, your duty is only to convey the message, and Allah is All-Seeing of His servants." After conveying the message, the Messenger's responsibility ends and his task is complete. This was the situation at the time when permission for fighting against those who did not accept Islam had not yet been granted, until they desisted; the subsequent command was that they should either fully submit and become obedient to the Islamic system, or else enter a covenant and, by paying the jizyah, come under the Islamic system. Then they are free, since in Islam there is no compulsion to change one's beliefs.

﴿وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِالْعِبَادِ﴾ "Allah is well aware of the affairs of His servants." He manages their affairs only according to His knowledge and insight, and all their matters are in His hands in every state; therefore He does not keep His servants in darkness. He tells them plainly what their end will be. He shows them what the outcome was, throughout the history of mankind, for the rebels and disobedient against Allah, and that His sunnah remains the same now as well. He says:

This is the end result for those people: a painful punishment awaits them. This punishment will be in both this world and the Hereafter. Here they may expect it, and in the Hereafter it is certain without doubt... In this world and the Hereafter their deeds will be void, ineffective. This is a strange depiction. Habt (حبوط) linguistically means: when an animal eats poisonous grass and swells up. Apparently, in that condition the animal becomes fat and healthy, but the result is that it is eventually destroyed and dies. Here, apparently, they have great achievements, but on the Day of Resurrection these will be of no benefit to them, and they will have no supporter or helper.

The Qur'an mentioned, along with the denial of the signs of Allah, the killing of the prophets (peace be upon them), who were killed unjustly, because the truth can never be combined with the killing of the prophets (peace be upon them). It also mentioned that they used to kill those people who enjoined justice and fairness. That is, they killed them because they professed and called to the divine system, which was a just system, and justice could not be established through any other system than it. From the mention of all these attributes, it is indicated that this rebuke and warning was directed at the Jews, because these are their historical attributes, and they are well known for them. Wherever they are mentioned, the mind turns to them. However, it is also possible that the address is to the Christians, because until the time of the revelation of the Qur'an they too had killed thousands of opponents of their religion. For whoever opposed the official religion of the Roman Empire was killed by them. Among them were also Christians who believed in monotheism and regarded Jesus (peace be upon him) as a human being. And these were people who also advocated justice and fairness in the system of government. Apart from the Jews and Christians, this ruling applies in every time and place to all those who commit such violent acts, and in every age such people have never been lacking.

It is worth understanding here what the words of the Qur'an, "those who deny the signs," mean. They do not mean only that someone denies the signs of Allah and utters a word of disbelief. The meaning of this term includes that someone does not believe in the oneness of God or the doctrine of Tawhid, and then does not believe in worshipping Allah alone. And it automatically includes that one does not believe in the source and origin from which legislation for human life is made and the values of good and evil are determined, that is, the Book of Allah. Therefore, whoever associates anyone else with Allah in these matters too will be considered a polytheist and counted as a denier of divinity, even if he repeats it with his tongue a thousand times. The expression of this meaning will be found in the following verses.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 23:

This is an interrogative question, and through it the strange and contradictory stance of these people is meant to be exposed. This stance was adopted by those who, by good fortune, received even a portion of the Book of Allah, such as the Jews with the Torah and the Christians with the Injil (Gospel). These books are a part of the Book of Allah in the sense that the Book of Allah is the entire record that was revealed from Allah to a Prophet in any time and place. For with Allah, Allah is one, the guardianship is one, and in reality the Book is also one. The Jews and Christians received a part of it, while the Muslims received the complete Book. This is because the Holy Qur'an is comprehensive of the fundamentals of religion (usul al-din) and confirms the previous scriptures. This question was put to those who were given a portion of the Book, so that the Book might also decide the differences that had arisen among them. It should be decisive in all the affairs of their lives, and decisive in their economy and livelihood. Yet they do not accept this call; a faction of them turns away and refuses. They do not judge according to the Book of Allah and the Divine Law. Therefore, this is a stance that is contrary to faith, and it is also contrary to their claim that they are People of the Book.

﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book? They are invited to the Book of Allah so that it may judge between them, and then a faction of them turns away while they are averse.﴾

Thus Allah expresses wonder at the conduct of some of the People of the Book, not all of them, that when they are invited to return to the Book of Allah in their doctrinal matters and in their practical matters, they refuse. How can they refuse this while being Muslims? They claim to be Muslims, yet they have expelled the Shari'ah from their lives, and still they keep believing that they are Muslims. This astonishing question is asked so that Muslims also understand what the reality of religion is and what the reality of Islam is, lest they become a laughingstock before Allah and face such a question from Him. If this is the condition of the People of the Book, who do not claim to be Muslims, if they do not have their judgments made according to the Book of Allah, then it is a moment of reflection for the people of Islam: that if they do not make their judgments according to the Book of Allah and the Shari'ah, how deserving will they be of censure, disapproval, wonder, detestation and ridicule from Allah. This is a wonder that cannot be removed. It is a great calamity whose extent has not been measured, and it is an invitation to such a great wrath of Allah that as a result a Muslim may become deserving of the wrath of Allah, may become cast away from His court, and may also be deprived of the mercy of Allah. We seek refuge in Allah.

ﷺ

That is because they say, "The Fire will not touch us except for a few countable days." And their own fabrications have deluded them in their religion.

This is the real reason for their turning away, which is why they do not have their disputes judged according to the Book of Allah. This contradiction in their position exists despite their claim that they are People of the Book. In truth, they are simply not serious about the reckoning on the Day of Resurrection. They have no confidence in the belief that Allah will do full justice on the Day of Judgment, and this is clearly shown by their saying that the Fire of Hell will not touch them, and that if any punishment is to be given, it will last only a few days. If this is not the reality, then why will the Fire not touch them? And why would their punishment be only for a few days? Why have they turned away from the fundamentals of religion? Why do they not have their judgments made according to the Book of Allah? If they believe in Allah's justice and fairness, then why is their position this way? This is not possible: if they truly believed in the reckoning of the Last Day, they would never have done such a thing. In reality, they are telling a lie in which they themselves do not believe, and they have trapped themselves in the net of their own fabricated beliefs. ﴿وَغَرَّهُمْ فِي دِينِهِمْ مَا كَانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ﴾ "Their own fabricated beliefs have deluded them in matters of their religion."

The truth is that whoever holds the correct belief in the Resurrection in his heart cannot adopt the crude notions that these people have adopted regarding the reckoning on the Day of Judgment and Allah's justice. The truth is that, for a reasonable person with the fear of the Hereafter in his heart, having a modest stance before Allah, it is impossible that he would be called to judgment according to the Book of Allah and would refuse or turn away.

In our own age too, the condition of Muslims is just like that of the People of the Book. Today's Muslims also consider themselves Muslims. And when they are invited, "Come, have your judgments made according to the Book of Allah and implement the Shariah," they turn away and refuse this. Among them, some well-off people have become so shameless. They say, "Life is the name of this world, and what is the connection of religion with the world?" These people think there is no need to bring religion into people's daily practical, economic and social relations. Rather, now they say that even in family life there is no need for religion. And despite holding these views, they continue to claim that they are Muslims. Then some of them are caught in the foolish delusion that Allah will cast them into the Fire only for a few days to purify them, and after that they will be led to Paradise. The question is: are they not Muslims? This is not the reality. These people have moved away from religion just as the People of the Book moved away, and indeed they have slipped out of religion as easily as a fish slips from someone's hand. They have departed from the reality that Allah had chosen. Therefore, Islam means submission and obedience, and Islam is the name of seeking guidance and instruction from Allah in every sphere of life.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 25:

"But how will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt, and every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged?"

…………What will their condition be? This is a frightening warning. The heart of the believer trembles; on hearing it, he feels that that Day will be extremely terrifying and serious, a Day of appearing before Allah. On that Day there will be true justice. The conception of that Day and its true awareness have no affinity with those false conceptions and the notions invented by people themselves. After this threat and warning, this ruling stands. It applies to the polytheists, to the atheists, to the People of the Book who claim to be Muslims, and to the Muslims of today who do not implement Islam properly in their lives. What will be the condition of these people on that Day, the coming of which is beyond doubt and on which We shall gather them all? And on the Day when Allah's system of justice will run according to its own methods, every person will receive the recompense of what he earned, in full, without injustice and without any consideration, and no one will suffer any excess. Although, in Allah's reckoning, there will be no leniency or concession for them.

………… The verse has posed a question, but no answer has been given to it. The hearts tremble, the body shudders, and the answer stood before the eyes of its own accord.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 26:

After this, every believer, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) himself, is directed to turn toward Allah, regarding Him as the sole Deity (al-Uluhiyyah) and as the one sole Guardian of this universe, both in the life of mankind and in the management of this cosmos, because these two aspects are manifestations of Allah's lordship (khudai) and His sovereignty (hakimiyyah), and in them He has no partner. Nor is there any equal or likeness to Him.

This is an extremely gentle and dignified voice. Its verbal structure is that of a supplication, yet its spirit carries profound meaning and humility and submission. In it, the open book of this unfolding universe is cast with a glance of loving attention. With great gentleness and great affection, the consciousness of man is stirred, and he is told that He is the Lord, the Manager of the universe, and at the same time the Manager of human affairs as well. By gathering His all-encompassing management together, an indication is given toward a great truth. That great truth is that the Deity and Guardian of this universe, and the Deity and Guardian of this human being within it, are one and the same. This human being is a part of this universe; he is not a reality separate from it. In both, the true disposer is Allah. The splendour of this universe lies only in the system of life of Allah, and this is also the duty of man. Just as this universe cannot step outside the religion of Allah, so too for man, to step outside the divine religion is a kind of deviation (inhiraf), foolishness (hamaqat) and corruption (fasad). Allah says:

﴿Say: O Allah, Master of the Kingdom! You give the kingdom to whom You will, and You take the kingdom away from whom You will; You exalt whom You will, and You abase whom You will.﴾

This is the truth that arises as a consequence of the belief in the oneness of Godhead (wahdat al-uluhiyyah). The meaning of one God is that He alone is the Owner. He is Malik al-Mulk (Master of the Kingdom). There is no partner with Him in this. Thereafter, He gives whatever He wills and to whomever He wills from His own, and this gift is a loan (ariyatan); when He wills, and from whom He wills, He takes back His kingdom. Therefore, here no one is the true owner of anything, so that he may dispose of it according to his own personal desire. Human ownership is temporary and given. It is subject to the conditions and restrictions under which the Giver has granted it. Governance and ownership will operate under His teachings. If it is done contrary to the conditions of the Giver, it will be void. In this world, it is incumbent upon Muslims to reject every such disposal, and in the Hereafter Allah Himself will call such a person to account.

Furthermore, it is within His power to honour whom He wills and to humble whom He wills. There is no one who can place any obstacle in the path of His command and will. No one can compel Him, and there is no one who can reject His decisions. He is the Lord of command; all affairs are in His hand. He is Allah, free from association (shirk), and in this exclusive right and this greatness He has no partner.

In this guardianship of Allah lies the good of all. He manages this universe and mankind upon the principles of perfect justice. He gives dominion and sovereignty to whom He wills, and takes it from whom He wills, and all of this is with justice and equity. He makes honourable whom He wills and humbles whom He wills, and all of this is in accordance with justice. In every state He is nothing but good: "In His hand is good." "He is over all things Omnipotent."

The management of human affairs and the arrangement of human matters with goodness are all part of the management of His great and mighty universe, and a reflection of this vast and wide system of life. He says:

﴿You cause the night to pass into the day, and You cause the day to pass into the night. You bring the living out of the dead, and You bring the dead out of the living. And You provide for whom You will without account.﴾

This great truth is expressed in the manner of a vivid picture, which fills the heart and mind with joy on one side, and on the other side delights the senses and the eye. An imperceptible, mutual movement takes the form of night and day: the night changes into day and the day is woven into the night, and the successive nights and days appear like the beads of a rosary. Living things come out of the dead and the dead out of the living. This continuous movement clearly shows that the hand of the All-Wise Lord is at work in this system. Whoever listens attentively, with his ears open, will realise that a voice founded on profound truth is coming from this universe.

The meaning of causing the night to enter the day and the day to enter the night may be that in summer a part of the night turns into day, and in winter a part of the day becomes night. It may also mean that the light of day penetrates the darkness of night and the night enters into the light of day. Whichever meaning is intended, in this scene one sees with the senses that the hand of power sets heaven and earth in motion, and that this earth, which is a dark chamber, rotates on its axis before the luminous lamp of the sun. Thus the dark part alternates with the lit part, and the lit with the dark. In this way the darkness of night gradually moves toward the light of day, and the light of day changes into night. Gradually the night grows longer and consumes the day, and in the same imperceptible way the day grows larger and consumes the night. This is a movement regarding which no human being can claim that its reins are in his hand, nor can any wise person say that this movement began by chance without the planning of a manager.

Likewise, the wonder of life and death is before our eyes. Life advances toward death, and from death life emerges, and this happens quite calmly and peacefully. With every moment that passes over a living creature, death is also mingled with its life, and death consumes its life, and from this life emerges again. From a living thing, cells die and perish, and new cells are created in their place and perform their functions. The cells that die come back to life in another period, and those among them that come to life again die again in the period of another. This is the condition of a living body. Then the circle of death widens, and the whole living being dies, but its cells take the form of particles that enter into other compositions and enter other living bodies, and this life enters into them. Thus this cycle of night and day continues in this way. No human being can claim that he himself can produce any of these living creatures, nor can anyone believe that this system of life and death came into being by itself, by chance and accident.

In this whole universe a movement is continuously in progress, and within the body of every existing thing a movement is continuously in progress. This is a great movement, yet extremely hidden, extremely deep and extremely subtle. This brief indication of the Qur'an unveils this continuous reality, and a signal is given to the heart and mind of man. This movement also proves that He is capable, that He is the originator who creates anew, and that He is the Manager. No one can strive to separate himself from Allah in any of his plans or welfare, Who is Subtle and the Manager. And how could they devise for themselves any system of their own, founded upon their own base desires, since they are part of this universe, and the arrangement of this universe is being carried out by Him, the All-Wise, the All-Aware?

Then how can they enslave and make servants of one another, and what justification is there for some to become lords and gods for others, when the provider of all is Allah, and all people are the dependents of Allah? He says:

﴿And You provide for whom You will without account.﴾

This is a final point, and through it the great truth is unveiled to the human heart: that the God is one, namely Allah. He alone is the guardian of the universe, He alone is the one who acts, He alone is the one who manages. He alone is the owner, He alone is the manager, He alone is the giver, and the religion too is His. He is the Owner of the Kingdom, He is the one who grants honour and humiliates, He is the one who gives life and causes death, He is the one who gives and takes. He is the Manager of this universe, who manages according to a system of justice; He is the one who is nothing but goodness.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 28:

Earlier, the stance of the People of the Book was censured and warned against. This final comment is also a further confirmation of that. Previously, the attitude of the People of the Book was condemned: when they are called to the point that they should judge by the Book of Allah, they turn away even from this. Whereas they had been made to understand that the Book of Allah is based upon that system of life which Allah sent down for His servants, and that this whole universe too is moving along according to the divine method (manhaj Ilahi), of which man himself is also a part. This was the preface to what follows: that it is not permissible for believers to establish friendly relations with the disbelievers in preference to the believers, because the disbelievers have no power in this universe, nor does their authority prevail here; here all affairs are in the hand of Allah, and Allah alone is the Protector and Helper of the People of Faith.

In the previous verse, the Qur'an awakened in the believers the awareness that all affairs are in the hand of Allah, that He is the Owner of every kind of power, that He adopts all arrangements, and that provision is in His hand alone. So now it is explained: then for what purpose do believers establish friendships with the disbelievers? How can these two contradictory matters be gathered together in the heart of a believer? On one side is faith in Allah and love for Allah; on the other side is love for the enemies of Allah, whose condition is that when they are called to the Book of Allah so that judgments may be made according to it, they turn away from it. Therefore, here a severe threat is given: if a believer loves those who do not judge according to the Book of Allah and the Shari'ah, then his faith is in danger. Friendship with disbelievers is possible in various forms: loving them in the heart, helping them, or seeking help from them; all of these are *muwalat al-kuffar* (friendship with disbelievers).

*Lā yattakhidhi al-mu'minūna al-kāfirīna awliyā'a min dūni al-mu'minīna wa man yaf'al dhālika falaysa min Allāhi fī shay'in*

"The believers should not take the disbelievers as friends and allies in preference to the believers. Whoever does this has no connection whatsoever with Allah."

Just so, such a person is nothing in the sight of Allah. He has neither connection nor relationship with Allah, neither is he upon the religion of Allah nor upon the creed, neither is there any link nor friendship between him and Allah. This person is far from Allah. He has become detached from everything through which any connection is established.

Yes, here an exception is made in some extraordinary circumstances. There may be some countries where, out of compulsion, such relations have to be maintained. But even in those circumstances and regions, only verbal *taqiyyah* is permissible. It is not permissible for a person to love the disbelievers in the heart or to establish deep relations with them. Hadrat Ibn 'Abbas (raḍiyallāhu 'anhu) says: taqiyyah does not relate to action; taqiyyah relates only to the tongue. Therefore, the taqiyyah that has been permitted does not involve establishing relations between believers and disbelievers. And in this context, the word *kāfir* has been used for the person who turns away from judging according to the Book of Allah, that is, throughout his life. Here this point was made incidentally, but in another place the Qur'an has explicitly used the word *al-kāfirūn* for such people. Moreover, taqiyyah does not include the idea that a Muslim should in any way give practical cooperation to the disbelievers. No such deception can be practised upon Allah.

Since *wilayah* (guardianship) and love are the work of hearts, and they are connected with the human conscience and consciousness, and the feeling of fear of Allah and taqwa can restrain one from this sin, Allah the Exalted has warned the People of Faith in a remarkable manner with His wrath and His vengeful retribution: *wa yuḥadhdhirukumu Allāhu nafsahu* ("Allah warns you of Himself"). And to Him is your return. This warning and admonition, advancing further, touches the hearts and directs their attention to this: behold, you are in the sight of Allah; Allah knows everything.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 29:

"Say (O Prophet): Whether you conceal what is in your breasts or reveal it, Allah knows it, and He knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, and Allah has power over everything."

This is the extreme of warning and admonition. Fear is stirred up, and it is made known that one should protect oneself from the retribution of Allah. Allah has far-reaching means of knowledge and power. There is no place to escape from Him, and no helper will be found against Him.

This warning and admonition goes further and touches the depths of the hearts. Now that terrifying Day is brought before the mind's eye, the Day on which every deed and every intention will be presented, and on which every person's complete store (of deeds) will be placed before him.

"The day is coming when every soul will find present before it whatever good it did, and whatever evil it did, it will wish that there were a vast distance between it and that day."

This is an address that penetrates to the depths of the human heart. A person's entire capital is placed before him, and he is reminded that one day he himself will stand before this capital of his. He will wish that it were far from him, but alas, this wish will never be fulfilled. Or he will wish that this day had never come, but it has come. He is seeing it. He has been seized. Now there is no escape and no place to flee!

This speech also continues its assault on the human heart. Now Allah warns people about His own Self: ﴿And Allah warns you about Himself﴾. But at the end, even in this frightening atmosphere, Allah shows the servant a ray of His mercy and indicates that there is still time and the opportunity has not ended: ﴿And Allah is Most Kind to His servants﴾. This early warning and admonition from Allah is also an act of His kindness, and it is proof that Allah desires the good of His servants.

This great, comprehensive assault against the relationship of friendship between the believers and the disbelievers contains various useful indications, guidance and advice. The reason this need arose at this time shows that in that era, between the Islamic camp and the opposing camp spread around it, there existed ties of kinship, economic and social relations. The relationships of the members of the Muslim community were established with their relatives and friends. These relationships existed with the people of Makkah, and also with the Jews around Madinah. The basis of these relationships was kinship or trade. Whereas Islam wanted that in its new society, people's mutual relationships be based solely on the foundation of the worldview, and on the system of life formed by that worldview. This is a matter in which Islam does not tolerate any weakness or compromise whatsoever.

Furthermore, it is also evident from this that the human heart, mind and outlook constantly need to free themselves from these difficulties and obstacles, and to break the bonds that stand in the way of the Islamic system and of coming to the path of Allah. Yet it should be kept in mind that Islam does not forbid good treatment even towards its enemies, even though they are enemies of its religion. This is because good treatment and good dealing is one thing, and *wilayah* (loyalty and allegiance) and friendship is a different matter. Friendship involves mutual love and mutual help and support. And a believer cannot do this from the heart with those who are not believers. A believer can only befriend believers, who are bound by the bond of faith, who are companions in the Islamic system of life, and who implement the Shariah and submit before it.

At the very end, the conclusion of this lesson appears in a decisive manner. It presents this issue decisively, and this is the very issue around which this entire surah revolves. This conclusion, in a decisive and concise manner, explains the reality of faith and the reality of religion, and a clear dividing line is drawn between faith and disbelief. This line is so clear that there is now no possibility of anyone developing any misunderstanding.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verses 31–32:

Love of Allah is not merely a verbal claim, nor is it some purely inward feeling. It must be accompanied by following the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. It is necessary to follow his biography and his footsteps. It is necessary to establish the Islamic system in one's life. Faith is not merely the utterance of a few words. Nor does it consist of awareness and emotions. Nor is it merely the upholding of a few outward rites. Rather, faith is the name of obedience to Allah and His Messenger, and the name of acting upon the path of which the Messenger of Allah is the bearer.

In explaining the first verse, Imam Ibn Kathir says: "This verse decides the case of everyone who claims to love Allah but whose conduct is not in accordance with the method of Muhammad. Such a person is in reality a liar, until he follows the Sharia of Muhammad and obeys the religion of Muhammad in all his sayings and actions, as is established from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in a authentic hadith: 'Whoever does an action that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected.'"

And in explaining the second verse, "Qul ati'ullaha wa'l-Rasul, fa in tawallaw..." (Say: Obey Allah and the Messenger; but if they turn away...), he says: "This shows that opposition to the way of the Prophet ﷺ is disbelief, and Allah certainly does not love a person with such attributes, even if such a person claims or believes that he is a lover of Allah."

Imam Shams al-Din Abu Muhammad Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyya, in his book Zad al-Ma'ad, says: "Whoever reflects upon the books of biography and the established hadiths will know that countless People of the Book and polytheists bear witness to the truthfulness and righteousness of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Yet this testimony does not bring them into Islam. Thus it becomes clear that Islam is something far greater than that. Islam is not merely knowledge and recognition, nor does it consist of recognition and affirmation. Rather, Islam consists of all three: recognition, affirmation and obedience. This submission and obedience is necessary in outward matters as well as inward matters."

The religion of Islam has a reality and an essence, and as long as that reality and essence are not present, there is no religion. That reality is solely the following of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the following of the Sharia, and the establishment of a judicial system in accordance with the Book of Allah. This reality springs forth from the creed of Tawhid, as Islam has explained that creed: that Allah is One and has no partner in His Being, that He has the right that people be wholly His slaves and servants, that they be implementers of Allah's commands, that the Divine Sharia be enforced among them, and that they establish values according to which people make their judgments and then be content with them. According to this creed, Allah is the sole Guardian, and therefore He alone is the Sovereign, and all collective relations among people should be founded upon this sovereignty, just as the whole system of this universe runs according to His law of nature. And it is evident that man too is a part of this universe.

As we have studied in detail, the first lesson of this Surah decides with complete clarity and plainness that the only system of life accepted by Allah is Islam. There is no need to flee from it or to escape from it. Whoever wishes to become a Muslim must accept this reality. This is the form of Islam; it is not the form that people in our time have fabricated for themselves. Those are mere illusions, mere superstitions.

Lesson 24: A Brief Overview

Some narrations, which describe the debate between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the delegation of Najran, state that the stories mentioned in this surah, such as the birth of Jesus, the birth of his mother, Yahya (John) and other events, were revealed in refutation of the doubts that brought this delegation. The foundation of their doubts was built upon the Qur'anic verse which says that Jesus is "a Word from Allah" ... which He cast to Mary, and "a spirit from Him." Likewise, regarding matters not mentioned in Surah Maryam, they sought an answer from the Messenger (ﷺ).

This may well be correct, but the way these stories are presented in this surah is exactly the way the Qur'an presents stories in general. That is, certain realities are kept in view, and through these stories the Qur'an impresses those realities upon the mind. These realities are in fact the central theme of the whole surah, revolving around that subject. The stories are presented in such a way that those realities become evident by themselves and are gradually fixed in the mind. These realities become living realities. It is an accepted fact that certain realities and concepts are impressed upon the mind in a very beautiful way through stories; they have a profound effect on a person and appear in a living form. Those realities become living realities, and it is an accepted fact that certain realities and concepts are impressed upon the mind in a very beautiful way through stories; they have a profound effect on a person and appear in a living form. Those realities appear in human life moving about, just as characters appear on a screen. Compared with purely philosophical and abstract modes of expression, the narrative mode is very effective.

If we reflect, these stories also clearly bring out the realities that are the theme of this surah, and this surah is focused upon those realities. The stories proceed along the same lines as the discussion in it. Therefore, in these stories, no specific incident occasioning their revelation is apparent; rather, the stories have taken those events which are actual events and through which the ideological aspect of Islam is clearly made manifest.

The central issue of this surah, as we have said before, is the doctrine of Tawhid: that Allah is one in His essence, that there is no deity besides Him, and that He is the sole Guardian and the Sustainer of this universe. The story of Jesus (peace be upon him) and the other stories brought here to complete it establish this doctrine of Tawhid well. These stories negate the concept of offspring for Allah, and therefore refute the concept of association (shirk). They make those notions appear far-fetched and incomprehensible. They prove that such doubts are false and that such notions are base. Therefore the events of Mary's birth are described in detail; the picture of Jesus's birth is drawn and the related events are given. These events are presented in a manner such that no doubt about his humanity remains in the mind of the reader. Then it is explained that he was a Messenger just as the other Messengers passed away, that he holds the same station as those Messengers held, and that his natural reality is the same as theirs. These stories offer such an interpretation and explanation of the extraordinary birth of Jesus, a supernatural event, that a satisfying understanding of that wonder comes before the mind, in which no complexity or unsolvable knot remains. Upon this understanding the heart and mind become fully content, and the matter becomes an ordinary and familiar one in which nothing appears supernatural. And the concluding passage at the end of the story is worthy of reflection.

"Indeed, the example of Jesus with Allah is like that of Adam. He created him from dust; then He said to him, 'Be,' and he was."

Thus the heart attains certainty and tranquility. It is astonishing that doubts should arise about this simple reality.

The other important issue stated in this surah is that, in the sight of Allah, the religion is Islam alone. This second issue is also based on the first, namely the doctrine of Tawhid. That is, the religion is Islam, and the meaning of Islam is obedience and submission. This is also explained with great clarity within these stories. Jesus (peace be upon him) says to the Children of Israel: "I confirm the Torah that came before me, and to make lawful for you some of the things that were forbidden to you." This statement shows the nature of prophethood: a Messenger is sent precisely in order to prescribe a system of life for people, to lay down for them the rules of lawful and unlawful, so that the believers may accept it and obey. Afterwards, this same meaning is confirmed through the words of the disciples: "When Jesus sensed disbelief from them, he said, 'Who will be my helpers in the cause of Allah?' The disciples said, 'We are the helpers of Allah. We believe in Allah; bear witness that we are Muslims. Our Lord, we believe in what You have sent down and we follow the Messenger; so write us down among the witnesses.'"

One important theme of this surah is the nature of the relationship between the believers and their Allah. These stories also deal extensively with the relationship with Allah. These stories relate the circumstances of those noble personalities whom Allah had chosen, some of whom were descendants of others. Within these stories, the story of the wife of Imran sheds light on the theme of the relationship with Allah: she addresses her Lord regarding her daughter as though she were seeing her. Likewise, there is the dialogue of Zakariyya (peace be upon him) with Mary, Zakariyya's humble supplication and entreaty before his Lord, and then the disciples' response of "Labbayk" to their Prophet and their subsequent supplication to Allah. Thus within these stories, living scenes of the relationship with Allah become visible.

When these stories end, there comes a concluding passage in which all those realities for which these stories were brought are restated, presented in summary form. In this summary, the reality of Jesus is explained. Realities are stated concerning the nature of creation and the role of the Divine will in creation. This exposition is purely intuitive. The People of the Book are invited to accept these realities, and they are once again given the invitation to mutual imprecation (mubahalah).

At the end of this lesson, a comprehensive and conclusive statement is given again, and it is commanded that you invite the People of the Book in general to this truth, whether or not they have come for debate, both those present at that time and those who exist in the periods after today.

"Say: O People of the Book! Come to a word that is equitable between us and you: that we worship none but Allah, associate nothing with Him, and that some of us do not take others as lords besides Allah. But if they turn away, then say: Bear witness that we are Muslims." (64)

Here the debate concludes, and it becomes clear what demands Islam makes upon people, what rules of life it establishes. Here the meaning of religion and Islam is explained. Every ugly form is cleared away, and that distorted system is stripped off which its adherents claim to be Islam and religion, though in reality it is not so. In sum, this was the principal theme of this lesson, and this was also the theme of this surah, which the stories expressed in the form of an engaging and interesting narrative containing profound allusions. The purpose and aim of narrating stories in the Qur'an is exactly this, and for this purpose these stories come in an appropriate style; and in various surahs these stories have been brought in this particular style.

The story of Jesus (peace be upon him) is also mentioned in Surah Maryam, and it is mentioned here too. Reflecting on both places shows that here some parts of it are stated briefly and some parts are given in detail. For instance, in Surah Maryam the birth of Jesus (peace be upon him) is described in detail, whereas the birth of Mary was not mentioned there. Here the dialogue with the disciples is detailed and the birth portion is brief, while here the concluding passage is very lengthy. This is because the subjects under discussion here were very important, such as the doctrine of Tawhid, the correct concept of religion, and the concept of divine revelation and prophethood, which were not under discussion in Surah Maryam. These points show what the Qur'anic style in narrating stories is: this style is always determined in view of the themes of the surah.

Now we shall discuss the verses. The story begins with a list of those who were chosen and whom Allah selected to bear the burden of prophethood. From the beginning of creation this prophethood was one, and the religion presented was one religion. These people were selected so that they would be leaders of the caravan of faith throughout the longest span of human history, across nations and ages. It is also indicated here that these people belonged to one lineage and were born of one another's offspring. It is not necessary that these people were naturally linked by a genealogy and were each other's biological descendants (although the genealogy of all of them ultimately reaches Noah and Adam, peace be upon them). Their true lineage is that Allah had chosen and selected all of them, and their genealogy was an ideological genealogy according to which this caravan of faith was moving.

In the context of the discourse, Adam and Noah are mentioned as individuals. But the families of Abraham and Imran are mentioned. This indicates that Adam, in his individual capacity, and Noah, in his individual capacity, were worthy of respect and chosen; but the descendants of Abraham and Imran were also worthy of respect. And this honour and distinction accord with the principle mentioned in Surah al-Baqarah, namely that the blessing and honour which comes to the family of prophethood does not come merely by blood inheritance, but is an ideological inheritance.

"And when Abraham was tried by his Lord with certain words, and he fulfilled them, He said: Indeed I will make you an imam for the people. He said: And from my offspring? He said: My covenant does not reach the wrongdoers." (124)

Some narrations state that Imran was of the descendants of Abraham (peace be upon him). In that case, the mention of this particular branch from the descendants of Abraham is made for a specific purpose: it is mentioned as an introduction to the stories of Mary and Jesus (peace be upon them both). It is also worth noting that Moses and Jacob from among the descendants of Abraham are not mentioned, because these were the leaders of the Children of Israel, that is, the Jews at the time of the Messenger (ﷺ), and since the coming discussion was about the Christians, there was no need to mention Moses and Jacob.
