Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 35:

After this introductory declaration of honour, the discussion now turns directly to the family of Imran.

Through the story of the vow, the heart of the wife of Imran is revealed in full. She was the mother of Maryam. Her heart is filled with the delight of faith. She offers her dearest possession to Allah, namely the child that is still in her womb. She offers him purely for Allah, and there is no condition or restriction attached to this offering. No polytheistic notion is associated with it, as is often the case with vows. In this act there is no idea of anyone's right other than Allah's. The expression "muharrar" (dedicated, freed for service) used for this unconditional vow is extremely meaningful. This is because the one who is truly free is the one who belongs entirely to Allah. He flees from everything and takes refuge in the presence of the Lord. He is liberated from the slavery of every person, every thing and every value, and adopts servitude to Allah alone. Only in this way does a human being become truly free from all forms of slavery. In every other case, some form of slavery remains, even if freedom appears apparent.

Only after grasping this point does it become clear that the doctrine of Tawhid (Oneness of Allah) is in fact a complete charter of freedom. How can a person be considered free when, in any matter, he is compelled to become the slave and follower of others besides Allah: in the world of his self and psychology, in the affairs of his daily life, in his customs and manners, in the values of his life, or in the laws and constitution of his life? These are the things that control his life. If a person's heart is captivated by the love of other than Allah, or he is bound under the yoke of servitude to other than Allah, or he is a victim of the love of something, in what sense can he be called free? While in his life such values are honoured and such laws are being implemented which are derived from other than Allah. In the world, true freedom was attained by human beings when they adopted the Islamic doctrine of Tawhid.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 36:

The prayer of the wife of Imran, perfumed with the fragrance of humility and submission, is: "O my Lord, accept my vow from me!" The vow is a piece of her heart, the very core of her being. From this it becomes clear that she was purely a Muslim (one who submits) and obedient to Allah. She has turned toward the direction of the Word of Allah (kalimatullah), completely single-minded, free from every bond, and in her heart there is nothing but the desire for the acceptance of the vow and the pleasure of Allah.

﴿Then when she had given birth to her, she said, "My Lord, I have given birth to a female," and Allah was most knowing of what she gave birth to, "and the male is not like the female. And I have named her Maryam, and I seek refuge for her in You and for her offspring from Satan, the accursed."﴾

She had thought that her child would be a boy, and the children who were dedicated in churches were generally boys, so that they would serve the temple, devote themselves solely to worship, and cut themselves off from the world. But when she saw that the child was a girl, she turned to her Lord in distress and said, with a most regretful tone:

﴿"My Lord, I have given birth to a female."﴾

﴿"And Allah was most knowing of what she gave birth to."﴾ Yet she says these words because she herself is turned toward Allah and presents an offering. It is as though through these words she is presenting an apology to Allah: that had it been a boy, he would have fulfilled his duties well. ﴿"And the male is not like the female."﴾ That is, for the purpose for which the vow was made, a boy would indeed have been more suitable. ﴿"And I have named her Maryam."﴾

Here, the manner in which the speech is conducted shows that the blessed wife of Imran is speaking to Allah face to face, though in seclusion; the whole matter of her heart is being told, clearly and plainly, and her entire possession is being presented directly in the presence of the Holy One. Such is the state of the relationship with Allah of these chosen servants of Allah: closeness, love, and direct connection with their Lord, conversing sincerely in simple words, without affectation or complexity. They speak in the manner of one whose Lord is very near to them, who loves them, hears them, and accepts them.

﴿And I seek refuge for her in You and for her offspring from Satan, the accursed.﴾

This is the final statement that a mother makes, in farewell, after presenting her child's vow. She entrusts her to the protection and mercy of her Lord, and seeks refuge for her and her progeny from the accursed Satan. These words are a manifestation of sincerity of heart; she gives this vow willingly and with a good disposition, and the protection she asks for her beloved offspring is that Allah shield her from the accursed Satan.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 37:

So his Lord accepted her with a goodly acceptance and caused her to grow up in a goodly growth. At last Allah accepted her daughter and raised her as a good girl. In the mother's heart there was a surging of sincerity and devotion to Allah; this was its reward. It was a pure vow, made solely for Allah, and in reality it was a preparation for the breathing of the spirit in the coming age. It was a preparation for bearing the Word of Allah (kalimat Allah), so that she would be ready for the extraordinary birth of Jesus, for which there was no precedent before it.

﴿And Zechariah became her guardian.﴾ He became her protector and responsible custodian. In that age Zechariah was the head of the Temple (haykal), and he was of the progeny of Aaron, and the custodianship and management of Solomon's Temple had remained in the hands of his descendants. Thus began the blessed process of Mary's nurturing and upbringing. Allah provided for this young worshipper a special sustenance from His particular bounty.

﴿Whenever Zechariah entered the sanctuary (mihrab) to see her, he found provision with her. He said, "O Mary, from where does this come to you?" She said, "It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without reckoning."﴾ Whenever Zechariah went into the sanctuary to her, he would find some food and drink with her. He would ask, "Mary! From where has this come to you?" She would reply, "It is from Allah. Allah gives to whom He wills without measure."

We do not wish to enter into the details of what that provision was, as various narrations have been reported. It is sufficient here to say that the provision was very blessed. There was blessing in her surroundings, and from every direction the things on which the word "provision" applies were being supplied. The provision was so abundant that even its guardian would be astonished, though he was a prophet. Seeing these bounties and blessings, he would ask in amazement how and from where this was coming. But Mary, like a truly faithful believer, would answer with great humility and submission, acknowledging Allah's favors. By acknowledging Allah's generosity, she would entrust the matter to Him.

﴿It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without reckoning.﴾ These are the words that show what the relationship of the servant with his Lord is, and how the honored servants keep the secrets that exist between them and their Lord as secrets, and speak about those secrets with great humility and modesty. They do not fall into pride or vanity. Here an extraordinary situation regarding the provision with Mary is shown, which even Zechariah, the prophet of his time, found astonishing. It is mentioned as a preface to the greater wonders of Allah's power that were to come, among which are the births of John (Yahya) and Jesus (peace be upon them both).

At this point, on seeing (a daughter like Mary and her abundant provision), a ray of hope arose in the heart of Zechariah (peace be upon him). He had no child. This was a natural desire, which Allah's power has placed in the heart of every human being: the strong desire for righteous offspring, so that a person's lineage continues and he has a successor after him. This is the desire that remains alive even in the hearts of great worshippers and ascetics, and in the hearts of those who have dedicated themselves to worship and who have devoted themselves to the service of the Temple. This is the nature with which Allah created people, and it is the result of a profound wisdom that the continuity of life in this world goes on, and grows day and night with multiplied progress. At this point, Zechariah (peace be upon him) comes forward.

Thus we find ourselves before an extraordinary event. This event is a manifestation that the will of Allah is unrestricted, and that He is free from the bonds of the chain of causes and effects to which man is accustomed to looking before and after, and about which man believes that no deviation from them is possible. For this reason, man remains skeptical about those events and occurrences which do not lie within the limits and bounds of this law. And when they are unable to deny them, when it is no longer possible for them to reject such events because they do occur, then they throw covers of stories and tales over those events.

Consider: Zakariyya is an elderly man and a shaykh, and his wife has been barren since her youth as well as in her old age. In the heart of this old man, the desire for offspring stirs, which is a natural desire. He sees Maryam, a righteous and beautiful girl, to whom abundant provision has been given. He communicates with his Lord and makes supplication that he too may be granted such pure offspring.

﴿هُنَالِكَ دَعَا زَكَرِيَّا رَبَّهُ قَالَ رَبِّ هَبْ لِي مِنْ لَدُنْكَ ذُرِّيَّةً طَيِّبَةً إِنَّكَ سَمِيعُ الدُّعَاءِ﴾

"At this state, Zakariyya called upon his Lord, saying: 'O my Lord! Grant me from Yourself good offspring. Verily, You are the Hearer of supplication.'"

What was the result of this heartfelt and moving supplication? It was accepted immediately, and this offspring and this acceptance were beyond the bonds of time and place. The ordinary, customary system was set aside, because the real cause is the will of Allah.

The prayer that issues from the heart, and from a pure heart, is accepted. This is because in that prayer hope was placed only in the One who hears prayer, and who can clothe it with acceptance whenever He wills. The angels gave Zakariyya the good news of a boy, and his name, Yahya, was given before his birth. His qualities and character were also described in advance: he would be a good leader, he would keep his own desires well under control, and he would have firmly grasped the reins of his inclinations and tendencies. He would be a believer and one who confirms the truth (mu'min wa musaddiq), and he would affirm whatever command of Allah came to him. He would be a righteous prophet (nabi salih), and a member of the caravan of the righteous (salihin).

Nevertheless, this prayer was accepted, and the ordinary circumstance that people see in their daily lives, and regard as an unbreakable law, did not stand in its way. People also think that Allah's will is bound by this same law. The matters that a person observes, and from which he then concludes that this is a law and that deviation from it is impossible, are a relative matter. This is not a final observation. A person's lifespan is limited, and his knowledge is limited. Human reason is confined within the bounds of physics. It cannot reach Allah's ultimate law, nor can it grasp absolute reality. Is it not fitting for a human being to remain humble, and to keep within his limits in accordance with the saying "Abar qadar khud bash" (know your own measure), and not to enter that boundless valley without an informed guide? For the valley of the possible and the impossible is boundless. It is strange that a person sets for Allah's will a boundary that lies within his own experience, which is the circle of his limited knowledge.

This acceptance of a heartfelt prayer was itself a matter of wonder even for Hazrat Zakariyya (peace be upon him), for after all he too was a human being. Thus there arose in his heart the desire to see how this extraordinary event would come about, although the daily observation of a human being runs contrary to it.

"Zakariyya said: 'My Lord, how can I have a son when old age has overtaken me and my wife is barren?'" The answer is given with great simplicity and ease; the matter is brought to its place, and a reality is presented which holds no difficulty in its understanding and no wonder in its occurrence. ﴿Qala kadhalika Allahu yaf'alu ma yasha'﴾ ("He said: 'Thus does Allah do what He wills'"). This is the method which is in fact in operation: it is repeated day and night. The will of Allah keeps working, and the affairs of Allah occur in this manner by day and by night. But people do not reflect well upon these events; they do not deeply observe and contemplate this craftsmanship of Allah, and they do not fix these realities in their minds.

In the same way, with ease and fluency, He does what He wills. What difficulty is there for Him in granting Zakariyya a son, even though he has grown old and his wife has become barren? Growing old and becoming barren are only observations of human beings, upon which they build rules for themselves, and so they set down a principle for themselves. As for Allah, the Exalted, how could He be bound by the laws and conjectures of the human mind? He reverses experiences however He wills; His will is free from every restriction.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 41:

But Hazrat Zakariyya's (ʿalayhi al-salam) eager longing was galloping at full speed. Nevertheless, he was a human being, and having suddenly heard the glad tidings, he became perplexed. He asked his Lord to appoint for him a sign of this marvel's appearance, so that he might be reassured and await it calmly. ﴿He said, "My Lord, appoint for me a sign."﴾ ……… Now Allah, may He be exalted, makes true reassurance arrangements for him. He is himself brought a little outside the sphere of his daily routine. It is decreed that the sign will be that for three days your tongue will be bound: you will turn towards people, but you will not be able to speak; you will turn only towards your Lord, mention Allah, and glorify and declare His oneness (tasbih and tahlil).

﴿He said, "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gesture. And remember your Lord much, and glorify Him in the evening and the morning."﴾ ……… Here the Qur'an falls silent, but we know that this event actually happened in this way: Hazrat Zakariyya's (ʿalayhi al-salam) tongue was bound, and he went out of all ordinary daily life. The law of people's daily life was also suspended. Behold, this was the very tongue that used to move vigorously; today it is bound. Speech with people is bound, and communion with Allah continues. The question is: upon which law of nature are they now proceeding? That law is that the will of the Absolute Deity is free from every restriction and bond. If we do not accept this principle in our lives, then what other explanation can we offer for these extraordinary matters? What other explanation can we offer for the birth of children to this aged man and this elderly woman?

This extraordinary event is mentioned here so that afterwards the actual extraordinary event of the birth of ʿIsa (ʿalayhi al-salam) may be described, which gave rise to countless doubts and incredible theories. The birth of the Messiah (ʿalayhi al-salam) was in reality one event in the series of events of Allah's unrestricted will. From here the account of the birth of the Messiah begins. First of all, Hazrat Maryam is purified, through worship and turning to Allah, for the acceptance of this spirit.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 42:

What was this distinction? It was that Allah would directly breathe into him one of His spirits, just as Allah had first breathed a spirit into the earthen body of Adam. And this extraordinary event was then presented to all of humanity in its own particular manner. In truth, this is a unique distinction in the history of humankind, and undoubtedly a great event... But until today humanity had no correct knowledge of this great event. By pointing to this clarification, the impression is given that the baseless suspicions which the Jews spread about the birth of Isa (peace be upon him), and the vile attacks they made, are deserving of condemnation. They spread doubts about the purity of Maryam, and their argument was that until now there has never occurred in the history of humankind a birth of this extraordinary kind. Therefore these Jews (may Allah destroy them) used to say that behind this event there is some disagreeable secret.

Here one comes to understand the station of the greatness of Islam, and it also becomes clear how lofty and trustworthy the pure source of Islam is. The People of the Book, including the Christians, were levelling all kinds of accusations against the Messenger ﷺ. They were denying him, they were his enemies, and they were always ready for disputation and wrangling. They spread doubts against the truth of Islam. Yet see: he brings from his Lord the message that the reality of Maryam (peace be upon her) is this, and that she is preferred over all the women of the worlds. Thus Islam raises the status of Maryam to the highest horizons. But the circumstances are such that the followers of Maryam have come to debate and dispute with him, and they make the veneration of Maryam (peace be upon her) a pretext for not believing in the Messenger ﷺ and for denying the religion of Muhammad ﷺ.

What a truth this is, and how great is the greatness of Islam! What greater proof could there be than that the Messenger ﷺ is truthful and is benefiting from a true source? Those who bring revelation to him are also truthful; they take the truth from their Lord. They announce the truth that they find concerning Maryam and Isa (peace be upon them). If you were not a true Messenger of Allah, they would not, in such circumstances, have declared this truth about your enemies.

"O Mary! Be obedient to your Lord, prostrate yourself before Him, and bow down along with those who bow down."

That is: adopt humility and submissiveness (khushu'), remain engaged in the obedience and worship of Allah, and live a life bound to Allah—and all of this is to prepare you for the great responsibility that is about to come.

This passage refers to the incident when a dispute arose among the attendants of the temple (haikal) over which of them should become her guardian (sarparast), at the time when her mother brought her to the temple. She was then a young girl. The mother had brought her so that she might fulfil her vow (nazr) and the covenant she had made with her Lord.

This verse mentions an event that is not recorded in the Old Testament, nor in the New Testament, meaning the versions in circulation today. Yet this matter was well known among the rabbis (ahbar) and monks (ruhban) of that time. That is, the incident of the attendants casting their pens (qalmen) was a famous event of that age, and it took place so that it could be decided who would take on her guardianship (kafalah). The Qur'an has not given the details of this incident, and perhaps this is because the Qur'an's listeners would already know this event to be well known; or because the Qur'an mentioned the event and did not feel the need to give more details, since the event itself would be only of this extent. For example, they may have agreed upon a particular method for the guardianship, that is, by casting pens they would determine to whose lot the guardianship should fall, just as lots are drawn today.

Some narrations mention that they cast their pens into the River Jordan, and all the pens were carried away with the waves except the pen of Zakariya, which remained in its place, and this was a sign among them as to whom the guardianship should fall.

In any case, all these events were in the realm of the unseen. The Prophet ﷺ was not present at that time, and this matter had not reached the knowledge of the Messenger ﷺ. It is possible that this matter was one of the secret matters of the people of the temple, the publication of which to the common people was forbidden; and the Qur'an, by disclosing it, informed the scholars of the People of the Book of that time that Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is a truthful messenger and that the Qur'an is based on divine revelation. No narration states that the People of the Book came to debate; if such an event had not occurred among them, they would have said that no such incident had happened at all.

Now begins here the account of the birth of Prophet Isa (peace be upon him). According to the customary practices of people, this is a great marvel, because it is contrary to the manner in which the will of Allah ordinarily operates.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verses 45–46:

Maryam (peace be upon her), by her purity, her single-minded devotion and her constant worship, became fit to receive this news and to be prepared for this great event. And see now: she is prepared, and now the angels are speaking with her. She is being given the news.

﴿When the angels said: "O Maryam! Indeed Allah gives you good news of a Word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, 'Isa, son of Maryam, honoured in this world and the Hereafter, and of those brought near (to Allah). He will speak to people in the cradle and in maturity, and he will be among the righteous."﴾

In this verse the matter is explained fully, and the good news is given to her. This good news concerns a Word (Command) from Allah, whose name will be the Messiah, 'Isa son of Maryam. Grammatically, the word "Messiah" is an apposition (badal) to "Word"; that is, the Word is the Messiah, son of Maryam. After this manner of expression, nothing further remains to be said... These and many other such matters are genuinely unseen matters, and it is not fully possible to reach their reality. It is possible that these are among the mutashabihat (ambiguous verses) about which it was said at the beginning of this surah:

﴿It is He who has sent down to you the Book; in it are verses that are muhkamat (clear in meaning), they are the foundation of the Book, and others that are mutashabihat (ambiguous). As for those in whose hearts is deviation, they follow what is ambiguous in it, seeking discord and seeking its interpretation.﴾

But this matter is very easy to understand if we wish to understand it with fear of Allah, and if the signs of Allah's craftsmanship and power are in our minds, and we know that Allah is free from the limits and restrictions that He Himself has set for this world-governance.

When Allah willed, He created Adam from clay. Whether the creation of Adam was directly from clay and the breath of spirit was blown into the clay, or an initial germ was created and it resulted in the existence of Adam, I do not enter into this discussion here, because in both cases that secret remains a secret, which we call the secret of life: the secret that gave life to the first creation. Whether the spirit was placed in the first figure of Adam or in the germ, in both cases it is a great miracle, because whether the germ is living or the spirit is suddenly placed in the life of a complete human, both forms are a miracle.

The question is: where did this life come from, and how did it come? In any case, we say with certainty that this life is something separate from clay and all those dead elements. It is an additional thing; it is a reality separate from the elements. It has certain traces and certain signs which are not present in clay or other elements, nor are they found in other dead material things. The question is: what is the reality of this secret, that is, of life? It is not enough, in order to deny this reality, to simply say that we do not know, as materialists nowadays say out of helplessness; but no wise person gives importance to their statement, nor does any scholar accept it.

We do not know this secret, despite the fact that in seeking the secret of life we have made the utmost efforts until today, but we have not been able to attain that secret, because we tried to obtain it through known material means, and those efforts went in vain. We tried to rescue life from the wilderness of death, but failed... We do not know, but Allah, who created death and life, indeed knows. He says: "and breathed into it of His spirit," and He expressed it with the word "Kun fayakun", that is "Be", and it was. Now, what is this breathing of the spirit? How, in the state of death, is this breath of spirit given and that state changes into the state of life, and this subtle secret remains beyond understanding?

What is its reality? What is its nature? This is the essence and nature whose perception lies beyond the range of human intellect's capacity, because it is beyond its station and rank. It has not been given the capacity to comprehend it. Can this reality, like oceans, fit in the skull of man? Therefore, man has his own purpose of creation and certain duties, namely the duty of vicegerency (khilafah) on earth; for this he does not need awareness of this secret. He was not created here for the business of life and death, so that the essence of life should be made known to him, or that he should be informed of the manner of the breathing of the spirit, and how, at the first step of life, this life was joined to the being of Adam, when the seed of life was placed in them.

Here Allah the Exalted says: when He breathed His spirit into Adam, by it Adam was granted this honour, to the extent that he was given preference even over the angels. Therefore it is necessary that this honour and this life be something other than a germ and a microbe. This is that breath of the spirit, because of which we hold the belief that man on this earth is a species of his own; his creation was distinctly separate, and in this universe he has an honoured and dignified station which other living beings do not possess.

In any case, our subject here is not the creation of man. In the context of the discourse we have shed light on this point for a while, because sometimes a doubt may arise in the mind of a reader as to how human birth can take place in this manner. The important point here is that Allah the Exalted informs us about the secret of life. Although we cannot grasp its essence, and although we cannot perceive the manner of the breathing of the spirit into the dead, we can understand the secret of life...

By creating Adam (peace be upon him) directly, Allah then established a natural path for the creation of humankind, namely that through the union of husband and wife the caravan of humanity proceeds. That is, by the union of the egg produced by the wife with the male germ, wombs became fruitful and generations continued. Just as this egg is alive, so too this germ is alive; both are in motion.

The caravan of life set out on this road and people became accustomed to it. Then came a point when Allah changed this long-established path: the ordinary law was suspended for a limited time, the rule was suspended for one individual, and an example was created in the form of Adam (peace be upon him), though not entirely like him. Here now a child is born only from a woman, and that same spirit is breathed into this woman which was breathed into the original creation, and signs of life came into being in the womb of this woman. Here metaphysical questions arise: Is this the breathing of the Word? Is the Word the name of the attention of will? Is the Word "Kun"? which sometimes is a reality and sometimes is merely an allusion to the attention of will. Is the Word itself 'Isa, or is the Word that by which he came into existence?... All these discussions are such that only doubts can result from them; no certainty is achieved through these discussions. The actual reality is that Allah brought into existence a life of a kind that has no parallel. By His unrestricted will He gave it existence. In this life He placed a spirit from Himself. We see the traces of this spirit, but we are incapable of perceiving its essence and nature. It is our duty to remain incapable of this, because such perception does not add to that capacity which is necessary for us to fulfil the duty of vicegerency on this earth.

This matter can be understood very easily in this form, and in this form no doubt arises about its occurrence... In short, the angels gave Maryam the good news. In this good news a command from Allah was to come; the name of this command was given as the Messiah 'Isa son of Maryam. His kind and lineage were also mentioned; the lineage was traced to Maryam. In the good news his qualities and his exalted rank with Allah were mentioned. His honour in this world and the Hereafter was mentioned, and it was also announced that he would be among those brought near to Allah. It was also mentioned that from the moment of his birth the manifestation of miracles would begin: he would begin speaking from the cradle among people. That is, he would speak in youth as well. And the most important of his qualities would be that he would be among the caravan of the righteous.

Here now a child is born only from a woman, and that same spirit is breathed into this woman which was breathed into the original creation, and signs of life came into being in the womb of this woman. Here metaphysical questions arise: Is this the breathing of the Word? Is the Word the name of the attention of will? Is the Word "Kun"? which sometimes is a reality and sometimes is merely an allusion to the attention of will. Is the Word itself 'Isa, or is the Word that by which he came into existence?... All these discussions are such that only doubts can result from them; no certainty is achieved through these discussions. The actual reality is that Allah brought into existence a life of a kind that has no parallel. By His unrestricted will He gave it existence. In this life He placed a spirit from Himself. We see the traces of this spirit, but we are incapable of perceiving its essence and nature. It is our duty to remain incapable of this, because such perception does not add to that capacity which is necessary for us to fulfil the duty of vicegerency on this earth.

This matter can be understood very easily in this form, and in this form no doubt arises about its occurrence... In short, the angels gave Maryam the good news. In this good news a command from Allah was to come; the name of this command was given as the Messiah 'Isa son of Maryam. His kind and lineage were also mentioned; the lineage was traced to Maryam. In the good news his qualities and his exalted rank with Allah were mentioned. His honour in this world and the Hereafter was mentioned, and it was also announced that he would be among those brought near to Allah. It was also mentioned that from the moment of his birth the manifestation of miracles would begin: he would begin speaking from the cradle among people. That is, he would speak in youth as well. And the most important of his qualities would be that he would be among the caravan of the righteous.

Maryam was a virgin, her life was pure, and her understanding of childbirth was exactly as she observed it in her surroundings. She received this glad tiding in the way a young unmarried girl would naturally understand it. She immediately turned to her Lord and petitioned that this matter was beyond the grasp of her understanding. Her intellect was bewildered.

﴿She said: "My Lord, how can I have a child when no man has touched me?"﴾

Here she is answered immediately, and in this answer she is directed to a simple reality which a human being, having become accustomed to the chain of causes and effects in daily life, has forgotten. This is because his sources of knowledge are limited, and he remains confined within the narrow sphere of habit.

﴿He said: "Thus does Allah create what He wills. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is."﴾

When Allah links this matter to the reality of the beginning of creation, astonishment disappears, bewilderment goes away, and the heart becomes content. A person himself begins to ask, with wonder, how he could have been amazed by a matter so simple and clear, which is most natural and easily understood.

In this way the Qur'an extends the Islamic conception, with such simplicity and natural manner, even to such great truths: in a natural manner, in a manner easily comprehended. And those doubts which philosophical sentiments used to further complicate, Islam clears away and settles in hearts, and they also come close to reason.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 48:

After this, further details of that glad tidings are given, the one for whose birth Maryam was chosen, and which is being fulfilled in a unique manner. It is told what the character and conduct of this one who is to come will be. The future history of Isa is related. Now the glad tidings and the history continue side by side, so the glad tidings are being given while history also moves along. This is the Qur'an's own style of discourse.

﴿And He will teach him the Book and the Wisdom, and the Torah and the Injeel﴾ ... "And Allah will teach him the Book and wisdom, and will teach him the knowledge of the Torah and the Injeel, and will make him a messenger to the Children of Israel." The word "Kitab" (Book) sometimes means writing, and sometimes it means the Torah and the Injeel. In that case, the mention of the Torah and the Injeel is an explanatory apposition (atf bayan) to "Kitab." Hikmah (wisdom) is the name of a faculty in a person's mind through which he places everything in its proper position, and through which a person can distinguish between right and wrong, and follow what is right. This hikmah and faculty is in reality a great good (khair kathir). The Torah was also the Book of Isa, just as the Injeel was his Book. The Torah was the foundation of the religion that he brought, and the Injeel was in fact a completion of that same religion. Through it, the reviving of the true spirit of the Torah was intended, that spirit which had departed from the Jews; their hearts had become empty of that spirit. Among those who debate about Christianity, most do not have in mind that the original basis of the religion of Masih is the Torah. In it is the system of Shariah on which the order of society rests. The Injeel made many additions and deletions to it. That Injeel, in itself, was only a struggle for the revival of religion. The aim of Isa (peace be upon him) was that, by going beyond the outward texts, the conscience and the spirit of a person should be purified. And that movement for the revival of the spirit, which caused society to plot against him, and for which he kept struggling, was this:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 49:

This verse shows that the mission of Hazrat Isa (peace be upon him) was meant only for the Children of Israel, since he was among the prophets of the Children of Israel. For this reason, the Torah, which was revealed to Hazrat Musa (peace be upon him) and which contained the law for organising the life of the Children of Israel, and in which the matters of mutual dealings and collective organisation were settled, was also the book of Hazrat Isa (peace be upon him). However, the Injil was added to it. The purpose was to bring about spiritual purity among the Children of Israel, to awaken their conscience and to illuminate their hearts.

And the miracle about which Allah gave good news to his mother, Hazrat Maryam, that this miracle would be with him, and with which he openly debated the Children of Israel, was also this very miracle of giving life. That is, breathing into a dead thing and putting a soul into it, a thing coming alive, raising dead people to life again, and restoring sight to those born blind. And curing the leper, and giving news of the unseen, such as what the Children of Israel had eaten and what they had stored in their houses, as if these things were hidden from sight.

……Here the verse speaks of the miracles that appeared through the tongue of Hazrat Isa (peace be upon him), which had been given as good news to Hazrat Maryam, and which later also appeared through the tongue of Hazrat Isa. Here the verse repeatedly emphasises that all these miracles which appeared, and which were actually presented before the Children of Israel, were from Allah and by Allah's permission. After every miracle, the permission of Allah is emphasised. This is so that, as a matter of caution, no one should consider these to be a personal excellence of Hazrat Isa (peace be upon him).

The connection of all these miracles is either with the creation of life, or with restoring life to a creature from which life has departed, or with human health, which is itself a means of sustaining life, or with the perception of matters that are apparently hidden from sight. The connection of all these miracles, in their reality, is with the miracle of Hazrat Isa's (peace be upon him) extraordinary birth. Allah brought him into existence in a manner for which there is no parallel except Hazrat Adam. If Allah can manifest such miracles through one of His creatures, why could He not Himself create Hazrat Isa as a miracle in that manner? Therefore there is no justification for the doubts that were spread about Hazrat Isa, nor is there any need for the stories that the Christians themselves composed about his birth. For when a matter falls under the will of Allah, then there is no impossibility left, and human habit cannot place any restriction upon Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verses 50–51:

This is the conclusion of the call of Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him). That is, this was the message which he gave to the Children of Israel. It clarifies the same fundamental points which have always been the essential principles of Allah's religion, and to which all the Messengers have called. These are truths of very great importance, especially when they are repeated on the tongue of Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him). This is because his birth itself was a cause of dispute, and these disputes arose because people did not reflect on the reality of religion and of the Messengers; namely, that the Messengers are one, and their religion is one. Therefore Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him) says:

﴿وَمُصَدِّقًا لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ مِنَ التَّوْرَاةِ وَلِأُحِلَّ لَكُم بَعْضَ الَّذِي حُرِّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ "And I confirm that which was before me of the Torah, and to make lawful for you some of that which was forbidden to you..."

Here the true religion which was the original religion of Christianity is being described. Thus the Torah which was revealed upon Hadrat Musa (peace be upon him) fully contained that true religion, and within it was the complete Shariah which organised collective life in the best manner; that is, in accordance with the needs of that age and the circumstances of the Children of Israel at that time, and from the standpoint that at that time it was a particular system of life for a particular group of people. Hadrat Masih relied upon this same Torah in his mission. He confirmed the Torah. Yes, in it some forbidden things were made lawful, and those things had been forbidden to them as a punishment, because they had committed certain sins and evil deeds. And for their training Allah had also forbidden certain things. After this, Allah, through Isa (peace be upon him), showed mercy upon them, and those things which had been forbidden were made lawful for them again.

From this it becomes known that every religion has this true nature: that it organises people's lives through legislation. The nature of religion is not merely the refinement of morals. Nor does religion suffice with correcting human concepts and their intuition and consciousness. Nor is it only the function of religion to prescribe some acts of worship so that people sit down as worshippers of those ritual observances. A religion which is content only with such partial matters is not religion in its true sense. Religion is only that which is a system for the whole of life, which is prescribed by Allah, and which establishes human life according to the methodology of Allah.

It is also correct that if creedal beliefs, acts of worship and moral values are separated from religion, then in that case religion becomes merely jurisprudence (fiqh). And then it does not work properly in human life. Then this becomes contrary to the religious temperament.

This is the accident which befell Christianity: due to certain historical causes, and also because it was revealed for a limited time, and it came as a preface to the final Prophethood of Hadrat Muhammad (ﷺ). The Shariah system became separated from the spiritual teachings of Christianity. The historical causes were that a severe enmity arose between the Jews and Masih (peace be upon him). After him too, there remained severe enmity between his followers and the Jews. As a result, this Shariah, the Torah, was also for a limited people and a limited time, and so were the moral teachings of Hadrat Isa. This was so that, according to the planned design in Allah's system of power, the final and comprehensive Shariah of Hadrat Muhammad (ﷺ) would be revealed, and would be a Shariah for the whole of humanity forever.

In any case, the situation became that Christianity became a great tree in which there was no system of Shariah. Therefore it always remained incapable of controlling the collective life of those nations which had accepted it. This is because for guiding collective life there is need for a conception of life which clarifies every sphere of life; which shows what the value and worth of the human being is in this entire universe; which has within it a strong system of worship, and also possesses a good moral and spiritual system; and after that it has an excellent collective legal system, and this moral and legal system is derived from its original conception of life. If religion is composed of these constituent elements, then it can organise collective life. At that time a person also understands the wisdom of religion, and then it guarantees the human system.

In short, when the moral teachings of Christianity were separated from the Shariah, then Christianity was no longer capable of becoming a complete system of life. Therefore a complete separation occurred in the lives of people between moral values and collective values, and there was no unity between their morals and their deeds. Thus their collective system did not remain a natural system which harmonised with their moral values. Therefore the collective system of the Christians has always either remained suspended in the air, with no connection to the spiritual world, or, if it did function, it was a lame and crippled system.

When humanity in the course of human history was afflicted with this situation, it was not an ordinary event but a great calamity. It was a very destructive calamity. It was such a great event that from it springs of misfortune gushed forth for humanity. People fell into bewilderment and distress. A flood of moral lawlessness came upon them, and such calamities came upon them that the godless material collective system has remained ensnared in them until today, and today Europe is its example. Whether this system is in those countries which still have a connection with Christianity, or in those countries where Christianity has ended, there is not much difference between the two. This is because Christianity, in the form in which Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him) presented it, and like every system to which the name of religion applies, was a system in which there was a complete Shariah, law and order for life, which was based upon the creed of Tawhid and which stood upon the moral concepts derived from that creed. Therefore present-day Christianity cannot be called Christianity merely because it does not contain the complete system of life which Hadrat Masih presented. Rather, Christianity would simply not be a religion at all. In short, apart from these constituent elements, no collective system can be established for solving the problems of life which is complete, which is sufficient for all the needs of the human soul, which solves the practical problems of human life, and which establishes the firm connection of human life with its Lord. And this is the reality which is one of the meanings and implications of the words of Hadrat Masih (peace be upon him), who says:

﴿وَمُصَدِّقًا لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ مِنَ التَّوْرَاةِ وَلِأُحِلَّ لَكُم بَعْضَ الَّذِي حُرِّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ "I confirm that part of the Torah which is before me, and I declare lawful for you some of the things which have been declared forbidden to you."

Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him) grounds the declaration of his mission in the Oneness of Allah, which in Islam is the first great truth. He says:

﴿وَجِئْتُكُم بِآيَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ (50) إِنَّ اللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبُّكُمْ فَاعْبُدُوهُ هَٰذَا صِرَاطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ "Behold, I have come to you with a sign from your Lord. So fear Allah and obey me. Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is the straight path."

Here he presents the ideological conception of life upon which the religion of Allah is established. He says that the miracles which I have presented I have not presented from myself. Of himself he is a human being; how could he produce such miracles? These are the miracles of Allah, and my call is founded upon the fundamental principles of fear of Allah and obedience. After this he says that just as Allah is my Lord, so He is your Lord, and that he himself is not a lord but a servant. Therefore worship and devotion should be directed to the one Lord, because worship cannot be directed to anyone else. After this, the expression of all these matters, namely that the Lord is one, that worship is to Him alone, and that obedience is owed to the Messenger and to the system of life which he brought, is the straight path; and whatever lies beyond it is misguidance, error and deviation.

After the announcement of the angels to Hadrat Maryam, then the description of the coming Prophet, his Messengership, his miracles and his words, the story now suddenly reaches the scene where Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him) perceives that the Children of Israel have gone to the point of disbelief and denial, and now a general appeal is made by Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him) for the spread of Allah's religion and for its establishment.

The context of the narrative here has a very large gap. It is not mentioned here that Hazrat Isa was born. Nor is it mentioned that his mother came with him before the people and spoke to them from the cradle, nor that when he grew up he began to proclaim his prophetic mission, nor that the miracles given as glad tidings to his mother were shown through his hands (although this is mentioned in Surah Maryam). Gaps of this kind occur again and again in the Qur'anic narratives. One wisdom in this is that there should be no repetition; the other is that the Qur'an presents only those parts of a narrative that relate to the subject of the surah in which they occur, and the remaining links are left out.

In short, when he presented the miracles and began preaching, Hazrat Isa (peace be upon him) perceived that these people were not going to accept faith, although such miracles could not have come from any human being, and it was clear that behind these miracles only the power of Allah was at work. The powers of Allah supported Hazrat Isa (peace be upon him). And alongside these matters, it was also a reality that Hazrat Masih had come for the purpose of making lawful, for the Children of Israel, those things which had been made unlawful as a punishment for their folly, so that the burden on them would be lightened and the restrictions and fetters removed.

So, at such a moment, he said: ﴿Who will be my helpers in the cause of Allah?﴾ That is, who will assist me in calling to the religion and in the establishment of the Islamic system? Who will help me in reaching Allah, so that I may discharge my duties well? ...... This is the method of work of a movement calling to religion: every caller needs helpers. Those who support him, who carry the banner of his call, who defend him, who continually spread this call, and who, after the caller's death or departure, take it up and carry it forward. Then ﴿The disciples said: We are the helpers of Allah. We have believed in Allah. Bear witness that we are Muslims.﴾

The disciples mentioned Islam in the sense that relates to the reality of the religion. They then made Hazrat Isa (peace be upon him) a witness to their Islam and prepared themselves for the help of Allah. That is, they got ready for the support of the Messenger of Allah, the support of the religion of Islam, and the support of the Islamic system of life. After this, they turn to their Lord and directly establish their connection with Allah in this matter, that they have become ready for it. Therefore, may you also be a witness to this.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 3, verse 53:

It is noteworthy that they turned directly to Allah and made this pledge to Allah as well. There is an important point hidden in this. The initial covenant of the believer is with Allah alone. When a messenger conveys a message to the people of faith, his duty is then complete, and now the believer's allegiance (bay'ah) is established with Allah Almighty. And even when the messenger departs from this world, this obligation and this responsibility remain upon the believer's neck. And in this allegiance, in this covenant of responsibility, is the matter that they will keep obeying the messenger. Therefore, faith is not merely the name of a belief that resides in a person's conscience, but is the name of following (ittiba'), and obedience to the messenger's system is also essential. This is the meaning around which the themes of this entire surah revolve. In this surah this theme has been repeatedly expressed in various ways.

Here, among the words of the disciples (hawariyyun), there is an important sentence: فَاكْتُبْنَا مَعَ الشَّاهِدِينَ ("Record us among the witnesses"). The question is: what testimony do they give, and of what matter are they witnesses?

In reality, a person who believes and becomes a Muslim, and bows his head before the religion of Allah, then it becomes his duty to bear witness concerning this religion. He should testify that this religion has the right to remain established and enduring. He should give such testimony that the good which this religion brings to humanity is his testimony. And this believer cannot give testimony until he makes his self, his character, and his entire life a living picture of this religion. He should make such a picture that people, upon seeing it, regard it as an example and bear witness that indeed, if this is the form of religion, then this religion deserves to remain alive, and that this religion is superior and better than all systems, methods and societies in this entire universe.

Clearly, no person can give this testimony until he makes this religion his code of life, until he makes it a collective system, and until he makes it the system of law for himself and his people. And until a society is established around him which conducts the affairs of its life in accordance with this system of life, which is a divine and firm system. Moreover, this testimony cannot be fulfilled until that believer begins jihad for the establishment of this system of life, and until he prefers death over life in this jihad, that is, against the society in which the Islamic system is not implemented in human lives. And this will be the testimony that the duty of establishing the religion is dearer to him even than his own life, whereas life is a dear possession for everyone. Therefore he is called a shahid (martyr), because he gives testimony.

Here these disciples prayed that Allah record them among such witnesses; they will bear testimony for the religion. That is, they pray that He grant them the ability that their lives become a living model of the religion of the Messiah (Masih), and grant them the ability to strive (jihad) to bring into existence a society in which this religion is established. If they fulfill its right, then they have, in effect, borne witness to the truth of this religion, that it is a true religion.

I will say here that whoever today claims faith and Islam for himself should pause and reflect upon this prayer. This is true Islam, as the disciples understood it, as genuine Muslims also hold this reality firmly in their hearts. And whoever does not bear witness for the religion and keeps it hidden, his heart is sinful. Know that whoever claims Islam and adopts a course in his practical life contrary to Islam, whoever believes in Islam but does not openly perform the Islamic obligations, and does not struggle to establish the Islamic system of life in practice, and does this either for the sake of his own peaceful life or gives his own life precedence over the life of the religion of Islam, then he has certainly been gravely negligent in bearing witness to the truth, or he has given testimony in favour of other systems against Islam. This is such testimony that also prevents others from coming to Islam, because they see that the people of Islam are bearing witness not for Islam but against Islam. And the end of that person who, on the basis of his claim that he is a Muslim, prevents all people from Islam is great ruin. Although he is not a believer in the religion but rather one who blocks from the religion (on this subject, the scholar Mawdudi has presented a valuable discussion in his book Shahadat-e-Haq, which you should definitely consult. Sayyid Qutb). Now comes the final part of the story of Isa (peace be upon him) with the Children of Israel.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 54:

The cunning that the Jews practised against their Messenger, Prophet Isa (peace be upon him), was a great scheme, and its web was very long and wide. As the Gospels mention, they levelled an accusation against him: that he had entered into relations with his betrothed, Yusuf the carpenter, although she was chaste and her marriage to Yusuf had not yet taken place. They accused Isa of lying. Then, after this, they made complaints against him before the Roman ruler Pilate, saying that he was inciting people to rebel against the Roman government, and that he had gone astray and was corrupting the beliefs of the common people. Thereupon Pilate ordered their arrest, so that they could inflict on him whatever punishment they wished, because although he was an idolater, he knew how to punish a person about whom he had no doubt or suspicion. These were their plots; rather, this was a part of those plots.

﴿And they schemed, and Allah schemed, and Allah is the best of schemers.﴾ They began to make secret plans against him, and Allah made a secret plan against them, and in such plans Allah is supreme.

There is only a verbal correspondence between the plan of Allah and the plan of the Jews. In reality, the plan of the Jews is a scheme (makr), and the response of Allah is a plan (tadbir), and the meaning of makr is also to plan. Allah, the Exalted, has used the word makr for Himself here in order to express the contemptibility of their scheme, because how can their opposition be compared with Allah? Where are they and where is Allah; what is their scheme and what is the plan of Allah in comparison with it, what comparison is there between the two? They wanted to kill Isa (peace be upon him) or crucify him. But Allah brought him safe and sound to Himself and purified him from those disbelievers and their filthy environment, that is, He removed him far from them. After this, he was given the honour that those who follow him would remain superior to those who disbelieve his teachings until the Day of Resurrection. And things happened just as Allah willed. And Allah shattered the schemes of the schemers.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verses 55–57:

How his death took place, and how he was raised up to the heavens, are unseen matters, and they fall within the category of mutashabihat (the ambiguous verses), the true interpretation of which none knows except Allah. Therefore there is no benefit in debating this matter. There is no benefit in it for belief (aqidah), nor is there benefit in it for the Shariah. Those who pursue it and make it a subject of argument and dispute ultimately reach only superficial and surface-level conclusions. They become further entangled in confusion and complexity, and they cannot bring forward any definitive reality. Nor does the heart find any satisfaction, because this is a matter whose interpretation Allah alone knows……………

As for the statement that Allah has made the followers of Isa (peace be upon him) superior to those who rejected him until the Day of Resurrection, its meaning is very simple. The followers of Isa (peace be upon him) are those who believe in the true religion of Allah, and that is Islam. Islam is the religion whose reality was known to every prophet, and every messenger preached Islam alone. Whenever anyone believed in the true religion, that belief was Islam. When those who believed in Isa (peace be upon him) confront those who reject him, the believers prove superior because of their faith. Therefore they are the followers of Isa. The religion of Allah is one. Isa (peace be upon him) came bringing this very religion, just as all the prophets before him and their messengers came bringing the same religion. And those who follow Muhammad ﷺ believe in all the messengers from Adam (peace be upon him) to Muhammad, the last of the prophets……………

This is the general meaning, and it agrees with the context of this surah. This meaning also conforms to the reality of religion and the reality of faith. And the final outcome for the people of faith and the people of disbelief is that they will all go before Allah.

In this verse it is decided that everyone will receive the recompense for what they did, and justice will be so complete that not even the smallest injustice will occur. In this matter, whatever the wishes of people may be, or whatever falsehood they have fabricated……………, the return to Allah is certain. There is no escape from it. For the disbelievers, punishment in this world and the Hereafter has been decreed, and there is no one who can reverse it. As for those who accepted faith and then did righteous deeds, they will be given their reward in full. There can be no decrease or increase in it, and Allah will never do injustice. And how would He, when He does not love the wrongdoers?

As for the claim of the People of the Book that they would enter the Fire for only a few days, and the major and minor premises they built upon this assumption regarding the justice of Allah the Exalted, all of that is their own carnal desire. It is corrupt, it is false, and it has no foundation or basis.

When the story of Isa (peace be upon him) reaches the point at which the Messenger ﷺ had been debating with these people, an epilogue comes after the story, and in this epilogue all the truths that are derived from the events of the story are unveiled. Now the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is told the statement that he should present before the People of the Book to conclude this debate. It is a decisive statement through which this entire discussion and dialogue comes to an end. It also contains the truth that you have brought, and to which you call. This conclusion comes forward with complete certainty and complete clarity.

This is the conclusion of the discussion, where it is first said that the revelation sent down to the Messenger (ﷺ) is the truth.

﴿That is what We recite to you of the signs and the wise Reminder.﴾ These are signs and reminders full of wisdom, which We recite to you. These stories and Qur'anic guidance are all based on the revelation of Allah, and Allah Himself recites to the Prophet (ﷺ) verses of wisdom and understanding. The manner of expression gives the impression that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) enjoys nearness to Allah and His good pleasure, since Allah Himself recites to the Prophet (ﷺ) verses of wisdom and understanding. Allah is All-Wise and possesses the lofty truths concerning human life and the self, and He has deposited them there in a particular manner and with a particular style. Only He can tell what the method of converse with the innate nature (fitrah) is, and what the manner of reaching the human fitrah is. And this wisdom is conveyed in a manner for which there is no previous parallel, that is, in the whole record of human wisdom whose source and origin is not Allah.

This is the commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran) on Surah Al-Imran, verse 59:

After this, the concluding reality settles the matter of Christ. It is stated decisively that Allah's will alone is the Creator of everything. Just as Allah created Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him), so too the process of creation with Allah is no more than this:

﴿Indeed, the likeness of Isa before Allah is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he was.﴾

The birth of Hadrat Isa, in that it departs from the ordinary course of human creation, is certainly astonishing. But when it is viewed in connection with the creation of Hadrat Adam (peace be upon him), nothing unique appears in it. In the matter of the birth of the Messiah, the People of the Book were engaged in debate, argument and wrangling, and in this regard they were fabricating strange tales and creating a mystical atmosphere, claiming that he was a wondrous matter merely because he was born without a father. These same People of the Book would recite in their scriptures, morning and evening, that Adam was created from dust, and then Allah breathed a spirit into that frame, and through it Adam became a living human being. And they did not fabricate such stories and did not engage in disputation concerning Adam. They thought about Adam that he too had a divine (lahuti) nature, because the elements from which Adam came into being as a human are the same elements from which Hadrat Isa came into being without a father. That is, Allah breathed His spirit into Hadrat Adam (peace be upon him), and He also breathed a spirit into Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him). And its mode was completed by a single word, "Kun" (Be). Allah said "Kun," and what He had intended to create became "Fayakun" (and it was).

How simple this reality is! The reality of Adam is this, and the reality is also this. Indeed, this is the only reality of the creation of all created beings. It is a reality that enters the human mind easily and clearly. It is a matter of wonder why this lengthy controversy and debate continued over these events, although this event was in accordance with Allah's great sunnah, which is pervasive throughout this entire universe, namely creating and resurrecting.

In fact, this is the manner of this Wise Reminder: it addresses human nature with natural logic, which is truly practical and simple. Because of this wise style of discourse, even the most complex and difficult philosophical problems of the world appear easy to it, like everyday routine matters.

When the discourse arrives at this clear decision, the address turns now to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he is told to remain steadfast upon his true position, which is being recited before him and being instilled in his awareness, just as it is being firmly established in the awareness of the believers, because some of the believers were being affected by the doubts of the People of the Book, and they were trying, through strange deception, to mislead the believers.

Sayyid Qutb says: "The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among those who doubt" (Qur'an 3:60). "Do not be among those who doubt it."

The Messenger ﷺ neither doubted nor had any hesitation in his heart. Whatever speech was revealed to him, he regarded it as coming from Allah. Not even for a moment did doubt approach him. The purpose here is that you remain firm upon this guidance. From this it becomes clear that in that era the enemies of the community of believers had spread a web of conspiracies against the people of faith, and they were trying to ensnare some individuals of the Muslim ummah in this plot. These conspiracies against the Muslim ummah are taking place even today and continue in every age. There is a need for the Muslim ummah to remain cautious against these deceivers and liars, because the enemies of the ummah of this kind bring a new net in every age.

In short, the issue of the birth of Masih (Jesus) has been resolved. The reality has become clear. Now Allah, the Exalted, directs the Messenger of Allah ﷺ towards ending this debate and disputation with these people, because the matter is now clear and the truth has come plainly to the fore. He is commanded that the final word is that these people should be invited to mubahalah (mutual imprecation).

Following this, the Messenger of God ﷺ, in the presence of a large gathering, issued a challenge of mubahala (mutual invocation) to those who had been disputing with him on this subject. That is, let all of them come forward and, with their hands raised in supplication, call upon God to curse the liars. The people were frightened by the consequences of this challenge, and they refused to accept the mubahala. Through this, it became clear that the position of the Messenger of God ﷺ was true. However, as some narrations mention, these people did not accept Islam because they held a high status in their society. Moreover, they were among the religious leaders of their community, and in that era the people of the church (Ahl al-Kanisah) held complete authority in their society, with great material interests tied to it. They were living a life of luxury and comfort within that society. It was not the case that no argument had been presented to those who were turning away from the religion of Islam; rather, some of their interests were such that they could not give them up, and they were surrounded by certain psychological desires which they could not overcome, even though the truth had become clear and there remained no doubt about it.

After the challenge of mubahala, this concluding passage now sets out the reality of revelation, the wisdom behind the stories in the Qur'an, and the reality of Tawhid (the Oneness of God). It is possible that these verses were revealed after the disputants refused the challenge of mubahala. They also deliver a stern warning to those who engage in disputes that cause corruption on God's earth, purely for their own sake rather than for the sake of God (fi sabil Allah).

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verses 62–63:

The truths expressed in these verses were already stated before. Here, after the invitation to mubahala (mutual imprecation) and the delegation's refusal of it, they are mentioned again for emphasis. What is new in this verse is that those who do not accept this truth are in reality mufsidun (corrupters), and they are warned that you are not hidden from Allah; He recognises you by your deeds of wickedness.

The corruption that the deniers of tawhid (divine oneness) spread by rejecting tawhid was a great corruption in the sight of Allah. Every corruption that arises in the world arises from deviation from the belief in tawhid. Nor is mere verbal affirmation of the belief in tawhid sufficient, because mere verbal affirmation has no worth. Nor is a religious affirmation that is purely negative (sufficient), because mere inner and verbal affirmation does not produce the effects that must appear in the practical life of human beings. In truth, the world has denied the necessary effects and results of the belief in tawhid, and has eliminated the effects of the belief in tawhid from human life.

The first requirement of the belief in tawhid is that our Lord is also one; then the servitude and worship of that Lord must also be one, because worship is exclusively for Allah; then obedience must be to that one Lord alone; and then all guidance must also be taken from that one Lord, that is, there should be no worship other than Him, no obedience other than to Allah, and no source of guidance other than Allah. Whether guidance is in legislation, whether it is in the values and philosophy of life, whether it is in morals and etiquette, in short, in all those affairs which relate to human life on this earth, guidance must be taken from Allah alone……… If the situation is not like this, then there is nothing but shirk (polytheism) and kufr (disbelief), whatever one may say with the tongue, and whatever abstract beliefs may be in the heart and consciousness, unless an atmosphere of submission, acceptance, obedience and compliance with commands and prohibitions is established in people's daily lives.

The truth is that the system of this entire universe cannot function properly until it is acknowledged that its Allah is one alone, who manages and arranges all its affairs. "Had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would certainly have been corrupted……" (Qur'an 21:22): "If there were in the heavens and the earth gods other than Allah, both would have been ruined." And the most distinguished manifestation of Allah's lordship in relation to human beings is that all servants worship Him, and that Allah prescribes for them a system of life and establishes for them the standards of good and bad. Therefore, whoever claims that any of these things belongs to him, he in effect lays hands upon the most exclusive rights of Allah the Exalted, and in this sense he makes himself the god and lord of people.

And in this sense, when many gods arise on this earth, then Allah's earth is filled with trial and corruption. People then begin to worship and serve other people. After this, some servants claim that they have the right that other people obey them personally, that they have the right by their own authority to make laws for people, and that they can decide the good and bad of people on their own. All these claims are in reality claims to divinity. If such people do not say verbally like Pharaoh, "I am your supreme lord" (Qur'an 79:24), then recognising such rights for such people is recognising shirk and kufr. And this is the worst trial and corruption in the world.
