Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 64:

That is why, after this admonition and rebuke, the context of the speech invites the People of the Book to come over to a position that is common between both parties. That is, only the worship of Allah, not associating anything with Him, and not taking one another as lords.

If they do not adopt this course, then our paths have parted forever. After that, there can be neither union nor dialogue.

﴿Say: O People of the Book, come to a word that is equitable between us and you: that we worship none but Allah, that we associate nothing with Him, and that some of us do not take others as lords besides Allah. But if they turn away, then say: Bear witness that we are Muslims.﴾

"Say: O People of the Book, come to a matter that is common between us and you: that we worship none but Allah, and do not associate anything with Him, and that none of us takes another as lord besides Allah. If they turn away from accepting this invitation, then plainly say: Bear witness that we are Muslims."

There is no doubt that this is a just invitation. It is an invitation in which the Messenger (ﷺ) does not seek to gain any kind of superiority or preeminence over them, nor do the Muslims seek any kind of superiority in it. It is a common position in front of which all stand on equal footing. No one seeks dominance over another, and no one makes another his slave. This is an invitation which only a corrupt-natured and mischievous person can reject, one who does not wish to bow before the truth.

This is an invitation that they worship Allah alone and associate no one with Him, neither a human being nor a stone. It is an invitation to Allah in which no human being is the slave of another human being: not the slave of a prophet, not the slave of a messenger, but all are servants and slaves of Allah. Prophets and messengers are those whom Allah has chosen for conveying the religion, not so that they become partners with Allah in divinity or lordship.

﴿But if they turn away, then say: Bear witness that we are Muslims.﴾ That is: if they refuse to accept that they will worship Allah alone and associate no one with Him, and refuse to accept that worship is for Allah alone, without any shirk. These are two manifestations through which the servant's stance toward Allah is expressed. So if they turn away from this principle, then you declare your Islam in accordance with it. Here, Muslims and those who take one another as lords besides Allah are presented in contrast to each other, which makes it decisively clear who the "Muslimun" are in Allah's sight: the Muslimun are those who worship and obey Allah alone, worship Allah alone, and also do not make one another their lords. This is the distinguishing characteristic of Muslims, which separates them from all religious communities and all schools of thought, and which sets their system of life apart from all other systems of life. Now, if this characteristic is found in them, they are Muslims; and if this characteristic is not found in them, they are not Muslims, however much they claim to be Muslims.

The essence of Islam is that a person becomes completely free from the servitude of created beings, and the Islamic way of life is the only system of life that guarantees a human being this all-encompassing freedom. The truth is that among all the systems of life prevailing on this earth, some take other people as their lord. This situation exists in the best of democracies as well as in the worst of dictatorships. The first characteristic of lordship is that people worship that lord, and that lord establishes for people their collective order, way of life, codes, laws, and the standards of good and bad. In all the systems of life prevailing in the world today, this right is held by certain individuals; in some cases this right is held by a collective group of people. This group of people which legislates for others, establishes standards of good and bad for them, and formulates thought and philosophy for them, is precisely the group which makes itself a lord on this earth. This is the meaning of this verse: "Let not some of you take others as lords." Those who follow them grant them the station of lordship and divinity, and then worship them besides Allah, even if they do not prostrate or bow before them. Therefore, worship is an act of devotion, and it is exclusively for Allah.

Only the Islamic system is the system in which the yoke of servitude to other than Allah is removed from a person's neck, and he becomes completely free. He becomes so free that he derives his conception of life, his collective order and organization, his system of life and way of living, and his standards of good and bad, solely from Allah. His status is exactly the same as that of any other human being on this earth. Thus, a person becomes equal in every respect with all the people of the world. All people stand on one level; all eyes are turned toward one Master; and none of them is the master of another.

It is in this and only this sense that Islam is the religion of Allah. This is the religion that all messengers brought, and Allah sent the messengers with this very meaning: to bring people out of the worship of human beings into the worship of Allah, and to bring them out of the oppression of people into the justice of Allah. Therefore, if anyone turns away from Islam in accordance with this meaning, he does not remain a Muslim according to the testimony of Allah, however much those who interpret may interpret, and however much those who mislead people may mislead. The matter remains this.

﴿Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam.﴾

Surah Al-Imran, verse 65 (part 1 of 2)

Lesson 25 at a glance

This section of the surah also follows the same lines on which the surah has proceeded from the beginning. That is, the struggle that exists between the People of the Book and the Muslim community, the ideological battle between the two sides, and the deceit, trickery and fraud that the enemies of the religion and of Islam used against the truth. By employing falsehood, slander and various kinds of conspiracies and stratagems, they constantly created confusion between truth and falsehood and spread doubts and suspicions. They remained constantly in ambush to harm this ummah, and they kept working at it without pause. The section answers and refutes all this, and in this section Muslims were being taught how to confront such a situation: they should stand upon the truth they hold with insight, and they should be certain that their enemies stand upon a false position. Moreover, in this surah it was warned what plans the enemies were making against you. At the end, these enemies were again described, and it was explained what their temperament, morals, deeds and intentions are. These matters were set out openly before the Muslim community so that it might know its enemies well. The knowledge and understanding they claimed was also exposed. Then the trust of those Muslims whom they were deceiving was removed from them; they were made to feel aversion toward them, and their deceptions were laid bare so that they could neither deceive anyone nor practise greed. These were the themes of the first lesson.

However, in this lesson too there is a discussion with the People of the Book, namely the Jews and Christians, but here it is stated that their position and view concerning Abraham (peace be upon him) are, at first sight, wrong. The Jews thought that he was a Jew, and the Christians thought that he was a Christian. Yet Abraham (peace be upon him) appeared in the world even before Judaism and Christianity came into existence; he appeared even before the revelation of the Torah and the Gospel. Therefore, making such claims about him is mere illusion for which there is no proof. It is stated that Abraham (peace be upon him) was upon the pure monotheistic religion (Din Hanif), which is the name of the straight path, and that those who deserve to be called his friends and followers are those who are upon that same way. And Allah too is the friend of the believers. Therefore, the claims of these people that they are the followers and friends of Abraham (peace be upon him) are declared false. Then it is stated that the Islamic view concerning the messengers is that Muslims accept all the messengers as true:

إِنَّ أَوْلَى النَّاسِ بِإِبْرَاهِيمَ لَلَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُ وَهَذَا النَّبِيُّ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَاللَّهُ وَلِيُّ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ
"Surely the people most entitled to Abraham are those who followed him, and this Prophet and those who believe; and Allah is the Guardian of the believers." (3:68)

After this it is stated why the People of the Book dispute concerning Abraham. What is the hidden purpose in it? It is stated that their aim is only to lead the Muslims astray in matters of their religion and to create doubts in their beliefs. Accordingly, they are rebuked in this regard:

يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ لِمَ تَكْفُرُونَ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ وَأَنْتُمْ تَشْهَدُونَ (70) يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ لِمَ تَلْبِسُونَ الْحَقَّ بِالْبَاطِلِ وَتَكْتُمُونَ الْحَقَّ وَأَنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
"O People of the Book, why do you deny the signs of Allah while you yourselves bear witness? O People of the Book, why do you confound the truth with falsehood and conceal the truth while you know?"

After this, the Muslim community is shown a glimpse of the conspiracies which they secretly carried out against the beliefs, confidence and peace of mind of the believers, employing great cunning. Their scheme was that some of the People of the Book would proclaim Islam in the morning and then return to their disbelief in the evening. Its purpose was to instil in those Muslims who were not firm a suspicion: why did the People of the Book become Muslims in the morning and adopt disbelief again in the evening? Clearly, within every community there are people who are not steadfast, especially since in their eyes the People of the Book possessed greater knowledge of scriptures and religions.

وَقَالَتْ طَائِفَةٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ آمِنُوا بِالَّذِي أُنْزِلَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَجْهَ النَّهَارِ وَاكْفُرُوا آخِرَهُ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ
"A group of the People of the Book said: Believe in what has been revealed to those who believe, at the beginning of the day, and disbelieve at its end, so that perhaps they may turn back." This was their extremely contemptible plan.

After this it is stated what the collective morals of the People of the Book are and what their attitude is regarding covenants. Some of them are known for their trustworthiness and integrity, but most of them have no integrity at all, and through this dishonesty and bad conduct they had found some grounds within their religious beliefs, whereas the original religion of the People of the Book was a true religion, and it had no connection with these practices.

وَمِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ مَنْ إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ بِقِنْطَارٍ يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ بِدِينَارٍ لا يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ إِلا مَا دُمْتَ عَلَيْهِ قَائِمًا ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَالُوا لَيْسَ عَلَيْنَا فِي الأمِّيِّينَ سَبِيلٌ وَيَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ
"Among the People of the Book there is one who, if you entrust him with a heap of wealth, will return it to you; and among them there is one who, if you entrust him with a single dinar, will not return it to you unless you stand over him constantly. That is because they say: 'There is no blame upon us regarding the unlettered.' And they speak a lie against Allah while they know it."

Here it becomes clear what the Islamic moral outlook is, where it arises from, and how it is connected with the fear of Allah.

بَلَى مَنْ أَوْفَى بِعَهْدِهِ وَاتَّقَى فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُتَّقِينَ (76) إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَشْتَرُونَ بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ وَأَيْمَانِهِمْ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلا أُولَئِكَ لا خلاق لَهُمْ فِي الآخِرَةِ وَلا يُكَلِّمُهُمُ اللَّهُ وَلا يَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهِمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَلا يُزَكِّيهِمْ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
"Indeed, whoever fulfils his covenant and guards against evil, then surely Allah loves the righteous. As for those who sell the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price, they shall have no share in the Hereafter; Allah will not speak to them, nor look at them on the Day of Resurrection, nor purify them, and for them there is a painful punishment."

This lesson proceeds further, and now it brings to light a crookedness of the People of the Book and shows how boldly they tell lies in matters of religion, and that they do this for worldly interests and for extremely petty gains.

وَإِنَّ مِنْهُمْ لَفَرِيقًا يَلْوُونَ أَلْسِنَتَهُمْ بِالْكِتَابِ لِتَحْسَبُوهُ مِنَ الْكِتَابِ وَمَا هُوَ مِنَ الْكِتَابِ وَيَقُولُونَ هُوَ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ وَمَا هُوَ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ وَيَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ
"And among them is a group who distort their tongues with the Book, so that you may think it is from the Book, while it is not from the Book; and they say: 'It is from Allah,' while it is not from Allah. And they speak a lie against Allah while they know it."

And among the other matters which they inserted into the Book through their cunning was that Jesus (peace be upon him) is God and that the Holy Spirit is also God. Accordingly, Allah refutes this claim here: Jesus (peace be upon him) brought no such verse, nor did he command these people to hold such beliefs.

مَا كَانَ لِبَشَرٍ أَنْ يُؤْتِيَهُ اللَّهُ الْكِتَابَ وَالْحُكْمَ وَالنُّبُوَّةَ ثُمَّ يَقُولَ لِلنَّاسِ كُونُوا عِبَادًا لِي مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ وَلَكِنْ كُونُوا رَبَّانِيِّينَ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تُعَلِّمُونَ الْكِتَابَ وَبِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَدْرُسُونَ (79) وَلا يَأْمُرَكُمْ أَنْ تَتَّخِذُوا الْمَلائِكَةَ وَالنَّبِيِّينَ أَرْبَابًا أَيَأْمُرُكُمْ بِالْكُفْرِ بَعْدَ إِذْ أَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ (80)
"It is not for any human being that Allah should give him the Book, the wisdom and the prophethood, and then he should say to people: 'Be my servants rather than servants of Allah'; rather, he would say: 'Be godly scholars, because of what you teach of the Book and because of what you study.' Nor would he command you to take the angels and the prophets as lords. Would he command you to disbelieve after you have submitted?"

In keeping with this theme, the covenant taken by Allah from the prophets, who were sent into the world one after another, regarding mutual relationship and cooperation is also mentioned here: that each earlier prophet would hand over this trust to the one who comes after him and would help him.

وَإِذْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثَاقَ النَّبِيِّينَ لَمَا آتَيْتُكُمْ مِنْ كِتَابٍ وَحِكْمَةٍ ثُمَّ جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مُصَدِّقٌ لِمَا مَعَكُمْ لَتُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهِ وَلَتَنْصُرُنَّهُ قَالَ أَأَقْرَرْتُمْ وَأَخَذْتُمْ عَلَى ذَلِكُمْ إِصْرِي قَالُوا أَقْرَرْنَا قَالَ فَاشْهَدُوا وَأَنَا مَعَكُمْ مِنَ الشَّاهِدِينَ (81)
"And remember when Allah took the covenant of the prophets: 'Whatever I have given you of Book and wisdom, then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you shall surely believe in him and surely help him.' He said: 'Do you affirm this and accept My burden upon that condition?' They said: 'We affirm it.' He said: 'Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses.'"

For this reason, it becomes obligatory upon the People of the Book to believe in the Final Prophet and to help him. But their practice is that they keep neither the promises they made with Allah nor the agreements they made with the earlier messengers.

The natural outcome of these premises is that whoever seeks for himself a religion other than the religion of Allah, namely the religion of Islam, is in effect rebelling against the whole system of the cosmos as Allah has ordained it.

أَفَغَيْرَ دِينِ اللَّهِ يَبْغُونَ وَلَهُ أَسْلَمَ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالأرْضِ طَوْعًا وَكَرْهًا وَإِلَيْهِ يُرْجَعُونَ
"Do they seek other than the religion of Allah, while to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly, and to Him they shall be returned?" Thus, those who depart from Islam, their case rests in the hands of Allah. Likewise, those who do not fully obey the Islamic system, their case also rests in His hand. It appears that they are so disobedient that they are outside even this cosmic order of Allah.

Here the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers are told to announce their steadfastness upon the religion of the one Allah. The religion lies within the guidance which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brought from Allah, and which other messengers brought before him; and Allah has declared that He will accept from mankind only this religion.

وَمَنْ يَبْتَغِ غَيْرَ الإسْلامِ دِينًا فَلَنْ يُقْبَلَ مِنْهُ وَهُوَ فِي الآخِرَةِ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ
"And whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers."

Now, for those who do not believe in this religion, there is no hope of guidance for them, nor any hope of escaping the grip of Allah, unless they repent. As for those who depart this world in a state of disbelief, all the wealth they spent in the path of goodness will not benefit them; and even if they offer as ransom gold filling the whole earth, that ransom will not be accepted.

At this station of spending and sacrifice in the way of Allah, the Muslims are urged to spend from their wealth on those things which they love:

لَن تَنَالُوا البِرَّ حَتّٰی تُنفِقُوا مِمَّاتُحِبُّونَ وَمَاتُنفِقُوامِن شَیئٍ فَاِنَّ اللّٰہَ بِہٖ عَلِیمٌ
"You will not attain righteousness until you spend of what you love; and whatever you spend, indeed Allah knows it well."

Purpose of this brief section: it gathers very great truths and countless guidances. It is a short sentence within the great battle that runs through this whole surah, whose parties are the Muslim community and its enemies. This battle has continued in this way for centuries. Even today the means and resources used in the battle are entirely different, but the line is still the same; only today the battle is on a long front.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq, through Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah, and Hadrat Ibn Abbas (رضي الله عنه), narrates that he said: The Christians of Najran and the rabbis (ahbar) of the Jews gathered before the Messenger (ﷺ) and began a debate with him. The rabbis said, "Ibrahim was a Jew," and the Christians said, "He was a Christian." Upon this, this verse was revealed: "O People of the Book! Why do you dispute about Ibrahim..." ("O People of the Book, why do you argue about Abraham" – peace be upon him).

Whether or not this is the occasion of revelation, the verses apparently bear witness that they were revealed concerning the baseless claims of the People of the Book. Their dispute was either with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), or they were quarrelling among themselves in the presence of the Messenger (ﷺ). Behind their dispute lay the notion that Allah had promised Hadrat Ibrahim that prophethood would remain among his descendants, and so they wished to have this excellence and guidance allotted to their own name. This was their real aim. Secondly, by this means they wished to deny the Messenger's (ﷺ) claim that he and his community follow the pure religion (din hanif) and are the heirs of the best hanifism. Moreover, by this means they wished to create doubts in the hearts of Muslims, or at least to plant doubt among some of the people of Islam.

This is why Allah refutes them in the strongest terms and exposes their wishful thinking, which is not based on any scholarly proof. For Ibrahim (peace be upon him) lived before the Torah and before the Gospel. How then could he be a Jew or a Christian? Therefore this claim is entirely contrary to reason. Merely by glancing over the history of the prophets, it becomes clear that their claim is false.

"O People of the Book! Why do you argue with us about Ibrahim, when the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him? Do you not then understand?"

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 3, verse 66:

They argued about Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him), then they also disputed about some jurisprudential matters, and when they were invited to come and judge according to the Book of Allah, they turned away. Both of these subjects were ones about which they had some knowledge. As for the matters that predate your existence, your books and this religion of yours in which you believe, concerning these you have neither knowledge nor authority. Even if there were an authority from us, therefore, your debating these matters would be mere argument for the sake of argument. It would be shooting arrows in the dark, a pointless undertaking with no purpose, and nothing but a pursuit of personal interest and the worship of desire. Those whose condition is such are by no means trustworthy, and it is neither proper to speak with such people nor proper to lend an ear to their words.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 67:

After exposing the argumentation of these people, ending the value of that dispute, and rendering them completely unreliable, Allah now states the real truth which is known to Him. For the true facts of very ancient events in human history are known only to Allah. Likewise, the reality of the religion revealed to Ibrahim (peace be upon him) is known only to Allah. And Allah's decision is decisive in any case. After Allah's decision, there is no room for anyone to say anything, except one who has, in every case and without any proof or argument, resorted to disputation.

﴿Ibrahim was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a upright Muslim (hanif muslim), and he was not among the polytheists.﴾

Thus, earlier there was an indirect statement that Ibrahim was neither a Jew nor a Christian, because the Torah and the Gospel were revealed later. Here it is explicitly stated that he was neither a Jew nor a Christian but a Muslim hanif. He did not incline toward any religion other than Islam, because he was a Muslim, and a Muslim in the sense whose details we have explained earlier. The phrase ﴿and he was not among the polytheists﴾ is a further emphasis on the previous phrase, that he was a Muslim hanif, and because whoever is a Muslim hanif is not a polytheist. Now, saying after "Muslim hanif" that he was not a polytheist is intended to convey several subtle indications.

The first indication is that the Jews and Christians, among whom deviation from belief has reached such an extent, are in reality polytheists. This is why Ibrahim could be neither a Jew nor a Christian, but only a Muslim hanif.

The second indication is that Islam is a distinct reality and polytheism is an entirely different thing. The two can never come together in one place. Islam is the name of absolute monotheism, and that monotheism is comprehensive in every respect, in all its characteristics and all its requirements. Therefore Islam does not fit with any shade of polytheism.

The third indication intended here is that the polytheists of Quraysh considered themselves hanifs and followers of the religion of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). They were the servants and custodians of the Ka'bah. They are being told that he was a Muslim hanif, and you are polytheists: ﴿he was not among the polytheists﴾.

Since Ibrahim was a Muslim hanif and not a polytheist, neither the Jews and Christians nor the polytheists can claim to be his heirs, nor can any of them claim to be the custodians of Ibrahim's religion, although they have gone very far from that religion. Belief and ideology are the bond on which people come together in Islam, whereas even when people share lineage, nation, race and homeland, they remain distant from one another if they are not Muslims. When believers gather on this firm foundation of the Islamic way of life, then in their view a human being is one who is human in a spiritual sense. That is, a human is distinguished because Allah has placed a pure soul in his body. Thus the proper gathering of humans can also be based on belief, which is one of the most important characteristics of the soul. The collective system of humans is not established on the foundations on which herds of livestock gather, such as livestock grazing in one place, livestock of one species, livestock of one pasture, and livestock confined together in one pen or prison. From the Islamic point of view, between one individual and another, one group and another, and one generation and another, there is no connection other than belief and ideology. In this, a believer loves another believer, a Muslim group loves another Muslim group, an Islamic community is connected with another Islamic community, and Muslim generations are connected with other Muslim generations, and in this path the limits of time and place cannot be obstacles. The distances of blood and lineage cannot be obstacles in the way of this connection. Distances of nation and region are not obstacles. They are ideological friends with one another, solely on the basis of ideology, and above all of them, the Divine Being is the friend of all.

Then those who followed Ibrahim during his lifetime, and walked upon his system and way, and judged according to his commands, they are his friends. Then this Prophet and those who are upon his religion according to the testimony of Allah are his friends; after that, those who believed in this Prophet are the friends of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and they became of one hue with him in their system of life and way of living. ﴿And Allah is the Protector of the believers﴾ — Allah is only the supporter and helper of those who have faith. This is because these people are the party of Allah; these are the ones who carry the banner of Allah; these are the ones who have love and friendship for Allah, and they have no walī (protector) other than Him.

These people are one family. They are one ummah, even if centuries pass, ages pass, the distances of land and homeland become long, the race and nation differ, and the clans and tribes differ; they are one, and they will remain one.

This is the most advanced form of human association, the one most suited to the human being, and it is this form that distinguishes him from a herd of animals. On the other hand, among the various kinds of societies, this society is the most general and unrestricted. This is because the foundation of this collective system is conditioned by a condition, and that condition is choice. It is within a person's power to fulfil that condition. That condition is ideological, and every individual is free and autonomous in adopting any ideology. When a person cannot change his lineage, even if we base the collective system on lineage, no person can in any case enter that lineage. Even if we establish collectivity on the basis of nationality, then no person can change his nationality. If we base the collective system on colour, no person can change his colour. Likewise, if we establish the collective system on the basis of language, no person can change his language either. Similarly, if the system is based on classes, then changing one's class is not easily possible. Rather, at times classes too are unchangeable, such as the untouchables in India and so on. This is why in all other societies there are barriers in the path of certain classes, and they cannot become members of that society. Only a society formed on an ideological foundation is free of this defect. This is because in an ideological society, the matter of adopting or not adopting an ideology lies within the choice of an individual, without his having to change his reality, his language, his class, or the attribute upon whose basis his barrier is being placed. Besides this, in this ideological society the human being's station and honour also increase, and its collective ideology is based on those elements that are human elements, not on those that gather animals together. Now there are only two paths for a human being: one, that according to the Islamic ideology of collectivity he gathers on spiritual and ideological foundations and lives as a human being; or else, like a herd and flock of animals, [gathered by] being of the same kind, or like livestock gathered together whose pasture is one, remaining within the limits and boundaries that have been set for those livestock.

Now the ummah of Islam is told what the real plan of the People of the Book is behind this contention, argument and debate. Therefore, the cunning of the People of the Book, their secret schemes, and the game they play with the religion are exposed before the ummah of Islam in the middle of the public square; the veil behind which these people used to hide and play their ugly game is torn to pieces, and they are laid bare before the community of Muslims and shamed.

The ideological enmity that the People of the Book harboured in their hearts against the Muslims was of this kind. They never wished that this ummah would ever come onto the right path. They did not like that this ummah should return to its own beliefs with full strength, full conviction and full confidence. Therefore, all their struggle is focused on this point: that they should divert this ummah from the Islamic system of life and turn it away from the Straight Path.

وَدَّتْ طَائِفَةٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ لَوْ يُضِلُّونَكُمْ……………"A group among the People of the Book wishes that they could lead you astray..."

This is their carnal desire. This urge lies hidden at the bottom of their hearts. Behind every one of their plots, this desire is deeply ingrained. Behind every one of their schemes, every debate, every disputation and every deception, this desire is the driving force, and this desire of these people is based purely on enmity, base desire and mischief. Therefore it is clear misguidance. This is because such a desire never arises from feelings of truth, goodness, guidance and sincere goodwill, and whenever they begin a struggle to misguide the people of Islam, at that very moment they themselves go astray.

وَمَا يُضِلُّونَ إِلا أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ……………"And they lead astray none but themselves, though they perceive it not."

And as long as the Muslims remain upon Islam, they will be able to counter the plans of these enemies well. The disbelievers cannot harm them in any way. Allah, at all times, is the protector of them from the conspiracies of the conspirators, and as long as they are firm Muslims, Allah Himself turns their plans back upon them.

Allah, at all times, is the protector of them from the conspiracies of the conspirators, and as long as they are firm Muslims, Allah Himself turns their plans back upon them.

Sayyid Qutb's commentary (Fi Zilal al-Quran), Urdu translation, on Surah Al-Imran, verse 71:

At this point, Allah sternly shakes the People of the Book, urging them to reconsider their doubtful and weak stance.

يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ لِمَ تَلْبِسُونَ الْحَقَّ بِالْبَاطِلِ وَتَكْتُمُونَ الْحَقَّ وَأَنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ

"O People of the Book! Why do you deny the signs of Allah while you yourselves witness them? O People of the Book! Why do you mix truth with falsehood, making the truth doubtful by clothing it in falsehood? Why do you conceal the truth knowingly?"

The reality is that, both then and today, the People of the Book witness the truth and reality, and clearly understand that this religion is the religion of truth. Among them were some who knew well that their scriptures contained glad tidings and indications concerning the Final Messenger ﷺ; some of them explicitly described these indications; and some bore witness to the truth on the basis of these glad tidings. But others, although they knew nothing from their own scriptures, clearly believed, upon seeing the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his religion, that this religion is the religion of truth, yet despite this they were resolutely committed to disbelief. This was not because there was any deficiency in proof and evidence, but purely because of carnal desires, personal interests, and the aim of misleading people. The Qur'an calls out to them specifically as "People of the Book," because the necessary demand of this attribute, People of the Book, is that they embrace this new Book of Allah.

Once again Allah calls them, so that He may shame them sharply for their act of clothing truth with falsehood, concealing truth, wasting truth, and doing all this knowingly, as a deliberate and premeditated plan. This is their extremely vile and detestable conduct……… The criticism that Allah made of the People of the Book of that time still applies to them from that time until today. Throughout the whole Islamic history, their role has remained this same. The beginning of this was made first by the Jews, and after the Jews, this same role was taken up by the Crusaders. And throughout this entire history, they inserted into Islamic sciences certain ideas whose refutation is possible only through the Qur'an. They mixed falsehood with truth in all Islamic sciences. Indeed, only the Qur'an has remained protected from their secret conspiracies, because Allah Himself took upon Himself the responsibility of its protection. It was Allah's responsibility that He would preserve the Qur'an forever and ever. They engaged in interpolation in Islamic history and mixed impurities into the events of Islamic history. They tried to introduce fabricated hadith into the corpus of hadith by inventing narrations. It was by Allah's grace that He raised up certain men who countered this, who gave outstanding scholarly effort in this field and purified the corpus of hadith from their forgeries. Except that, due to the limited struggle of humans, something escaped, but it became rare and limited. They also applied embellishment to the corpus of Qur'anic exegesis and turned it into a barren wilderness in which it became difficult for a person to find the signposts of the way. They placed their own men among some of the leaders of Islam; hundreds of people became Muslims in name while continuing to plot against Islam. And today, see how, in the form of orientalists and the students of orientalists, and many leaders whom the Jews and Crusaders have appointed over us, they work to protect the interests of the Jews and Crusaders in this so-called Islamic world. This is because these enemies of Islam, if they came out openly, could not achieve these interests.

These conspiracies are continuously in operation. And even today, if we can find any refuge from them, we can find it only in the lap of the Qur'an, which is the most protected Book. If we make this Qur'an our counselor in this historical struggle, we can find a secure refuge.

Here the Qur'an also records some of the efforts of those people which they made to lead the community of Muslims astray from their religion. And they carried out this work, as is their habit, in an extremely cunning and base manner. Allah says:

How crafty a method this is! As we have said, these people also used such base weapons. For it was possible that some weak-natured people, people of limited understanding, people who were not very steadfast, and who did not know well the reality of their own religion, could be influenced by it. Doubt could arise in their hearts. Especially the Arabs, who were unlettered, and among whom it was common knowledge that the People of the Book had greater information about religion and the heavenly scriptures than they did. When they saw that these people accepted faith and then apostatised, they would obviously have concluded that these people had discovered some hidden weakness or defect in this religion. Or that those who themselves apostatised fell into doubt, unable to decide where to go, and had no firm footing in any state. And this deception of the People of the Book continues to this day. Yes, its form and methods have changed in keeping with the conditions of the age.

Yes, in today's age the enemies of the Muslims have understood that they can no longer deceive the people of Islam by giving a fresh coat of paint to those old conspiracies. Therefore all the enemies have devised some modern methods on that same old pattern, and through them they lead the Muslims astray. Now these people have left in the Muslim world a formidable army of teachers, philosophers, researchers and holders of PhDs. All these people are, behind the scenes, agents of the enemies of Islam. Then these enemies have also ensnared our writers, poets, artists and journalists in their net. The names of these people are like Muslim names, because they are the children of Muslims, and some of them are even Muslim scholars.

The sole task of this army of agents is to spread doubts and suspicions in the hearts and minds of Muslims, and to adopt various methods for this. Sometimes they work through the door of learning and literature; sometimes they work in the guise of journalists and artists. These people are engaged in reducing the value of the principles of Islamic life, in ridiculing the Islamic worldview, and in making interpretations of Islamic principles and texts which those texts cannot in any way bear. They constantly beat the drum that the Islamic system of life is reactionary, and they are always busy propagating that the Islamic worldview should be abandoned and removed from practical human life, as though human life is endangered by it and it is endangered by life. These people propagate in the consciousness and conduct of Muslims such concepts, traditions and principles as are contrary to Islamic concepts, and through which Islamic conduct and Islamic traditions are, in a sly way, broken down and dismantled. The more attractive these agents make these modern jahili concepts within the views of Muslims, the more they distort the appearance of the traditions of faith. Moreover, these agents set sexuality free from every restraint and bond, and uproot the foundations upon which pure morality is established, and they drag society down into the filth which they spread everywhere. And, above all, these agents distort Islamic history in exactly the same way as they distorted their own heavenly scriptures and introduced alteration into them.

But you will be surprised: despite all these deeds, these agents are still Muslims! Why should they not be Muslims? Are their names not like those of Muslims? And along with these names they proclaim and affirm their Islam every morning after sunrise, yet by performing the deeds mentioned above they, as it were, deny Islam by evening. In this way these agents play the same role that the earlier People of the Book used to play. The only difference is that there is some difference between the earlier age and today's environment and method of operation.

The People of the Book would agree among themselves: "Declare your belief in Islam at the start of the day, and by evening announce that you have given it up, so that doubt may enter the hearts of the Muslims and they too may turn back from Islam. But keep this matter secret. Do not disclose it, and do not inform anyone except those who follow your religion." وَلا تُؤْمِنُوا إِلا لِمَنْ تَبِعَ دِينَكُمْ "And do not place your trust in anyone except one who follows your religion."

When the verb آمن is followed by the particle لام and is transitive, its meaning is to regard as trustworthy and to trust. That is, place your trust only in one who holds to your religion. Reveal your secrets only to your co-religionists, in opposition to the Muslims. Let the Muslims not come to know of these matters.

Today too, the conduct of the companions of Zionism and Crusaderism is the same. These people reach an agreement on one matter among themselves: that the one who is devoted to the Islamic view of life should be killed the moment an opportunity presents itself. Such opportunities may not be available to them, and it may be that the complete understanding that exists among these agents of Zionism and Crusaderism will not be found again. But this understanding exists on one side between a (client) (Client) and, on the other side, his agent. In it, these principals sometimes tell their agent their real secrets, when they are certain that he will not disclose them. After this, they present themselves in another form and do not appear in the guise in which they had prepared these plots. For these agents, the circumstances are first set right and the environment is made favourable to them. All facilities are provided to them. And those who understand the truth of this religion on this earth are either out of sight or rejected by their societies. Therefore they say: وَلا تُؤْمِنُوا إِلا لِمَنْ تَبِعَ دِينَكُمْ "And reveal your secret only to those who follow your religion."

Here Allah turns His Prophet's attention to this, that he should declare that guidance is indeed the guidance of Allah alone, and whoever does not accept the guidance of Allah will never attain guidance, in any form and by any means. قُلْ إِنَّ الْهُدَى هُدَى اللَّهِ "Say: Indeed, the guidance is the guidance of Allah."

This decision comes in response to their statement: "Believe in the morning in what has been revealed to the believers, and in the evening deny it; perhaps they will turn back in this way." The Muslims are warned against the implementation of this vile scheme. If it were to happen, they would in effect re-enter disbelief. Therefore guidance is solely the guidance of Allah, and the stratagems these deceivers adopt are pure disbelief. And this decision comes in between, as a parenthetical interjection, while the speech of the People of the Book has not yet ended.

أَنْ يُؤْتَى أَحَدٌ مِثْلَ مَا أُوتِيتُمْ أَوْ يُحَاجُّوكُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّكُمْ "Or that anyone else should be given the like of what you have been given, or that they should argue against you before your Lord." This phrase is evidence for their position: "And reveal your secret only to those who follow your religion." These people were afflicted with such envy and jealousy that another person should be honoured with prophethood and the Book in the same way that you were honoured with prophethood and the Book. They were gripped by the fear that the people of Islam would attain assurance in their religion and in Islam, and would become aware of the truth that the People of the Book have concealed, though they know it. And moreover, that on the Day of Resurrection the Muslims would present it before Allah as evidence against the People of the Book. These people thought, as it were, that Allah would not punish them except through the verbal testimony of the Muslims. This is a notion that does not arise from correct faith in the being and attributes of Allah, nor can such notions arise in the minds of those who possess correct knowledge of Allah's being and attributes, of prophethood and messengerhood, and of the duties arising from faith.

Accordingly, Allah directs the believers and the noble Messenger (ﷺ) to this matter, that they should inform them that this is the grace and bounty of Allah, and it is His will that He bestows the Book and prophethood upon whichever people He wills.

قُلْ إِنَّ الْفَضْلَ بِيَدِ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَاللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ (73) يَخْتَصُّ بِرَحْمَتِهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَاللَّهُ ذُو الْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمِ "Say: Indeed, bounty is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing. He specifies for His mercy whom He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty."

Allah's will has now decided to honour others, apart from the People of the Book, with prophethood and messengerhood, especially since they continue to oppose the covenants made with Allah, continue to break the obligation that their forefather Abraham (peace be upon him) placed upon them, continue to betray the trust that Allah committed to them, and continue to break the commands of their Book and the laws of their religion. And then, if anyone calls them to come and judge by the Book of Allah, they refuse. And because of all these deeds of theirs, leadership and guidance of mankind are freed from the Islamic system of life, the Islamic leaders and the guidance of the Holy Qur'an. This was the very point at which Allah withdrew leadership from the Children of Israel and the People of the Book, and entrusted that trust to the Muslim community. This was a great grace and favour of Allah upon that community.

وَاللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ "And Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing." And يَخْتَصُّ بِرَحْمَتِهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ "He specifies for His mercy whom He wills." His bounty and generosity are vast, and His knowledge is also vast, so He knows well the place upon which His mercy should descend. وَاللَّهُ ذُو الْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمِ "And Allah is the Possessor of great bounty." What greater bounty can there be for a people than that He guides them through a Book? And what greater good and blessing can He bestow upon anyone than to grant them messengerhood? And what greater manifestation of mercy can there be than that He sends a Messenger among a people?

When the People of Islam heard this, a sense of Allah's grace and bounty arose in their hearts. They realised that they had been chosen for a great duty, and that this honour had been bestowed upon them specifically. So they preserved this honour with great eagerness; they held on to it with great firmness and resolve, and defended it with great strength and steadfastness. They became alert against the conspiracies of envious and deceitful people. This was the Qur'an's method of training, because it is the word of the All-Wise and All-Knowing. And even today, this same element can be the means of reform and training for the Muslim Ummah, in every age and every generation.

Going forward, further circumstances concerning the People of the Book are described. It is told how much inconsistency is found in their conduct, and it is definitively made clear upon which correct and true values the religion of Muslims, that is Islam, has been established. In this regard, it is explained what kinds of people are found among the People of the Book in their mutual dealings.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 75:

Concerning the People of the Book who at that time stood opposed to the believers and the Muslim community, and who were engaged in debate and dispute, the Qur'an's comment is extremely just and based on truth. Their qualities are described without any reduction or exaggeration, and the condition described in these qualities still applies to the People of the Book today. In short, the People of the Book were carrying on enmity against Islam and the Muslims, were devising deep and malicious plots against the Muslims and against Islam, and were always ready for severe mischief and corruption against the Muslim community and the religion of Islam. Despite all these realities, among them there are those who are good: the Qur'an neither conceals their virtues nor diminishes their description, even though at that time they were in a state of contest and debate with the people of Islam. Therefore the Noble Qur'an says that among the People of the Book there are some people who, even if great rights of others come into their hands, do not waste them.

﴿وَمِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ مَنْ إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ بِقِنْطَارٍ يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ﴾ "Among the People of the Book there is one who, if you entrust him with a heap of wealth, will return it to you." But among them there are also those who are utter traitors, greedy, and deceitful, who do not return anyone's right, even if it is very small; yes, they will pay only when you press them insistently and stand over them. And to justify seizing the right of others, they also fabricate a philosophy in which they knowingly lie against Allah.

﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ بِدِينَارٍ لا يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ إِلا مَا دُمْتَ عَلَيْهِ قَائِمًا ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قَالُوا لَيْسَ عَلَيْنَا فِي الأمِّيِّينَ سَبِيلٌ وَيَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ "And among them is one who, if you entrust him with a single dinar, will not return it to you unless you stand over him. That is because they say, 'There is no blame upon us regarding the unlettered (non-Jews).' And they attribute the lie to Allah while they know." The reason for their moral condition is that they say, "We are not accountable regarding the Ummiyyin (non-Jews)," and they fabricate this statement, attributing it to Allah, while they know that Allah has not said any such thing.

This is also a particular characteristic of the Jews. Only the Jews used to say this. Their standards of morality and conduct were different: trustworthiness and honesty were meant only for dealings between one Jew and another Jew. As for the non-Jews, whom they called Ummi, and by whom they meant only the Arabs, they felt no harm in wasting their property and seizing it unlawfully. They committed crimes such as deception, fraud, adulteration, and exploitation against non-Jews with great casualness. Without any hesitation, they used base weapons against them and committed contemptible acts.

What is surprising is that they claimed that their God and their religion commanded them to do this. But in reality they knew well that they were lying, because Allah, the Exalted, does not command any shameful act, such as that one group should command another to consume the wealth of another group unjustly and oppressively, and should not keep the covenants it has made, nor fulfil its responsibilities, and should continue to harm them without any reluctance or difficulty. But they were Jews, the Jews who have made enmity and hostility towards humankind their religion. ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ "They attribute the lie to Allah while they know."

This point in the Qur'an establishes a single moral principle for human beings. This is its sole ethical standard, and it ties its moral outlook to God and to God-consciousness.

In short, this is a moral principle. Whoever observes it, keeping the covenant of God and acting with awareness of God's fear, will have God's love and will be granted honour and esteem. But whoever breaks the covenant made with God for the sake of the fleeting "thaman qaleel" (a small price) of this world, even if the entire world seems to be within their reach, will have no share in the Hereafter, because this whole world, compared with the Hereafter, is also a small provision (mata' qaleel). Such a person will never be accepted by God, and no leniency will be shown to them. They will be neither purified nor cleansed, and their condition will be that they remain afflicted with a painful punishment ('adhab alim).

Here it is indicated that fidelity to covenants is connected with the fear of God. Therefore, the keeping of covenants must not vary in any circumstance, whether one is dealing with a friend or with an enemy. Fulfilment of covenants does not depend on expediency, because the matter of keeping a covenant is bound up with God. Its connection is not with the person with whom the covenant was made.

This is Islam's moral outlook, both in the keeping of promises and in general social ethics. In collective affairs the first relationship is with God. A Muslim keeps the Divine Being before his eyes first of all; he first fears the wrath of God and seeks His pleasure. In Islam, the motive beneath morality is not expediency, nor is its cause social custom, nor do moral norms prevail merely because of social pressure, since society is sometimes on the right path and sometimes misguided, and in it misguiding values and standards may become prevalent. Therefore, moral norms must be fixed on unchanging criteria by which an individual may measure his conduct and a society may understand its standards. Along with being unchanging and stable, these moral standards must also be connected to the higher realm from which they are drawn. These standards and their source must be above human terminology and human needs, since human needs and expediencies change daily. Hence it is necessary that these principles and standards be derived from the Divine Being, in such a way that one first ascertains what the pleasure of God is; His good pleasure must be kept in view and His fear must be in the heart. Thus Islam gives humanity a moral system whose roots lie not in this world but in the higher realm, and it derives its moral standards and principles from that luminous, stable and exalted source.

This is why, concerning those who break promises and betray trusts, the Qur'an says that they sell the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price. Therefore, the first bond of a covenant is between God and the servant, and afterwards it relates to one human being and another. Accordingly, as far as God is concerned, such covenant-breakers will have no share in the Hereafter. Yet if they seek some worldly gain in exchange for this breach of covenant and violation of oaths, such worldly interests have no value compared with the Hereafter. Therefore, because of their breach of covenant, there will be no reward for them on the Day of Judgement, since the covenant they made with people was also a covenant with God.

Here it is also made clear that, from the standpoint of literary expression, the Qur'anic style of description is extremely vivid. The fact that God will not regard them and that they will receive no indulgence is expressed in such a way that God will neither speak to them, nor look at them with favour, nor purify them. This is the manner commonly known among people for deliberate disregard. The Qur'an has adopted this pictorial mode of expression so that on the Day of Resurrection a living and intuitive picture of their disgrace may come before the eyes. Such a living and intuitive mode of expression is more captivating than purely abstract description. This is the Qur'anic manner of expression: very beautiful, graceful and lovely.

Now proceed further and observe some other examples from the People of the Book. One example concerns those misguiders who use the Book of God itself as a weapon for leading people astray. They twist their tongues and speak with cunning, so that the meaning becomes something other than what it is. They distort the verses of the Book in such a way that the meaning and understanding conform to their pre-determined desires, and in exchange for this distortion they receive a contemptible fee. The fee is tied to the petty aims of this world. Among the alterations and interpretations they made were the beliefs they fabricated concerning Messiah (ﷺ)... rather, concerning Jesus (peace be upon him) and Mary, and those beliefs were convenient for the clergy and the rulers of the time.

When the People of Religion fall into moral corruption, they become a means of adulterating religious truths, and they do this while wearing the garb of religious scholars. The conditions that the Qur'an describes here about a group among the People of the Book are something we know well from our own times. The People of the Book would make interpretations of the texts of the Book; through twisting language they would change its meaning, and in this way they would derive predetermined conclusions. And they would believe that this is the meaning of the Book of Allah, and that this meaning expresses the will of God. Yet the conclusions they derived were in conflict with the fundamental principles of religion. They had confidence that most of the listeners were unlettered and ignorant, and that they could not distinguish between their self-invented conclusions and the true meaning of the verses. Yet their conclusions were fabricated and false, and they would forcibly drag the verses to those conclusions.

This pattern of the People of the Book is fully found in some religious leaders of our own era, who present themselves in the name of religion as a form of oppression. They distort religion, and they make a jest of their own carnal desires. They carry the verses of Allah upon their shoulders and wherever they see any benefit, they sacrifice them to it; wherever they find any worldly interest at all, they obtain it through these verses. In short, carrying the verses of Allah, these people keep running after worldly purposes. Then, by breaking the necks of these verses and twisting them thoroughly, they fit them to those interests. They make such changes in the meanings of words that they conform to their aims and inclinations, even if these inclinations conflict with the foundational concepts of religion and the basic principles of religion. In this field they carry out a threefold struggle, commit every kind of slander, and always sit in ambush, seeking somehow to extract from a word of the Holy Qur'an a meaning that conforms to their carnal desires, so that through it their prevailing and self-serving desires become established.

﴿They say, "This is from Allah," but it is not from Allah. And they speak falsehood about Allah while they know it.﴾

"They say that what we are reading is from Allah, whereas it is not from Allah. They knowingly attribute words to Allah."

The condition that the Qur'an has described of a group among the People of the Book is a disease that is not peculiar to the People of the Book. Any nation that entrusts the work of religion to such people as are self-styled religious, and for whom religion becomes so cheap that its value is not even equal to the lowest of their worldly interests, falls into it. And their sense of responsibility becomes so dulled that their hearts do not hesitate even to fabricate lies against Allah. They alter the verses of Allah for the sake of flattering people and servants, and in order to fulfil their unhealthy desires they commit distortion of the religion of Allah. As it were, Allah, the Exalted, warns the Muslim community of this dangerous station where feet slip, and because of which the Children of Israel lost their station of leadership.

According to the overall impression of these verses, it appears that this group of the Children of Israel would find, from the Book of Allah, some sentences containing figurative expressions, and then, by twisting those verses, they would derive from them meanings which those verses could not bear. Thus, through their interpretations, they would extract strange meanings and give the unlettered people the impression that these meanings are the implications of the Book of Allah, whereas they themselves were their inventions. They would tell people, "This is what Allah has said," whereas Allah had never said any such thing. The aim and target of these interpretations was to establish the divinity of Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him): that is, the three hypostases, Father, Son and Holy Spirit, three and also one, and that He is one God. Yet Allah, the Exalted, is free from their conception. They would narrate from Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him) words that supported their assumptions. So Allah, the Exalted, refuting their distortions and interpretations, said that how is it possible that Allah chooses a servant for prophethood, grants him this great office, and then that servant commands people to take him as a deity? Let them take angels as deities? This is simply not possible.

The Prophet ﷺ affirms that he is a servant (ʿabd), and that Allah is the one Lord, without partner, and that it is the duty of all people to worship Him alone. Therefore it is not possible that he would claim for himself the station of lordship (rubūbiyyah). For the station of divinity (ulūhiyyah) would then require that people worship the Prophet as well. Hence no prophet can say to people: "Be servants to me besides Allah" (kūnū ʿibādan lī min dūni Allāh) ……………"Become my servants besides Allah." The call of a prophet is rather: "Be rabbānīs (people devoted to the Lord)……………" (kūnū rabbāniyyīn) "Become rabbānī, all of you." This is because the Book whose knowledge you have acquired teaches exactly this, and what you teach in its instruction also demands it. Therefore the demand of the knowledge of the Book and of teaching it is that only Allah be worshipped. So how can a prophet order people to take prophets and angels as lords besides Allah? For how can a prophet, after people have embraced Islam, command them to disbelieve? Whereas his station is to guide people, not to lead them astray after they have been guided. He is their leader toward Islam; he is not their leader to remove them from Islam.

On the basis of this principle, the claim attributed by some to ʿĪsā (ʿalayhi al-salām) becomes impossible. Likewise, their lie is made clear: the claim that all these verses and narrations which they recite could be from Allah and His Messenger. Therefore the standing of what these people say is nullified, and the claim they repeat again and again in Islamic ranks, to create doubts and confusion, is rendered baseless. For the Qur'an has thoroughly exposed them, and they have been stripped bare before the Muslim community in the open field.

The example of these people is exactly like that of the People of the Book who claim to possess religious knowledge, as we have explained in detail earlier. These people deserve that these verses of the Qur'an be presented before them, because they too distort the Qur'anic texts, and they too have set up many lords besides Allah. They constantly remain on the lookout to twist the verses so as to extract from them the meanings that they themselves have fabricated.
