The Almighty took an exceedingly fearful and firm covenant, and He Himself became a witness to this covenant, and He made all His prophets witnesses to it. This covenant was taken from all the messengers. Its content was that whichever messenger is given the Book and wisdom, it shall be his duty that, after him, he affirms the messenger who comes later, if that later messenger is himself confirming and endorsing his teachings. Along with this affirmation, it is also the duty of the earlier messenger to support the later one and to obey his law (shari'ah, the revealed law). This covenant was agreed between Allah and every messenger.

The Qur'an has folded up the longest record of human history and gathered all the messengers into one place. They are all assembled in a single scene. Allah, exalted is His majesty, is addressing them together. Did they affirm this covenant and accept the weighty responsibility of Allah? Allah asks, ﴿Do you affirm this and take upon yourselves My heavy covenant in this matter?﴾ They all reply, ﴿We affirm.﴾ Then the Lord of Majesty makes Himself a witness to this covenant and makes them witnesses as well. He says, ﴿Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses.﴾

This is a great and awe-inspiring scene, which the Qur'an depicts. On seeing it, hearts tremble. In this scene, all the prophets and messengers are seen standing in the presence of the Lord. It appears that this caravan of the noble ones of the earth stands linked together, leaning upon one another, and all of them are waiting for the divine guidance of the higher world. All of them represent the one truth, concerning which Allah's command is that the whole of humanity be built upon its foundation, a foundation free of deviation, free of duality, free of contradiction, and free of conflict. The representatives of this truth are those who are chosen from among people. Each chosen one has been transmitting this truth to the next chosen one. In this way, he also transfers himself to the chosen agent who comes after him, because the self of a prophet is not his own. Nor does he have any personal aim or desire in this mission, nor does a prophet work for personal or individual honour and esteem. He is a servant chosen as an agent and a responsible propagator. It is the Divine Being Himself who, in different eras, transfers the call of Islam to different generations, and the chosen messengers direct it in whatever way they wish.

As a result of this concept of religion and the covenant agreed in this regard with Allah, the religion of Allah becomes pure. No personal partisanship enters into it. That is, the person of the messenger does not influence it either. The people of the messenger have no influence upon this religion. Through the hidden influences of its followers and their families as well, this religion remains pure and clean. Likewise, the personality of the followers and the status of their people and tribe have no effect upon it. The religion of Islam is one in which every matter lies in the hands of Allah. The religion is one, Allah is one, and with this one religion, the caravan of messengers in the history of humanity is also one, a most noble and distinguished caravan.

In the light of this truth, those who call themselves the People of the Book now become clearly visible to us. These people do not believe in the Final Prophet, and they remain behind. They claim that they do not believe because of their own religion, whereas the very demand of their religion is that they should believe in the Final Prophet and rise to support and assist him. But these people do not believe out of mere bigotry. This is because the messengers through whom this religion reached them were taken by Allah under a most firm covenant, and they bound themselves to this covenant with their Lord. This covenant was agreed openly and in an assembly, that they would support the Final Prophet. Therefore, those who do not believe in the Final Prophet are, in reality, defiant transgressors and wrongdoers. They are covenant-breakers. They are the ones who break the very order of this universe, which is obedient to its Lord, which is the obedient servant of the law of nature. This is because this very law is the governor of the entire universe, and this whole universe runs according to its will.

The truth is that only the sinful (fasiq) can turn away from obedience to the final Prophet, and only the one who is aberrant and rejected can turn away from this religion of Allah. Such a person will be aberrant and rejected within the whole natural order of this universe, and within this entire obedient universe he will be a corrupter and a source of mischief.

The religion of Allah is one. All the Messengers came with one religion, and all of them made a firm covenant upon it. The covenant of Allah is also one, and all the Messengers are parties to it. Therefore, believing in this religion, believing in and following this Messenger, supporting this Messenger, establishing the Islamic system, and confronting all other systems is in fact fidelity to that covenant. Hence, whoever turns away from the religion of Islam has, in effect, turned away from all the religions of Allah, and has broken the general covenants of Allah……because that Islam, whose establishment as an Islamic system on this earth is required, its following and sincere demonstration of devotion to it, is in fact the Islam and the natural law (namus-e-qudrat) of this entire universe. This Islam is the Islam of every living creature, every beast and bird, in this universe.

This is the commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 83.

It is the deep form of Islam and submission, a form that is cosmic (takwini), one that affects human consciousness, from which fear of Allah arises in the human conscience: the form of a great law of nature, which is all-subduing and all-compelling. It makes all the dead and living things of the entire universe obedient to one divine sunnah (Sunnat Ilahiyyah) and one divine law (Shari'ah Ilahiyyah), and according to which the destiny and end of both are one. This is Islam: ﴿وَإِلَيْهِ يُرْجَعُونَ﴾ "and to Him they shall all be returned."

Therefore all these things will inevitably return in the end to that Allah who encompasses everything, is the manager of all, and is the master of great majesty and glory, and there is no escape from this end.

If a person desires his success and felicity, if he desires comfort and tranquility, if he desires peace of heart and good condition, then for him there is no path other than turning towards the Islamic system of life: in his own self, in his system of life, and in his collective system, so that his life harmonizes with the system of this entire universe, and there is no need to devise a separate system of life for himself contrary to this natural order of the universe. This is because his self-made system will be in conflict with the system of the universe created by Allah Ta'ala, and this human being is bound, willingly or unwillingly, to live in accordance with it. The system that is in his thought and consciousness, that is in his practical life and his mutual relationships, that is in all his struggles and activities. When it harmonizes with this cosmic system, this harmony will create a cooperation between him and the great forces of this entire universe, and there will be no conflict between them. This is because when a human being takes the path of conflict with the cosmic forces, he is shattered to pieces and destroyed. And if his existence is not erased, then at least he is no longer capable of fulfilling the duty of khilafah (vicegerency) as Allah Ta'ala has prepared him for it. And if he were to harmonize with the laws of nature and cosmic principles, which control him himself and the entire universe spread around him, whether living or non-living, then in that case he would be the custodian of all the secrets of the universe; he would subdue its forces, benefit from them, and thus attain comfort, ease and tranquility, and be freed from restlessness, anguish and fear. For example, the benefit of the universe would be that instead of using a cosmic force for burning and destruction, he would use it for cooking food and obtaining warmth, and would derive light from it.

Human nature, in its original reality, is in harmony with these cosmic forces and laws. The human intuition seeks obedience to its Lord in the same way that all the living and non-living things of this universe prostrate before Him. When a human being adopts a path contrary to the laws of nature, he not only goes against the order of nature but also goes against those laws of nature which exist and operate within his own self. This is why he always appears distressed, broken, bewildered and restless, and his life is ruined in the same way as the life of a misguided, straying person today, whom we see everywhere. Yet today's human being has achieved great victories in the field of knowledge and stands at the peak of material progress.

The truth is that at this time humanity is afflicted with an extremely bitter spiritual void, and this is a void that human nature cannot forget. That is, humanity is deprived of the taste of certainty. Its life is deprived of the Islamic system, because only this system of life can create a balance between these material advancements and the laws of nature, in which human effort and the course of the laws of nature come into one direction.

At this time humanity is wandering in scorching sun that burns, and it is deprived of the dense shade of the Islamic system of life, in which it could live a pleasant life, and be freed from evil and corruption, in which it is caught only because it has strayed from the straight path of Islam and its familiar highway. On this difficult road, one finds nothing but bewilderment and confusion, anguish and restlessness, agitation and misguidance. It is constantly a victim of hunger, poverty, and the feeling of spiritual emptiness and deprivation. And from this very situation it has found only this one way of escape: it adopts forbidden and destructive means such as hashish, charas and heroin. Through frenzied haste, foolish actions and moral degeneration, it wishes to fill this void, but it fails. And this situation remains as it is despite this immense material progress, unlimited production and the immense conveniences of all of life. Rather, this anguish, this bewilderment and these anxieties keep increasing, and they increase in the same proportion as material progress increases and worldly conveniences and comforts increase.

This frightening and bitter void is driving humanity towards a terrifying ghost. But wherever it reaches while running, at every place this ghost is seen standing behind it. Today, whoever goes into the wealthy and developed era of the West, the first impression that settles on his feelings is that all these people are running. Some ghost is driving them away and they are running from it, rather they are running from their own selves and their own shadows. Very soon this person comes to realize that these material advancements and sensual pleasure have plunged these people into filthy mire. They have become victims of countless psychological diseases. Their nerves have become paralyzed. They are afflicted with the agitation of licentiousness, and they fill this spiritual deficiency through the use of forbidden things, intoxicants and other deadly substances. Therefore they have become criminals to the point of madness, and their lives are empty of every kind of decent concept.

These people have lost their very personality, because they have forgotten the real purpose of their existence. They have been deprived of spiritual felicity, because they have abandoned the Islamic way of life, which, by creating harmony between the spiritual and physical life of a human being, frees him from those spiritual diseases in which they are afflicted. And they are in this confusion because they are deprived of the recognition of God, to which they have to return.

Not only in historical and geographical terms, but in the true reality of the matter, the Muslim Ummah is the community that has firmly adopted that covenant which was agreed upon between Allah and His prophets. It alone has realized the truth that the religion of Allah is one, and the system of life He has sent down is also one. And the caravan of the prophets is also one, who in history always presented this one religion. This is because Allah Ta'ala commands the Last Prophet to proclaim this great truth, namely that this Ummah believes in all the prophets, respects all the messengers, and is well acquainted with the temperament of the religion of Islam: the religion other than which no other religion will be accepted by Allah.

This is the Islamic conception of life, which is very broad. It includes all the earlier prophethoods, and under the banner of the Islamic system are gathered all the messengers who ever carried out the duty of God's message. The foundation of the Islamic system is the creed of tawhid (oneness of God), and according to its conception the source of guidance for all the prophets is one, namely the Divine Being, and the Divine Being alone; and belief in all the prophets is obligatory.

It is worth noting here that the first verse commands belief in God Himself. Then comes the command to believe in the Book that was revealed to the Muslims, then mention of belief in the books revealed to the prophets before the Muslims. And after this comes the phrase وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ…………… ("and to Him we have submitted" [Arabic: wa-nahnu lahu muslimun]). Affirming Islam in these words carries a particular meaning. It was first said that the meaning of Islam is to bow in submission, to obey, and to be humble and lowly; it is the following of commands, and the obedience of the Islamic system, the Islamic method of conduct and the Islamic order. And these meanings are drawn from the first verse, أَفَغَيْرَ دِينِ اللَّهِ يَبْغُونَ وَلَهُ أَسْلَمَ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالأرْضِ طَوْعًا وَكَرْهًا وَإِلَيْهِ يُرْجَعُونَ ("Do they seek other than the religion of Allah, while to Him has submitted whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and to Him they will be returned?"). The reason is that the only meaning of Islam for the created things of this universe is that they are obedient; they are subject to the cosmic system and bound within the law of creation. This is why Allah, at every suitable occasion, clarifies this particular meaning of Islam, that Islam is the name of a practical system, so that it settles in people's hearts that Islam is not merely a verbal affirmation or mere assent, which settles in the heart and after which the practical effects of that faith and assent need not come into being, such as obedience to the Islamic system of life and the practical struggle to establish this system in human life. In short, before the general explanation and statement that follows, this is an extremely important point which needs some reflection, and in which it is emphatically said: وَمَنْ يَبْتَغِ غَيْرَ الإسْلامِ دِينًا فَلَنْ يُقْبَلَ مِنْهُ وَهُوَ فِي الآخِرَةِ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ…………… ("Whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers").

After these verses, which continuously explain the meaning of the word Islam, no interpretation can now be given to the meaning of Islam, nor can these verses be distorted, nor can they be mangled, nor can any other meaning of Islam be stated which is unknown to the Qur'an. Islam is, in any case, that Islam which this entire universe obeys, in the system which Allah has established for it.

It is by no means possible that Islam be limited merely to the affirmation of the two testimonies (shahadatain), and that after the utterance and affirmation of the two testimonies, the meaning and reality which is part of the meaning of Islam should not follow from it. That is: the Divine Being is one without partner, and the Divine Being is self-subsisting (al-Qayyum), sustaining the system of the universe. We must worship Him and seek guidance from Him. And that Muhammad (ﷺ) is the Messenger of Allah, and we must obey him, accept the system which he has brought, implement in our lives the Shari'ah which he has brought, and make all our decisions in accordance with the Book which he has brought.

Likewise, Islam is not limited to the extent that a person merely affirms in his heart that Allah is one, believes in the unseen, accepts the Last Day, and acknowledges the Books of Allah and the Messenger as true, without any practical meaning appearing in his life after this affirmation, and without that reality of the matter (haqiqat nafs al-amri) coming into being, as we have explained in detail above.

Then, Islam will not be limited merely to acts of worship and the rites of servitude, nor will it be limited to meditation and remembrance, nor merely to some system of moral and spiritual reform. Unless all these matters appear in the practical form of an organized system of life, founded on Divine teachings, in which hearts also turn towards Allah, the rites of worship and the symbols are also for Allah alone, contemplation and remembrance are also for Allah, in which the reform of hearts takes place through fear of God, and guidance and right direction are given to people, then all these matters will have no good effects, for until a pure, clean and radiant collective system is established, none of these matters will produce good results.

This is Islam as Allah desires it; the meaning of Islam is not that which one destitute generation among the various generations of people wishes under the pressure of its carnal desires. Nor is the meaning of Islam that which the enemies of Islam wish to dress it in, those who are entrenched against Islam and who have left their agents among the Muslims to carry out these distortions, which are at work everywhere.

So now, since the meaning of Islam has become clear to people, yet there are still some who do not wish to accept Islam in the meaning in which Allah desires it, merely because, knowing it, they do so only under the sway of their carnal desires, then certainly such people will be in severe loss in the Hereafter. Allah will neither guide them to the right path, nor will He deliver them from punishment.

This terrifying warning makes every heart that has even an atom's weight of faith tremble, and those in whose hearts there is a sense of responsibility regarding both this world and the Hereafter. This is the appropriate punishment for the person who is given a beautiful opportunity for salvation, yet does not take advantage of it but turns away from it.

Their deeds will not benefit them, even if they spent in the world as much gold as would fill the whole earth. Even if they did such deeds thinking them to be goodness and blessing, it will avail them nothing, for as long as the deed was not done for the sake of Allah. Therefore such deeds will not reach Allah, nor will those deeds be for Allah. After the time has ended, even if they fill the whole world and offer it as expiation, it will not be accepted. They will not be able to escape the punishment of the Resurrection, because the appointed time has ended and the doors have been closed.

This is how the question is settled decisively within the context of the discourse, and it is stated in emphatic terms that leave no room for doubt or suspicion.

After declaring that spending contrary to Allah's principles, and wealth not spent in the way of Allah, are of no effect, and after deciding that once the abode of action has ended, even if one were to spend the whole earth filled with gold in charity, it would not be accepted, Allah the Exalted here makes clear what kind of spending is pleasing to Him.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 92 (part 1 of 2):

Imam Ahmad, with his chain of narration, reports from Abu Ishaq ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah, who said: "I heard Anas ibn Malik say: Abu Talhah was the wealthiest of the Ansar in Madinah, and among all his property the most beloved to him was a well called 'Bair Haa' (Haa). It was opposite the Prophet's Mosque. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to visit this well and drink its pure, sweet water." Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: When this verse was revealed, "Lan tanalu al-birra hatta tunfiqu mimma tuhibbun" ("You will never attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love"), Abu Talhah said: "O Messenger of Allah! Allah the Exalted says: 'You will never attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love,' and my most beloved property is the well Haa. It is a charity for the sake of Allah. I hope for its reward and its recompense with Allah." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Bakhin, bakhin! This is a profitable and valuable property. This is a profitable property. I have heard it, but my advice is that you distribute it among your relatives." Abu Talhah said: "I will do so, O Messenger of Allah." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) distributed it among his relatives and paternal cousins. (Narrated by Muslim and Bukhari.)

Bukhari and Muslim also narrate that Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah! I have received a share in Khaybar, and I have never obtained any property better than it. What do you advise me regarding it?" He (ﷺ) said: "Keep the principal property for yourself and make its produce a charity for the cause of Allah."

Following this same path, most of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) hastened ahead of one another, and thus, seeking goodness from their Lord, they kept responding to this verse. In that age, when Allah guided them to Islam, they answered the call of Allah and freed themselves from slavery to wealth and property. They were delivered from inner miserliness and stinginess, and they were purified of personal greed. Thus they reached that lofty station which was exceedingly elevated, exceedingly radiant, shining, free, and light, released from every chain and bondage.

Part Four at a Glance

This part consists of the final portion of Surah Al-Imran and the initial portion of Surah An-Nisa, up to the verse "Wal-muhsanatu minan-nisa'" ... The final portion of Surah Al-Imran comprises four sections which run alongside the theme and subject matter of the surah, concerning which we discussed in detail while commenting on Surah Al-Imran, namely in Part Three. There is no need to repeat that discussion here; the commentary there may be consulted.

Briefly, it should be understood that the first of these four sections consists of the dialogues that took place between the People of the Book and the believers in the early period of Madinah. These dialogues took place against the historical backdrop whose timing we have already determined at the beginning of the surah, namely the period after Ramadan 2 AH through to after Shawwal 3 AH. Prior to this, Surah Al-Imran comments on that great battle. Through these commentaries, the nature of the Islamic conception of life, the reality of religion, the reality of Islam, and the reality of the system that Islam presented, which all prior Messengers also presented, have been explained. These commentaries also clarified the reality and stance of the People of the Book, who used to dispute with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in religious matters and debate with the Companions. It was made clear how far the People of the Book had strayed from the religion of Islam, and this surah also unveiled the conspiracies they were hatching against the community in Madinah, and it was explained what hidden motives were operating behind their conspiracies. By shedding light on all these matters, the Islamic community is warned about all these affairs and told that it faces a great danger. It should not be negligent and should not accept any statement of the enemy in these matters.

The second portion of the verses, which covers a large part of this surah, encompasses another battle. This battle is not confined merely to deceit and verbal contention and debate, but is a battle of arrows and spears, consisting of blows and fighting. That is, the Battle of Uhud, its events, and the causes and consequences of the events that occurred in it. This commentary on the Battle of Uhud is in that particular style which is a masterpiece of the Qur'an and its miraculous quality. These verses were revealed at the conclusion of that battle, so in them too light is thrown on various aspects of the Islamic conception of life, and provision is made for the training of the Islamic community with reference to the incidents of that battle. From the viewpoint of the Islamic conception of life, the mistakes that occurred in that battle, namely the disunity that arose in the Islamic ranks and certain actions that caused agitation and distress, in light of these events, the Holy Qur'an guided the Muslim community in these circumstances to remain steadfast on its path, to overcome the difficulties encountered on that path, and to attain the rank and status befitting the great trust that Allah has entrusted to the Muslim Ummah, and for the honour with which Allah has favoured this Ummah by giving it this system and the great duty for which it has been chosen, it should render thanks to Allah.

In the third section, the address turns once again to the People of the Book, and they are drawn to attention that they are breaking the covenants, one by one, which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had concluded with them as soon as he arrived in the blessed city of Madinah. They are warned that they have deviated from the correct Islamic conception of life, and that throughout their entire history, at various times, they have continuously committed crimes against their prophets. After this, the Muslim Ummah is cautioned not to follow the People of the Book in their thought and action, to be patient over the losses of life and property they are suffering in the path of truth, and never to be influenced by their enemies under any circumstances.

In the fourth section, it is explained what the nature of the relationship with their Lord is for true believers: when they reflect upon the signs and manifestations of the Divine in this universe, faith in Allah becomes firmly rooted in their hearts. They turn towards their Lord and the Lord of the universe with great humility and submission. Their Lord accepts such prayers of theirs, forgives their sins, and grants them a great reward. In contrast, the condition of the disbelievers is that they are given only the brief enjoyment of this worldly life, that is, on this earth, and that in the Hereafter their abode is Hell, which is prepared for them, and it is an exceedingly evil abode. The surah concludes with that call in which Allah the Exalted invites the believers to patience, to bearing hardships, to uniting together and being vigilant against their enemies, and to keeping the fear of Allah in their hearts at all times, so that they may be successful in this world and the Hereafter.

These four lessons, which are interconnected and presented within a single line of discourse in Part Three, complete the subject matter and proceed along the same lines that we discussed in detail at the very beginning of Part Three, and further details will be explained when we discuss them in detail and expound the commentary of the verses.

The second portion of this part consists of the initial portion of Surah An-Nisa. It will be discussed in the introduction to Surah An-Nisa, Allah willing, and it is Allah who grants success and resolve.

Lesson 26 at a Glance

In this lesson, this battle of disputation and debate with the People of the Book reaches its extremes. Although these verses do not come within the context of the debate with the delegation of Najran, as is also mentioned in the narrations, nevertheless in their theme and meaning they resemble those verses and complete those that were revealed concerning the delegation of Najran. The subject is the same, although the direct address is particularly towards the Jews. It is made clear what secret conspiracies they are hatching, and in what ways, against the believers of Madinah. This debate culminates in complete boycott and complete separation, and then, in this lesson, the address soon turns back to the Muslims, and only they are addressed.

It is explained what the reality of the Muslim Ummah is, what its system of life is, and what its duties are, exactly in the manner in which, after concluding the dialogue with the Children of Israel in Surah Al-Baqarah, the Muslim Ummah was addressed. In this respect, a complete parallel is found between these two surahs.

This lesson begins by stating that all foods were lawful for the Children of Israel. However, Jacob (peace be upon him) had, out of abstention from certain things, declared them prohibited for himself. This was long before the Torah was revealed. It appears that the list of forbidden foods prevalent among the Jews was, since Islam had permitted the use of some of these items, a source of strong objection for the Jews. Yet these items had been made forbidden only for the Jews, and that too because they committed disobedience, and these things were made forbidden for them as a punishment.

Afterwards, the objections they raised regarding the change of the qibla are also answered. Earlier, in Surah Al-Baqarah, a lengthy discussion had already taken place. Here it is shown that the Ka'bah is the House of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and that it is the first house built on this earth exclusively for the worship and servitude of Allah. Therefore, the opposition of those who claim to be heirs of Abraham (peace be upon him) to the designation of the House of Ibrahim as the qibla is incomprehensible.

After this, the People of the Book are warned that they reject the signs of Allah and prevent people from taking the path of Allah. They have left the right and straight path and are wandering on crooked roads. And they wish that this misguidance would overspread the Islamic system of life as well, although they have recognised the truth well, and they are not unaware.

In such circumstances, the Holy Qur'an suddenly leaves the People of the Book and addresses the Muslim Ummah, and warns them in forceful words that they should not obey the People of the Book, because obeying them is pure disbelief. It is not befitting for believers to fall into disbelief at the very moment when the Prophet is presenting before them the Book of Allah, when the Messenger of Allah is among them and is personally teaching them that Book, purifying them, and instructing them in the fear of Allah, and exhorting them to remain steadfast upon Islam throughout their lives and to meet their true Creator in that state as Muslims. The Messenger of Allah and the Book of Allah are reminding them how Allah joined them together; it was a great blessing of His that under the banner of Islam He united their ranks. Previously, their condition had been that they were fragmented and at war with one another. Indeed, they were standing on the brink of a pit of fire and were about to fall into it when Allah saved them from it, and this deliverance came to them through the Islamic system of life. Then this Book commands you, commands you, to take the form of a community whose mission in this world is to call to goodness and righteousness and to forbid evil, and to be guardians of the ideal, for you are to bring the Islamic system of life into operation. Then you are being warned that you should not lend an ear to the whisperings and intrigues of the People of the Book, for these people are within your ranks, and by sowing discord among you they wish to uproot you from your foundations, just as they themselves were ruined in this world and the Hereafter because of their own divisions. In the narrations, the background of this warning of the Qur'an is described: that the Jews, by creating dissension between the Aws and the Khazraj, sowed the seeds of a great fitnah.

After this, the Qur'an reminds the Muslim Ummah of what its position and station is on this earth, and what role the Muslim Ummah is to play in the drama of human life.

"Kuntum khayra ummatin ukhrijat lin-nas, ta'muruna bil-ma'ruf wa tanhawna 'anil-munkar wa tu'minuna billah"

"You are the best community brought forth for mankind: you enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and believe in Allah." In this way Allah guides you as to what your mission is, and what the character and order of your society should be.

After this, the enemies of the Muslims are given attention. It is stated that they cannot inflict any real harm on the followers of Islam, nor can they gain dominance over the Muslims, a dominance that is complete and lasting. They can, however, cause them distress during their struggle. Yet if the Muslims remain steadfast in the Islamic way of life and in their own methodology (manhaj), then the help of Allah will remain with them. Allah has imposed humiliation upon these enemies of God. They will always remain in a state of wretchedness. The wrath of Allah will encompass them. All of this will happen solely because they constantly committed transgressions throughout their history, and unjustly killed their own prophets. Among the People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab), however, there are also those who always supported the truth, believed, and adopted the methodology of the followers of Islam in enjoining good (amr bil-ma'ruf) and forbidding evil (nahy 'an al-munkar). The mission of spreading goodness and righteousness became their cherished goal. Such people are, indeed, among the righteous (al-salihin). But as for those who chose the path of disbelief and did not submit before Islam, they will be held accountable for their disbelief. Their wealth will not benefit them, and their children will not be of any use to them. Ultimately, they will face a great destruction.

This section concludes by warning the believers not to establish any secret friendship with other people in opposition to the believers, because these others conceal hatred and enmity against the Muslims in their hearts. Hostility against the followers of Islam drips from their words, and the volcano of animosity brewing in their hearts against the followers of Islam is extremely dreadful. Out of intense rage and hatred they bite their fingers, and when a calamity or affliction befalls the followers of Islam, they become extremely pleased; and when some success appears for the followers of Islam, they become deeply distressed. At the end of these explanations, Allah makes a promise to the believers that He is their Guardian and Protector. If they exercise patience and adopt the attitude of being God-fearing, Allah will defeat all the schemes of their enemies. ﴿Indeed, Allah is encompassing of what they do.﴾ 

These lengthy explanations and varied indications show how the People of the Book had infiltrated the ranks of the Muslim community and the believers in that era, what conspiracies they were hatching, and the unrest they were spreading. They also show that this lesson created a critical situation at that time. Moreover, it becomes clear here how strongly the Islamic movement needed firm guidance at that time, so that it could clearly understand the nature of the relationships and connections between itself and the comrades of jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance), and so that a definite distinction could be established between the Islamic ideology of life and jahiliyyah. This guidance and explanation was also meant to serve the Islamic movement and the generations that would follow, and to alert the coming generations as to who their inherited enemies are. These are enemies who come onto the field with new forms and new means, yet they are, in reality, one and the same.

The Jews had the habit of seeking out every kind of doubt and every argument, and they used every sort of trick, deceit and cunning so that they might cast some doubt on the truth of the Prophetic mission of Muhammad (ﷺ), create an intellectual crisis within the Islamic movement, and stir up unease in people's hearts. Thus these people were constantly spreading doubts and suspicions. When the Holy Qur'an claimed that it confirms the Torah (Tawrah), they got an opportunity to raise an objection: if the Qur'an is a confirmation of the Torah, then what is the justification for its declaring lawful certain things that were forbidden to the Children of Israel? The narrations state that in this regard they cited the example of camel meat and camel milk, because these things were forbidden to the Children of Israel. Although apart from camels and their milk there were also other things that were forbidden to the Children of Israel, but Allah had made them lawful for the Muslims.

Here the Holy Qur'an draws their attention to a historical reality which they were deliberately ignoring. Their aim was to create doubt about the Qur'an's claim that it confirms the Torah. They would argue that it declared lawful things that were forbidden to the Children of Israel, whereas the reality was that all the foods which are lawful in the Muhammadan Shari'ah were also lawful for the Children of Israel. However, there were some things which the Children of Israel themselves had made forbidden upon themselves before the Torah was revealed. This refers to Israel, that is Prophet Ya'qub (Jacob) (peace be upon him). The narrations state that he was afflicted with a severe illness, and he vowed that if he recovered, he would abstain, as a voluntary act, from eating camel meat and from drinking camel milk, and both of these things were very dear to him. Allah accepted his vow and pledge, and the practice of the Sunnah of Ya'qub (Sunnat Ya'qubi) continued among the Children of Israel, and they too made forbidden the things which their father had made forbidden. Similarly, Allah also made certain other things forbidden to the Children of Israel as a punishment, because they had committed certain transgressions. The reference to these prohibitions is made in the verses of Surah al-An'am (146):

﴿And upon those who were Jews We prohibited every animal with claws; and of cattle and sheep We prohibited to them their fat, except that which is on their backs or the entrails or what is mixed with bone. That was their due for their rebellion. And indeed, We are truthful.﴾

Before this prohibition, these things were lawful for them.

By refuting them, Allah directs them to the reality that the basic principle regarding food and drink is that they are permissible, and that some things were forbidden to the Children of Israel in view of their particular circumstances. Therefore, if some of those things have been declared lawful for the Muslims, there is nothing objectionable in it, because in their original nature they were lawful. Hence no doubt can be cast upon the Qur'an and the divine Shari'ah on account of this lawfulness.

On this occasion the Holy Qur'an challenges them: let them bring the Torah and read it, and see with their own eyes that the causes of the prohibition of these things were exclusively specific to them. These causes are not of a general nature.

﴿Say: Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful.﴾

After this, Allah warns them that those among them who fabricate lies against Allah are wrongdoers. They do not act justly with truth, nor do they act justly with themselves, nor do they act justly with humanity. And the punishment of wrongdoers is also not hidden from anyone. Therefore the Holy Qur'an here suffices with calling them wrongdoers, because with wrongdoing their end as wrongdoers is already determined, since they are fabricating lies against Allah, while they themselves are going to be presented in the court of Allah. What will they answer there?

Among the objections of the People of the Book was also one concerning the change of the qibla (taḥwīl al-qibla), and they would repeat this objection again and again. This objection arose because when the Messenger ﷺ migrated and came to Madinah Tayyibah, he prayed facing Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) for sixteen, seventeen or eighteen months. Although earlier, in Surah al-Baqarah, this subject had been discussed in detail, and it had been explained that the Ka'bah was in reality the true and original qibla, and that Bayt al-Maqdis had been made the qibla temporarily, under certain wisdoms, a clarification of which Allah had already made in its place, yet despite this clarification of the truth, the Jews kept repeating the same objection again and again. They did this so that doubt and intellectual confusion might be created in the hearts of the believers, and so that ambiguity might be introduced into a clear reality. Today too, in our era, this work is carried out in a very organized manner by the enemies of religion on every subject of the Islamic worldview. Therefore, Allah, once again, refutes their doubts and deceptions.

"The words 'Allah has told the truth' point to the fact that what Allah has explained earlier on this matter is correct: that the Ka'bah was built by Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and Isma'il (peace be upon him) so that it would be a place of pilgrimage for people, a place of security and safety, and the qiblah and place of worship of the believers. Therefore, here it is commanded that you follow the way of Ibrahim, and the way and outlook on life of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was a comprehensive monotheistic outlook, in which there was no trace of shirk. ﴿Then follow the religion of Ibrahim, inclining (to truth), and he was not of those who associate others with Allah.﴾ The Jews claimed that they were the heirs of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). The Qur'an therefore tells them that this is the reality of the religion of Ibrahim, and that religion is that every kind of shirk is to be abhorred. And here this reality is expressed twice: once by saying that he was a hanif, and a second time by saying that he was not among the mushrikin. And the state of the Jews is that they are mushrikin.

After this, it is decided that facing the qiblah is one of the principles of the religion, because this is the first house on this earth built for the worship of Allah. And from the beginning of its construction it has been specifically dedicated to this purpose, that it remain exclusively for those who perform tawaf, worship, and bow and prostrate. Moreover, it is a blessed place, and in the sense that the teaching of the religion of Ibrahim is given here, it is a place of guidance. And in it there are clear signs that this is the station of Ibrahim. One interpretation is that it refers to the historic stone on which Ibrahim (peace be upon him) would stand while building the Ka'bah. It was adjacent to the Ka'bah, but the rightly guided caliph Hadrat 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) moved it somewhat back, so that those performing nafl prayer beside it would not be inconvenienced by those performing tawaf. Therefore the Muslims were commanded to pray beside it: ﴿And take the station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer.﴾

Among the virtues of this House, one matter is mentioned here: whoever enters this House will be secure. Therefore this House is a place of security for everyone who enters it. And this status is not possessed by any other place on this earth. This status has continued since the time it was built by Ibrahim and Isma'il. Here, even in the Age of Ignorance among the Arabs, it retained this status, although they had largely deviated from the religion of Ibrahim and were not pure monotheists like Ibrahim (peace be upon him). According to the saying of Hasan al-Basri, even in that evil age this honour and status were given to it. He says: "If a person killed another, he would wrap a woollen cloth around his neck, and in that state, if the heir of the victim found him, he would not say anything to him inside the Ka'bah, and would wait for him to come out." In short, this House of Allah enjoyed this distinction even at a time when the people around it were immersed in ignorance. Allah, the Exalted, reminding the Arabs of His favours, says: ﴿Have they not seen that We made a sanctuary secure while people are being snatched away from around them?﴾ (29:67)

There is also another reason for the honour of the Ka'bah: hunting within its boundaries is forbidden, and it is also forbidden to take birds from their nests there. Moreover, cutting the trees there is also forbidden. Bukhari and Muslim have narrated from Hadrat Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) (the wording is Muslim's) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said on the day of the conquest of Makkah: "This city has been made sacred by Allah from the time He created the heavens and the earth. It is therefore sacred by the sanctity conferred by Allah until the Day of Resurrection. Fighting in it was not made lawful for anyone before me, and it was made lawful for me only for a short part of the day. So it remains sacred by the sanctity from Allah until the Day of Resurrection. Its thorn bushes shall not be cut, its game shall not be chased away, nothing lost in it shall be picked up unless one wishes to announce it, and its grass shall not be cut..."

This is the House of Allah that Allah has chosen for the Muslims, and this is His House, to which He has given this nobility. On this earth it is the first house built solely for worship. It is the house of their forefather Ibrahim, and within it there are signs and evidences that testify that it was built by Ibrahim (peace be upon him). Islam too is bound to the religion of Ibrahim. Therefore the House of Allah built by Ibrahim deserves most of all that Muslims turn towards it, the one that is a place of security on earth, in which there is guidance for people, and which is a centre of the religion of Islam.

Accordingly, it is established here that Allah has made the Hajj to the House of Allah obligatory upon people, for those who have the means; and if someone with the means does not perform Hajj, then he commits kufr."
