Here the manner of expression deserves attention: the obligation of Hajj is stated in extremely general and inclusive terms. For this it uses the words ʿalā al-nās, "upon all people." The first indication in this is that this Hajj has been made obligatory even upon those Jews who at that time were debating with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and waging war against him, asking why the Muslims had begun to face towards it in worship. Yet Allah had Himself demanded of the People of the Book too that they perform Hajj to this House and turn towards it, because it was built by their forefather Ibrahim (Abraham), and because it is the first House on this earth built for Allah alone, to be worshipped in exclusively. Therefore the objecting Jews were deviating from their own obligations; they were negligent and were disobeying Allah.

The second indication in this generality is that from all people the demand is that they acknowledge this religion and perform its obligations and rites, and that they too turn towards the Kaaba and perform Hajj just as the people of faith do. If all these people do not do so, then they are in effect committing disbelief (kufr), even if they verbally claim that they are upon this religion. Allah is free of need from all the worlds; He has absolutely no need that all people believe or that all people go for Hajj. Rather, the benefit in Hajj is for them, and their success alone lies in it. They should believe and worship Allah.

Hajj is obligatory once in a lifetime, and this obligation falls upon a person when he attains the capacity (istitaʿah) for it, which includes bodily health, the possibility of travel, and security of the roads. There is a difference of opinion regarding the time of its obligation. Those who hold that these verses were revealed in 9 AH, which is called ʿĀm al-Wufūd (the Year of Delegations), and some narrations also come in this regard, or whose opinion is that Hajj became obligatory in 9 AH, base their argument also on the fact that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed Hajj only after 9 AH. Earlier, in the second volume, while discussing the Decision of the Change of Qiblah, we had said that the delay of Hajj by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cannot be proof that the obligation of Hajj itself came later. It is possible that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ postponed Hajj due to some engagements and special circumstances. For example, the polytheists used to perform Hajj naked, and they continued this practice until after the Conquest of Makkah. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ may have disliked mixing with such people. When in 9 AH Surah Bara'ah was revealed and it was declared forbidden for polytheists to circumambulate the Kaaba, then in the following year the Messenger of Allah ﷺ himself performed Hajj. Therefore it is possible that Hajj had become obligatory before this, and that this Surah was revealed in the early period of the Hijrah, for instance near the Battle of Uhud.

In any case, whenever Hajj became obligatory, its obligation was established by this decisive text (naṣṣ qāṭiʿ), namely that Hajj is obligatory upon all those who have the means to travel. Hajj is an annual gathering of the Muslims: they assemble near this House, from where the call of Islam began, from where the religion of their forefather Ibrahim also began, and which Ibrahim established as the first House for the worship of Allah. Therefore Hajj is a highly purposeful gathering. It has certain special memories, and the focus of all these memories is that a person's special connection with his Lord is established, and the human soul responds to the call of Allah with "Labbayk," because it is through this soul that a human being becomes human. This is a purpose upon which all humanity should gather, and they should assemble every year in this House, from where once the call of a purely "human spiritual gathering" began, and this call was on purely human foundations.

This threat and warning of this kind has come repeatedly in this surah and in other similar surahs. Its first effect is that the People of the Book are confronted with the reality of their position, and their true condition is laid bare: they present themselves as great believers and great pious people, whereas in reality they are among the disbelievers, because they deny the verses of the Quran that Allah has revealed. Therefore, whoever denies any part of Allah's revelation has, in effect, denied the whole Book. The logical consequence is that if they themselves had truly believed in the preserved Book that was in their possession, they would necessarily have believed in the guidance revealed upon every Messenger who came. This is because the reality of religion is one. Whoever attains this reality will believe in all the Messengers who come after, and who take the covenant from them. This is such a frightening reality that it should make them tremble, cause them doubt about their final end, and make them concerned about their outcome.

The second effect is that some of the members of the Muslim community, who used to be deceived by the People of the Book because of their being People of the Book, also have their eyes opened, since Allah Himself explains the reality of the People of the Book to them and openly pronounces the verdict of disbelief upon them. Therefore, after this, there remains no room for anyone to have any kind of doubt that the People of the Book are in error and the people of Islam are upon the truth.

Allah threatens them in such severe words that hearts are shaken. "وَاللَّهُ شَهِيدٌ عَلَى مَا تَعْمَلُونَ" ("And Allah is Witness over what you do"), and "وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ" ("And Allah is not unaware of what you do"). This is a frightening warning. When a person comes to feel that Allah is a witness over his deeds and that He is not heedless of them, and that the deeds are of what kind? Pure disbelief, pure deception, pure corruption, and pure misleading of others, then it is natural that fear arises in his heart.

Allah places on record this reality: that what they deny of the truth, they deny knowingly and with full awareness, and that while understanding, they prevent people from that truth. While "وَأَنْتُمْ شُهَدَاءُ" ("while you yourselves are witnesses"), that is, they had full certainty that the reality they were rejecting was the truth, and that what they were keeping the common people away from was something in which the common people's good lay. And this attitude of theirs is extremely detestable. Therefore, it is not appropriate to place any trust in a person of such character, nor is it appropriate to make such a person a close companion. The correct remedy for such a person is that he be shown complete aversion and be subjected to thorough criticism.

Allah has introduced these people in the following words: "Why do you bar from the path of Allah those who believe, seeking to make it crooked…?" That is: "What is this attitude of yours, that you block from Allah's path the one who obeys Allah's word, and wish that he should walk a crooked way?"

This is a meaningful observation, and it contains a great secret. That is, the path of Allah is the perfectly straight path, and all the paths other than it are crooked paths. When people are barred from the straight path, and when faith is deprived of the Islamic system of life, then rectitude and straightness will vanish from all human affairs, and the standards of good and evil will no longer remain sound and intact. Every department of the affairs of this earth will become crooked. This will be a great corruption. Corruption will arise in the system of nature, because the system of nature will be violated; corruption will arise in human life, because that life will be founded on crookedness; and this great corruption will come about because people will have been prevented from the Islamic system of life.

Then this corruption will also take place in human thoughts, corruption will be in the human conscience, corruption will be in human morals, corruption will be in human conduct, corruption will be in human relations, corruption will be in human dealings. In short, there will be corruption in all those relationships that arise between one human being and another. Moreover, this corruption will also arise between them and the system of the universe in which human beings live. Thus, people will either live under the Islamic system of life, and in that case they will be upon the straight path and in a state of righteousness, and good will be theirs; or they will walk crooked and winding paths, and in that case they will be afflicted with crookedness, corruption and evil. In the world there are these two paths, and these are the two conditions that can befall the life of mankind. In one condition, they will be travelling on the highway of the Islamic system of life, and then good and betterment are theirs; or they will be travelling on that highway, and then good and betterment are theirs; and if they深 deviate from that highway, then in that situation evil and corruption alone will be their lot.

Here the debate with the People of the Book now ends. Now they are set aside, and now the address is to the Muslim community. Now directions are being given to the Muslim Ummah. They are being admonished and warned against the schemes of the enemy. It is explained what the distinguishing features of the Muslim community are, what its concept of life and its system of living are, and what means are there by which this system of living can be put into operation.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 100:

This ummah was raised up on this earth for the sole purpose of establishing the Islamic system of life on this earth and of charting its course accordingly. It is a unique, distinguished and prominent ummah. Its very existence springs from the Islamic system of life, so that it may play in human life the role that no one else plays. This ummah has been brought into being so that it may affirm the Islamic system of life and implement it in practice, and so that the destination of this system may be visible. In it, the texts and rulings of the Qur'an and Sunnah should be seen practically moving and walking within people's lives; Islamic texts should be seen practically in human consciousness, human morality, human conduct and human relationships.

The purpose of establishing the Muslim ummah cannot be fulfilled, its course cannot be determined, and it cannot bring into being this bright, beautiful and distinguished practical life within human life, until it takes all its guidance from Allah, Glorified is His Majesty, and until human leadership accepts the principles of Allah's guidance in all its affairs. It must not reject the guidance of all people, abandon all human obediences, or cease to follow all human beings. It must either carry out all these matters, or else it must accept disbelief, misguidance and deviation from the right path.

This is the principle that the Qur'an emphasises repeatedly and on various occasions. And it is this principle upon which the consciousness, thinking and morality of the Muslim community have flourished wherever it has had the opportunity. Among these opportunities, one was the time when the People of the Book were debating with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Islamic movement in Madinah had to confront the deceit, secret conspiracies and enmities of the People of the Book. Yet these guidances are not restricted to the particular circumstances of Madinah. These guidances are permanent guidance for the ummah of Muslims. They are the same guidance for every age, every era and every generation. They are the same guidance for every age, every era and every generation. This is because it is the principle of life of the Muslim ummah, and this is its very purpose of existence.

This ummah has been raised so that it may lead all of humanity. Now, by what logic is it permissible that it should follow jahiliyyah (ignorance), when its very purpose of existence is to eliminate jahiliyyah, uproot it completely, and connect human beings to Allah? The leadership of humanity should be carried out in accordance with the Islamic system of life. And when this Muslim ummah falls from the position of leadership, it will be considered that the Muslim ummah does not exist. And if it has any existence, that existence is also without purpose. It was established so that it might lead humanity according to a correct concept of life. Its belief must be entirely correct, its consciousness firm, its morals of a high standard, its system stable and its organisation strong. Only in such circumstances can human intellect flourish, and further paths can become available to it. It can become thoroughly acquainted with this entire universe; it can become aware of the secrets of this universe, and it commands that it be used for the good of this universe. It can subdue these forces and their treasures. But the exalted leadership of the ummah, which commands the conquest of the universe, commands that all these forces be used for the good of humanity. It does not subdue these forces in order to use them for the destruction and ruin of this universe. Nor does it seek from these natural forces the means by which one may obtain the maximum pleasure and become lost in animal desires. The purpose of conquering the universe is solely that the ummah strengthen its faith in Allah, that this subjugation be in accordance with Allah's guidance, and that in this matter it take guidance from no source other than Allah.

In this lesson, Allah warns the Muslim ummah against following other than Allah, and shows how it can create proper conditions and how it can protect itself. Accordingly, the first command given is that the Muslim ummah must not follow or obey the People of the Book; if it does so, the People of the Book will lead it to disbelief, and there will be nothing else.

To obey the People of the Book, to take guidance from them, and to imitate their ways is proof that the Muslim ummah has accepted inner defeat and has renounced its position of leadership. Furthermore, it casts doubt upon the capacity of the Islamic way of life to provide guidance for life in our era, to organise it, and to promote its growth and development. In truth, this is a hidden disbelief that seeps into the human soul. This disbelief is unconscious, and a person does not even perceive its danger. That was the Islamic perspective; as for the viewpoint of the People of the Book, what is it? The thing they are most eager for in the world is to turn the Muslim ummah away from its creed. Therefore, for the Muslim ummah this creed is a rock of salvation; it is a line of defence for it and the true source of its strength and glory. And the enemies of this ummah are well aware of this secret. They knew it before, and they know it today. They employ every deceit and every stratagem to distance this ummah from its beliefs and ideologies. They expend all their energy and all their strength in this endeavour. And when they cannot confront this ummah openly, they employ secret deceit against it; and when these people are no longer capable of accomplishing this task alone, they then seek help in it from the hypocrites, who call themselves Muslims and profess Islam, yet who organise their forces and dig tunnels from within the walls of the Islamic fortress, turning people away from Islam. In their eyes they make beautiful those systems of life that oppose the Islamic system; they devise methods that go against Islam, and they impose upon this ummah a leadership that is not Islamic leadership.

When the People of the Book see that they are finding among the people of Islam individuals who are subservient to them, their followers, and who listen attentively to what they say, they engage these people's services and use them for the purposes for which they lose sleep. They will then grant them positions of leadership and set people to follow them, so that these agents may place the entire ummah on the path of disbelief and misguidance. It is for this reason that Allah's decisive and clear word comes:

"O you who believe! If you obey a party of those who were given the Book, they will turn you back into disbelievers after your faith."

In the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the Muslims feared nothing more than returning from Islam to disbelief, and from being entitled to Paradise to returning to Hell. This is the characteristic of every sincere believer. In truth, in this situation this warning is a whip that heats the conscience; the listener will be fully prepared to hear the compassionate voice of the one who warns. Alongside this, the themes of warning and reminder continue without interruption. How evil is the one who denies the truth and leads believers astray after they have come to faith, in circumstances where the verses of Allah are being recited to them continuously, the Messenger of Allah is present among them, all the factors that led to their faith are present, the Islamic call is being given constantly, and the light of faith is shining at the crossroads of disbelief and faith.

Yes, in such circumstances, for a believer to turn back into disbelief after having believed is indeed a grave matter. And when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ completed his term and joined his Exalted Companion, the verses of Allah were still present, and the Sunnah of the Messenger ﷺ remained. Today we are addressed by these verses in exactly the same way as the people of the earlier generations were addressed. And even today the path to success is clear and the banners of success are raised high. ﴿Whoever holds fast to Allah has indeed been guided to a straight path.﴾

Yes, salvation lies in holding fast to the bond of Allah. Allah, glorified is His majesty, exists. He is Living and Self-Subsisting. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was very strict with the Companions regarding the Islamic outlook on life, Islamic beliefs and the Islamic system of life. But in matters of purely practical and experiential affairs of life, he left them free, that is, in those matters where the reality depends upon experience, such as methods of agriculture, methods of warfare and combat, and other similar matters that belong to purely scientific and experimental fields, and in a sphere where the Islamic outlook on life and Islamic beliefs have no role, or which are not connected with the Islamic system of life. Nor is the connection of these matters a separate thing: pure sciences, experimental affairs and other applied matters are one category. The purpose of the revelation of Islam is that human life should be run according to the Islamic system. It is Islam that set the human intellect to work in such a way that, through the power of knowledge and understanding, it brings forth new material inventions, and that this work is carried out within the framework of the Islamic system of life.

Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal (rahimahullah) narrates a hadith, through the transmission of Sufyan, Jabir, al-Sha'bi and Abdullah ibn Thabit (rahimahumullah). He says: Umar (radiyallahu anhu) came into the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I came across a Jewish brother of mine from the Banu Qurayzah, and he wrote for me some comprehensive things from the Torah. Shall I not present them to you?" It is said that as soon as he heard this, the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ changed. Abdullah ibn Thabit (radiyallahu anhu) says: I said to him, "Do you not see what the signs on the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ are?" Umar said: "I am content that Allah is my Lord, Islam is my religion, and Muhammad is my Messenger." It is said that upon this, the signs of anger disappeared from the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "By Allah, in whose hand is my soul, even if Musa (alayhis salam) were to appear among you today and you were to follow him and leave me, you would certainly go astray. You are my portion among all the nations, and I am your portion among all the prophets."

Hafiz Abu Ya'la narrated from Jabir (radiyallahu anhu), through the narration of Hammad, from al-Sha'bi, that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not ask the People of the Book about anything, for when they themselves have gone astray, how can they guide you? If you ask them about something, you will either confirm a false matter or deny a true matter. By Allah, if Musa (alayhis salam) were among you today, he would have no option but to follow me." In some narrations it is: "If Musa and Isa (alayhima al-salam) were alive, they would have no option but to follow me."

These are the People of the Book, and these are the commands of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ regarding this matter: in all those affairs that relate to beliefs and outlooks, or that relate to the system of life and Islamic law, one must completely abstain from the People of the Book. However, in those matters that relate merely to the sciences, the benefit from all nations and communities is permissible in accordance with the spirit of Islam and its clear guidance; yet it is necessary to link these sciences also with the system of life based on faith, with the awareness that it is the Being of the Creator who has given humanity the power to subdue this nature. He has changed the direction of nature and used it for the welfare of humanity, and arranged peace, tranquility and facilities for humanity. Therefore they thank Allah that He has granted us the power to subdue these cosmic forces, and one way of giving thanks is to worship Him in every matter, and then to use this knowledge, understanding and mastery of the universe for the welfare of humanity.

As for the subject of the believing outlook on life, the views about the creation of this universe, the purposes of human existence, the human system of life and its organisations and laws, and human moral system and conduct, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade taking anything in these subjects from a non-Islamic source of thought, and because of this the blessed face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ changed. Although it was a minor matter, Allah warned the Muslim community very severely that if they did so, it would be a manifest act of disbelief.

This is the guidance of Allah, and this is the example of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. As for us, who continue to claim Islam, our condition is that we take the principles of our knowledge, that is the Qur'an and Hadith, from the Orientalists or from the students of the Orientalists. And consider carefully: we also take our views on the philosophy of life, the origin of human existence and human life from them, or from the philosophers of the Greeks, Romans, Europeans and Marxists. Then observe that we take our system of life, our regulations and laws from these counterfeit sources. We take our conduct, our morals and our manners from that filthy pond which is extremely foul, and in which the filth of modern materialistic civilization has accumulated, which is devoid of every religious concept, even if it were some religion other than Islam. Despite this, we remain under the illusion that we are Muslims. This is a claim whose sin is greater than the sin of manifest disbelief, because by holding such a false claim we in effect confess that the Islamic system of life is not successful in the present age, or if it is successful, then we have distorted the form of Islam and taken the present conduct to be Islam. And we are bearing witness to these matters, whereas those who are not under this illusion are in fact not giving such testimony.

The reality, and it should be tied firmly in the mind, is that Islam is a complete way of life. It is a system possessing several distinctive characteristics: in terms of its doctrinal concepts, in terms of its system of life and system of law, and in terms of its moral principles and rules upon which our collective relations are established, and this religion should not abandon them. These relations may be political, economic or social. Furthermore, it is also a reality that this system claims the position of leadership of all humanity. Therefore, the necessary, logical and inevitable result of this is that there should be on this earth a revolutionary community which raises the banners of this system and guides humanity. And, as we have explained above, the claim of leadership inherent in the Islamic system is not consistent with the idea that Muslims should benefit from other nations or take guidance from them.

Also, let this reality be kept constantly before our eyes: when this religion came, it came for the welfare of all humanity. And today, those who call people to the rule of this system are also calling for the welfare of all humanity. Whoever bears this call in any age will also be for this same purpose. Indeed, the oppressive systems of life under which humanity is crushed, which we see with our own eyes, have the dire need of the just life of Islam. There is no path other than this divine system of life through which humanity can attain salvation. Therefore there is an urgent need that the Islamic system of life preserve and keep alive all its distinctive features, attain the position of leadership among all humanity, and once again deliver this world from hardships and difficulties.

The efforts humanity has made in the subjugation of the universe, the successes it has achieved in various fields, and the facts it has discovered in the fields of medicine and industry are miraculous compared to the past, and humanity is continuously advancing in these fields and gaining new conquests. But what is the effect of all these conquests on its life? What is the state of its psychological world? Is it prosperous in this field too? Does it have peace of heart? Is its life secure? Certainly not. It is presently afflicted with comprehensive misery, restlessness and fear. It is suffering from nervous and psychological diseases. It is trapped in the vast quagmire of aimlessness and crime. Yet it has made no progress in the field of humanity, the purpose of human existence and the purpose of human creation. Therefore, when today we study the mental world of the child of modern civilization and find out what he considers the purpose of human creation, he appears utterly bankrupt, backward and dwarfish compared to the Islamic concept of life. Rather, in this field he appears as though a curse surrounds him, in which man himself degrades his own self and his station in this universe. And as a result of this degradation, man's priorities and interests also fall. Thus man feels a void in his life, and this void consumes the heart of this weary human being. His soul is dying in bewilderment and confusion. This is only because there is no concept of the Divine in his soul, and severe economic conditions have distanced him from the concept of the Divine, and false scientific concepts have led him astray. If this knowledge had progressed in the colour of the Islamic system of life, then each of its achievements would have brought man closer to the value of humanity. But the condition of modern humanity is that the more it advances in the field of knowledge, the more it moves away from the recognition of God, because of its extinguished and defeated soul. It is deprived of the light in which it could see its true purpose of existence, and proceed with its knowledge towards that purpose which Allah Himself has granted it. And the capacity by which it is making this scientific progress is also something granted to it by Allah. Consequently, humanity is not finding the system of life that creates harmony between its movement and the movement of this universe, that creates conformity between its nature and the nature of this universe, that creates harmony between its laws and the laws of nature, a system that creates harmony between its powers and capacities, that connects its world with its hereafter, that creates balance between the rights of an individual and of a community, that creates justice between its duties and obligations; and that all these tasks are accomplished in a most orderly manner, naturally, comprehensively and pleasantly.

In our age, some people work without the Islamic system of life, and those who in this age speak of the Islamic system of life and look towards it with hopeful eyes, these people taunt them with reactionary backwardness. They think that those who speak of the Islamic system of life are in fact harbouring in their hearts merely a longing for a brief golden period of Islamic history that has passed. But because of their ignorance or their ill intention regarding Islam, they are depriving humanity of the leadership of the Islamic system of life, which can guide them most excellently towards progress, peace, security, tranquility and contentment, and which can guide them towards worldly advancement and prosperity.

We who call to the Islamic system of life know well what we are calling humanity towards. We are seeing humanity in its real bitterness. We feel the foul stench of that filthy pond in which humanity is smeared. But on the distant, lofty horizon we see the banners of salvation fluttering, which are showing the glimmer of deliverance to humanity scorched and weary from the heat of the desert, and this pure, clean and luminous peak is calling humanity towards itself out of that filthy pond. We are certain that if the leaders of humanity do not accept this system of life, humanity will suffer a humiliating calamity in the whole of human history, and it will be the worst calamity in all of human history and evil in every sense.

The first step on this path should be that this system of life be distinctive and unique, that its bearers seek no guidance from the surrounding jahiliyyah (ignorance), and that this system remain continuously pure and clean, until, by the permission of Allah, it again takes up the leadership of all humanity. Allah is most merciful and generous, and He will not leave humanity forever at the mercy of the enemies of mankind, who call people again and again towards jahiliyyah. This is the very point which Allah Almighty enjoins upon the first community of Muslims in His Book, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ also repeatedly emphasised this point in his teachings.

The Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 101 (part 2 of 2):

After this warning and admonition that no guidance should be taken from the People of the Book, and that they should not be obeyed or followed, the Muslim community is now enjoined that its life, and the system of life it lives by, rests upon two fundamental principles. These are principles which the community must keep in view, and which are necessary for it to bear the trust (amanah) whose responsibility Allah has placed upon it, and for the sake of which Allah has brought this ummah into existence. These two fundamental principles are inseparable from one another, namely brotherhood (ukhuwwah) and faith (iman). That is, believing in Allah, fearing Him, and remembering Him at all times and in every moment of every affair of life. And maintaining brotherhood with all those who are believers in Allah in this sense. It is this brotherhood through which the Muslim community becomes living, strong and established on a firm foundation, and thus becomes capable of discharging the great role it has to perform in human life and human history, namely the duty of enjoining what is good (amr bil-ma'ruf) and forbidding what is evil (nahy 'anil-munkar), and establishing the order of life in this world upon what is good (ma'ruf), and purifying it from the pollution of what is evil (munkar). He says:

These are the two central pillars on which the structure of the Muslim community (jama'at muslimah) rests, and it is with these two that it performs its weighty and great role. If even one of these two pillars should fall, the structure of the Muslim community would collapse, and after that it would have no role left to play in this world.

The first pillar is the pillar of faith and taqwa (God-consciousness). That taqwa and fear of God which becomes the means of fulfilling the rights of Allah, Glorified is His Majesty. A constant and watchful fear of God, in which there is no negligence, in which there is no interval, and which remains continuously established throughout a person's whole life, until death comes upon him. ﴿O you who believe! Fear Allah as He should be feared……﴾ "O you who believe! Fear Allah as He should be feared." Fear Allah in the way that His due fear is owed. No limit has been set for this fear of God; it is the task of the fearing heart to determine to what level it reaches in its fear of God, to the extent that it can imagine and to the extent of its strength. The believing heart, the more it advances in this field, the more new horizons will open before it, and its steed of longing will find spur and momentum. And the more closeness to Allah it attains through its fear of God, the more its longing will turn toward a yet higher station. And upon whatever station it stands, it will seek stations higher than that, and eventually it reaches such a state in which its heart remains ever awake, and then it never sleeps.

﴿And do not die except while you are Muslims……﴾ "Do not die except while you are Muslims." Death is a hidden and unseen moment, the knowledge of which has been kept concealed from man. Therefore, whoever resolves that he wishes to die only in the state of being a true Muslim, there is only one way for him: he should immediately become a Muslim, and remain a Muslim at every moment. After taqwa and fear of God, the mention of Islam points to a broad wisdom and meaning, namely, complete submission: complete surrender to Allah alone, obeying Him, following His system of life, and making judgments according to His Book. This is the meaning that has been repeated again and again in this surah, as we have stated above. This is the first pillar on which the Muslim community stands, so that it may establish its existence and perform the important role assigned to it in this universe. For without this pillar and its foundation, every gathering of people would be considered a gathering of ignorance (jahili). In that case, that gathering would not be a gathering upon the Islamic method, which could be called the assembly of the Muslim Ummah. Thus there would be societies based on jahiliyyah, in which there would be no guided leadership, one that is truly a guide to humanity, but rather jahili leaderships would arise.

The second foundation on which the edifice of Islamic society rises is the foundation of Islamic brotherhood: brotherhood purely in the name of Allah, companionship in the Islamic way of life, and companionship in striving to establish the Islamic way of life.

﴿And hold fast, all of you together, to the rope of Allah, and do not become divided. And remember the favour of Allah upon you when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together, so that by His favour you became brothers. And you were on the brink of a pit of Fire, and He saved you from it. Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses that you may be guided.﴾

This brotherhood flows, as it were, from the fear of Allah and from faith; that is, it is the first foundation of Islam. And the basis of this brotherhood is the rope of Allah: that is, the foundation of the covenant made with Allah, the foundation of His religion and the foundation of His method. The foundation of this brotherhood is not the foundation of a gathering of jahiliyyah, nor the foundation of any other purpose of jahiliyyah, nor upon any other rope besides the rope of Allah. It is solely upon the rope of Allah: ﴿Hold fast, all of you together, to the rope of Allah, and do not become divided﴾.

This brotherhood, whose foundation is holding firmly to the rope of Allah, is described by Allah, the Exalted, as a great favour upon the first Islamic community. He says that this is a blessing with which Allah honours only those whom He loves. Here Allah reminds them of this His bounty. He says: consider the state in which you were in the age of jahiliyyah, namely that you were ﴿enemies﴾. Each one was the enemy of the other. Look: who can present a more striking example of enmity than that of Aws and Khazraj in Madinah? These were two tribes of Yathrib, who lived in the neighbourhood of the Jews, and these Jews kept kindling the fire of enmity between them. They constantly blew into it, and they kept this fire so fresh that it would burn up and reduce to ashes every kind of relationship between them. For the Jews this was a fine field of activity, and they worked in it night and day, and by it they lived. So Allah provided for the reconciliation of the hearts of these two Arab tribes, and this was Islam. It was Islam alone that joined the hearts of those tribes who were full of hatred. And it was the rope of Allah alone that all of them held firmly, and by the favour of Allah they became brothers. It is only Islamic brotherhood that can produce unity among people, and by means of it they can forget their historical enmities, or forgive their tribal vendettas, or abandon their personal interests and sectarian traditions, and then all people stand together in one rank before Allah, the Majestic and Exalted.

﴿And remember the favour of Allah upon you when you were enemies, and He brought your hearts together, so that by His favour you became brothers.﴾

Then Allah reminds them of another favour: that they were on the edge of a pit of fire and were close to falling into it, but Allah saved them from it. And they were saved in this way: they held firmly to the rope of Allah and believed. This was the first foundation of Islam. Then He placed love in their hearts and they became brothers, and this love and companionship was the second foundation of the collective system of Islam. Therefore He said: ﴿And you were on the brink of a pit of Fire, and He saved you from it﴾.

In the verse the expression "He brought your hearts together" is used. The word "heart" is used because human connection and consciousness are joined together in a bundle of hearts, and they are in the hand of Allah. They have been bound with the rope of the covenant and the compact made with Allah. Thus in this verse the picture of the Muslims of that time has been given the garment of words; rather, their situation appears as a living and moving scene: ﴿and you were on the brink of a pit of Fire﴾, and the situation was such that you were about to fall, when suddenly the hand of Allah's power saved you. As if the hand of Allah is perceptible and visible, and the rope of Allah is seen in a tangible way, and the people are saved, narrowly, from a situation of extreme danger. This is a living, moving spectacle. The hearts of those who witness this scene are pounding, and the danger is present before them. After centuries and generations, it is as if eyes are seeing it.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned in his Sirah that this verse was revealed concerning Aws and Khazraj. What happened was that a Jew passed by a gathering in which people of Aws and Khazraj were sitting together like brothers, and this was very grievous to him. So he sent a man and told him to mention the events of the Battle of Bu'ath between them in that gathering. This man kept mentioning those events in their gatherings in his own manner. In this way people became inflamed against one another. They began to look at each other with angry eyes, they kindled the spirit of revenge in each other, they took up their banners, weapons were demanded, and the place called "Harrah" was nearly settled for a renewed battle. The news reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He came to them, calmed them and said: "Do you call to jahiliyyah again while I am among you?" After that he recited this verse to them. They were deeply ashamed, and immediately peace was made between them. They embraced one another and threw down their weapons. May Allah be pleased with them.

When Allah made the truth clear to them, they came onto the path of guidance, and concerning them the word of Allah, the Exalted, proved true: ﴿Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses, that you may be guided﴾.

The Muslims loved one another, were established upon the system of Allah, and were advancing on the path of leading all humanity, and were holding firmly to the rope of Allah; and the Jews were striving to cut that rope. This is one example of the continuous plots of the Jews which they have continually carried out against the community of Muslims. And these plots they always begin when Muslims try to hold to the rope of Allah and attempt to adopt the Islamic way of life. And their attempts succeed only because the Muslims begin to follow the People of the Book, and their intrigues are based on such deep stratagems that they nearly set the Muslims of the first age against one another and turned them back from Islam into the state of kufr. They aimed to cut the strong rope of Allah that connects them, through which they had become brothers and had become united and gathered together. This portion of the verse also shows the connection between this verse and the verses before it.

It is worth noting here that whether or not this was the occasion of revelation, the verse nevertheless describes a general situation beyond that particular event, because its context and its surrounding verses indicate that at that time there was a powerful continuous movement by the Jews to set the Muslims against one another and to create division among them. They were constantly engaged, using all their resources, in stirring up mischief and discord within the Islamic ranks. That is why the Noble Qur'an repeatedly warns the Muslims to be watchful against the plots of the Jews and the People of the Book, who are sowing the seeds of doubt and hypocrisy among them and are always striving to bring intellectual disorder into them. This has been the attitude of the Jews towards Muslims in every age. Today too they are doing the same, and tomorrow their conduct will be the same, in every Islamic society and in every age.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 104:

The question is: after confronting these Jewish conspiracies, and being established on these two foundations, what is the manifesto and objective of the Muslim ummah? Its duty is the duty of iqamat al-din (establishing the religion). It is the establishment of the Islamic system of life on this earth. It is to make truth prevail over falsehood, to make what is good (al-ma'ruf) prevail over what is evil (al-munkar), to spread goodness and to restrain evil. This is the aim for which Allah Himself, with His own hands, in His own sight, and according to His particular method, brought this ummah into being. This aim is defined in the following words:

﴿Let there be among you a community that invites to good, enjoins what is right, and forbids what is wrong. It is they who will be the successful.﴾

So it became necessary that such a community should always exist, one that invites to goodness, commands what is right, and prohibits what is wrong. Within it there must necessarily be a authority, a power, that invites to goodness and performs the duty of amr bil-ma'ruf (enjoining what is right) and nahy 'an al-munkar (forbidding what is wrong). That such an authority or sovereign power is necessary to carry out this work is clearly indicated by this verse. That is, the invitation to good must always exist, and anyone can do this. But here the words amr bil-ma'ruf and nahy 'an al-munkar are also mentioned alongside it. If the Islamic call is feasible without a sovereign authority, then amr bil-ma'ruf and nahy 'an al-munkar are not possible without obtaining sovereign authority. For the resolution of this issue, the correct Islamic concept of life is that a sovereign authority is necessary which enjoins what is right and forbids what is wrong. This sovereign authority will be founded upon the aim of inviting to good, and its purpose will be the repelling of evil. This sovereign authority will be one that is attained as a result of complete unity and harmony. It will come about through holding firmly to the rope of Allah and after the establishment of Islamic brotherhood. That is, this sovereign authority, or state, or government, will be founded on these two bases: unity and brotherhood, and its aim will be the establishment of the Islamic system of life in human existence.

This sovereign authority will be established in such a way that the general public will be invited to that system, which is pure goodness. People will be introduced to it, so that they understand what the reality of this system is. They will be told that the Islamic system desires sovereign authority so that it may enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. And people will either obey it, or it will cause them to obey it. This is because Allah, the Exalted, says:

﴿And We did not send any messenger except that he be obeyed by the leave of Allah.﴾

Therefore, this must be kept in mind: the meaning of an Islamic system of life on this earth is not merely that preaching, admonition and proclamation continue. That is only one part and component of the Islamic system. Its second important component is that a sovereign authority be established which discharges the duty of enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, which promotes what is right in human life, and which eradicates what is wrong. It must also preserve the "distinguished community" so that no ordinary or base person can sacrifice this ummah to his desires, his inclinations and his lusts, and cannot use it for his personal interests, and no one can destroy the morality based on goodness and virtue in society according to his own opinion and his particular notions, even if he thinks that what he is doing is right and proper.

This is why the duty of inviting to good, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong is not an easy or simple task. Especially when one considers its nature and sees that it clashes with people's desires and inclinations. It conflicts with the personal interests and benefits of some people. It strikes at the arrogance and pride of some people. Oppressive usurpers and rulers who impose themselves by force are also affected by it. Some fallen classes, in whom there is no drive for progress and elevation, regard it as a calamity. Some are so lacking that they do not have the courage to bear its hardships. Some are oppressive classes with whom justice does not sit well. Some are so misguided and crooked that the straight path does not even appeal to them, and among them there are some who like what is wrong and are enemies of what is right... Yet humanity and the Muslim ummah can only attain success when goodness prevails among them, when what is right is right and is recognized as right, and when what is wrong is recognized as wrong. The logical requirement of all these matters is that there be a sovereign authority in which goodness prevails, which performs the duty of forbidding what is wrong and enjoining what is right, and which also has the power to enforce its commands and prohibitions.

Therefore, the establishment of a community founded on these two pillars is absolutely necessary: faith in Allah and Islamic brotherhood. Through their power of faith, their power of God-fearing, and the power of mutual affection, love, harmony and unity, it can discharge the duty for which it has been raised. This is because the aim given to the Muslim community, and the duty imposed on it, cannot be fulfilled or crowned with success without these two characteristics. This is why Allah, the Exalted, says:

﴿And it is they who will be the successful.﴾

In short, the establishment of this kind of community is a fundamental necessity for the establishment of the Islamic system of life. It is the inherent need of the Islamic system. This community will provide the environment in which the Islamic system will breathe, will live, and will appear in the form of a reality. This environment will be an environment of goodness, will be mutually supportive and cooperative, and in it the call to goodness will be prevalent. In it goodness, virtue, truthfulness and justice will be recognized as what is right. Evil, baseness, falsehood and oppression will be considered wrong in it. In this environment goodness will be easy and committing evil will be difficult. In it, the effort required to act upon goodness will not be as great as the effort required for evil. In it truth will be strong against falsehood. In it, justice will bring more benefit than oppression. In it, those who do good will find helpers readily available, and those who commit evil will face resistance and opposition. This is why it is necessary to establish such a society in which truthfulness and goodness can flourish without struggle. For this, its entire environment and each of its members will be supportive, and in which there will be great difficulties and obstacles to the growth of falsehood and evil, because the whole environment will not be favorable to it.

The Islamic conception of the universe, its conception of life, its conception of authority, its conception of deeds, its conception of events, its conception of things and persons, are all, by their foundation and their nature, entirely different from all other jahili (ignorant) conceptions. Therefore, this comprehensive Islamic conception of life requires an environment in which it can flourish and in which its own values of life can grow. Hence there is a need for a good environment separate from the jahili environment, and it requires its own society, not the society of a jahili community.

This environment and this society should be for the Islamic conception of life, so that this conception remains alive and this environment is also alive for it. In this environment this conception should flourish, and it should be able to breathe freely in this environment. It should be able to progress in it, and there should be no obstacle in its path: neither internal obstacles that create difficulties in its way, nor external obstacles that resist it. And if such obstacles come into existence at any time, the Islamic call should confront them, because it is an invitation to goodness, an invitation to enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. And when any such coercive force places obstacles in the way of the Islamic call, there should be those in that society who defend it, and these people should be the guardians of the Islamic system.

This environment is provided in the form of the Islamic community, and this community is founded on two bases: faith in Allah and Islamic brotherhood. Faith in Allah is necessary so that its conception of the universe, its conception of life, its values, its conception of deeds, and its conception of persons and things are in harmony. All these conceptions should conform to a single measure and be derived from a single source. All the problems of life should be resolved according to them, and the decisions of the whole of life should be in accordance with the Shariah revealed by Allah. And that community should follow with love the leadership that is established in accordance with the Islamic system of life. It should be founded on Islamic brotherhood. Its formation should be based on the principles of love and mutual cooperation and support. These are principles under whose shade selfishness and greed come to an end, and the feelings of selflessness and sacrifice are doubled. People sacrifice with great ease, freedom and warmth, and they live with complete tranquility, joy and confidence.

In short, the first Islamic community in Madinah Taiyyibah was established on these two principles. Its faith in Allah was extremely firm, based on the knowledge of God (ma'rifah ilahi). Because of this knowledge of God, the reflection of the divine attributes fell upon their consciences. God-fearing, awareness of God's supervision, constant vigilance, and a sense of the divine presence in this community reached such a level that its parallel is rare in human history. And along with knowledge of the Creator, they were embodiments of sweet and beautiful love. In economic terms they were mutually supportive and cooperative, and possessed deep and sincere sympathy. And they had reached such a high station in this field that, had they not practiced this standard in action, it would have been mere fantasy. In short, the story of brotherhood and mu'akhat (pairing in brotherhood) between the Muhajirun and the Ansar was a reality, but it was of such an exceptional and lofty standard that even today it appears merely as a tale, although it was a reality, and that story actually took place on that soil, though it appeared astonishing and legendary. In short, on this kind of faith and this kind of brotherhood and fellowship, the Islamic system will be established in every age.

This is why, within the context of the discourse, the Muslim community is repeatedly warned to refrain from division and unjustified disagreement. Those who were chosen before them to bear this trust, and who engaged in factionalism, and how they were ultimately destroyed and ruined, and how Allah took that honour from them and entrusted it to the Muslim community, are a lesson for them, so that they remain bound together. Moreover, the evil end that awaits those people on the Day of Resurrection is an added warning: on the day when some faces will be black and some white, and those whose faces are black will be these people.

This passage is not a tafsir of a specific verse with isnad or hadith, so I translate it as it stands, with the Qur'anic quotations rendered in ﴿ ﴾ markers.

In the context of the discourse, the Qur'an presents one of its scenes, full of moving images. We stand before a terrifying scene, so frightening that it cannot be fully portrayed in words, nor can its features be described in language.

Before us stand two kinds of people. They are living human beings, with faces and features. Some people have faces that are radiant; joy flows from them, they are cheerful and bright, and their faces have turned red and white with delight and happiness. In contrast, there are other faces that are dull with grief and sorrow, their colour has drained away, and they have become black from exhaustion. Yet even in this condition they are not excused; they are not left to their own state, but are made to weep further and are rebuked.

﴿Did you disbelieve after you had attained faith? Then taste the punishment for your disbelief.﴾

﴿As for those whose faces will be bright, they will be in the mercy of Allah, and they will abide therein forever.﴾

Thus, in the depths of the conscience of the Muslim community, the fear of the evil consequences of division and disagreement settles. And they come to know how great a blessing of Allah faith and affection are. In this scene the Muslim community sees with its own eyes how terrible an end those People of the Book met, who caused division. The community is warned against following them, lest it too meet the same dreadful end and be seized by a painful punishment, on a day when some faces will be white and cheerful, and some faces will be black and downcast.

Now, after portraying both groups and stating their ends, the Qur'an concludes this whole discussion with its characteristic closing words. These words follow the same lines along which the themes of this surah proceed: that the revelation of Allah is based on truth and wisdom; that reward and punishment on the Day of Resurrection is a serious matter; that the commands of Allah in this world and the Hereafter are based on the principles of justice and fairness; and that whatever is in the earth and in the heavens belongs entirely to Allah; and that all matters will ultimately be decided before Him.

The matter is not as the People of the Book presume, that they will be punished in the Fire only for a few countable days and then will come out.

After this, the attributes of the Muslim Ummah are described, so that it may come to know its position, its worth and its reality. After this, the People of the Book are introduced before the Muslim Ummah. Their status is not diminished; by stating their reality, hope is given to them that if they believe, it will be beneficial for them. Therefore the believers are assured that their enemies cannot cause them any harm: despite their plots, their deceptions and their fighting, they cannot inflict any loss upon the Muslims, nor can they gain victory over them. As for the disbelievers, they will remain in Hellfire in the Hereafter, and whatever they spent in this world without faith and God-consciousness will bring them no benefit in the Hereafter.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 110 (part 1 of 2):

At the beginning of these verses, a heavy burden is placed upon the shoulders of the community of believers. This burden is placed because Allah has honoured and dignified this community and has given it a station that no other community has attained until today.

﴿You are the best community brought forth for mankind, enjoining what is right, forbidding what is wrong, and believing in Allah.﴾

"Now, in the world, the best group is you. You have been brought into the field for the guidance and reform of mankind. You enjoin good, you forbid evil, and you believe in Allah."

Here the verb ﴿ukhrijat﴾ is in the passive past form. This is a particular expression and deserves attention. Through it is manifested the subtle power of Allah's hand, which is bringing this ummah out and thrusting this community, push after push, from the darkness of the unseen onto the stage of manifestation. It is being revealed from behind that veil beyond which peering is not the work of any human being, and nor does a human know anything behind that veil of the unseen. From ﴿ukhrijat﴾ it is understood that a hidden and unknown power is moving them gradually and imperceptibly. The process is such that suddenly a community emerges on the stage of this universe, and it has to perform a specific role on the stage. This role is extremely important, and a particular station in this universe is determined for it.

﴿You are the best community brought forth for mankind……﴾ "Now, in the world, the best community is you, who have been brought out for the guidance and reform of mankind." This is the matter that the community of Islam should fully comprehend, so that it may feel its true worth: that it has been brought out for the reform of all mankind, so that it may serve as the vanguard, and that it may have the station of leadership in this universe. For it is not merely a community, but the best community. And Allah's will is that on this earth there be leadership of goodness, not leadership of evil. This is why it has been declared beneath its stature of leadership that it should take guidance from other jahili communities. Its duty is rather to bestow upon other jahili nations gifts from its treasury of knowledge and morality. And its stores should always contain such commodities as it continues to give to other deprived nations and peoples. It should give those nations and peoples correct beliefs and conceptions, correct thought, a correct system of life, correct morality, and correct knowledge and understanding. This is the obligation that is imposed upon it by reason of its high status, and this obligation becomes incumbent upon it by reason of its purpose of existence. It is part of its official responsibilities that it remain the vanguard for the other nations in every field. It should always remain in the station and position of leadership and always be the centre of the nations. Therefore, this position has certain effects and results. That position is not acquired by mere claim, but is entrusted to the community that is worthy of it. When it is worthy, by reason of its conceptions and thoughts and by reason of its exalted system of life, only then is it given. For the community must be ahead of all nations in the field of knowledge, and in terms of progress and construction as well it must be ahead of the nations and peoples, so that it attains the station of khilafah fil-ard (vicegerency on earth) and proves itself worthy of it. This is why the system of life that the Muslim community will call to demands many excellences from it, and its first demand is that it remain ahead in every field, if it wishes to remain steadfast in this position and fulfil its requirements and its duties.

The first requirement of the station and status of this community is that it purify this life from evil and corruption, and that it possess such strength as to be able to discharge the duty of enjoining good and forbidding evil. For it is the best community and has been brought out for the reform of people. And that best community did not become the best merely by Allah's favour or by some special relation of beloved-ness, nor was it made the best community by chance, without purpose or intention. For Allah the Wise is free of such, and such an act cannot be expected of Him. Honour and dignity in the sight of Allah are not obtained on the basis of those vain fancies in which the People of the Book became entangled, and who used to say: ﴿We are the sons of Allah and His beloved.﴾ "We are the children of Allah and His beloveds." Certainly not! This was a positive act; according to the plan, the intention was to save humanity from evil, the aim was to establish what is good, and, with the believing conception of life, to clearly define the boundaries of good and evil in the world.

﴿You enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and believe in Allah……﴾ "You enjoin good, forbid evil, and believe in Allah."

Enjoining good and forbidding evil are in fact the duties of this best community, with which it must rise, even if in discharging these duties it has to bear hardships, for this is a thorny path. In it, evil has to be challenged, people have to be called to goodness, and society has to be protected from the causes and means of corruption. All these tasks are exhausting, but all these tasks are necessary for the establishment and preservation of a righteous society, and besides this, those patterns cannot take root according to which Allah the Exalted wishes to order human life.

Alongside enjoining good and forbidding evil, it is also necessary to be a firm believer, because in an Islamic society the standards of good and bad are established by the scale of faith alone, so that the right recognition of good and evil can be made. For the righteousness of one group alone is not sufficient; sometimes corruption and evil spread to such an extent that the collective values of society change and become disordered. Therefore, for good and evil a firm conception is needed, in which the virtues of deeds and the vices of qualities are clearly separated, the good is distinguished from the evil, and this conception of life is based upon eternal principles and foundations separate from any particular scheme of reform.

And it is clear that these aims can manifest themselves only as a result of faith, that is, the correct conception of the universe and the correct conception of its relationship with its Creator, the correct conception of man and his purpose of existence, and the correct conception of man's station and status within the universe. Then, as a result of these correct conceptions, correct moral principles come into being, which are based upon fear of God and hope for His mercy and good pleasure. And because of these principles, people willingly incline toward establishing these moral principles; Allah's sovereignty rules over their hearts, Allah's Shari'ah rules over their society, and thus the guardianship of these principles and rules also continues.

Furthermore, faith is necessary so that those who call to good, those who enjoin what is right, and those who forbid what is wrong may be able to proceed on this thorny path, bearing hardships with steadfastness, relying upon this power of faith. Especially when they confront the tyrants of evil, and these tyrants are young and robust, while they are confronting the tyrant of the desires of the self, and that desire is at its peak of intensity and is very youthful; while they are confronting fallen souls whose resolve has become blunt and whose lamp of hope has been extinguished. In such circumstances, their provision for the journey is only the power of faith, their equipment for battle is only faith, and their reliance is only upon Allah. Their condition is that all provisions other than the provision of faith have been exhausted, and all equipment other than the equipment of faith has been used up, and all supports other than Allah have fallen one by one.

Earlier, it was commanded: "Let there be among you a group that calls to good and enjoins what is right and forbids what is wrong." There, the duty of enjoining good and forbidding evil was imposed upon the ummah. Now it is said: you are the best ummah; your attribute and distinguishing feature is that you enjoin good and forbid evil. In this there is a hint to the ummah that if this attribute is not found in you, or is not found at some time, then it is as though your real existence does not exist. For in human society this is your identity. If you take up the duty of enjoining good and forbidding evil, you will be deemed present; and if you abandon this duty, you will be deemed non-existent, and as it were the attribute of faith and Islam will be deemed non-existent.

In numerous places in the Qur'an, this duty of the Muslim community has been clarified both explicitly and by allusion, the discussion of which we will undertake at those places. But in the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ too, attention has been drawn repeatedly to this official duty. I wish to present some select ahadith here:

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (رضي الله عنه) narrated that he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; if he is not able to, then with his tongue; and if he is not able to, then with his heart. And that is the weakest of faith."

Ibn Mas'ud (رضي الله عنه) narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the Children of Israel fell into sins, their scholars forbade them, and they did not desist. Then their scholars sat with them, ate and drank with them, so Allah struck the hearts of some of them against the hearts of others, and cursed them through the tongue of Dawud (peace be upon him), Sulayman (peace be upon him), and Isa son of Maryam (peace be upon them both)." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) sat up (he had been reclining) and said: "No! By Allah in whose hand is my soul, you must enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and you must turn them firmly back to the truth." The word "tamurun" means "ta'tifunahum" (turn them) and "turddunahum" (bring them back). (Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi)

Hudhayfah (رضي الله عنه) says the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Allah in whose hand is my soul, you must enjoin what is right and you must forbid what is wrong, or else it is near that Allah will send upon you a punishment from Himself, and then you will call upon Him and He will not answer your call." (Tirmidhi)

And Urs ibn Umayr al-Kindi (رضي الله عنه) narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When an evil is being committed on earth, the one who sees it and disapproves of it is like one who is absent from it, and the one who is absent from it but is pleased with it is like one who sees it." (Abu Dawud)

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (رضي الله عنه) narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Hamzah is the master of the martyrs, and the man who stood before an oppressive ruler, enjoined him to do good and forbade him from evil, and as a result was killed, is the master of the martyrs." (Narrated by al-Hakim)

These and many other countless ahadith describe this distinctive feature of Islamic society and show that in an Islamic society this duty and its discharge are absolutely essential. Because of this attribute, guidance and training of society continues to be arranged, and apart from being a Qur'anic command, this is a provision whose benefit and worth we are completely heedless of. Now we turn to the final part of the first verse.

﴿And if the People of the Book had believed, it would have been better for them. Among them are believers, but most of them are defiant transgressors.﴾

In these phrases, the People of the Book are encouraged to believe. Faith would be better for them; by it they would be saved from the division and ruin into which they have fallen. They were afflicted with sectarianism even in their doctrinal conceptions, and their personality was not unified, so their doctrinal conceptions did not have the capacity to become the foundation of any collective system of life. Because their collective systems were founded upon other conceptions apart from their own beliefs, therefore their collective system always remained lame, crippled, and suspended in the air, its roots never spreading deep into society, just as those systems of the world which are not founded upon a complete doctrinal and ideological basis remain suspended in the air, which are not built upon a conception of life that presents a complete solution to the riddle of this universe, which do not define the purposes of human existence, which do not define man's place in this universe. And believing is beneficial for them in the Hereafter as well, because they will be saved from the evil end that awaits non-Muslims in the Hereafter.

In this verse, it is plainly acknowledged that some of these People of the Book are righteous too: ﴿Among them are believers, but most of them are defiant transgressors.﴾

Some of the People of the Book had believed, and they were very good Muslims. For example, Abdullah ibn Salam, Tha'labah ibn Sha'bah and Ka'b ibn Malik, among others. It is these people that this verse alludes to. Although in this verse the allusion is general, and in another verse it is detailed. However, the majority of them remained deniers of the religion of Islam. Therefore they broke the covenant of Allah that He had taken from the Prophets: that each of them would believe in the Prophet who would be sent after him, and would support him. They became disobedient to the religion of Islam in this manner: they did not submit before the will and command of Allah regarding the sending of the final Prophet, merely because this Messenger was not from the tribe of the Children of Israel. And by not obeying this Messenger, they also deprived themselves of the honour of having their life's decisions made according to Allah's final Shari'ah, although Allah's will and command was that all of humanity should live their lives according to this Shari'ah.

Since some of the believers still maintained ties with the Jews of Madinah, and at that time the Jews were a dominant power in Madinah tawdry—being a military power as well as an economic power—and some of the Muslims even acknowledged this status of theirs, the Qur'an considered it necessary to criticise this status of these disobedient ones, to free the Muslims from their awe, and to make clear the decline in their standing that resulted from their disbelief, disobedience and crimes. Moreover, the manner in which they had split into sects, and because of which Allah had imposed humiliation and disgrace upon them, was clearly recorded here.

In these verses Allah gives the believers a guarantee of victory and support, and ultimately an explicit guarantee of their safety. Whenever they face their enemies on the battlefield, this guarantee will be available to them, provided they hold firmly to the rope of their religion and place their trust in their Lord.

﴿Lan yadurrukum illa adha, wa in yuqatilukum yuwallukumul-adbar, thumma la yunsaroon﴾ ("They will not harm you beyond a little annoyance; and if they fight you, they will turn their backs to you, then they will not be helped.")

Therefore they cannot inflict any real harm on the Islamic da'wah (the call to Islam), nor can they have any effect on the formation of the community of Muslims (jama'at-i-muslimah), nor can they eliminate the Islamic call from this earth. Yes, when they clash with the Muslim community they can cause pain; they can inflict temporary sufferings of this kind, which pass away with the passing of time. But when they confront the Muslims on the battlefield, defeat is written for them, and in the end they will be defeated; there is no victory in their destiny against the Muslims. They will find no helper against the Muslims, and they will not be able to escape the reach of the Muslims. This is because the stroke of humiliation has fallen upon them, and this evil end has been decreed for them. Therefore, wherever they are, they will remain humiliated: either they will remain under the protection of Allah or under the protection of the Muslims. When they enter under the protection of the Muslims, their property and their lives will be safe, except where some right has been established against them; thus they will attain peace and tranquility. From that time until today, the true peace of the Jews has been obtained under the responsibility of the Muslims. Yet the Jews are so ungrateful that on this earth they hold enmity toward no one more than toward the Muslims.

﴿Wa ba'u bi-ghadabin minallah﴾ ("and they returned with the wrath of Allah"), that is, as if they were wandering from place to place, roaming about, and in the end returned bearing upon their heads the provisions of Allah's wrath.

﴿Wa duribat 'alayhimul-maskanah﴾ ("and humiliation was stamped upon them"), that is, neediness was imposed upon them. The sense of neediness has permeated their conscience and awareness.

After the revelation of these verses, all these events occurred to the Jews in their history. In the battles that took place between the People of the Book and the Muslims, Allah granted the Muslims victory and success, as long as the Muslims kept their religion, their system of life, and their way of life close to their hearts and maintained the Islamic system of life in their lives. Then Allah decreed humiliation and disgrace upon the enemies of the Muslims, except when peace was attained for them through the covenant and responsibility of the Muslims, or when the Muslims themselves abandoned the Islamic system of life and left their religion.

Sayyid Qutb's commentary (Fi Zilal al-Quran) on Surah 3, verse 112:

The Qur'an also reveals why humiliation and disgrace were decreed as the lot of these people. What is the cause? The cause is in fact a general one, whose effects and consequences can apply to every nation, however lofty its claims in matters of religion. The cause of their humiliation and disgrace was disobedience to Allah and wrongdoing.

﴿That is because they used to disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right. That is because they disobeyed and used to transgress.﴾

"And all of this happened only because they kept rejecting the signs of Allah and killed the prophets unjustly. This was the consequence of their disobedience and transgressions."

Therefore, outright denial of the signs of Allah, not implementing them in their own lives, not running their system of justice according to them, killing the prophets unjustly, and killing those who are upholders of justice among the people, as mentioned in the second verse of this Surah, are all causes. That is, through disobedience and wrongdoing alone they became deserving of the wrath of Allah, and defeat, humiliation and disgrace were decreed for them. And these are the very causes that today are found in full measure among the corrupted and deviant generation of Muslims on this earth, the generation that wrongly applies the word Islam to itself. Today these causes are presenting themselves before Allah in the mirror of their conduct, so Allah is also treating them today in exactly the same way that He once treated the Jews for these same causes; that is, defeat, humiliation and disgrace have today become their lot. When someone among them today asks, "Why are we not dominant on this earth, although we are Muslims?", before asking this question he should have known what Islam is and who a Muslim is, and only then should he ask.

Nevertheless, at the time of the Messenger ﷺ there were some good people among the People of the Book. Although they were few, it was necessary that they be treated justly. Therefore an exception was made to the general rule stated in the above verse. It was made clear that they are not all alike; among them good believers also arose. Their relationship with Allah is exactly like that of a good Muslim and a sincere Muslim, so they will deserve the reward that the true believers deserved.

The People of the Book are a bright picture of believers. Some of them accepted faith with sincerity, and this faith sank deep into their hearts. Then this faith was complete and all-encompassing. These people joined the ranks of the Muslims and became guardians of the religion of Islam. They believed in Allah and the Last Day. They fulfilled the requirements of faith, and they began to act in accordance with the fundamental characteristic of the community of which they had become a part, namely that it is the "best of nations." They adhered to the duty of enjoining what is good and forbidding what is evil. Even before this, their souls had been inclined toward good, and they competed with one another in doing good. They outdid one another. Therefore, from the higher realm there was sent down this testimony in their favor, that these people are certainly among the righteous. And a true promise is made to them that none of their rights will be denied, nor will any of their rights be withheld. It has also been declared that Allah well knows that they are among the God-conscious (muttaqin).

This is a picture that is shown here so that those who desire to have this testimony recorded in their favor may see it on this bright horizon and develop these qualities within themselves.

This is one front; on the other side are the disbelievers, those disbelievers whose wealth benefits them nothing, and for whom their children are of no use. Then whatever they spent in the world is of no benefit to them. On the Day of Resurrection, their spending will bring them no benefit. Why? Because this spending is not connected with that straight path of good which Allah has drawn. That is, the good which is based on faith and the Islamic worldview, whose concept is clear, whose goal is constant, and whose way leads to Allah. Otherwise, a temporary impulse toward good may arise now and then, but it will not be constant, and it will be an inclination whose direction a slight storm can turn. It will not rest on any clear, comprehensible, and firm foundation, nor will it be connected to a complete, comprehensive, and straight system of life.
