"In this way the truth is presented in the form of a scene in which there is nothing but movement. This movement is full of life, and this is the beautiful and graceful manner of expression of the Qur'an, in which even an abstract truth appears to be in motion."

Neither their wealth nor their children will avail them anything against Allah. They will not be able to pay the ransom for their crimes, because there, neither force nor wealth will prevail. These people are the inhabitants of Hell, and whatever wealth they spend in the world will be wasted and will have no effect, even though they regard the deeds on which they spend their wealth as good works. This is because true goodness is that whose shoots sprout from the tree of faith, and whose connection is with faith. But the Qur'an does not describe it in the way that we do. It presents this truth in the form of a living and moving scene, which pulses like a vein.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 3, verse 117:

We stand at a place before us is a green, flourishing field, its harvest ready for reaping. The field is in full bloom. Suddenly a strong wind blows; it is an extremely cold, icy wind, and the ripe crop is scorched by the intense cold. It has been observed that the crop is charred by the severity of the cold. The words are used in such a way as if this field is being struck with great speed and force, and the entire field is ruined and destroyed.

This whole process is accomplished in the twinkling of an eye. In an instant the field is razed to the ground and destroyed. This is also the example of the spending of those who disbelieve in this world: although they spend apparently for good deeds and noble purposes, and likewise their wealth and children will avail them nothing. On the Day of Resurrection they will all be rendered worthless. There they will possess no true wealth, nor will there be any reward for them, nor will they be of any benefit.

﴿And Allah did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves.﴾ Allah has not wronged them; they themselves have turned away from the system of life that gathers all individual goods and virtues, brings them onto a straight path, and, having strengthened them, leads them to a single center. It has a fixed goal, an intelligible motive, and a particular method of righteousness. In it, goodness is not left at the mercy of a temporary emotion, a hidden desire, or an incoherent action; rather, goodness and benevolence are carried out in accordance with a constant, enduring method.

These people chose for themselves the path of misguidance and disobedience; they turned away from safeguarding the rope of Allah, and as a result all their deeds came to nothing, to the extent that the wealth they spent apparently in good causes was also lost. When their field too has been destroyed, then of what use is their wealth to them, and of what use is their offspring to them? They have wronged themselves by this. This is because they themselves adopted the path of disobedience and aversion for themselves.

In short, this is a decisive matter: no spending in the way of Allah and no righteous deed is beneficial unless its connection is with the method of faith, unless it is based upon the motive of faith. This judgment is Allah's; it is Allah's saying, so no room remains for humans to say anything in it. Only those who challenge the signs of Allah can challenge this judgment, but their challenge is not based upon knowledge and wisdom; it is based upon neither guidance nor the clear proofs of the Divine Book.

This lesson, which began with the deviation and corruption in the conduct of the People of the Book, in which it was explained what fallacies lie in the disputation and debate of the People of the Book, in which it was explained in detail what conspiracies these People of the Book are hatching against the Muslims, in which the Muslim community was told what its duties and responsibilities are upon this earth, regardless of what these corrupt, deviant people who are waging war say. At the end of this lesson, which is the long lesson in this entire surah, the Muslim community is sternly warned that it must never maintain secret friendship with those who are its natural enemies. It is not appropriate for it to make these enemies its confidants or to rely upon them, since they are sworn enemies of all those who have believed. This warning and admonition from Allah establishes a lasting principle, and we see its fulfilment today with our own eyes. This is a form that the Holy Qur'an has recorded as an ever-living image, but the bearers of the Qur'an today are heedless of it. Consequently, because of this heedlessness, mountains of calamities are falling upon them, and in the future they will surely be afflicted with evil and corruption, and they will be treated with humiliation, if they do not understand.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 118:

This is a complete picture, one that reflects the inner states of the human soul. It presents the outward features of a person, clearly shows his inner condition, displays his outward impressions, and also reveals the movements of his coming and going. This picture presents a model of a person who appears before our eyes every day, in every place and in every age, and among the enemies surrounding the Muslim community such models were visible yesterday and are visible today. These are the kind of models who, when the Muslims gain dominance, become their friends, yet every heartbeat of theirs denies them, and every limb of theirs rejects them. But the Muslims are deceived by them; they love them, trust them, and yet in contrast these people desire nothing for the Muslims but distress and failure, and they spare no effort in making the Muslims disobedient and in strewing thorns on their paths. They are constantly plotting against them, whenever they get the opportunity, whether by night or by day.

This picture, whose strange features the Holy Qur'an has described, applied first of all to the People of the Book who lived in Madinah as neighbours of the Muslims. It is a picture which, through its features, shows that these people were concealing the immense malice they held in their hearts against Islam and the Muslims. They were preparing conspiracies against the Muslims day and night, and their intentions towards the Muslims were always deceitful. And the hidden emotions within them were constantly boiling. In contrast, the condition of the simple-hearted Muslims was that some of them still had misunderstandings about them, some still held affection for them in their hearts, and they still felt assured that if they told them any secret, they would keep it safe as a trust. Therefore, they made some of these People of the Book their close friends, companions and confidants, and they did not hesitate to disclose to them even the inner secrets of the community. So Allah, the Exalted, gave them this light, by which the community of Muslims saw into their inner selves and became aware of the reality. Along with this light, they were given a severe warning and were informed of the secret plans and conspiracies of these their natural enemies, and it was made clear that they were enemies who could never be sincere towards them, and that love and close companionship from the Muslims could not remove their inner rancour. This comment and this warning are not confined to any particular period of Islamic history; rather, it is an everlasting reality. It is a confrontation with a permanent situation, and we see its manifestation before us in our present age as an open observation.

Today Muslims are heedless of the command of their Gracious Lord. He has commanded that they should not take as intimate friends anyone other than themselves, especially those who are inferior to them in their origin, inferior in their system of life, and inferior in their resources. Therefore they should not trust them, nor make them confidants, nor seek counsel from them. But the extent of the Muslims' heedlessness is such that they have forgotten this advice of their Wise Lord, and they have made such people their advisers and point of reference in every matter. In every affair, on every subject and concerning every problem, in every thought, every idea, every method and every approach, they have made these people their teachers and guides.

Today Muslims are heedless of this severe warning and threat of Allah. They are making friends with those who are enemies of Allah and His Messenger, and they have opened the doors of their minds and hearts to these enemies. Yet Allah, the Exalted, says this to the first community of Muslims, and says it to the community of Muslims of today, and to the community of Muslims of every age, and He warns them.

﴿They wish you would suffer; hatred has already appeared from their mouths, and what their breasts conceal is greater.﴾

Also the Almighty further says:

Here you are, you love them, but they do not love you, though you believe in the whole Book. And when they meet you, they say, "We believe," but when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you in rage.

Allah the Exalted says:

﴿If good touches you, it distresses them; but if misfortune befalls you, they rejoice at it.﴾

We often receive the blows of experience, yet we do not come to our senses. Again and again, plots and acts of sabotage against us are exposed, carried out in various disguises, yet we do not take lessons from them. Again and again, words escape the tongues of these enemies that reveal the rancor in their hearts, a rancor that the continuous love and friendship of the Muslims have not been able to erase, and that the religious tolerance of the Muslims has not been able to cleanse. Still, we repeat the same behavior and open our hearts to them. We choose friends from among them, both in our personal lives and in our way of life. Our tolerance toward these people reaches such a point, or our spiritual defeat becomes so severe, that we compromise and make concessions even in our ideology. Because of this tolerance or spiritual defeat, we fear even mentioning our ideology in their presence. With them we are tolerant in our system of life as well, and we do not build it on the foundation of the Islamic ideology of life. For their sake we even distort our history and erase the landmarks of our path, so that the account of our history does not mention the battles in which our forefathers achieved victories over them. This mental defeat is what brings upon us the punishment that descends upon every nation that disobeys the command of Allah. This is why we are humiliated and disgraced, we become weak and feeble, we become ashamed and unsuccessful, and we suffer the losses over which our enemies rejoice. We fall into the failure and ruin that they plot within our ranks.

But look, this Book of ours shows us the way by which we may save ourselves from these enemies, just as this Book taught this lesson to the first Jama'at-i-Islami (the first Islamic group). How will we be protected from these harms? How will we be safe from the rancor hidden in their hearts against us, which occasionally escapes as a spark from their mouths?

﴿But if you are patient and mindful of Allah, their plotting will not harm you at all. Indeed, Allah is encompassing of what they do.﴾

So that way is the way of patience and resolve, and the way of standing firm against them, even if they are very powerful. It is the way of remaining steadfast against their cunning and conspiracies. If they adopt the method of plots and secret intrigues, then our method shall be patience and firm adherence to our ideology of life. It shall not be the way of being swept away, being destroyed, or being humiliated before others. Nor is it a sound policy to abandon all our principles, or some of them, in order to please our enemies or because of their anticipated mischief and corruption.

Against the enemies of Islam, the second method is the method of fear of Allah: fearing Allah alone and keeping the awareness that He alone is watching. God-consciousness and fear of Allah are the means by which human hearts are bound to their Lord. Such a bond is formed only with those who enter the system of Allah and hold firmly to the rope of Allah alone. When a heart attains the recognition of the Divine Being, all fear of forces other than Allah is removed from within it, and the more firm its resolve becomes, the more its connection with Allah grows strong. Therefore, it does not bow before anyone, nor does it make friends with those who are enemies of Allah and His Messenger, merely to save its own life or to earn worldly honor and reputation.

This is the only path for the Muslims: the path of patience and God-consciousness, and the path of holding firmly to the rope of Allah. Whenever in Islamic history the Muslims held firmly to the one rope of Allah alone and adopted the Islamic system of life in their entire lives, they attained a position of honor and dignity, they prevailed, Allah protected them from the plots of their enemies, and their word was exalted. And whenever in their history the Muslims clung to the rope of their natural enemies, those enemies who are engaged, secretly and openly, in rebellious struggle against their ideology of life, and whenever the Muslims lent an ear to the counsel of these enemies, and they made them friends secretly or openly and made them their helpers, advisors, and experts, then Allah decreed defeat in the destiny of such Muslims, gave strength to their enemies in their own land, humiliated such Muslims before them, and they continued to reach the most evil end. Islamic history bears witness that this principle of Allah is unalterable. It is a Sunnah (established way) of His in which no change is possible. Whoever does not observe this repeatedly recurring Sunnah of Allah upon this earth, his eyes will see only the signs of humiliation, weakness, contempt, and feebleness.

With this sentence, this lesson concludes, and the first part of this Surah also concludes here. The battle with the people of disbelief is at its peak here, and the camps of the people of Islam and the people of disbelief have become completely separated from each other here.

Before concluding this lesson, another reality is also worth noting. It is that Islam shows complete tolerance even toward its clear and open enemies. It only advises the people of Islam not to keep secret friendships with the people of disbelief, but it does not command them to deceive the disbelievers, to harbor rancor against them, to hate them, or to adopt the method of cunning and conspiracy against them. Islam only advises them to protect themselves, to defend the Islamic unity, and to take measures to maintain the Islamic identity. That is, Islam has only warned them of the danger, and drawn their attention to their own defense, while that danger surrounded them from every side, and all their enemies were participating in it.

As for the people of Islam, they deal with other people in accordance with Islamic tolerance. Their conduct with people is based on purity and clarity. They meet people with goodness and with love. They protect themselves from plots, but they do not themselves plot against anyone. They protect themselves from the rancor of others, but in their own hearts there is no rancor toward anyone, except when others are in rebellion and enmity against their religion and system of life, when they are stirring up mischief against their ideology, and when they create obstacles for people on the way to coming onto the straight path of Allah. In such circumstances, it becomes an obligation upon Muslims to fight such belligerent enemies, so that mischief may be stopped and the obstacles placed in the way of Allah may be removed, obstacles that stand as barriers to the establishment of the Islamic system. Yes, the struggle against such people will also be jihad fi sabilillah (striving in the way of Allah). It will not be for personal aims or personal revenge. This jihad will be for the good of all humanity. It will not be only against the persons of those who blocked the path of Islam. And this will be so that the message of the Islamic system of life, which is goodness, may reach people without hindrance. Thus, the fighting will not be so that the mujahideen may gain dominance in the world, attain exaltation on this earth, and exploit people. Rather, the sole aim will be to establish the Islamic system of life, under whose just shade all people may live with justice. This jihad is not for raising the banner of any nation, nor is it undertaken to establish imperialism in the world.

This is the reality that is confirmed by many texts of the Qur'an and the Sunnah. The history of the first Jama'at-i-Islami is its interpreter. And that group, in any case, was living its life in this world in accordance with these texts. It is also a reality that the Islamic system of life is nothing but goodness. Those who obstruct the path of the Islamic system are enemies of all humanity, and it is the duty of the Islamic system to pursue them and to strip such people of leadership over humanity. And this is the very duty for which the Islamic community and the Khayr Ummah (the best nation) have been raised.

**Lesson 27 at a Glance**

Until now, in this surah, we have been in the arena of debate and argument: statements and commentary, guidance and warnings. In this second lesson, however, we leave the field of speech and argument and enter the field of the sword and the spear. This struggle is known as the Battle of Uhud.

The Battle of Uhud was not fought only on the battlefield. Its field was much wider. It took place within the human conscience and beliefs as well. The battlefield was only a small part of this broad arena. The struggle took place in the depths of the human soul, in human thought and awareness, in human desires and inclinations, and in human actions and obstacles. Within this struggle the Qur'an trained the human soul through a method that is very subtle, deep, effective and comprehensive. In doing so, the Qur'an gave greater attention to those enemies who were fighting against Islam on the battlefield.

When we enter this struggle, we find that the Muslims were granted victory at first, but in the end that victory turned into defeat. The beginning was a clear victory, and the outcome was rout and collapse. Yet as a result of that collapse and defeat, the Muslims gained a clear victory in the fields of knowledge, understanding, awareness and experience. Their eyes were opened. With their own eyes they saw the realities that the Qur'an had described again and again. Their awareness of these realities became firm to the point of certainty. Their souls were purified. The impure elements were separated from their ranks, and the community (jama'ah muslimah) began to move forward. It was freed from the burden of those whose beliefs were not clean, whose values of life were immature, and whose thinking was unstable. This problem was resolved in such a way that the majority of hypocrites separated from the Muslim ranks, the signs of hypocrisy became clear and visible, and the qualities of truthfulness became distinct and evident, both in words and in deeds, both in awareness and in conduct.

As a result of this struggle, it also became clear what the demands of faith are, what the demands of the call of faith are, and what the demands of rising up to carry the movement of faith are. Furthermore, it became clear how much intellectual capacity is needed to carry this movement forward, how much single-minded preparation is needed, and how much firmly established organisation is needed. After organisation and arrangements, how much strict obedience and submission is needed, and after organisation and obedience, how much reliance upon Allah is needed. On every step of this path, complete trust in Allah is required, and after striving with full effort, the outcome, whether in the form of victory or in the form of defeat, is to be left to Allah. Whether one remains alive as a ghazi (warrior) or dies as a shaheed (martyr), all such matters are to be placed in the hands of Allah. What one is to do and where one is to go, all these matters are to be entrusted to Allah.

As a result of these events, the balance sheet of the Muslim community was drawn up, and the guidance that the Qur'an gave to the community after these events was, in its value and worth, far more important than the spoils of war that the Muslims would have obtained had they returned from the field of Uhud with a clear victory. This is because, at that time, the Muslims needed these experiences a thousand times more than they needed to return from the battlefield with victory, triumph and spoils. In this way, the store of experiences that was left for the ummah coming after the community was more important and more lasting than the victory and spoils that the Muslims would have gained had they won.

In the background of this defeat, the plan of the higher world was that through this event, the weaknesses that existed in the ranks of the Muslims would be made manifest. These were, for example, their physical weaknesses, their moral weaknesses and their intellectual confusion. It is evident that these weaknesses could be revealed only in the case of defeat. The plan of the higher world was that at that time, in accordance with the continuing sunnah of Allah, and in a completely natural manner and within the chain of causes, the Muslims should suffer defeat. For the Muslims at that time, this defeat was more beneficial, so that the community would undergo these experiences, take a lesson from them, and thus receive practical training. Its thinking would mature, it would understand events in their natural way, and within its ranks the genuine would be distinguished from the counterfeit. The shortcomings that existed in its organisation and training would be removed, and then a great store of experiences and events would be recorded for the coming ummah, a treasure so precious that its price could never be paid. That is, the worth of this lesson would be greater than even victory and triumph in that battle.

This struggle ended on the battlefield, and now the Qur'an has taken it onto its pages, and those pages form a field larger than the battlefield. Then this struggle began in the field of the human soul, and finally it extended into the field of the collective life of the Muslim community. In this way, Allah, by His power, shaped this community on the foundation of knowledge and wisdom, and in the light of analysis and insight. Then this community was prepared in accordance with what was Allah's will. In it lay the good of this community that it should suffer harm, that it should be subjected to trials, that it should be afflicted with calamity, and that it should be struck with grief and sorrow.

Regarding the events of this battle, the concluding remarks and commentary given here contain something that deserves attention and wonder: alongside the scenes and events of the battle, guidance about those events is also given at the very moment they occur, and together with that guidance, instruction is given which provides the means for the purification of the soul and the cleansing of the heart and sight. The thoughts of the Muslims are cleansed of dust and grime. Their ideas and conceptions are freed from the constraints of carnal desires. From the character of the Muslims, greed and avarice, malice and rancour, covetousness and miserliness, hidden desires, and sinfulness and wickedness are purified with great wisdom.

In these subsequent discussions and commentaries, especially in relation to the events of the battlefield, the matter of usury is also discussed, and the practice of usury is forbidden, though this may appear out of place. After that, the command is given that every important matter must be consulted upon and acted upon. Nevertheless, the consultation (shura) that took place regarding the Battle of Uhud and the decisions that were made did not produce good results on the surface, and the battle ended in defeat. This too is a matter of wonder (a detailed discussion will come later).

After this, the Qur'an, on this occasion, also discusses human psychology. It takes up various aspects of human life, and it weaves the discussions of the different aspects and movements of this life into one another. These diverse discussions appear complete in relation to one another, and at times they appear strange.

But those who are acquainted with this divine method of working are not surprised by the mixing of wide and varied discussions and by their intertwining with one another. This is because the movement of Islam has entered a struggle that is not merely a struggle of the battlefield, in which only weapons, horses and fighters, or at most military strategies and tactics, are needed. Rather, it is a wide and all-encompassing struggle, of which the battle on the field is only one part or one department. The real struggle is that great conflict which takes place in the world of the human conscience, and which was taking place at that time within the collective organisation of the community. The purpose of this struggle was to purify the human conscience, to make it pure and free, and to cleanse it of all the impurities that affect its clarity and purity, and which cause the human conscience to sit far away from nearness to Allah. Furthermore, this struggle was also connected with those organisational affairs on which the life of the Muslim community depended, in accordance with the Islamic system of life. This is the shura system, upon which the whole structure of collective life was raised. It is not only the system of government, but the entire Islamic system of life, which is founded on the principle of mutual cooperation, and in which an oppressive system such as usury is forbidden, because usury and mutual cooperation are two opposing principles.

Islam, in training the Muslim community, was not doing so merely from the point of view of a battle fought on a field. Rather, it was training the community in light of that great conflict which was taking place in a wider arena: in the field of the human soul, and in the field of man's practical life. When Islam turned its attention to riba (usury), it declared it forbidden. When it turned its attention to spending in the way of Allah, it encouraged people to do so, whether in prosperity or in adversity. It made obedience to Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ) necessary for receiving Allah's mercy. It commanded the suppression of anger and the practice of forgiveness and pardon. It commanded goodness and seeking forgiveness. It forbade persisting in sin and commanded repentance. And it declared all these matters to be causes of Allah's pleasure. It informed them that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had been sent to them out of compassion. It commanded that the principle of shura be upheld even in the most difficult circumstances, that the principle of shura be upheld. It commanded that uprightness be adopted in dealings and that dishonesty not be practised. It commanded that wealth be spent and that stinginess and miserliness be avoided. In short, these and other instructions were given during the commentary on the Battle of Uhud.

Islam gave attention to all these commands, because these are the elements through which the Muslim community was being prepared for a wider struggle and conflict, in which armed fighting on the battlefield was also included. But this struggle was not limited to fighting alone. Rather, it was a struggle of wider responsibilities, so that as a result a great revolutionary victory might be achieved. This great and complete victory would embrace the human soul, all its desires, every kind of its greed and covetousness, and all its malice and rancour. Furthermore, even in peaceful conditions, it would consist of a great victory for the Muslim community in the field of values and conduct.

Having given full attention to all these matters, Islam decided that the creation, formation and activities of the whole of humanity should be examined from the standpoint of the Islamic worldview, and that the whole of humanity should be made to revolve around one axis. What was that axis? That worship should be for Allah alone, and devotion should be for Allah alone. Human beings, with a full sense of responsibility and with the fear of Allah in their hearts, should turn towards their Lord. The manhaj (method and way) of Allah should prevail over this entire universe, and the whole of humanity should live in every situation in accordance with that same manhaj. The various conditions of human life should be connected and linked to the Islamic system of life, and all the results of human effort should also conform to the results of the Islamic manhaj. And every movement of the human soul, all organisations, and every detail of human order and administration should prove to be supportive and effective in bringing about those final results.

Therefore, in the midst of the commentary on the Battle of Uhud, many other subjects were also discussed, which are by no means out of place in relation to that struggle. This is because the human soul can never triumph in the battle of fighting unless it first triumphs over its own awareness, perception, habits and morals. As for those who turned their backs on the day of confrontation, the cause of their slip was that, because of certain weaknesses within them, Satan made their feet slip. (155) And those who, in the ideological struggles, were triumphant under the leadership of their prophets, were triumphant because before entering those battles they had already repented of their sins, and they advanced while beseeching Allah for success, and they entered the field of battle relying upon the firm support of Allah. Therefore, purity from sins, attachment to Allah, and reliance upon Allah are in reality the equipment through which help and victory are granted. For this reason these factors cannot be separated from the field of battle. Accordingly, abolishing the usury-based economic system and establishing a system of mutual cooperation (Co-operation) is also, as it were, one of the important causes among the causes of victory. Compared with a society based on usury, a society of mutual cooperation and mutual guarantee (takaful) is much closer to victory. Likewise, swallowing one's anger and pardoning mistakes is also an important weapon among the implements of war. Keeping one's ego-driven self (nafs ammarah) under control is also a kind of military training. A society in which people are economically mutual supports of one another, in which they have affection and love for one another, and in which they overlook one another's shortcomings, is also an active and effective force that guarantees victory.

Along with these factors, there were some further realities on which this lesson relies from beginning to end. For example, the importance of divine decree (taqdir) and the fact that what Allah has decreed must come to pass. Therefore, regarding whatever mistake occurred, one should firmly correct one's view of life and one's ideas, recognising that whatever happened occurred in accordance with the sunnah of Allah. Human activities and endeavours, the correct conduct of human beings and their mistakes, obedience to command and disobedience of human beings, firmly holding on to the Islamic manhaj and falling short in it, the results of all these are determined in accordance with the sunnah of Allah. All these manifestations of the sunnah of Allah emerge precisely from behind the veil of divine decree. All these are examples of the will (mashi'ah) of Allah, and whatever comes to pass is the settled decision of Allah. Therefore there is no need to grieve over them.

In conclusion, addressing the Muslim community, this point is put as follows: if you are granted victory, do not become arrogant, for it is not due to anything of your own. You are instruments of Allah's plan and His decree, and by bringing you into the field of jihad, Allah is displaying the examples of His power. Therefore the reward for all this striving rests with Allah alone, because you are doing Allah's work. You have no entitlement to any of the fruits of worldly victory, and victory is not obligatory for you. It is Allah who grants victory to whomever He wills, and He never grants it for worldly aims. Rather, He grants it for the lofty purposes that He desires. Likewise, when defeat falls to someone's lot, it too occurs in accordance with the Divine Way (sunnah ilahiyyah), and its real causes exist within the Muslim community in the form of weaknesses and shortcomings. Even in defeat, there is some wisdom hidden in Allah's knowledge, such as the purification of the community's souls, the separation of wrong people from its ranks, the exposure of realities and bitter realities, the strengthening of high values, the establishment of standards of good and evil, and the setting of examples and models for those who come later to take warning and learn lessons.

In the view of Islam, military success, political success, or economic success has no value unless it is founded upon the divine system of life, and unless the truth that Allah wishes to establish in people's lives is granted dominance. In that case, every victory would be a victory of Allah, and would be for the Islamic system of life. If this condition does not exist, then whatever victory is achieved will be a victory of jahiliyyah (ignorance and pre-Islamic disorder), won against another jahiliyyah. Such victory will benefit neither life nor humanity. Goodness would lie in the banners of goodness being raised solely for the sake of truth, and truth is one in its reality; it does not admit of multiplicity. It is the Islamic and divine way of life, and no other way has any right to exist alongside it.

The victory of the Islamic system of life is not possible until this victory first takes place in the field of the human soul, and then the truth is granted this victory in the practical life of the human being. When the human soul loses its self-regard within itself, eliminates greed and the desires of the self from itself, purifies itself from filth and rancor, completely breaks its bonds of appetite, and its gaze is directed only towards the Divine Being, and it becomes free from all the burdens and bonds in which it is held, in short, when it has striven with its full effort, and after its utmost exertion, it becomes free of its outward material strength, its material resources, and its apparent means, and begins to rely solely upon Allah, and when it makes decisions in all matters of its life in accordance with the command of Allah, and considers the establishment of this sovereignty of Allah the supreme aim of all its striving and victory and triumph, in short, when it has completed all these matters well, then its military success on the battlefield, its political success in any country, and its economic success will be considered true victory. Only then will its victory be a victory in the sight of Allah. Otherwise, it will in reality be considered one jahiliyyah's victory over another jahiliyyah. And in the sight of Allah, victory of this kind has neither value nor weight.

This is why, in the course of the commentary on the Battle of Badr, the matters mentioned above have also been discussed, which may appear incongruous at first glance. Diverse matters have been brought together, and in the conclusion and commentary on that battle, all these matters have been included. These matters have been brought into that wide field of battle, of which the field of Badr is one part, and of which Uhud is one of many aspects.
