Before we present the Qur'anic commentary on the events of the Battle of Uhud, it seems appropriate here to present the events of the Ghazwa (battle) of Uhud in the order in which they are narrated in the books of Sirah (biography of the Prophet), so that we may understand well the points on which Allah comments, and so that we may grasp what method of training Allah has adopted in the Qur'an while commenting on these events.

The situation was that the Muslims had been granted complete victory at Badr. This was an event which, given the circumstances in which it occurred, appeared as a very great miracle. Allah caused the standard-bearers of disbelief and the great chiefs to be beheaded at the hands of the people of Islam. Those who were killed were the chiefs of Quraysh.

After this, Abu Sufyan ibn Harb was appointed chief of Quraysh. Immediately upon being appointed chief, he began preparations to take revenge upon the Muslims. The caravan of Abu Sufyan had been the target of the Muslims at Badr, and it carried a considerable amount of Quraysh's trade goods. In that caravan, he had escaped. After Badr, the polytheists decided that all the trade goods of this caravan should be used as initial capital in the war against the Muslims.

Abu Sufyan assembled an army of three thousand men, composed of Quraysh, their allies, and Abyssinians. In the month of Shawwal, 3 AH, he set out with that army. These people brought their women with them as well, so that out of zeal for their protection they would not attempt to flee. He headed for Madinah and encamped near Mount Uhud.

On this occasion, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) consulted his companions. The question was whether he should go out and confront them or remain in Madinah. The personal opinion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was that the Muslims should not go out, but rather should fortify themselves within Madinah: the men would fight in its narrow lanes and at points of combat, and the women would take part in the battle from the rooftops of the houses. Along with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in this opinion was the chief of the hypocrites, Abdullah ibn Ubayy, who also agreed with him. Upon this, a large number of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) came forward, and among them the majority were young men who had not been able to take part in the battle of Badr. These people advised that we should go out and fight on the battlefield. They also insisted considerably on their advice. It became evident that the opinion of the majority of the community was this. He stood up, entered his chamber, the room of Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her), and returned wearing his armour. In the meantime, those people had changed their opinion. They thought: we have compelled the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to go out and fight without good reason. Now they submitted: "O Messenger of Allah, if you prefer to remain inside Madinah, let us do so." Upon this the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is not fitting for a Prophet that, once he has put on his armour, he should take it off until Allah decides between him and his enemy." Thus the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave them a prophetic lesson, and that lesson was that consultation (shura) has a set time, and when the time of consultation has passed and the time of resolve and determination has come, and the time for acting upon the settled decision has arrived, then one relies upon Allah alone. After that there is no room for hesitation. Consultation is not convened again, and opinions are not reconsidered. After consultation, matters reach their conclusion, and now the decision rests in Allah's hand, and He reveals whatever He wills.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had also seen in a dream that his sword had broken at one point and become blunt, that a cow was being slaughtered, and that he had put his hand into a strong coat of mail. He interpreted this dream thus: the blunting of the sword means that someone from my family will die; the slaughter of the cow he interpreted as meaning that some of his companions would be killed; and he took the meaning of the coat of mail to be Madinah. Therefore, after this dream, he was seeing with his own eyes the outcome of the Battle of Uhud. Yet despite this, he acted upon the method and decision of consultation, and furthermore, after consultation, he carried out the decisions through his own striving. This was because he was training a nation, and the training of nations takes place through events and occurrences. There is a long series of experiences, the essence of which emerges in the form of a few incidents. Moreover, through his decisions the decree of Allah was to be made manifest; those decisions upon which his understanding was firm, and upon which his heart was at peace. Thus he was acting in accordance with the decree of Allah. Yet despite this, his heart was feeling these events.

In any case, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out with a thousand Companions. To lead the prayers for those who had remained in Madinah, he appointed Ibn Umm Maktum. When he reached the area between Madinah and Mount Uhud, the chief of the hypocrites, Abdullah ibn Ubayy, withdrew with a third of that army. He said that they opposed him and listened to the words of the young men. Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Haram, the father of Jabir, pursued them, berated them severely, and insistently tried to persuade them to return. He called out to them: "Come and fight in the way of Allah, or at least defend." They replied: "If we were certain that you were fighting, we would not turn back." Upon this, Abdullah abused them severely and returned.

After this, some of the Ansar put forward a proposal at that moment: that help should be sought from the Jews, who are our allies. But the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) also rejected this proposal, because this battle was in reality a battle between disbelief and faith; the Jews had no interest in it, and victory and triumph lie in Allah's hand. This victory comes when one relies upon Allah and hearts become sincere for Him. He said: "Who are the people who will descend with us into the desert to confront these people?" Upon this, some of the Ansar went out with him, and he descended into the final part of the valley. He placed his back towards Mount Uhud and ordered the people not to begin fighting until he gave the command.

When morning came, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arranged an army of seven hundred men for battle. Of these, only fifty were cavalry. He appointed Abdullah ibn Jubayr as commander of fifty archers and ordered them to remain steadfast at the pass where he had assigned them, and not to leave that position under any circumstances, even if they saw birds tearing at the flesh of the army of Islam. These people were on the mountain behind the army. He said that these people should rain arrows upon the polytheists so that they would not attack the Muslims from behind.

He gave the banner to Ibn Umayr, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appointed Zubayr ibn al-Awwam on one side of the army, and on the other side he appointed Mus'ab ibn Umayr. On the day of Uhud, the young men offered themselves for battle. He inspected them and rejected those whom he found unfit to take part in the fighting. They were Abdullah ibn Amr, Usamah ibn Zayd, Usayd ibn Zuhayr, al-Bara ibn Azib, Zayd ibn Arqam, Zayd ibn Thabit, Arabah ibn Aws, and Amr ibn Hazm. Those who were declared fit were Samurah ibn Jundub and Rafi ibn Khadij. They were fifteen years old.

Quraysh prepared three thousand soldiers for battle. Of these, two hundred were cavalry. They appointed Khalid ibn al-Walid over the right wing and Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl over the left wing.

On this day, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave his sword to Abu Dujanah Simak ibn Kharashah, who was a hero who, in battle, displayed great pride and boastfulness.

The first of the polytheists to appear was Abu Amir the Fasiq. This Abu Amir was known by the title Rahib (the monk), but the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) named him Abu Amir al-Fasiq. In the Age of Jahiliyyah (ignorance), this man had been the chief of the tribe of Aws. When Islam came, he turned against Islam and openly began hostility towards the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He left Madinah, joined Quraysh, kept gathering them against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and kept inciting them to war against him. He would assure them that when his people saw him, they would accept his word and abandon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He was the first to come before the Muslims. He called out to his people, and when he introduced himself, they replied: "O Fasiq, may Allah not give you eyes." Upon this he replied that after him his people had been destroyed. After that he fought fiercely against the Muslims.

When the battle began, Abu Dujanah displayed his valour. Alongside him, Talhah ibn Ubaydullah, Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nadr ibn Anas and Sa'd ibn Zubayr performed notable deeds. As the day rose, the Muslims defeated the disbelievers. Of them, they killed seventy brave and notable men, and the rest of the enemies of Allah fled in defeat; they reached the camp, where the women were. The women gathered up their garments and began to flee.

When the archers saw that the disbelievers had been defeated and had fled, they abandoned the positions where the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had stationed them, and where he had commanded them never to leave. These people called out to one another that the spoils were being plundered, O people! Their leader reminded them of the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), but they paid no heed. They thought that the polytheists would not return, so these people too fell upon the spoils and vacated the pass.

Khalid ibn al-Walid learned that the pass had been vacated by the archers, so he attacked with the polytheists' cavalry by way of the pass. He saw that the route was empty. Thus Khalid's military stratagem succeeded, and he fell upon the Muslims from behind. When the polytheists and the defeated army saw that Khalid had fallen upon the Muslims, they surrounded them from the front.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 3, verse 121 (part 3 of 3):

Now the whole situation of that battle changed completely; the battlefield turned against the Muslims. Confusion spread through the ranks of the Muslims, restlessness seized the people, and they became extremely frightened. This was because Khalid's attack was so terrifying and so sudden that no one had expected it. Many people were killed, and among the Muslims those whose fate had been written as martyrdom were martyred. Now the polytheists got the opportunity to reach the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He had been left alone; so few people remained to protect him that they could be counted on the fingers. They defended the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and were martyred. The blessed face of the Noble Messenger (ﷺ) was wounded; his lower jaw and a blessed tooth were injured, and the helmet on his head broke into pieces. The polytheists struck him with stones, until he fell on one side.
After this, he fell into a pit which Abu 'Amir al-Fasiq had dug and covered from above so that the Muslims would fall into it, and the rings of his armour had sunk into the blessed face of the Messenger (ﷺ). In the midst of this terrible situation, someone called out that Muhammad (ﷺ) had been martyred. So this dreadful cry destroyed whatever strength remained to them. Therefore the remaining Muslims fled, and on hearing the news of the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) death, they became so despairing and so downcast that their strength gave way. Now they dismissed the thought of fighting from their hearts.
All the people fled, except Anas ibn an-Nadr, who did not flee. He came to Umar ibn al-Khattab and Talhah ibn 'Ubaydullah, who were sitting with some of the Muhajirun and Ansar. They had let their hands hang down, and he said: "Why are you sitting here?" They said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has been martyred." He said: "Then what will you do, living after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)? Arise, and give your life for the same cause for which the Noble Messenger (ﷺ) gave his life." Then Anas ibn an-Nadr charged upon the disbelievers. At that time he met Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, and he called out to him: "Sa'd, I feel the fragrance of Paradise from beyond Uhud." Then he fought fiercely until he was martyred. There were more than seventy wounds on his body, and no one could even recognise him. Finally, his body was identified by his sister through his fingertips.
Now the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned towards the Muslims. The first to recognise him from beneath the helmet was Sa'id ibn Malik. He raised a loud cry: "O assembly of Muslims! Glad tidings, glad tidings, this is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gestured with his hand: "Be silent." The Muslims gathered around him, and they climbed the mountain pass with him. Among them were Abu Bakr, Umar, al-Harith ibn as-Summah al-Ansari and others. When they had climbed well up the mountain, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) met Ubayy ibn Khalaf. He was mounted on his horse named 'Awd. He used to say, while feeding that horse in Makkah: "On it I will kill Muhammad." When the Noble Messenger (ﷺ) was informed of this, he said: "If Allah wills, I will kill him." When the Messenger (ﷺ) came upon him, al-Harith took a spear and struck the enemy of Allah on the upper collarbone (collar bone) of his chest. He fled, roaring like a bull. He became certain that he had been killed, just as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had prophesied. Before returning, he died on the road.
On this occasion Abu Sufyan came up onto the mountain and called out: "Is Muhammad among you?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not answer him." Then he said: "Is Abu Bakr among you?" Still the Muslims did not answer. "Is Umar ibn al-Khattab among you?" Still no answer was given to him. He had asked only about these three. Upon this, he said to his people: "As for these three men, you have already finished them off." At this, Umar (ra) could not contain himself and said: "O enemy of Allah! Those you have mentioned are all alive. Allah has preserved for you those whom you would not like." Then he said: "Some people have mutilated the bodies of the martyrs. I had not ordered them to do so, but I did not disapprove of their action." (This was a reference to the incident in which his wife Hind did to the body of Hamzah. When the Abyssinian killed him, Hind slit open his stomach, took out his liver, chewed it, and then threw it away.)
After this he raised the slogan: "Uʿlu Hubal... (Let Hubal be exalted)." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You are not answering him." The Companions said: "What should we answer?" He (ﷺ) said: "Say: Allah is most high and most majestic... (Allahu a'la wa ajall)." Then he said: "We have al-'Uzza, and you have no 'Uzza." Again the Messenger (ﷺ) said: "You are not answering him." The Companions asked: "O Messenger of Allah, what should we say?" He said: "Say: Allah is our Master, and you have no master (Allahu mawlana wa la mawla lakum)." Upon this Abu Sufyan said: "Today is in exchange for Badr, and in war there are ups and downs." Umar (ra) then said: "There is no equality. Our slain are in Paradise and your slain are in Hellfire."
When this battle ended, the polytheists returned. Some Muslims suspected that they might go to Madinah, take women as captives and plunder. This weighed very heavily upon them. The Noble Messenger (ﷺ) said: "Ali! Go out, follow them and see what they do and what they intend. If they have left the horses aside and loaded their goods on camels, then they are heading for Makkah; but if they have driven the camels and mounted the horses, know that they intend to march upon Madinah. By Allah, in whose hand is my soul, if they intend Madinah, I will surely go towards them and fight them in Madinah."
Ali (ra) said: "I went out and followed them, to see what they did. They left the horses and mounted the camels. When they had travelled some distance, they reproached one another. They said: 'You have achieved nothing. You destroyed their strength but you left them. Some of their leaders remain who will gather against you again. So return from here and uproot them completely.'" This matter reached the Noble Messenger (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made an announcement in Madinah and ordered that they set out and overtake the enemy on the road. "Now only the one who was present at Uhud may go with us." Abdullah ibn Ubayy requested the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "I will go with you." He (ﷺ) said: "No." The Muslims, even in that dreadful situation, answered the call of the Messenger (ﷺ), although they were covered with wounds. They said: "We have heard and we obey." Jabir ibn Abdullah sought permission and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I wish to remain with you in every place, but on the day of Uhud my father stopped me so that I would stay to protect my sisters." Upon this, the Prophet (ﷺ) granted him special permission to accompany him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims set out from Madinah and reached Hamra' al-Asad. Here Ma'bad ibn Abi Ma'bad al-Khuza'i came to meet him. He had become a Muslim, but Abu Sufyan did not know of his Islam. The Messenger (ﷺ) told him to meet Abu Sufyan and frighten him. He met him at Ruha'. Abu Sufyan did not know that he had become a Muslim. "Ma'bad, who is coming behind you?" Abu Sufyan asked. He replied: "Muhammad and his companions are coming. They are angry with you, and they are coming with a force greater than any they ever set out with. Those companions of Muhammad who did not take part in that battle have become regretful." Upon this, Abu Sufyan said: "What is your opinion?" He said: "I cannot say that you should not depart before that army emerges from behind that hill." Upon this Abu Sufyan said: "We have decided to test our strength against them once more and uproot them completely." Upon this Ma'bad said: "Do not do such a thing; I am your sincere well-wisher." Upon this they returned to Makkah.
On the way, Abu Sufyan met some polytheists who were going to Madinah. Abu Sufyan said: "Will you convey my message to Muhammad? If you do so, I will host you and your horses in my place when you come to Makkah." Those who were going said: "Yes, we will convey it." Then Abu Sufyan said: "Tell Muhammad that we have decided to fight once more, so that we may uproot you and your companions." When this news reached Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Muslims, they said: "Hasbuna Allahu wa ni'mal wakil (Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best disposer of affairs)." This message had no effect upon them. The Muslims stayed there for three days, waiting for Abu Sufyan; then they learned that the polytheists had gone very far along their road, so the Muslims returned to Madinah.
(Due to its great length, the complete commentary on this verse could not be included. We apologise for this. Please read the remainder of the commentary of this verse in Fi Zilal al-Quran, volume ...)

Who were these two groups? In the Sahihayn, a hadith from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah is related on this matter: they were the Banu Harithah and the Banu Salamah. They had been affected by the treacherous conduct of 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy, and so that conduct had created turmoil in the ranks of the Muslims at the very first step. The two groups were close to showing cowardice and sitting down weakened, but Allah's help arrived and Allah made their feet firm, as the verse makes clear: ﴿And Allah was their protector﴾.

Hadrat 'Umar said: I heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah say, "This verse was revealed concerning us: ﴿When two groups among you were about to lose heart﴾." He said, "The two groups were us, the Banu Harithah and the Banu Salamah, and I would not wish (or it is not pleasing to me) that the verse had not been revealed, because in it Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And Allah was their protector﴾," meaning Allah is their friend and helper. (Bukhari and Muslim)

Thus Allah brings out into the open what is hidden and concealed in the depths of hearts, and only Allah knew that these tribes were inclined toward cowardice. This weakness had entered their hearts for a moment, and immediately Allah saved them from falling. He removed that weakness from their hearts, and by His friendship He supported them, so they advanced rather than turning back. In relating the events of that battle, Allah repeated them so that the events and scenes of that battle might be presented in a living and luminous form, and so that the thoughts that trouble human souls might be placed on record, and people might be given the awareness that Allah is with them and is aware of the matters of their hearts. For this reason Allah said: ﴿And Allah is Hearing and Knowing﴾, so that this reality may firmly settle in their hearts, they may be shown the path of salvation, and it may be impressed upon their sense that Allah is their helper, supporter and friend, and the one who holds their hand in any weakness. When they are about to fall, He is their supporter. This was said so that they would know from where to seek help and where to take refuge in times of weakness and frailty. Therefore they are directed toward that direction, beyond which there is no other direction for Muslims.

﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾.

In short, these two glimpses in the opening scene are shown most appropriately and in a fitting atmosphere; the glimpses combine their musical rise and fall, and appear before the eyes with their symbolic character at the most suitable moment, in an environment where people's hearts are ready to respond, be affected, and accept these truths. From these two introductory verses it becomes clear how the Qur'an revives hearts, trains them, and directs them to the right course, and how commentary is attached to events while they are still fresh. Thus the difference becomes evident between the manner in which the Qur'an narrates stories and relates events, and the manner adopted in ordinary human historical sources. Although human sources contain a great deal of detail about events, despite those details the events do not penetrate hearts, nor do they have any connection with human life, nor is the aim to revive hearts and give them warmth, nor is the guidance and training of people intended, as the Holy Qur'an keeps these matters in view in its narration of stories, and it is a most firmly established style of expression.

Thus begins the account of that battle in which the Muslims did not attain victory, although they had come close to victory and success. The account begins in this way: a man ('Abdullah ibn Ubayy) gives preference to his own self and personality over his system of life, and in following him all those people follow behind him whose personal considerations were more important to them than their creed. Then at the very beginning two groups are also somewhat affected by the circumstances, although they were righteous, and the outcome of that battle turns out such that some people abandon their military duty and become caught up in greed for the spoils of war, and because of them those who had shown the highest examples of sacrifice in that battle also suffer defeat, merely because some people violated discipline or because some weaknesses still remained in their system of life.

Before the details of that battle are described and commented upon, in which the Muslims suffered defeat, the battle in which the Muslims attained victory is mentioned, namely the Battle of Badr, so that along with this defeat they keep that victory and success in view, and by comparing the two they reflect upon the causes of victory and defeat. And they should also know with certainty that victory and success are in the hands of Allah, and that what happens is what has been decreed with Allah. Just as the divine decree operates in victory, so too defeat is decreed. Wisdom lies beneath victory, and the wisdom of Allah operates behind defeat as well, and in both conditions the final outcome is in the hands of Allah; in every state He is the One who is the Causer of causes.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 3, verse 123:

The victory that the Muslims attained at Badr was miraculous, as we have stated above. This victory was achieved despite the scarcity of material means. At that time the Muslims did not have the well-known material means. In this battle, the two pans of the scale, namely the believers and the polytheists, were not balanced, nor was their condition such that they were close to balance. The polytheists numbered one thousand, and they had set out for battle as a general mobilisation, because Abu Sufyan had sought their help, and their objective was also defined: to protect Abu Sufyan's caravan. These thousand men were equipped with every kind of military equipment. They had set out to protect their wealth. Besides this, they also had to protect their honour and dignity. In contrast, the Muslims were only three percent, and they had not set out expecting to encounter such a great army equipped with weapons; they had set out for a light and easy undertaking. They had set out to lay hands on an unarmed caravan, and they wished to seize it. Along with their small number, they did not even have equipment. Behind them in Medina, the polytheists were still present and were still powerful in their own place. Likewise, a large section of the hypocrites was present in Medina, and they held a high position in Medinan society. Besides this, there were Jews in Medina who were always on the lookout to strike at the Muslims in Medina. Moreover, they were a small group of Muslims surrounded within the Arabian Peninsula by a great power of disbelief and polytheism. And apart from all these factors, they were still oppressed refugees who had been expelled from Mecca, and there were some Ansar who had given shelter to these Muhajirun. In any case, their status in that society was that of a tender sapling.

By mentioning these circumstances, Allah explains that in such circumstances the true cause of so great a victory is solely the help of Allah.

﴿And Allah had already helped you at Badr when you were weak. So be mindful of Allah, that perhaps you will be grateful.﴾ Before this, Allah had already helped you at the Battle of Badr, although at that time you were very weak. Therefore, you should avoid ingratitude towards Allah. It is hoped that you will now be grateful.

Only Allah granted them help, and He granted it for a wisdom which is explained in these verses. Neither they themselves nor anyone else was their helper or supporter. Therefore, if they must fear anyone and be apprehensive of anyone, they should fear only Allah and cultivate His fear within themselves, because victory and defeat are in His hand. He is the one who is the source of authority and power. It is only the fear of Allah that can incline them to gratitude. In every state, the favours and bounties of Allah that are continuously bestowed upon them place upon them an obligation to thank Allah fully, in a manner worthy of those favours and bounties.

This is a glimpse, in which they are reminded how victory at Badr was granted to them. Then the scenes that took place on the field of Badr are presented; these scenes are recalled to their minds afresh, as though they had only just happened. Look:

﴿When you said to the believers: "Is it not enough for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?"﴾ ... "Remember when you were saying to the believers: 'Is it not sufficient for you that your Lord should aid you with three thousand angels sent down?' Indeed, if you are patient and fear Allah, and they come upon you suddenly, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels bearing marks."

These words were uttered by the Messenger (ﷺ) on the day of Badr, and were said to that handful of believers who had set out with him, who had seen the army of the polytheists. This handful of Muslims had set out only to intercept the caravan, which carried trade goods; it had not even crossed their minds that they would face an army equipped with weapons and provisions. On that day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) informed them of the matters of which Allah had informed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so that their hearts would be strengthened and they would remain steadfast. They were, after all, human beings, and they needed help that was within the grasp of their thoughts and understanding, and in a form to which they were accustomed in receiving assistance. They were also told that this special help from Allah was conditional upon two requirements: first, that you exercise patience and adopt the attitude of God-fearing piety. Patience is necessary because when an attack comes, there is need for patience in the face of the shocks of the attack; and taqwa (God-consciousness) is that which connects a person's bond with Allah, whether the outcome is victory or defeat.

Here, the Qur'an teaches them that ultimately all matters return to Allah, and that in all things and events the real factor is the Being of Allah. The sending down of the angels is good news for the believers, so that their hearts may be content, they may remain steadfast, and they may attain tranquility and peace. As for victory, it comes directly from Allah; it is connected with Allah's power and His will, without any intermediary, without any means, and without any cause.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 126:

The Qur'an has placed great emphasis on the governance of the Divine Will (mashi'ah ilahi) in the Islamic conception of life. It has striven to purge it of every doubt and suspicion, and it has repeatedly mentioned that worldly causes are never effective in any circumstance. Between the power of Allah and the heart and mind of the believer, a special connection is established. The veils that stand between Allah and His servant are lifted. A direct relationship is established between Allah and the servant, and this relationship is never obstructed, just as it is in the world of existence and the world of realities.

These guidances are repeated again and again in the Qur'an. They are emphasized in various styles, and this truth settles deeply in the hearts of the Muslims. They possess a wonderful, profound, luminous and serious awareness of this truth. They know that Allah alone is the agent and the effective one in all the affairs of this universe. They also feel that they are commanded by Allah to provide the means and resources, to strive, and to exert their utmost effort in every matter. Yet they also have a firm awareness of this truth: that what will happen is what the Divine Will desires. Along with this firm conviction, they obey, and with conscious balance they remain active at all times. Despite this, the Qur'an instilled this awareness in the thinking of the Muslims only after a period of time. Certain events occurred, these events trained the Muslims, lessons were drawn from these events, and in this surah there are many examples of such training.

In these verses, the scene of Badr is before our eyes. In this scene, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) promises the believers that a special help will be sent down from Allah, on the condition that they act with patience and steadfastness, and in the battle, instead of fearing people, they adopt only the path of taqwa (God-consciousness) and fear of Allah. Precisely at the moment when they face the disbelievers, after this, the Qur'an, going even into the background of the descent of the angels, makes clear that the real effective power is the Divine Being. All affairs are in His hand and subject to His will, and victory and support will be granted only by His permission and His will. ﴿وَمَا النَّصْرُ إِلَّا مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ﴾ "And victory is only from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise." He is the Mighty, the Possessor of authority, and He is capable of granting help and victory. And along with this, He is also the Wise, and His power operates in accordance with His wisdom. And He grants victory because His wisdom is hidden within it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 127:

After this, the wisdom behind this victory is also explained here. What kind of victory? A victory none of whose aims are connected with the self of a human being.

It is a fact that victory comes from Allah. It manifests the decree of Allah. In the case of victory, a Messenger and his companions gain no personal benefit. Nor is there any personal purpose in it for them. Furthermore, in achieving victory, the Messenger has no role, nor do those with him have any role in it. Rather, they are a means for the manifestation of the divine decree. Divine power uses them in whatever way it wills. They are neither the true cause of this victory and help, nor its makers. They are neither the conquerors, nor do they obtain worldly gains as a result of this victory. The hand of divine power sets certain individuals in motion, and then itself supports them, so that the wisdoms that are with Allah may be manifested and the purposes He intends may be brought into effect.

﴿Liyaqta'a tarafan minal-ladhina kafaru﴾ ("that He might cut off a part of those who disbelieve"). They are killed, their manpower is reduced, their lands pass out of their hands, and their territory keeps shrinking. Or the circle of their oppressive rule is narrowed. Their wealth is diminished by the loss of war booty, and as a result of defeat and rout their activities are reduced.

﴿Aw yakbitahum fayanqalibu kha'ibin﴾ ("or He might disgrace them, so that they return frustrated"). That is, they suffer humiliating defeat, and they return failed in their aims, subdued.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 128:

أَوْ يَتُوبَ عَلَيْهِمْ……………"or He may turn to them in forgiveness." This is because at times, as a result of the victory of the Muslims, the disbelievers take a lesson and learn, and as a result of that victory they accept Islam; consequently Allah forgives them. The quality of disbelief departs from them, and having found the path of guidance, they remain steadfast in Islam.

أَوْ يُعَذِّبَهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ ظَالِمُونَ……………"or He may punish them, for they are wrongdoers." One form of punishment is that the people of Islam overcome them. Another form is that, when they are taken captive, they suffer punishment, or they end their lives in disbelief and ultimately become deserving of the punishment of Hell. This punishment is given to them because they commit wrongdoing by disbelieving, put the Muslims into trial, and commit mischief on earth. Moreover, by standing against this reformative system of life, which has come to be implemented in the world in the form of the Islamic way of life and the Islamic Shari'ah, they commit wrongdoing. In short, all the oppressions that come into existence because of disbelief, and because of which the way of Allah is obstructed, are included in this.

Nevertheless, all this programme takes place under the wisdom of Allah, and human will has no part in it. Even the Messenger of Allah ﷺ himself, according to this verse, is excluded from interfering in this programme, and the authority to decide these matters is exclusively vested in the Being of Allah. This is because such decisions befit the Divine Being. In them the Divine Being is unique and has no partner.

Thus the being of the believers steps back from the scene of victory and triumph. They themselves go out of the sphere of the causes of victory and have no part in its outcomes. In this way they are protected from the pride that generally arises in the hearts of conquerors, and they are also safeguarded from harshness, arrogance and the sense of superiority, due to which most conquerors become unable to contain themselves, and their spirit and conduct become unbalanced. Therefore, the believers feel that the powers of decision are not in their hands; all powers belong entirely to Allah.

In short, whether people are obedient or disobedient, the affairs of all of them belong to Allah Almighty. The decisions about people's destinies, whether they are good or bad, Allah has kept in His own hand. This is the reality of the Islamic movement, and this is the place of people in it, whether they are good or bad. In this field, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the believers' task is only this: to carry out their duties in a good manner, and to leave the results to Allah. They should seek reward from Allah alone for their deeds; He will give them their full reward and will be their Guardian and Helper.

The verse "you have no part in the decision" has also been brought here because, in the coming verses, the statement of some people is quoted: هَلْ لَنَا مِنَ الأمْرِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ……………"Do we have any share in the affair?" (3:154), and: لَوْ كَانَ لَنَا مِنَ الأمْرِ شَيْءٌ مَا قُتِلْنَا هَا هُنَا……………"If we had any share in the affair, we would not have been killed here." (3:157). This verse is in fact an advance answer to these assumptions: yes, there is no partner in the powers of Divinity; victory is not in anyone's control, nor is defeat. Your task is only obedience to the command, the performance of duty, and complete loyalty. These are the things required of you. As for what outcomes follow after them, that is the work of Allah Almighty; no one has any part in it. This includes even the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. This is the true reality that should be before the Islamic conception of life, should take root in the depths of the human self, and should be higher and more exalted than events, circumstances and the agents of action.

This reminder of the Battle of Badr and the conclusion of these fundamental truths of the Islamic conception of life ends with the expression of the general reality that, ultimately, both victory and defeat are subject to the power and wise policy of Allah Almighty. And here, at the close of this discussion, an even more general reality is brought forward: that the command of Allah operates throughout this entire universe. Therefore, He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 129:

The point is that these matters are subject to the will of Allah, which is unrestricted and is bound up with His unrestricted sovereignty. He disposes of the affairs of His servants without restraint, just as He is the sole Owner of the heavens and the earth, with no partner. He does not oppress His servants, nor does He show partiality toward any of them, neither in forgiveness nor in punishment. He judges between His servants with wisdom and justice, and alongside wisdom and justice His attributes of mercy and pardon also play their part, for pardon and forgiveness are what befit Him.

﴿وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ "And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." The doors are open for His servants: they can benefit from His mercy and forgiveness at all times, and they can return and repent at all times, because all affairs are in His hand. His imposing obligations, the fulfilment of those obligations, and the leaving aside of matters beyond those obligations are due to His wisdom and His will, which is not bound by any restriction. His wisdom and will operate behind causes and means.

Before the context moves on to narrate the central events of the Battle of Uhud, recording their outcomes and mentioning their details, guidance is being given here concerning that great battle, which we mentioned at the beginning of this discussion. That great battle was fought on the field of human psychology and continues across the whole surface of human life. In this connection, there is talk here of usury and the business of interest. Here, there is talk of the fear of Allah, obedience to Allah and obedience to His Messenger. It is commanded that charity in the way of Allah be practised in every period, whether of ease or of hardship. Reference is made to the noble system of mutual assistance in the Islamic economic system and, in contrast to it, the accursed economic system of interest; to the restraining of anger; to pardoning and forgiving people; to the spreading of goodness within the community of Muslims; and to seeking forgiveness for sins and not persisting in errors and shortcomings.

This is the whole of Sayyid Qutb's commentary on verses 130–131, so I have translated the passage as given. Quranic quotations here are limited to fragments of the verses; where they appear, they are rendered as the commentary quotes them.

All these instructions are given here at the very moment when the discussion of the military battle is about to begin in the context of the speech. Through them, the aim is to point to one of the important features of the Islamic worldview. The Islamic worldview looks at the human personality and its activities from a comprehensive perspective, and it turns the human being and his striving around one single axis. That axis is this: that in his whole life the human being must obey and worship Allah, alone, without partner. In every matter he must turn to Him alone. And the Islamic system of life alone must cover the whole of life, must dominate every condition and every circumstance of the human personality, and must be implemented in every aspect of human life. After this, these instructions point to the connection that exists amid the variety of human life, and the effects of this connection on the final outcomes of human endeavour are also explained, as we have already stated earlier.

The Islamic system of life takes hold of every aspect of the human self; it organises the life of the Muslim community completely. It does not make decisions by dividing it into pieces. Therefore it prepares equipment for the battlefield and also creates the capacity for war within the individuals who carry out the work. It purifies the hearts of the believers as well. It purifies their minds, and it creates within the human being such moral strength that they are able to gain control over the desires of the self and the physical appetites. Love and affability are cultivated within the Muslim community, and all these qualities are interlinked. When we discuss all these characteristics in detail and comment on each of these instructions, it will become clear that all the qualities and instructions have a deep connection with the practical life of the Muslim community. And these qualities are linked with the destiny of the Muslim community both on the battlefield and in the field of life.

The discussion of interest and the interest-based economic system has been explained in detail in Fi Zilal al-Quran, Part Three. Therefore we do not consider it appropriate to repeat that whole discussion here. However, it will be appropriate to reflect here on the words ضعافاً مضاعفة (multiplied manifold). This is because some people of our time take shelter behind these words and express the meaning that what has been prohibited is ضعافاً مضاعفة (multiplied manifold). As for interest that is four percent, five percent, seven percent or nine percent, they say it is not ضعافاً مضاعفة (multiplied manifold), and therefore it is not prohibited.

In refutation of this, it is sufficient to say only this: the qualifier ضعافاً مضاعفة (multiplied manifold) in fact expresses the actual situation that existed at the time of the revelation of the Quran; this qualifier does not restrict or condition the ruling. The verse that occurs in Surah al-Baqarah is definitive, and it declares every form of riba to be prohibited. Therefore there is no qualification or limit in it. There the words are not وَذَرُوا مَا بَقِيَ مِنَ الرِّبَا……………("leave what remains of riba"), whatever rate of interest that interest may be.

After this discussion of principle, we will now explain why the qualifier ضعافاً مضاعفة (multiplied manifold) has been attached to riba. Simply, this attribute points to the history of the interest-based system, in which interest transactions were conducted at rates that doubled and quadrupled. Rather, it shows that whatever the rate of interest, this attribute of ضعافاً مضاعفة (multiplied manifold) is an inseparable attribute of the destructive system of interest.

The summary of the interest-based system is that the circulation of all wealth in a society begins according to this system; therefore the activities in interest-based dealings are not simple activities like simple interest. One aspect of this circulation is that in this system the transfer of money keeps happening repeatedly, so that it turns into compound interest; therefore, because of the repeated charging of interest, the amount of interest eventually multiplies many times over, and it inevitably becomes ضعافاً مضاعفة (multiplied manifold). Thus, by its very nature, wealth in the interest-based system keeps growing twofold and fourfold. Therefore the application of ضعافاً مضاعفة (multiplied manifold) is not confined to the situation that was prevalent in Arab society at the time of the revelation of the Quran, but in every age, every kind of interest-based system has this property: that it keeps multiplying two and four times.

And, as we have given details in the third part, a feature of this system is also that it completely corrupts people's psychology and morals. Moreover, this system also completely damages the economic and political condition of the country. Therefore the effects of the interest-based system fall upon the collective life of the Ummah, and it has consequences for the destiny of the Ummah, as we have mentioned in the third part.

At the time when Islam was creating the Muslim Ummah, it was also laying the foundation of a moral and psychological system of life for this Ummah; it was also building the political and economic life of this new Ummah on healthy principles. In this connection, this new Ummah faced battles, and the effects that followed are well-known and famous events of Islamic history. Therefore the sudden mention of the prohibition of riba in the midst of narratives of battle is also understandable, because the Islamic system of life is a comprehensive and wise system. Moreover, after the prohibition of riba, the saying that fear Allah and hope that mercy will be shown to you, and then the saying that protect yourselves from the fire that has been prepared for the disbelievers, are also understandable from this point of view.

The meaning is that whoever fears Allah and has the fear of Allah in his heart will never be able to consume interest; likewise, the person in whose heart is the fear of the torment of Hell will also never be able to be an interest-eater. In other words, whoever has faith and wishes to remove himself from the line of the disbelievers can never be an interest-eater. Faith is not merely the name of empty words; rather its requirement is also that, for the establishment of the Islamic system of life and for colouring the whole of life in the colour of Islam, faith has been appointed as the vanguard.

It is impossible that faith and the interest-based system should come together in one place. Wherever the interest-based system is established, that society will be regarded as wholly excluded from the religion of Islam, and its end will be in that fire which has truly been prepared for the disbelievers. Whatever discussion is made on this matter will be an unnecessary discussion, because in this verse the prohibition of interest-based dealings has first been stated. After that, the believers have been invited to fear Allah, to act upon this command, and to protect themselves from the fire that has been prepared for the disbelievers. This theme has not been brought in this manner without purpose, nor has it been stated this way by accident. All these instructions are purposeful, have been brought as emphasis, and the intention is to fix this reality in the minds of the Muslims in exactly this sense.

They have been given the hope that if they abandon interest-based dealings, they may hope to succeed, because success can be obtained only as a result of the piety of Allah. The natural outcome of piety is success. And success is so that the Islamic system is established in human life. In Part Three we have explained in detail how this ill-omened interest-based system has destroyed human societies, and what kinds of calamities it has kept the whole of humanity afflicted with. It is appropriate to bring the discussions given in Part Three back to mind once more, so that we may know what the concept of success is from the Islamic point of view, and how success depends upon our uprooting this wicked interest-based system from its foundations.

Therefore we do not consider it appropriate to repeat that whole discussion here. However, it will be appropriate to reflect here on the words ضعافاً مضاعفة (multiplied manifold). This is because some people of our time take shelter behind these words and express the meaning that what has been prohibited is ضعافاً مضاعفة (multiplied manifold). As for interest that is four percent, five percent, seven percent or nine percent, they say it is not ضعافاً مضاعفة (multiplied manifold), and therefore it is not prohibited.

In refutation of this, it is sufficient to say only this: the qualifier ضعافاً مضاعفة (multiplied manifold) in fact expresses the actual situation that existed at the time of the revelation of the Quran; this qualifier does not restrict or condition the ruling. The verse that occurs in Surah al-Baqarah is definitive, and it declares every form of riba to be prohibited. Therefore there is no qualification or limit in it. There the words are not وَذَرُوا مَا بَقِيَ مِنَ الرِّبَا……………("leave what remains of riba"), whatever rate of interest that interest may be.

After this discussion of principle, we will now explain why the qualifier ضعافاً مضاعفة (multiplied manifold) has been attached to riba. Simply, this attribute points to the history of the interest-based system, in which interest transactions were conducted at rates that doubled and quadrupled. Rather, it shows that whatever the rate of interest, this attribute of ضعافاً مضاعفة (multiplied manifold) is an inseparable attribute of the destructive system of interest.

The summary of the interest-based system is that the circulation of all wealth in a society begins according to this system; therefore the activities in interest-based dealings are not simple activities like simple interest. One aspect of this circulation is that in this system the transfer of money keeps happening repeatedly, so that it turns into compound interest; therefore, because of the repeated charging of interest, the amount of interest eventually multiplies many times over, and it inevitably becomes ضعافاً مضاعفة (multiplied manifold). Thus, by its very nature, wealth in the interest-based system keeps growing twofold and fourfold. Therefore the application of ضعافاً مضاعفة (multiplied manifold) is not confined to the situation that was prevalent in Arab society at the time of the revelation of the Quran, but in every age, every kind of interest-based system has this property: that it keeps multiplying two and four times.

And, as we have given details in the third part, a feature of this system is also that it completely corrupts people's psychology and morals. Moreover, this system also completely damages the economic and political condition of the country. Therefore the effects of the interest-based system fall upon the collective life of the Ummah, and it has consequences for the destiny of the Ummah, as we have mentioned in the third part.

At the time when Islam was creating the Muslim Ummah, it was also laying the foundation of a moral and psychological system of life for this Ummah; it was also building the political and economic life of this new Ummah on healthy principles. In this connection, this new Ummah faced battles, and the effects that followed are well-known and famous events of Islamic history. Therefore the sudden mention of the prohibition of riba in the midst of narratives of battle is also understandable, because the Islamic system of life is a comprehensive and wise system. Moreover, after the prohibition of riba, the saying that fear Allah and hope that mercy will be shown to you, and then the saying that protect yourselves from the fire that has been prepared for the disbelievers, are also understandable from this point of view.

The meaning is that whoever fears Allah and has the fear of Allah in his heart will never be able to consume interest; likewise, the person in whose heart is the fear of the torment of Hell will also never be able to be an interest-eater. In other words, whoever has faith and wishes to remove himself from the line of the disbelievers can never be an interest-eater. Faith is not merely the name of empty words; rather its requirement is also that, for the establishment of the Islamic system of life and for colouring the whole of life in the colour of Islam, faith has been appointed as the vanguard.

It is impossible that faith and the interest-based system should come together in one place. Wherever the interest-based system is established, that society will be regarded as wholly excluded from the religion of Islam, and its end will be in that fire which has truly been prepared for the disbelievers. Whatever discussion is made on this matter will be an unnecessary discussion, because in this verse the prohibition of interest-based dealings has first been stated. After that, the believers have been invited to fear Allah, to act upon this command, and to protect themselves from the fire that has been prepared for the disbelievers. This theme has not been brought in this manner without purpose, nor has it been stated this way by accident. All these instructions are purposeful, have been brought as emphasis, and the intention is to fix this reality in the minds of the Muslims in exactly this sense.

They have been given the hope that if they abandon interest-based dealings, they may hope to succeed, because success can be obtained only as a result of the piety of Allah. The natural outcome of piety is success. And success is so that the Islamic system is established in human life. In Part Three we have explained in detail how this ill-omened interest-based system has destroyed human societies, and what kinds of calamities it has kept the whole of humanity afflicted with. It is appropriate to bring the discussions given in Part Three back to mind once more, so that we may know what the concept of success is from the Islamic point of view, and how success depends upon our uprooting this wicked interest-based system from its foundations.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 132:

After this, a final emphasis is given: ﴿And obey Allah and the Messenger, that you may receive mercy.﴾ "And obey Allah and obey the Messenger, so that there may be hope of mercy upon you." This is a general command to obey Allah and the Messenger, and the mercy of Allah is made dependent upon this general obedience. However, after the prohibition of usurious dealings, the mention of this divine mercy as a consequence is not devoid of wisdom. It also intends a particular meaning and allusion. That is, in a society whose economy is founded upon the usurious system, obedience to Allah and His Messenger becomes absolutely impossible. Moreover, the heart that consumes interest, in whatever form and in whatever manner it may be, does not retain the spirit of obedience to Allah and obedience to the Messenger. Thus this consequence and sequel to the prohibition of riba is also a kind of further emphasis that this ill-omened system should be brought to an end.

Here, the emphasis on obeying Allah and obeying the Messenger ﷺ also relates, apart from the trade of riba, to those events of the Battle of Uhud in which the clear commands of the Messenger ﷺ were violated. The allusion intended is that success can be attained only if you obey Allah and the Messenger; this alone is the place of hope and this alone is the path of salvation.

Earlier, in the third juz of Surah al-Baqarah, where we discussed the usurious system, we stated that along with the mention of riba, the mention of spending in the way of Allah (infaq fi sabilillah) and the virtue of charity (sadaqah) was made because in the collective system these two are opposing directions, indicating two separate systems of economy. One is the usurious economic system, and the other is an economic system based on mutual cooperation. Accordingly, here too, when the discussion of riba was undertaken, along with it the encouragement to spend in the way of Allah in every circumstance was also given. Thus, after the prohibition of riba and the warning of the Fire prepared for the disbelievers, and while calling people to the fear of Allah and keeping them always hopeful of divine mercy, they are invited to hasten toward the forgiveness of Allah, to enter those gardens which are wider than the expanses of the heavens and the earth, and which have been prepared for the people of taqwa. The first attribute of the muttaqin mentioned is: ﴿Those who spend in ease and in hardship﴾ "Those who spend in prosperity and in adversity." Therefore these people are the opposite party to those who consume the usurious system and gather through it doubled and quadrupled sums. Then further attributes of the muttaqin are described. The complete verses are:

﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose width is as the heavens and the earth, prepared for the righteous. (133) Those who spend in ease and in hardship, and those who restrain anger and pardon people; and Allah loves the good-doers. (134) And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins — and who forgives sins except Allah? — and do not persist knowingly in what they have done. (135)﴾

"Hasten along the path that leads to the forgiveness of your Lord and to the Garden whose breadth is as the heavens and the earth, which has been prepared for those who fear Allah, who spend their wealth in every condition, whether in hardship or in ease, who restrain their anger and pardon the faults of others. Such good-doers are dearly beloved to Allah. And those who, when they commit some immorality or, by committing a sin, wrong themselves, immediately remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins — for who else forgives sins but Allah? — and do not persist knowingly in what they have done."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 133:

The manner in which this verse expresses these acts of worship is such that they are described in a completely tangible way. It is as though there are people racing toward a fixed goal in a prize competition. ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord……﴾ "Run along the path that leads to the forgiveness of your Lord; ﴿and to a Garden, the breadth of which is as the heavens and the earth……﴾" Run toward the Garden whose breadth is like the heavens and the earth. "Run! That is the Garden, and there is forgiveness!" ﴿prepared for the God-fearing.﴾ "Which has been prepared for those who fear Allah."

After this, the attributes of the God-fearing are described: ﴿Those who spend in ease and in hardship……﴾ "Those who spend both in hardship and in prosperity."

That is, they are steadfast in spending at all times; they continue on their course. In prosperity they do not go beyond their bounds, and in adversity they do not turn back from their path. Prosperity does not make them arrogant and heedless, and adversity does not, by disciplining them, cause them to forget their purpose. The awareness of their responsibilities is always with them. They have become free of greed and avarice. They are always conscious of Allah's watchfulness, and the fear of Allah remains alive in their hearts at all times. The human self, which by its nature is stingy and has a natural love of wealth, needs a stronger impulse to keep it steadfast in spending in the way of Allah at all times. This impulse must be stronger than the love of wealth, so that it can break the natural bond of greed. And this impulse can only be the impulse of the fear of Allah. And what is this? It is an extremely subtle and profound awareness, with which the soul soars high. It becomes pure and is freed from confinement and bondage.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 3, verse 134:

In this atmosphere of the battle between truth and falsehood, this quality is alluded to here for a particular reason. During this struggle, the call to spend in the way of Allah (infaq fi sabilillah) is repeated again and again, and alongside it, criticism is directed at those wealthy people who shy away from spending in the way of Allah. The details of this point will be explained during the interpretation of the texts. In this atmosphere of the battle between truth and falsehood, spending has a special importance. And its repeated mention here is because the position of some workers of the Islamic call regarding spending in the way of Allah required it.

﴿And those who restrain their anger and pardon people.﴾ This means that the fear of Allah shows its effects in this field as well. The same causes and the same effects that applied to spending apply here: anger is a natural emotional reaction that produces heat in the blood of a human being. It is, as it were, a kind of the ordinary natural reaction of a human being, rather it is a natural need of a human being. And a person can bring this natural reaction under control only through that spiritual strength which is attained as a result of the light of taqwa (God-consciousness). This violent force is subdued only when a person is armed with spiritual strength and his gaze, rising above personal needs and personal defence, is fixed on a lofty human horizon.

Yes, restraining anger is the first stage, and it is not sufficient. Rather, at times a person restrains his anger but afterwards resentment is born in his heart, and it stirs in his heart the fervour of revenge. The outward anger, once cooled, gives birth to hidden envy, and deep enmity arises. In such a case, these outward reactions of rage and fury are relatively better compared with grudge and malice. For this reason, Allah the Exalted says afterwards that as a result of anger, envy and malice should not arise; rather, after that, one should act with forgiveness and pardon and overlook mistakes. If anger is hidden within the heart, it places veils over the hearts, and rather, the fire of resentment begins to smoulder within hearts. The human conscience becomes smoky. When a person forgives and pardons with his whole heart and soul, this veil is removed from the hearts, and the human soul soars in the atmospheres of light. Hearts feel coolness, and the human conscience attains peace and tranquillity.

﴿And Allah loves the doers of good.﴾ This means that such righteous people are very dear to Allah. What kind of righteous people? Those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah in both hardship and ease are righteous. Those who, after restraining anger, pardon and overlook people are righteous people. Such people are beloved to Allah. The use of the word love for such people is extremely beautiful, touching and radiant, and it harmonises well with this noble and luminous atmosphere.

With this declaration of love for goodness and good-doers, springs of goodness well up in the hearts of the believers, and these springs pass on from believer to believer, and enthusiasm and zeal for goodness arise in those hearts. Thus, this is not only an impactful expression, but this forceful mode of expression also carries behind it a great reality.

The community whom Allah loves, and who loves Allah, is one in which pardon and forgiveness are common, and in which there is no grudge or envy. It is a community whose members are connected and bound to one another. Its members are brothers to one another. It is a strong and firm community. Therefore, it is united and cohesive in its inner life as well, and on the battlefield it is a solid structure (bunyan marsus). Thus, this theme of pardon and forgiveness also harmonises with the theme of battle.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 135:

In connection with this, another attribute of the believers is also mentioned.

﴿And those who, when they commit an immoral act or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins — and who forgives sins except Allah? — and do not persist knowingly in what they have done.﴾

This shows how broad-hearted the Islamic Shariah is. Allah calls people to generosity and mutual tolerance only after He Himself has dealt with them with great magnanimity, and He informs them of this, so that they may develop a taste for generosity, kindle a lamp with the light of God, and learn lofty morals. Among the believing God-fearing, those who are exalted in rank are indeed great. But it is the unparalleled generosity of the religion of Islam that it counts among the God-fearing even those ﴿who, when an immoral act is committed by them or they wrong themselves by committing a sin, immediately remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins.﴾ And among sins, the "immoral act" (fahisha) is, from the Islamic standpoint, one of the worst and greatest sins. Yet it is the broad-heartedness and generosity of this religion that it does not cast out even the one who commits such a loathsome sin as indecency, nor are the doors of mercy closed to him. Nor does this religion regard such people as Muslims of a second rank; rather, it raises them to the lofty station of the God-fearing.

Yes, for elevation to that station there is only one condition imposed upon them, and even through this condition the temperament and inclination of this religion become clearly known. The condition is that after committing disobedience they immediately remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins, and that they do not persist in that deed while knowing that what they are doing is a sin. And that they not be submerged in disobedience with shamelessness and boldness; in other words, that they remain within the bounds of the servitude of Allah and ultimately bow before Him in submission. Thus they remain under the protection of Allah, and they remain within the sphere of His pardon, forgiveness and grace.

Islam knows that man is a bundle of weaknesses, and at times, owing to these human weaknesses, he may also commit indecency. At times the fleshly bodily inclinations are stirred, and under animal urges he descends to the level of bodily desires and inclinations; and going further still, under the heat and pressure of bodily appetites, inclinations and tendencies, he is compelled even to violate the commands of Allah, glorified be His majesty. The religion of Islam takes account of this natural weakness of man, and therefore does not adopt a harsh attitude toward him. And when a person, by committing these errors, wrongs himself, this religion does not immediately drive him away from the mercy of God, especially when he commits indecency or falls into a major sin. If the lamp of faith is alight in his heart, that is sufficient to support him. If the springs of faith in his heart have not dried up and his bond of relationship with God has not been completely severed, then in his heart there remains alive the feeling that he is a human being, a creature prone to error, and that his Lord is Forgiving and Merciful. Therefore this weak and sinful person remains hopeful, stays in good health and well-being, and his journey in this world does not end. He holds a strong rope, and its end does not slip from his hand. However much his human weaknesses may cast him down, as long as the lamp of faith is lit in his heart, he will attain his destination. As long as he holds fast to that strong rope, he will certainly come back onto the right path. As long as he remembers Allah, and fear of Allah is found in his heart, as long as he seeks forgiveness for his sins and affirms the servitude of Allah, and does not disobey Him out of arrogance, he can return to the right path.

This religion does not close the door of repentance to this creature, even if this weak creature falls for a time into the pit of misguidance. This religion does not leave this sinful human being alone and helpless in some uninhabited desert. Nor does it leave him despairing and anxious about his end. He is always given hope of forgiveness. He is guided. His trembling hands are taken in hand. His faltering steps become firm and steady. He is given a lamp of hope in which he finds his way, and thus he reaches a safe and secure place of rest, and enters a zone of peace.

Islam demands only one thing from man: that the springs of faith in his heart have not dried up, that his spiritual world has not become dark, and that he has not forgotten his true Creator. If he is remembering Allah, if the guiding beacon of light is present in his soul, if the voice of his conscience is calling him in his heart, and if the moisture of faith remains in his soil, then it can be hoped that the lamp of faith will be lit again in his heart, that he will return to the haven of peace and tranquillity, and that the seed of faith can be sown again in his field of the heart.

You too will surely face a clear example. If your sinful child believes that for the mistake he has committed there is nothing in the house but the stick, he will not look back; he will keep running, will adopt further waywardness, and will never return home. But if, alongside the stick, there is in the house a compassionate hand that passes over his head, which overlooks his weakness when he apologises, pats him encouragingly, and accepts his apology when he asks for forgiveness, then in that case there is a possibility that he will come back home.

Islam adopts exactly this attitude toward this weak and sinful human being. The Creator knows that if there is weakness and frailty in the human personality, on the other hand there is also some capacity in it. If on one side a burden of materialism is loaded upon him, on the other side within him there is also the swift movement of spirituality. If on one side his being contains the inclinations of the animal soul, on the other side Divine tendencies have also been deposited within him. Thus, whenever he falls down, entangled in animal filth, the hand of divine power lifts him up, raises him upward, and when he slips, it gives him a pat and sets him on his feet again, so that he may proceed on the right path, provided that the remembrance of Allah is in his heart and he has not entirely forgotten his Creator, and provided that he does not persist deliberately in error.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever seeks forgiveness (istighfar) is not considered to be persisting in error, even if he does so seventy times a day." (Narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Bazzar. He related it through the narration of Uthman ibn Waqid in its chain, although in its chain there is an unknown Companion. Yet Ibn Kathir declared it sahih and said: "a hasan hadith.")

Yes, while keeping the door of repentance open, Islam by no means leaves people free in waywardness. Nor does it regard those who are wrongdoers and who fall into the pit of error as praiseworthy, nor does it describe that filth by the name of beauty, as those who follow the so-called "realism" do. Rather, Islam only acknowledges slips and the natural weaknesses of man, so that despair does not arise within a person and the lamp of hope remains lit. In this way Islam encourages the emotions of modesty and shame, and forgiveness from Allah is granted for human shortcomings, because who other than Allah can forgive? Islam does not encourage sin; however, if someone feels remorse, Islam encourages him. It urges him toward istighfar, yet it also does not permit carelessness in committing sins, nor permits persistent wrongdoing and making it one's habit, because those who attach no importance to committing offences and keep committing sin upon sin have gone beyond the limits. Walls have been erected before them.

Thus Islam calls this humanity to take the lofty horizon as its goal, yet alongside this call of its invitation, it is always ready to show mercy and compassion. For Islam knows well what the limits of human strength are. Therefore Islam always keeps open the door of hope for man, and carries him forward as far as his strength allows.

(For details, see my book "Islam aur Alami Salamti," the chapter "Zameer ki Salamti" ["Soundness of Conscience"].)

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 136:

By seeking forgiveness for sins they committed, they are not merely doing something negative. Nor are they merely doing something negative by spending in both prosperity and adversity, or by suppressing their anger and pardoning people. Rather, they also do positive deeds and are doers of good. Therefore, forgiveness from their Lord awaits them, and they will dwell in gardens beneath which rivers flow. And after forgiveness, they will also receive the honour of Allah's love. Here there is action in the depths of their souls and also action in their outward life. Both are actions; both involve movement and both involve progress.

All these qualities mentioned here, and the battle that is about to be mentioned later in the context, have a specific connection between them. Just as the interest-based economy, or the Islamic economic system of mutual cooperation, was connected to the battlefield, and the day and night of the Islamic community were affected by it, so too the effects of these psychological characteristics and collective attributes fell upon the Muslim community. We indicated this point when we began discussing this subject. For example, overcoming stinginess, controlling anger, restraining oneself against committing sin, turning to Allah, seeking His forgiveness, and making His pleasure one's goal are conquests that are absolutely essential for victory over the enemy on the battlefield. Those people were enemies of Islam because they were representatives of stinginess. They were followers of their own desires, they were sinners and shameless, and they were enemies of Islam because they did not submit their own selves, their desires, and their system of life to the commands of Allah, His Shari'ah, and His chosen system of life. This was precisely the cause of enmity with them, and this was precisely the field of conflict. And for this reason, jihad against them was initiated. Apart from these reasons, there were no other causes for the battles and jihad of the Muslims, nor are there any now. A Muslim's enmity is also for Allah's sake, his fighting is also in the way of Allah, and his jihad is also for Allah. There is complete harmony between all the above-mentioned instructions and the description of the battle that follows them. Moreover, these matters were also connected to the circumstances in which this battle took place. For example: the disobedience to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the greed for accumulating war booty, and as a result, ignoring the clear instructions of the Messenger (ﷺ); the separation of Abdullah ibn Ubayy and his companions from the army of Islam merely out of self-conceit. And, as will become clear in the context, some people committed grave errors. Furthermore, there was also a flaw in the ideas and conceptions of those people, because they did not refer every matter back to Allah and His Messenger, and some people, in despair, would ask whether this movement of ours would yield any result, and some had the notion that had we had any standing, we would not have been killed here, and so on.

The Qur'an deals with all these circumstances. One by one, some matters are clarified, and regarding some matters it gives final decisions. Concerning these realities, it stirs the human soul, awakens it, creates fervour within it, and brings these realities to life within human existence. And the Qur'an accomplishes this task according to its unique method, examples of which will be found throughout the context.

In short, with the third clause of this passage, the account of the battle now begins; but within these events too, the fundamental realities of the Islamic conception of life have been impressed upon the mind. As for the events of the battle, they are used merely as a pivot and axis, and these realities revolve around these events.

At the beginning of this paragraph, attention is drawn to the fact that there is a permanent law (sunnah jariyah) of Allah in this universe, and this law concerns those peoples who reject the truth. The purpose of mentioning this principle and law is to make the Muslims aware that the defeat they will suffer in this battle is a temporary matter, and that it is not a permanent law of Allah in this universe. This temporary defeat too was based on a specific wisdom. After this, they are urged to act with patience and to keep themselves exalted on this earth through the power of faith. If in this battle they suffered defeat and received wounds, then previously, in such battles, the people of polytheism had also received wounds and suffered defeat; but in that too, the profound wisdom of Allah was at work, the explanation of which will become fully clear to them. This wisdom is that the impure people be separated from the ranks of the Muslims, that impurity be removed from their hearts, and that a model of the martyrs of Islam be prepared, who give their lives for their ideology, and that Muslims face death eye to eye. Whereas before this, they had harboured in their hearts the wish for martyrdom in the path of truth, so that they might weigh their promises and their aspirations on the scale of reality. And above all, that they might eradicate kufr from the face of the earth and establish an organised Islamic community on firm foundations in the face of the unbelievers. Thus, beneath all these events lay a lofty wisdom, whether these events were victories or calamitous defeats. He says:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 137:

The Muslims suffered a severe blow in this battle. A large number of them were martyred, they were forced into retreat, and they were made to endure great spiritual and physical distress. Seventy of the Companions were martyred, the blessed teeth of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were broken, and the blessed face of the Prophet ﷺ was wounded. The polytheists surrounded the Prophet ﷺ and troubled him, and the Companions received deep wounds. Because of this defeat the people of Islam were severely shaken. This was therefore a calamity which, after the remarkable victory of Badr, was perhaps entirely unexpected. So much so that when the people of Islam encountered this misfortune, they spontaneously began to say: "How did all this happen? We are Muslims, and yet we can be afflicted with such circumstances?"

Here the Qur'an turns the believers' attention to the Sunnah of Allah in this earth; it reminds them of the principle according to which events are decided on this earth.
