These events are not unprecedented at all, because the natural laws that have been established for human life in this universe are operating, and life here runs in accordance with them. Deviation from them is not possible at all, and events here do not occur by chance, without any principle; rather, these events are in exact conformity with the natural laws. If they study these laws and reach their essence, they will easily come to know the wisdom that lay behind these events, and then the purposes that lay hidden beneath these events will also become clearly visible to them. They will well understand how firm is the system according to which these events and incidents occur. Furthermore, they will be well assured about the wisdom that was concealed within them, and they will clearly understand what the future course is for them in the light of past events. Now, after this light has come, they would expect that, since they are Muslims, such events should not happen to them, and that they should receive victory and help, without their providing the means of victory, the first of which is obedience to Allah and to the Messenger of Allah.

What is the Sunnah of Allah to which the context here directs them? It is the end of those people who, throughout human history, have denied the truth; and that the days and nights of people in the world keep changing. People are put to trial so that their souls may be purified. Their power of patience is tested, and this trial is conducted by breaking mountains of afflictions and hardships. And that those who act with patience will eventually attain victory, while those who adopt a posture of disbelief will be wiped off the face of the earth.

Amid the explanation of these Sunan of Allah in these verses, the believers are encouraged to bear difficulties, to be sympathetic to one another in severe circumstances, and to be patient over the wound they have received, because the wound was not inflicted on them alone; their enemies too suffered wounds equal to theirs, although the believers hold loftier ideals than them. They are upon the path of guidance in comparison with them, and their system of life is better than theirs. And after these difficulties, ultimate victory and success are also destined to be attained by the believers.

*"Indeed, there have passed before you precedents, so travel through the earth and observe what was the end of those who denied."* (3:137)

*"This is a clear proclamation for mankind, and a guidance and an admonition for those who fear Allah."* (3:138)

The style of the Qur'an is to link the present of humanity with its past, and by connecting past and present it cares for the future of humanity. The Arab society, who were the first addressees of the Qur'an, had no life worth the name; they had no store of knowledge, and before Islam they had no reservoir of experience, so that the Islamic movement could present before them a complete model drawn from their own cultural store. It was Islam and the Qur'an, Islam's book, that accomplished this feat: it bestowed on the Arabs a new life and gave them the form of a community which, in later ages, led the entire world.

The tribal social order under whose shade the Arabs were living was not capable of expanding their thinking to the extent that they could give a logical connection to the events of the life of the Arabian Peninsula, much less that they would seek a logical connection between all of humanity living on this earth and its calamities and events, and between the global events occurring throughout the entire earth and the natural laws operating in this universe and human life running in accordance with them. They could not even have thought about such a search for connection.

The intellectual and cultural revolution that took place among the Arabs as a result of the Qur'an and Islam is a far-reaching revolution. It was not a revolution that arose in a society gradually through intellectual and cultural progress, nor was it a revolution that arose because of the requirements and capacities of the life then prevailing and in motion. Rather, this great revolution arose as a result of a purely Islamic outlook on life; this faith brought them a gift and, lifting them up, raised them to the level of the Islamic outlook on life. And this outlook on life accomplished all this work in the brief span of barely a quarter century, whereas the advanced nations around the Arabs, armed with a store of knowledge, reached that height of lofty thought only after centuries, and after many generations had passed, these nations discovered that there are certain natural laws operating in this universe and that it runs under these immutable natural principles. And when they discovered these laws of nature and natural principles, they still did not arrive at the truth that above these immutable laws there is also an immutable Divine will, which is not confined even within these natural laws; and that beyond the laws of nature, authority over all affairs belongs to Allah the Exalted. As for the Muslim community, it had attained this conviction from the very first day. Its conception of this universe had become very broad, and within its feeling and consciousness a balance had been established between the permanence of natural laws and the unrestricted will of Allah the Exalted. For its practical life was founded upon the immutable principles of natural laws, yet after that it also had the assurance that the will of Allah is unrestricted.

*"Indeed, there have passed before you precedents..."* means: "Times have passed before you." In those periods events occurred in accordance with the natural laws; so similar events will occur in your time too. Therefore, be prepared for such outcomes as well, for those nations which in the history of earlier peoples faced circumstances like yours, and certain realities came to pass before them, received similar results.

*"...so travel through the earth..."* because the whole earth is a planet. In this planet human life is flowing. This earth and life within it is an open book. Both sight and insight have abundant material in it.

*"...and observe what was the end of those who denied..."* This is the end whose traces are visible everywhere on the earth. Moreover, later generations have recorded the traces and evidence of it in their histories. The Qur'an has related a large number of these Sunan and histories. In many places of the Qur'an they are mentioned, and in some places it has described in detail the places of events, their times, and the persons and characters involved. Whereas in some places it has used only allusions and left aside the time and place; the event is stated in summary. Here too an summary allusion has been made to this human history, and from it a general and abstract lesson is drawn: that the end which befell those who denied the prophets yesterday has likewise been determined for those who deny today, and will be their end tomorrow as well. This allusion has been made so that the Muslim community may be settled and certain about its own end, and be warned not to slip along with the deniers. For at that time there were circumstances that required this assurance, and there were also circumstances that required warning the Muslims against stumbling. The later context of the discourse throws detailed light on these circumstances.

After the indications of the laws of nature and the Divine Sunnah in human history, people are called to take lesson and admonition from these events of human history.

"هَذَا بَيَانٌ لِلنَّاسِ وَهُدًى وَمَوْعِظَةٌ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ" ... "This is a clear proclamation for mankind, and a guidance and admonition for those who fear Allah."

This is a clear and explicit warning for people; guidance and advice for those who fear Allah. It is an exposition for all of mankind. Thus it is a far-reaching revolution for humanity, and people cannot benefit from this revolution until it is set forth to them. But only a specific group will be able to benefit from this exposition. Only these people will be able to take lesson and admonition. Only these people will profit. Who are the muttaqun (the God-fearing)?

It is a fact that only a heart that is believing grants acceptance to the word of guidance, because it is always open to guidance, and only a God-fearing heart can benefit from eloquent and effective admonition. Such a heart, upon hearing the word of guidance at any time, begins to throb and becomes ready to accept it. It is rarely the case that mere knowledge of truth and falsehood benefits someone, or that mere knowledge of guidance and misguidance is beneficial. Truth, by its very nature, is so clear that it does not need any lengthy speech or exposition. In fact, what is lacking is the impulse to accept the truth, and people do not know the path to accepting the truth. Inclination toward truth and the paths to accepting it can only be found when a heart is filled with faith and certainty, and faith remains secure when it is backed by taqwa (piety) and fear of Allah. This is why the Qur'an repeatedly emphasizes that the truth, guidance, light, admonition and lessons-bearing matters stated in this Book are beneficial only for the believers and the God-fearing. Because faith and taqwa open the windows of the heart to guidance, light, lesson and admonition. Only on the strength of faith and taqwa can a person bear the hardships of the path of truth. This is the essential matter, and this is the reality of the issue. The problem is not solved by knowledge and information alone. One can see many people who, despite possessing a large store of knowledge and understanding of the truth, are worshippers of falsehood and lost in it, merely because their carnal desires have overpowered them, against which knowledge and understanding are helpless, or because they are dismayed by the difficulties which always confront the bearers and callers of the truth.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 3, verse 139:

After this, the address turns toward the Muslims. Their hearts are consoled, they are given comfort, and they are exhorted to steadfastness. ﴿Do not lose heart, nor grieve; you shall have the upper hand if you are believers.﴾ ... "Do not let your hearts be broken, do not grieve; you will prevail, if you are believers."

﴿Do not lose heart...﴾ The word "wahn" (weakness, feebleness) is derived from this root. "Do not grieve" means: do not grieve over the calamities that are befalling you, or over the worldly gains that have slipped from your hands. You are dominant and superior, because your way of life is superior. You prostrate before none but Allah alone, whereas they bow before one of Allah's creatures, or bow before something they have associated with Allah. Your system of life is superior and more excellent than their system of life. You live according to the system that Allah has established, whereas they follow the system that human beings have devised. Your role is superior to theirs. You are the bearers of the trust for all of humanity, the guides and leaders of all humanity, while they have been cast away from Allah's system and have gone astray. Your station on this earth is a lofty station. You are among the inheritors of the legacy that Allah has promised you. As for those people, they are heading toward nothingness and extinction. Therefore, if you become true believers, you alone will remain exalted and supreme in this world. And if you are true believers, then do not fear, do not grieve, and do not let your hearts be broken, for it is the Sunnah of Allah that at times misfortune will befall you and at other times you will be victorious; and after jihad, trial, and the distinguishing of the genuine from the false, your end will be good.

"If a wound has touched you now, a similar wound had already touched the opposing party. These are the vicissitudes of time, which We cause to alternate among people. Allah wished to see who among you are true believers, and to separate out those who are truly witnesses to the truth, for Allah does not love the wrongdoers. And through this trial He wished to distinguish the believers and to crush the disbelievers." (Quran 3:140-141)

Here, mention is made of the wound that befell the Muslims and also of the wound that befell the deniers. The wound inflicted upon the deniers refers to the Battle of Badr, for on that occasion the polytheists were struck and the Muslims escaped unscathed. However, the wound inflicted upon the deniers may also refer to the Battle of Uhud, in which, although at the outset the Muslims had gained victory and the disbelievers had been defeated, seventy of them were killed. Afterwards the polytheists fled, and the Muslims pursued them, striking at their skulls. The standard of the polytheists fell, and no one remained who would advance to raise it, until finally a woman raised the standard. Thereupon they gained courage and gathered around her. Then the turn of the polytheists came when the archers disobeyed the commands of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); they disputed among themselves, and in the final phase of that battle there came upon the Muslims the calamity that is mentioned here. This was a full punishment for their having disobeyed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and for their dispute among themselves. Thus the Sunnah of Allah that He has decreed for this universe became manifest. The disobedience of the archers to the commands of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the disputes that arose among them despite the counsel given, came about because greed for the spoils of war had arisen in their hearts. Allah has indeed decreed victory for the Muslims in jihad and fighting, but only for those who perform jihad purely for the sake of Allah, and whose aim is not some worthless benefit of this lowly world. Because of this event, another Sunnah of Allah also became manifest: that Allah causes victory and triumph to alternate among people. Sometimes the people of truth are granted victory, and sometimes the people of falsehood are granted victory, in accordance with their deeds and their intentions. Through these days, believers and hypocrites are sorted and separated, errors are committed, and spiritual impurities are removed from people's hearts.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 3, verse 140:

إِنْ يَمْسَسْكُمْ قَرْحٌ فَقَدْ مَسَّ الْقَوْمَ قَرْحٌ مِثْلُهُ وَتِلْكَ الأيَّامُ نُدَاوِلُهَا بَيْنَ النَّاسِ وَلِيَعْلَمَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا

"If a wound has touched you, a similar wound has already touched that people. And these days We alternate among people, so that Allah may know those who believe."

Now, the translation of this verse: "اس وقت اگر تمہیں چوٹ لگی ہے تو اس سے پہلے ایسی ہی چوٹ تمہارے مخالف فریق کو بھی لگ چکی ہے ۔ یہ تو زمانہ کے نشیب و فراز ہیں جنہیں لوگوں کے درمیان گردش دیتے رہتے ہیں ۔ تم پر یہ وقت اس لئے لایا گیا تھا کہ اللہ دیکھنا چاہتا تھا کہ تم میں سے سچے مومن کون ہیں۔"

The ups and downs of life, the alternation of ease and hardship, are circumstances that bring out the hidden capacities of the human self. Through them people's dispositions become known, and it becomes clear who has been purified of ideological impurity and who still carries ideological residue. Who is hasty and who is steadfast? Who falls into despair and who places complete trust in Allah? Who surrenders himself entirely to destiny, and who is content with the decree, or who adopts willfulness?

Here the Islamic community is purified, and it becomes evident who is a believer and who is a hypocrite. The true condition of both groups becomes clear and comes into view. The inner states of people are also revealed to the people of this world. In this way, every kind of weakness that arises from the lack of moral and ideological harmony among people is removed from the ranks of Islam, when the community contains people of varied and ambiguous inclinations.

Allah knows the believers and He knows the hypocrites. Allah knows what is in the breasts (Alim bi-dhat al-sudur). But through the events of life, through victory and defeat, hidden people come into the open; hidden qualities become manifest in the form of life's events. Now faith appears in the form of an outward act, and hypocrisy also takes concrete and embodied form. Therefore there will be reckoning and accounting for these matters, and reward and punishment will follow. Allah does not call to account matters that He merely knows, but reward and punishment depend upon matters that have come into action.

And the succession of life's ups and downs, of hardship and ease, one after another, is a criterion whose result is never wrong. It is a balance in which there is no deficiency or excess. In this measure, hardships and peace are equal. Many personalities face difficulties with patience and perseverance, but when ease comes they become self-indulgent. The condition of the people of faith, however, is that they stand firm in hardship and show patience, and when the time of comfort and ease comes, they still do not lose their composure. In both states their repentance is directed toward Allah. Their conviction is firmly established on this: in prosperity and in adversity alike, the agency belongs to the Divine Being.

Allah was training the Muslim community, and this training was taking place at a time when the Muslim community was about to take charge of the leadership of the whole world. So Allah tested and trained it, after the success and prosperity of Badr, by afflicting it with the failure and adverse conditions of Uhud. After an astonishing success and victory, He tested and trained it by inflicting upon it an unexpected defeat. Although these two events were not without cause, and both were in exact conformity with Allah's established sunnah in this universe, operating under secondary causes, what are the causes of victory and defeat? Their purpose is that the community may become firmer in obedience to Allah and His Messenger, that its trust and reliance upon Allah may increase, that it may draw ever closer to the Divine Being, and that it may come to know the temperament of the Islamic system of life and its obligations as one knows a matter with certainty of knowledge and truth of certainty.

Now the matter moves a little further. The community is shown further aspects of divine wisdom. These wisdoms are shown during the narration of the events of this battle and in the mirror of life's ups and downs, that is, after the purification of the ranks of Muslims and the separation of the people of faith from the people of hypocrisy, some other wisdoms: ﴿وَيَتَّخِذَ مِنْكُمْ شُهَدَاءَ﴾ "and that He may take martyrs from among you."

This is a strange manner of expression in which deep meanings are hidden. It is as if Allah Himself selects the martyrs. Among the mujahideen, selection for the station of martyrdom takes place, and Allah makes this selection for Himself. Therefore it is not a calamity or a loss that someone be martyred in the way of Allah; rather, Allah takes him for Himself and chooses him. This is, as it were, a special honour for them. Allah chose them and raised them to the station and rank of martyrdom, so that they might become wholly Allah's and be included in His close assembly. ﴿وَيَتَّخِذَ مِنْهُم…﴾ "Allah will choose from among them…"

Then, according to one meaning, these people are witnesses for Allah, and by giving their lives they bear witness to the truth that Allah has sent down upon the Messenger ﷺ. These people testify that this message is the message of truth, and they give this testimony in such a manner and style that no doubt remains and no further cross-examination is needed. After that, the matter is decided. Because they give this testimony with a continuous struggle whose end is the offering of their lives, thereby they accept this truth with their blood and present it to the world in a decisive form. Allah demands of these chosen people that they bear witness that the way of life sent down from Allah is true. They have believed in it. They have become sincerely devoted to it. It has become so dear to them that it is dearer than their own lives, and that people's lives cannot be set right until they conform to this truth. They have firm certainty of it. Therefore they leave no stone unturned in removing falsehood from people's lives, expelling it, so that this truth is established throughout the world and is implemented in the system of government of people too. In short, these martyrs are martyrs for all these matters, and their martyrdom consists in jihad and death in the way of Allah, and it is a testimony in which there is no room for dispute or argument.

Now let us look at the other aspect. When someone utters with his tongue the testimony "La ilaha illa Allah, Muhammad Rasul Allah," this testimony is not a testimony until the one who professes it fulfils its meaning and requirements. Its meaning is that he should not regard anyone as a deity besides Allah, and he should not take any source of law or code of legislation other than Allah. Because among the particular attributes of divinity, the most distinctive is that it legislates for people. And among the particular forms of servitude on the part of servants, the most distinctive is that the servant derives his system of life and system of law from Allah. Its practical form is that he derives the law from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who is the Messenger of Allah and the lawgiver on His behalf. And apart from these two sources, there should be no other source of law in his view.

Then the requirement of this testimony is that a person begins the struggle which, as a result, makes divinity and sovereignty on this earth belong to Allah alone, just as the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ preached it. And this Islamic law becomes the system of life. This system should prevail, it should be followed, and it should exercise authority over the whole of people's life, and no aspect of life should be exempt from its authority.

In this sense, this system of life demanded that when a person gives his life in its way, the martyr has given his life. Therefore he has become a witness to whom Allah made the demand that he bear this testimony, because Allah has placed him at the station of witnessing. For this reason he has become a martyr.

This is the deep understanding of that wondrous manner of speech: ﴿وَيَتَّخِذَ مِنْكُمْ شُهَدَاءَ…﴾ and this is the meaning and requirement of the testimony "La ilaha illa Allah, Muhammad Rasul Allah." It is not the meaning of this testimony by which the testimony becomes a joke, a mere waste of time, and from which concessions are derived.

﴿وَاللَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ "And Allah does not love wrongdoers." "Shirk is indeed a great injustice." In Sahihayn it is narrated from Hadrat Ibn Mas'ud ؓ, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, "Which sin is the greatest?" He said, "That you set up a rival to Allah while it is He alone who created you."

Earlier in the context, an allusion was made to Allah's sunnah regarding those who deny. And now a verdict is pronounced that Allah does not love wrongdoers. Therefore there is an indirect emphasis that those who deny will certainly reach their logical end, and so Allah does not love them. The effects of this manner of expression also come to light: a believer begins to hate injustice and the unjust. Creating this atmosphere against injustice and the unjust is closely connected with this occasion of urging toward jihad and the pursuit of martyrdom. Therefore the believer fights against what Allah wishes to eliminate, and fights against those whom Allah utterly dislikes. And this is the place of martyrdom for the believer: there he offers the sacrifice of his life, and it is from such people that Allah chooses the martyrs.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 3, verse 141:

After this, the theme now turns to the question: what wisdom lies hidden behind these tragic events? It is explained that through them the Ummah was meant to be trained, purified, and prepared for its noble character, so that it might become an instrument and a means of God's decree, destroying the disbelievers and becoming a veil for the hand of divine power to punish those who deny. ﴿And that Allah may purify those who believe and destroy the disbelievers﴾ ... "And He wanted, through the trial, to separate the believers and to crush the disbelievers." Tamhees (purification, sifting) is a stage that comes after separation and distinction. This is a process that reaches completion within a person; it is completed in the conscience. It is an experience through which the hidden corners of personality are revealed before the eye. Upon these hidden corners the light is focused, so that rust, impurity and adulteration are removed from them, they become clear and visible, and this personality becomes firmly established upon truth with excellence.

Often it happens that a person cannot make a correct assessment of his own self and personality. He is not aware of his hidden weaknesses and the ups and downs of his self. Thus he has no accurate knowledge of his strength, nor a correct understanding of his weaknesses. Some of his hidden weaknesses are such that they manifest only when they are stirred up.

Allah, glorified is His mention, had taken charge of this process of sifting Himself. This sifting was being carried out in such a way that the Muslims were confronted with the ups and downs of life: they would be given victory and also defeat, hardship would come and also good circumstances would be encountered. They were to be thoroughly rubbed. And after this bitter friction, the people of faith would come to know about themselves what they had previously known. Through events, experiences and various practical situations, their sifting was carried out.

Sometimes a person is caught in the delusion that he is strong and brave and free from the grip of greed and desire, and when he is placed upon the touchstone of practical experience, and when he actually encounters real circumstances, he discovers that there are still great weaknesses in his personality which have not yet been removed. And that he does not yet have the capacity to bear the full pressure of hardships; therefore it is in his own interest that he should learn of his weaknesses in advance, so that he may strive to reshape his personality anew, and prepare himself to bear the difficulties that are bound to confront him on the path of his call. And because of this way of life, these difficulties are inevitable.

Allah's plan was that He should thoroughly train this first Islamic community, which He was to prepare for the leadership of all humanity. According to this plan, this community was to accomplish a great task on this earth. Therefore Allah sifted this community in this manner, and at Uhud He confronted it with circumstances that were unexpected, so that this community might raise its level somewhat and prepare itself for the role that Allah had determined it was to perform, and that role was ﴿and that He might destroy the disbelievers﴾. And this is because destroying falsehood through truth is one of the established ways (sunnah) of God. But this destruction becomes possible only when truth becomes manifest and its weaknesses are removed through rigorous training and sifting.

Now comes the next wise point, in the form of a rhetorical question of negation. The Muslims' thinking about the call to Islam is corrected, and it is explained what the Divine way (sunnah Ilahi) is in this matter. It is explained that there is an unalterable law of Allah regarding victory and defeat, deeds and their consequences. It is explained that on the path to Paradise there are thorns laid down, there are difficulties, and that in this path difficulties can be resolved through patience and steadfastness. Through empty wishes and good desires alone this ascent cannot be crossed. You will have to face difficulties on this path and cleanse your ranks of the weak.

﴿Or did you think that you would enter Paradise while Allah has not yet made evident those of you who strive and made evident those who are patient?﴾ (3:142) ﴿And you had certainly wished for death before you encountered it. And now you have seen it while you were looking on.﴾ (3:143)

The rhetorical negative interrogative form is used at a point where the addressee is to be warned about a extremely dangerous intellectual error. The error here was that people thought it was enough merely to declare with the tongue that "I have become a Muslim" and "I am ready for death", to be ready to lay down one's life for the cause of Islam. By this declaration alone, they had, as it were, borne all the hardships of the path of the call to Islam, and now they had become deserving of both Allah's pleasure and Paradise.

Here they were told sternly that this thinking of yours is not correct. You will have to pass through the real experience of hardships, there will be a practical test, you will have to take part in jihad, and you will have to embrace trials. And after that, in the state of these difficulties, there is to be no wailing and lamenting, but patience, and you will have to endure them.

Here, some words in this verse are startling: وَلَمَّا يَعْلَمِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا مِنْكُمْ ……………"Has Allah not yet seen which of you are those who strive" وَيَعْلَمَ الصَّابِرِينَ……………"and who are the patient ones?"

Therefore, on this path, merely engaging in jihad is not sufficient; patience in the face of difficulties on the path is also necessary. These difficulties are continuous, of various kinds, and they do not end when the jihad on the battlefield ends. Rather, it often happens that the difficulties on the battlefield are very few compared with those that come after jihad, for which patience is demanded and in which the trial of faith takes place. In our daily life there are never-ending difficulties: remaining steadfast on the horizon of faith, continually fulfilling the requirements of faith in both awareness and action, overcoming human weaknesses through patience on the paths of life, remaining firm on Islam in daily dealings with all people and in all matters with one's own self, and especially showing patience and steadfastness at those points where false powers appear to achieve success and seem as though victory is now destined for them. Then sometimes the struggle is long, the road appears long and harsh and full of difficulties; in such circumstances, continuing to be patient, persisting in jihad, and against difficulties and the desire for ease in the battlefield, against whispers and the weariness of the self, steadfastly continuing to show patience and firmness; in short, developing the resolve to overcome the unknown and hidden difficulties that exist on this path, of which the battlefield is only one, all these are the requirements of this verse and the difficulties of the way to Paradise. In short, these objectives are not achieved through words and wishes alone.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 3, verse 143:

﴿And you used to wish for death before you met it; now you have seen it with your own eyes.﴾ "You were wishing for death, but that was when death had not yet come before you. Now it has come before you, and you have seen it with your own eyes."

Here the Qur'an once again brings them face to face with death, the very thing they used to wish for, and which they had already witnessed on the field of Uhud. They are made to stand before this scene so that they may weigh the words and expressions that are on their tongues against the realities that confronted them on the field of action, and compare the wishes that are in their hearts. Thus they are taught to examine every phrase and word that comes from their tongues, to see how much meaning lies behind those words, and to make this assessment in the light of the realities that occurred at Uhud. In this way they will come to know the worth of the words they utter with their mouths, the value of the wishes they cherish in their hearts, and the place of the promises they made when weighed against these heavy realities. Then they are also taught here that words that merely dissolve into the air, or wishes that arise in the heart, cannot admit them into Paradise. Rather, they will be able to enter Paradise only when they give those words the garb of reality and bring those wishes into the field of action, so that they display true jihad, appear steadfast in patience amid the hardships of that path, and see these realities with their own eyes in the real and practical world of people, for the sake of Allah.

For Allah, it was not difficult to make the believers triumph in their very first day, without placing them in difficulties or causing them hardship, granting success to His Prophet, to this message of guidance and to this system of life He had prescribed. He was capable of sending down angels who would fight alongside them, or of destroying the polytheists alone, just as those angels destroyed the peoples of 'Ad, Thamud and Lut (peace be upon them).

However, the objectives that had been set were not merely victory and triumph. Among the objectives was also the training of the community of Muslims, because this community was to discharge the duty of leading all of humanity. At that time humanity was weak and feeble, a slave to its carnal desires and bodily inclinations, practically steeped in ignorance and intellectually deviated. For this purpose a leadership was needed that was intelligent and demanded high capabilities from its leaders, and the first of these demands was that they be firm and steadfast upon truth and righteousness. They must be patient in the face of difficulties, and must know where their ranks are weak and where they are strong. They must also know where the human soul stumbles, where there is danger of deviation from the straight path, and what the remedy for all these weaknesses is. Then, whether conditions are good and success is achieved, they must still be patient, and whether conditions are severe, they must still be patient. The truth is that seeing defeat after victory and being patient over it was, in those circumstances, an extremely bitter and unpleasant situation.

Before issuing the commands to place the community of Muslims in the position of global leadership, Allah subjected the community to such a rigorous training. This was so that it would become ready to undertake that great and formidable task which it was to perform on the surface of the earth. And it was the will of Allah that He would send to this great mission the person whom He had selected and chosen for it.

Now the will of Allah employs various means in the preparation and training of the community of Muslims. It is made to pass through various conditions and events. Sometimes the community is granted a decisive victory, and then it rejoices, its confidence in itself is restored, and this is accomplished through the special help of Allah. It is also made to taste the experience of triumph, and in the intoxication of that triumph it displays patience and seriousness; it succeeds in overcoming pride, arrogance, intoxication and haughtiness, does not abandon humility and gratitude to Allah. And at other times it is made to pass through defeat, severity and pain, and then it seeks refuge in the presence of Allah. It comes to know its own personal strength, and it learns how dangerous the consequences will be for it if it deviates even slightly from the Islamic system of life. Thus it will also taste the bitterness of defeat, and along with it, it will also prevail over falsehood, because it is upon the truth. Its own weaknesses and faults within its ranks will become known to it: where the desires of the self creep in, and where its feet slip, so that in the next stage it may be able to remove all those weaknesses. It will advance carrying a wide store of experiences from both victory and defeat. This was the Sunnah of Allah, and the system of divine decree and destiny was operating in accordance with it. There was no possibility of deviating from it even a hair's breadth, and there is none now.

This was a small provision of the lessons of experience gained from the events of Uhud, a portion of the experiences which have been recorded in the verses of the Qur'an for the community of Muslims, for every Islamic revolutionary community, and for every community that arises in every age, every time and every place.

After this, the Qur'an, in accordance with its distinctive method, presents here certain great and important events in its own particular style for the training of the Islamic community. Let us behold:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 3, verse 144:

The first part of this section refers to a specific event, which occurred at the Battle of Uhud. When the archers abandoned their assigned position on the mountain, the polytheists attacked them from that direction, fell upon the Muslims, and the Muslims were defeated. The teeth of the Messenger (ﷺ) were martyred, wounds appeared on his face, and blood began to flow from his blessed face. The two sides became locked in close combat, the Muslims scattered, and no one knew where anyone else was. In these circumstances, someone called out in a voice: "O people! Muhammad (ﷺ) has been killed." This cry had a very harmful effect on the Muslims. Many of them returned to Madinah, climbed up the mountain, were defeated, and, in despair, left the battlefield. A few individuals remained with the Messenger (ﷺ), and in these circumstances he (ﷺ) stood firm with those few, and he began calling out to the Muslims to come back. So they gathered again, and their hearts were calmed. At that time, Allah, in a perceptible manner, caused drowsiness to overcome them, and gave them tranquility of heart and peace and calm, while the details are coming later.

This event, which had completely stunned those people, is made a point of attention by the Qur'an, and in connection with it, it brings forward the important truths of the Islamic worldview. By making it the subject, important indications are given here about the reality of death and life, and light is shed on the history of faith and the circumstances of the caravan of faith.

﴿And Muhammad is no more than a messenger; messengers have passed on before him. So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? And whoever turns back on his heels will not harm Allah at all; and Allah will reward the grateful.﴾

"Muhammad is nothing but a messenger; there were messengers before him. So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? Beware, whoever turns back will not harm Allah in the least; but Allah will reward those who remain grateful to Him."

Indeed Muhammad (ﷺ) is only a messenger; messengers came before him; all those messengers have died, and Muhammad (ﷺ) too will die in the same way as those messengers died. This is a reality that cannot be denied. When this reality came before you in that battle (although as a false rumour), why did it remain hidden from your sight? This is an extremely astonishing matter.

Muhammad (ﷺ) is a bearer of the message from Allah. He came so that he might convey the message of Allah. Allah, in Himself, is the Ever-Living, who does not die. His message is everlasting. Therefore, how could it be appropriate that if the bearers of the message die or are killed, you would abandon your way of life and turn back on your heels? This too was a clear reality which, amid the confusion of that battle, had disappeared from their sight, although it was fitting that it should not have disappeared from the sight of the people of faith, because it was an extremely simple and plain matter.

Man is mortal, but the way of life remains. The Islamic system of life is a separate reality, which holds a permanent status entirely independent of those who carry it and who convey it to people, whether they are messengers or, after the messengers, the callers and preachers of the Ummah. The Muslim who loves the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and this love is of a kind for which no parallel is found in the whole of human history, has a duty to distinguish between the person of the Messenger and the way of life that this person spread among people. This is because the way of life that he (ﷺ) gave is ḥayyun lā yamūt (living, never dying)... Its connection is with Allah, who is ḥayyun lā yamūt (the Ever-Living, who never dies)... It becomes their duty to make this distinction because they are lovers of the Messenger. These people did not want that a thorn should even pinch the Messenger (ﷺ). Look at Abu Dujanah, who made his back a shield for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Arrows were raining upon him, and he remained right where he was, firmly in place. And see that he (ﷺ) remained with only nine men, and one after another of them was martyred; all of them were finished off, but he (ﷺ) did not let harm reach him. And today, everywhere and in every age, when people hear your name, they are moved with ecstasy because of love, and they love you wholeheartedly, with their entire being and with all their emotions.

O lovers of the Messenger! The value of the call is greater than the caller. ﴿And Muhammad is no more than a messenger; messengers have passed on before him...﴾ "Muhammad is nothing but a messenger; other messengers too have passed before him." Those earlier messengers too were bearers of this same call, whose roots reach far back into ancient times; again and again this call has flourished in the great fields of history. Its beginning came alongside the beginning of humanity, and these messengers have been its guides along the highways of life, in a leading manner, with peace and safety.

Therefore this message and this system are greater than the caller, and they outlast the caller. Callers come and go, but this message flows on through the ages and generations. Its adherents remain connected and joined to its first source. That source and origin which itself sent those messengers, that source remains. Toward it the believers turn. It is their goal, and it is not permissible for the people of faith to turn back on their heels and, abandoning the guidance of Allah, apostatise, while Allah is Ever-Living.

This is why a severe rebuke is directed at their attitude here. He says:

﴿So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? Beware, whoever turns back will not harm Allah in the least; but Allah will reward those who remain grateful.﴾

The expression is such that it brings before the eye a living picture of apostasy. "You will turn back on your heels": ʿalā aʿqābikum, and "whoever turns back on his heels": ʿalā ʿaqibayhi. This is a sensory and visible movement: a living person turns back on his heels. This turning is a embodied form of apostasy. Abandoning the Islamic way of life is exactly like a person suddenly turning back on his heels. Yet here, by this turning, the intended meaning is not this physical movement, but the psychological state in which a person adopts an ideological retreat. Someone called out that Muhammad (ﷺ) had been killed, and upon hearing this, a thought and a question came into the minds of some Muslims: what is the benefit of fighting the polytheists now? Thus a mental movement and this mental reversal were expressed through a physical movement, that is, their minds turned back in the same way as they were physically retreating in the Battle of Uhud. This is the reality to which Anas ibn al-Nadr (رضي الله عنه) pointed. People had laid down their weapons, and it was said to them that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had been killed. On this he said to them: "Then what will you do living after Muhammad (ﷺ)? Rise up and be martyred for the same cause for which he (ﷺ) was martyred."

﴿Beware, whoever turns back on his heels will not harm Allah in the least...﴾ "He will only harm himself. He causes harm to himself by turning back, and through this reversal of position Allah suffers no loss. Allah is free from need of the people; He has no need of their faith. It is His mercy that He prescribed for people this system in which lies their own happiness and benefit. Whoever turns away from this system will himself be afflicted in this world with a bad end. He will be bewildered in his own self and in his society as well. Because of his action this system will be disturbed, human life will be disturbed, and the entire human population will be disturbed. All affairs will fall into disorder, and people will be caught in calamities of their own making, merely because they turned away from this system, the only system within which the whole of human life can function rightly. Man can find peace only, and only under the shade of this system can the human self come into harmony with its own nature, and can move in harmony with the whole universe within which it lives."

﴿And Allah will reward those who remain grateful.﴾ "These grateful ones are those who appreciate the blessing that Allah bestowed upon them by giving them the Islamic way of life. They give thanks by obeying this system; they also give thanks by praising Allah, and by establishing it they gain the happiness of this world. This is their reward in this world. The best reward for their gratitude, and after that, they will be rewarded in the Hereafter, and that will be an otherworldly felicity far greater than this worldly prosperity, and there will be an accountability."

Thus, through this comment on that event, Allah (Exalted) turns the personal attachment of the Muslims, which was centred on the person of the Messenger (ﷺ), away from it and joins it directly to the Divine Being, who is the true source of this call. This is because the pure spring of the Islamic call was not made to flow by the Messenger (ﷺ). He only guided people toward it and invited them to benefit from that surging river, just as the other messengers before him had likewise guided and invited caravans of thirsty creatures to quench their thirst from that pure spring.

Thus Allah intended to take hold of people's hands and place in them that firm rope which Muhammad (ﷺ) did not tie, but rather he came so that people might be bound to that firm rope. He would leave them in that state, and they would depart from this world in a condition where people hold that rope firmly.

So Allah wished that the Muslims' connection would be directly with Islam, and their covenant would be directly with Allah, and their accountability regarding that covenant before Allah would be unmediated. They would be answerable directly before Allah, so that they might feel the sense of their responsibilities, responsibilities which do not end with the death of the Messenger (ﷺ). Thus they have made a direct pledge to Allah, and they are directly accountable to Him concerning it.

Thus it was the will of Allah that the Muslim Ummah would be struck by the shock which it was destined to suffer one day. Allah knew that when this shock came it would be unbearable for them. Therefore Allah had them rehearse that shock at this place; He practically made it reach them, that is, He let them feel this grief concerning the death of the Messenger in advance, before this shock truly came and left them utterly prostrate.

And when, at the time of the Messenger's death (ﷺ), they were struck by that shock, they indeed could not bear it. A personality trained like ʿUmar (رضي الله عنه) stood up, drew his sword, and cried out that no one should dare to utter the words that Muhammad (ﷺ) had died.

It was Abu Bakr (رضي الله عنه) who immediately stood up, he who was close to God, whose connection with the divine decree was firmly direct. He recited this very verse and reminded those who had become enfeebled and lost their senses. When they heard this divine call, their senses were restored, and they came to their senses.

The Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 145:

After this, the Qur'an touches the natural fear that exists within the human soul. This is an extremely inspiring touch. It removes that fear at once, and an unshakable truth about life and death is stated. Furthermore, the treatment of people by Allah after death and the mention of reward and punishment are brought up.

﴿It is not for any soul to die except by the permission of Allah, at a term appointed. And whoever desires the reward of this world, We will give him thereof; and whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, We will give him thereof. And We will reward the grateful.﴾

"No living being can die without the permission of Allah. The time of death is written down. Whoever acts with the intention of worldly reward, We will give him from the world itself, and whoever acts with the intention of the reward of the Hereafter will obtain the reward of the Hereafter, and We will certainly reward those who are grateful."

For every person there is a written and fixed time of death, and no one can die before living out that written term. Therefore fear, dread, panic and agitation cannot advance the term of life by a single moment. Courage, steadfastness, initiative and loyalty do not reduce a person's lifespan. Shame on cowardice! May the eyes of cowards be deprived of sleep! The day appointed for each person cannot be reduced by a single day, nor increased.

By stating this truth, the reality of destiny and of the appointed term settles into the human soul. Therefore the human soul stops brooding over it and pays it no heed at all. Its thought is then devoted entirely to fulfilling duty, keeping covenants and meeting the demands of faith. As a result, it is freed from the bonds of greed and miserliness, and it also gains control over fear and agitation. Now it moves forward on the path of truth, confronting all its difficulties and fulfilling its obligations with great patience, calm, and reliance upon Allah, because according to this new outlook, the time of death is in the hand of Allah and is written.

Let us go one step further. Once it is settled that the lifespan is written and the time of death is determined and fixed, it is shown that the real concern is that you should look at your earnings, to see what preparation you have made for that coming time, and what further gain you intend. The soul is asked: look at your earnings, to see what preparation you have made for that coming time, and what further gain you intend. The soul is asked: O soul! Do you wish to cast aside the requirements of faith and confine success and failure within this world alone, living only for this world? Or are your eyes also fixed on the higher horizon? Do you have concern for a far greater world beyond this limited one? Alongside the grief and arrangements for this limited life in this world, do you also have the intention of the Hereafter?

﴿Whoever desires the reward of this world, We will give him thereof; and whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, We will give him thereof.﴾

There is a great difference between these two lives, and a great distinction between these two intentions, even though in both cases the time of death is the same as what is appointed. The difference is this: the one who lives only for this world and seeks only its recompense, what difference is there between his life and the lives of insects, worms and beasts? Both have an appointed time. But the one whose eyes are fixed on the abode of the Hereafter lives a noble and generous life worthy of humans. Allah has chosen him; he is the vicegerent of Allah on this earth, and he too will depart from this world at its appointed time. ﴿It is not for any soul to die except by the permission of Allah, at a term written.﴾ ﴿No living being can die without the permission of Allah; the time of death is written.﴾

﴿And We will certainly reward the grateful.﴾ Who are these? They are those who attain the station of humanity and value the honour that Allah has bestowed upon man. Therefore they keep themselves a little above the level of the animals, offer thanks to Allah, and this gratitude takes the form of fulfilling the requirements of faith.

In short, in this manner, after fixing the reality of life and death in the mind and, in relation to the goals and priorities of life, letting people choose for themselves, the Holy Qur'an places before humanity two paths and invites them to reflect on which path they choose: whether they choose the life of insects and worms, or the life of honoured humanity. Thus the human soul, abandoning fear of death and agitation over the hardships of the world, is inclined to move towards a more beneficial task, and it makes this choice by its own discerning will, because it can adopt either of the two paths. If it wishes, it may take the path of the world; if it wishes, it may take the path of the Hereafter. Whichever path it takes, it will receive its recompense.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 3, verse 146:

After this, the Noble Quran, by way of example, presents the example of the believers of earlier times. This is because throughout the long history of humanity, on the paths of life, the caravan of faith has always continued to move onward. This example is of those who remained true to their promise of faith. They displayed valour alongside their prophets. When they were afflicted with calamity, they did not lament and wail. And in that place of jihad, they strictly observed the etiquette of faith. They kept looking death in the eye, and not a single "uff" was heard from their mouths; they only kept seeking forgiveness from Allah. They regarded even their minor mistakes as a grave fault and described them as "israf" (extravagance). They sought help from their Lord against the disbelievers only through patience and steadfastness. And it was this conduct of theirs because of which they attained the reward of both worlds. This reward was given to them because they, with extreme humility, raised their hands in supplication, and remained firm on the fronts of jihad with goodness and sincere intention. This is why they became an example for the Muslims.

The calamity of defeat that befell the Muslims at Uhud was the first calamity of this kind. Before this, at Badr, Allah had granted them victory, even though they were many times fewer than their opponents. After that victory, the notion had settled in their minds that this victory was perhaps, for them, a cosmic Sunnah of Allah. But the experience of Uhud was sudden for them. They were confronted with an unexpected trial.

This is why the Quran made its longest commentary on the incident of Uhud. In it, at times the believers are consoled, and at times they are sharply rebuked; at some places their words are affirmed, and at others they are made to understand through parables. Thus their souls were trained, the correction of their outlook on life was made, and they were prepared for the battles that lay ahead, because their path was long, they faced difficult stages, heavy duties were placed upon them, and the great revolution of which they were the representatives was a monumental matter.

The example presented here is a general example. In this example, no single prophet is spoken of, nor is any single nation spoken of; rather, the caravan of faith is spoken of. The etiquette of the believers is spoken of. It is shown that trial is a stage that comes before every call and every religion. All the followers of the prophets are your predecessors. Therefore the caravan of faith is in reality one, and it is one continuous succession. It is made clear that the outlook on life is one, and that all of them are regiments of one single army of faith.

﴿And many a prophet has fought, and with him many devoted servants of Allah. They did not lose heart for what befell them in the way of Allah, nor did they weaken, nor did they submit. And Allah loves the patient.﴾

"How many prophets have passed before, alongside whom many worshippers of Allah fought. They did not become broken-hearted at the hardships that came upon them in the way of Allah; they showed no weakness, and they did not bow before falsehood."

Many prophets have passed away alongside whom Islamic communities fought. They did not show weakness. The difficulties that came upon them, the trials and hardships they faced, the pain and sorrow in which they were afflicted, was not less than what you suffer; yet they did not show weakness. They did not end this struggle. They neither bowed before those difficulties nor before their enemies. Such is the stature of the believers, because they are striving for faith and for a way of life. ﴿And Allah loves the patient﴾ ... "Allah loves such patient ones." Those whose souls do not show weakness, whose strengths do not become feeble, whose resolve does not soften. They neither bow nor submit. This expression, that Allah loves the patient, is an extremely effective expression. It carries a special allusion. This love and this message of love is a balm for all pains and sorrows; through it all wounds are healed, and all bitterness and all fatigue come to an end.

Here, only the outward stance of those earlier believers has been mentioned, that they adopt this steadfastness in the face of outward difficulties. But the following verse depicts their inner states and the portrait of their faith and consciousness. It is shown how humble they are before the Divine Presence. It shows how they confront the fear that overtakes their souls, which is stupefying and extremely terrifying, and which fully seizes the human soul, because the danger is certain. Yet even such fear and danger cannot affect the attentiveness of these believers toward Allah; even in such circumstances they keep their connection with Allah. And in such circumstances, on the surface, the only demand a person could make would be: "O Allah, grant us victory." But they ask only for forgiveness and pardon in this way; thereby they, in effect, acknowledge their shortcomings and errors in discharging their duty. And after that, they pray for steadfastness and for victory over their enemies.

Their prayer was no more than this: "Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excesses in our affairs, make our feet firm, and help us against the disbelieving people."

Their request was not for any wealth or blessing. They did not ask for any reward, neither the reward of this world nor the reward of the Hereafter. They stood before the Lord of Majesty with great reverence. They turned toward the Divine Being even though they were in the state of battle. Even in that state they asked only for the forgiveness of their sins and prayed only for steadfastness. They prayed for success against the disbelievers. Even that victory and triumph they did not seek for themselves alone; in it they also ask for the defeat of disbelief and a fitting punishment for the disbelievers. This is the respect and courtesy before the court of the Lord, Most High, which He deserves, and which is the custom of the people of faith.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 148:

This is the example of the believers, who ask nothing for themselves, even though Allah has given them everything. He gave them what a seeker of this world could ever wish for, and He also gave them everything that a seeker of the Hereafter could wish for. ﴿So Allah gave them the reward of this world and the excellent reward of the Hereafter.﴾

Now Allah bears witness that these people were among the muhsinin (those who do good). They displayed the finest etiquette in the presence of Allah, and they displayed the finest conduct in jihad. Therefore Allah announced that He loves them, and this is a blessing more valuable than every kind of reward. ﴿And Allah loves those who do good.﴾ ﴿Allah loves such righteous people.﴾

The paragraph ends in this manner, presenting the most fundamental truths of the Islamic conception of life, through which the first Islamic community was excellently trained, and which are a source of insight for every movement that arises in every generation and for the ummah of every age.

Now this commentary moves one step further. Some more events of this battle are placed before us so that vision-giving conclusions may be drawn from them. The ideological correction of the believers, the training of their souls, and their being made aware of where on this path there is a danger of slipping, and being told that snares of conspiracy are laid around them and the enemy is sitting in ambush.

The truth is that because of the defeat at Uhud, the disbelievers of Madinah, the hypocrites and the Jews got the opportunity to plot afresh, because until then the people of Madinah had not become sincerely well-disposed toward the Muslims. In that city the Muslims were still strangers. The Battle of Badr had established a barrier of awe and dominance around this strange movement and this new plant, because the Muslims had achieved a thoroughly decisive victory at Badr. When defeat occurred at Uhud, this situation changed. These hidden enemies of Islam got the opportunity to express their inner malice and hatred, and to carry out poisonous propaganda within society. In the households in which people had been martyred, or in which people were severely wounded and there was an uproar, the way was paved for their poisonous propaganda and conspiracies, so these people now began openly to engage in intrigues.

In the coming paragraphs the major events of this battle are depicted and its important episodes are recorded. Allah first warns the Muslims not to follow the disbelievers: you will be victorious, and the awe of you will be re-established in the hearts of the disbelievers. They are told that at the beginning of the battle you achieved victory, and this was according to My promise, which you wasted by showing weakness, by disputing among yourselves, and by disobeying the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). After this, both aspects of that battle are presented to them in a living and vivid form: the disarray after the rout, then the provision of reassurance and tranquillity for the believers, and the grief and despair in the hearts of the hypocrites, whose thoughts about Allah were not good. They are also told that in this battle Allah's subtle wisdom was at work in turning the course of events toward defeat, and that death has a fixed appointed time. So they should beware of the misleading propaganda through which the disbelievers are spreading error, and know that in the end they must all be presented before Allah, whether they die a natural death or are martyred, for the destination is in any case that place.

If this set of verses is examined closely, it contains a large amount of vivid, lifelike imagery. Apart from these scenes, the most fundamental truths of both human life and the Islamic concept of life are established in it. It also states some unalterable principles of the universe. As for that battle, its glimpses are presented full of life, with great speed and great depth. No important aspect of the battle has been left out, and it has been recorded in such a way that reading it stirs a tumult in both the mind and the emotions. In truth, the entire living atmosphere of the battlefield, with its details, circumstances and events, has been recorded in these verses. They also point to the unease that arises in the human conscience and to conscious and unconscious movements of the heart. Because of this, all the events described in the detailed books of the Sirah (biography) of the Prophet (ﷺ) come to mind, and as a result of this reflection, the real truths of the Islamic concept of life are seen moving in living form, building the correct concept of life for Muslims.

There is no doubt that to record all the observations and all the realities of this battle, in such a small number of words and sentences, in a manner full of life, and with this particular style of movements and allusions, is not possible for any human expression. Nor is there any parallel to it in the history of human literary eloquence. Only the one who knows the secrets of the style of expression and the limits of human capacity for expression can grasp this, especially those who deal with difficult expressions and who have insight into the art of interpretation.

*"O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will become losers. Rather, Allah is your Protector, and He is the best of helpers."* (3:149–150)

In the Battle of Uhud, the Muslims suffered defeat. A large number were killed and a large number were wounded. This gave the disbelievers, the hypocrites and the Jews of Madinah the opportunity to rise again and to frighten the Muslims about the consequences of supporting Muhammad (ﷺ). They informed them of the horrors of war, and especially frightened them about the consequences of further confrontation with the polytheists of Makkah and the allies of the Quraysh. Clearly, this atmosphere of defeat and collapse was very well suited to shaking hearts, scattering the Islamic ranks, creating distrust in Islamic leadership, casting doubt on the benefits of continuing the policy of insisting on confrontation with stronger powers, showing the advantage of abandoning that policy, promoting talk of reconciliation with the victors, and arousing personal grief and sorrow in this regard. These people wanted to use this atmosphere to uproot the community of believers, and then to carry it on to the eradication of the Islamic worldview, and to persuade the people of Islam to bow before those stronger than themselves.

For this reason, Allah, the Exalted, warned the Muslims in severe terms against obeying the people of disbelief in matters of policy. If they follow them in this matter, the result will certainly appear in the form of loss. There will be no gain and no benefit in it. Rather, the outcome will be that they will return on their heels into disbelief. For the believer there are only two paths: either he remains continuously at war with disbelief and its people, and continuously struggles against falsehood and its people; or he turns back on his heels and apostatizes. We seek refuge in Allah from that. Apart from these two paths, there is no third path, such as separating oneself, standing neutral, remaining in between, and yet holding firm to one's position and protecting one's religion. It may be that such a thought occurs to a person, especially in the atmosphere of defeat in this battle, when, struck and wounded, he thinks that it may be possible for a believer to withdraw from the confrontation with the dominant powers, to reconcile with them, to follow them, and, at the same time, to protect his religion, keep his belief correct, keep his faith intact, and keep his existence intact. But this thinking is a dangerous illusion, because whoever does not advance in this struggle between truth and falsehood will certainly be pushed backward. Whoever does not struggle against disbelief, evil, falsehood, misguidance and disobedience will certainly be humiliated and disgraced, will turn back on his heels, and will enter into disbelief, evil, misguidance, falsehood and disobedience. His faith will not be able to save him, and his worldview will not be able to save him. And if, at the same time, he is following the disbelievers, listening to them and relying on them, then in reality that person has abandoned the position of his faith and his worldview. He has already been defeated spiritually, because when an ideological person bows before his opponents, he has already broken spiritually. For now he is influenced by their whisperings and takes guidance from them. This is indeed defeat. He can then at any time return to the belief of disbelief, and no one can save him from this final defeat. Although at first he may not realize that he has fallen onto a path whose end will be regrettable. The true believer is one who, because of his belief and his leadership, becomes independent of his ideological enemies and the enemies of his leadership, and whenever he lends an ear to those enemies, he has in effect begun a journey on his heels. This is a natural and practical reality, and Allah, the Exalted, informs the believers of it, warns them, and calls out:

*"O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will become losers..."*

What greater loss can there be than for a person to turn back on his heels and, after faith, to take up the path of disbelief once again? If faith departs, then what benefit can make up for its absence?

The question is: you may incline toward the disbelievers because you hope for their support, and because victory is with them at this time. This is a great delusion in which you are caught. Therefore, to refute this delusion, the address suddenly turns to the source of help and support:

*"Rather, Allah is your Protector, and He is the best of helpers."*

The guardianship of the Muslims returns to Allah. They can seek help only from Him. And when Allah is the one who helps someone, what need does he have for any other helper? When Allah is the helper of someone, what need does he have for any help from His servants?
