But this thinking is a dangerous illusion, because whoever does not advance in this struggle between truth and falsehood will certainly be pushed backward. Whoever does not struggle against disbelief, evil, falsehood, misguidance and disobedience will certainly be humiliated and disgraced, will turn back on his heels, and will enter into disbelief, evil, misguidance, falsehood and disobedience. His faith will not be able to save him, and his worldview will not be able to save him. And if, at the same time, he is following the disbelievers, listening to them and relying on them, then in reality that person has abandoned the position of his faith and his worldview. He has already been defeated spiritually, because when an ideological person bows before his opponents, he has already broken spiritually. For now he is influenced by their whisperings and takes guidance from them. This is indeed defeat. He can then at any time return to the belief of disbelief, and no one can save him from this final defeat. Although at first he may not realize that he has fallen onto a path whose end will be regrettable. The true believer is one who, because of his belief and his leadership, becomes independent of his ideological enemies and the enemies of his leadership, and whenever he lends an ear to those enemies, he has in effect begun a journey on his heels. This is a natural and practical reality, and Allah, the Exalted, informs the believers of it, warns them, and calls out:

*"O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will become losers..."*

What greater loss can there be than for a person to turn back on his heels and, after faith, to take up the path of disbelief once again? If faith departs, then what benefit can make up for its absence?

The question is: you may incline toward the disbelievers because you hope for their support, and because victory is with them at this time. This is a great delusion in which you are caught. Therefore, to refute this delusion, the address suddenly turns to the source of help and support:

*"Rather, Allah is your Protector, and He is the best of helpers."*

The guardianship of the Muslims returns to Allah. They can seek help only from Him. And when Allah is the one who helps someone, what need does he have for any other helper? When Allah is the helper of someone, what need does he have for any help from His servants?

Following this, the believers are consoled and given the good news that soon they will cast awe of the Islamic movement into the hearts of the disbelievers. This is because they associate others with Allah in His Divinity, and the ideology of shirk has no power or proof behind it in this world, while in the Hereafter a very evil abode has been prepared for them.

﴿Soon We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve, because they ascribed partners to Allah, for which He has sent down no authority. Their abode is the Fire, and wretched is the abode of the wrongdoers.﴾

This promise comes from Allah, the Mighty, the Lord of absolute power. He can cast awe into the hearts of the people of disbelief. He is responsible for determining how this confrontation will end; He guarantees that His friends will be victorious and His enemies will be defeated.

This promise of Allah remains valid even now for every confrontation in which the two sides are the people of disbelief and the people of faith. Whenever the people of disbelief face the people of faith, Allah casts the awe of the people of faith into their hearts. But the important matter and the important condition is that the reality of faith must exist in the hearts of the believers. They must have true awareness of Allah's help, have complete certainty that Allah is their helper, and have not the slightest doubt that Allah's army always prevails, that Allah keeps full control over His affairs, and that the disbelievers cannot defeat Allah nor get ahead of Him. Their situation must be bound to Allah's promise, which will certainly be fulfilled even if apparent circumstances seem to contradict it, because Allah's promise is always true, even if our eyes see otherwise.

The disbelievers come under awe because their reliance is not correct. Their trust is neither in power nor in the One who possesses power. They have associated with Allah gods that hold no power in their hands, because Allah did not take these partners to Himself by giving them any power.

The manner of expression that Allah has not sent down any "sultan" (authority) upon them carries a profound meaning. The Qur'an repeatedly adopts this manner of expression. Sometimes it says that false deities have no sultan, and sometimes it says that false beliefs have no sultan.

The reality is that every concept, belief, ideology, personality, and organization is as effective as the hidden strength and the impulse to dominate that it contains. The continuation and permanence of its struggle depends on the measure of this inner strength. And this inner strength depends on the measure of truth present within it, and on the degree of harmony between that strength and the truth upon which Allah has established this entire universe. Moreover, it is seen what degree of harmony exists with the laws and norms (sunan and nawamis) of this universe. Allah gives a person or institution only as much strength and authority as they are in harmony with the laws of nature that are effective and operative in this universe. If this harmony does not exist, then that person, ideology, or institution is hollow, flawed, weak, and destined to perish, however strong it may appear outwardly, however adorned it may be made to look, and however swollen it may seem.

The condition of the polytheists is that they ascribe other deities as partners with Allah. This shirk takes various forms. It begins when people give some attribute of Allah to someone other than Allah, or give to someone other than Allah some manifestation of Allah's attributes. Among these distinguishing features, the most important is the right of legislation, which He exercises for the various circumstances of His servants' lives, and the right to determine the values according to which people must make decisions regarding the affairs of their lives, both individual and collective, and that the right of sovereign rule over servants belongs to Allah alone, and that it is His exclusive right to require obedience to His laws and to the standards of good and evil He has established. After this, shirk occurs again in the acts of worship that are specific to Allah, that is, in worship (ibadat).

Now, consider this: what measure of the truth upon which Allah established this universe do these gods, whom the polytheists associate with Allah, possess? It is Allah alone who established this universe upon truth and created all creation so that they should acknowledge His servitude alone, not ascribe partners to Him, and take their law and standards of good and evil from Him alone, and worship Him alone in the manner that worship of Him is due, without any shirk and without any sharing. Therefore, any ideology that opposes the principles of Tawhid upon which this universe is founded from its very base is hollow, false, and opposed to the truth. This is the secret of its weakness and frivolity, and this is why it has neither strength nor authority within it, and cannot influence the current of life. Rather, it does not possess the fundamental elements (potentials) of life at all.

As long as the polytheists remain engaged in shirk (and shirk is a doctrine for which Allah has sent no authority), whether they practice it in the form of deities or in beliefs and concepts, they are in effect relying on weakness, emptiness, and illusion. Therefore they will always remain humiliated, degraded, feeble, and frail, and they will always be overawed whenever they face the believers, because the believers' trust rests on a truth that is majestic and powerful.

The fulfillment of this promise can be seen at any time whenever truth and falsehood clash. Many times it has happened that falsehood came against truth with its resources and abundant military equipment, while truth was unarmed; yet despite this situation, falsehood became frightened and overawed and began to tremble. It has continually trembled before every movement and every takbir slogan, although it had great armed hosts with it. But as soon as truth swooped down upon those great armies, falsehood cowered, scattered in panic and dismay. Agitation spread through its ranks, even though it was very large in number and resources, and truth was a tiny few in comparison. Thus the truth of this decree has been proven again and again: ﴿Soon We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve, because they ascribed partners to Allah, for which He has sent down no authority...﴾ "Soon We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve, because they ascribed partners to Allah, for which He has sent down no authority."

That was the matter concerning this world. As for the Hereafter, what will happen there is that their end will be extremely distressing and evil, and it will be befitting of these wrongdoers: ﴿Their abode is the Fire, and wretched is the abode of the wrongdoers.﴾

Here Allah presents the Battle of Uhud itself as an example of this principle. In the initial clash of that battle the Muslims had won a decisive victory. The polytheists were being killed until they fled. They abandoned their spoils, their standard fell and no one remained to lift it; only one woman had the courage and raised that standard. This victory was turned into defeat only when weakness entered the hearts of the archers. They rushed forward to gather the spoils, disputes arose among them, and they disobeyed the commands of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was both their Prophet and their leader. Thus the Qur'an, at the height of that encounter, directs attention to the events that occurred, the misfortunes that befell, the circumstances in which they happened, and the way they appeared to unfold, in a very striking and vibrant manner full of life and movement. Read carefully:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 152:

Here the Qur'an has fully painted all the scenes of the battlefield through words. It shows the scenes of both victory and defeat. In the form of words, a reel can be seen moving, in which all the scenes of the battlefield come forward one after another. Rather, inner treachery, the postures of bodies and the prick of conscience are all clearly visible. It conveys the meanings of its expressions in such a way that it is as if it were a reel showing scenes. In every movement a fresh picture appears, moving and alive, especially the scene when people are fleeing up the mountain while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is calling them, but they do not listen to a single one of them. They are terrified, they are distressed, and they are going upward to turn their backs and flee, abandoning the battle. Alongside these images, inner whisperings, states of the heart, impressions and disquiet are also clearly visible. Such a great quantity of living, moving and walking images, and then within them decisions, guidance and excellent commentary, and all of this in this same brief passage. This is the unique style of expression of the Holy Qur'an, and this is the unique method of training of the Holy Qur'an.

﴿And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them with His permission...﴾ "Allah fulfilled the promise of help that He had made to you. At the beginning, by His command, you were killing them." This is the initial picture of the battle, when the Muslims had begun to slay the polytheists. "Tahussunahum" means "tuhmidūna hissahum" (you were extinguishing their sense) or "you were uprooting them completely." This was before the desire for spoils could mislead them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had told them, "You will be granted victory, but only as long as you remain patient." So this word proved true.

﴿Until, when you lost courage and disputed about the matter and disobeyed after He showed you that which you love, among you are those who desire this world and among you are those who desire the Hereafter...﴾

"Until, when you lost courage and disputed about the matter and disobeyed after He showed you that which you love; among you are those who desire this world and among you are those who desire the Hereafter." This is an assessment of the condition of the archers. Some of them were deceived by the spoils of war. A dispute arose between them and those who wished to fully obey the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The matter reached the point that they decided on disobedience and rebellion, especially when they saw the signs of victory with their own eyes. Two groups arose among them: one group intended the spoils of war, and the other preferred the reward of the Hereafter. Discord arose within their hearts, and unity was lost in the ranks of Islam, and neither was their aim one. Greed clouded sincerity, although in ideological wars sincerity is the first condition. This is because an ideological war is different from others. It is fought on one side on the battlefield, and on the other side it is also fought within the human conscience itself. Until victory is achieved on the field of conscience, victory on the battlefield is not possible. It is a war that is solely for Allah, so those who succeed in it are only those whose hearts become purified for Allah. When they raise the banner of Allah, Allah grants them help only then. When Allah sifts them and makes them pure, and they succeed only in His battles, although they are raising the banners of falsehood. There is also wisdom in this, the knowledge of which belongs only to Allah. But those who raise the banner of truth and then are not single-minded for the truth, are not sincere, such people Allah never grants help. They are put to trial until they are sifted and those who work for Allah become perfectly pure. This is the matter that the Holy Qur'an wishes to make clear to the Muslim community in the light of its stance. This is the reality that is being impressed upon the first Islamic community at a time when it was afflicted with the bitter realities of defeat, it had received a painful blow, and this blow had come because of its own wavering stance. ﴿Among you are those who desire this world and among you are those who desire the Hereafter...﴾ (Ibn Kathir). Thus Allah opens up the state of their hearts before them; the secrets of their hearts are made manifest, and they come to know why defeat occurred, so that they may avoid it in future.

Along with this, Allah also makes clear to them one aspect of His wisdom and planning: the hardships they had to endure and these events, which occurred purely due to apparent causes. But see the power of Allah: ﴿Then He turned you away from them to test you...﴾ "Then Allah turned you back from the disbelievers in order to test you." The reality is that behind all the actions of a human being, destiny is at work. When they showed weakness, disputed among themselves and disobeyed orders, Allah turned back their strength; their power was ended, they could not perceive the arrival of the polytheists, and the archers were removed from the pass. Even those fighting on the field were pushed back. They began to flee. All these events occurred in such a way that they were the result of their own deeds. But behind these apparent events there was also wisdom and planning: that Allah wished to put the believers to trial, to test them by subjecting them to the most severe conditions, fear and panic, slaughter and wounding, and defeat and failure. And as a result of these difficulties, the hidden corners of those hearts would also come to light; hearts would be purified, and weak people would be separated from the ranks, as will be explained later. It is the case that events appear outwardly as the result of their apparent causes, but even while these apparent causes exist, planning is at work behind them. Therefore there is no contradiction between the two. Behind every event there is an apparent cause, and behind that apparent cause the wisdom and planning of Allah are also at work, and this planning comes from the All-Subtle, the All-Aware.

﴿And Allah had certainly pardoned you...﴾ "And the truth is that Allah pardoned you nonetheless." That is, Allah pardoned your weakness, mutual dispute and disobedience. Thus, that you fled and turned back on your heels, all of this Allah pardoned. And this pardon is purely His grace and generosity. He pardoned your human weaknesses and overlooked them, because your intention was not evil, and you were not insisting on error; for this weakness and this error of yours lie within the circle of faith. You bow before Allah and also submit before the commands of your leadership. ﴿And Allah is full of bounty toward the believers.﴾

His first bounty is that He pardoned them. As long as they remain upon the Islamic system, they affirm their servitude to Him. They do not themselves claim the divine attributes of lordship and sovereignty; they do not themselves set up for themselves a way of life, a system of law, values of life, and measures of good and evil, but take them from Allah alone. If, while accepting this principle, some error occurs from them due to human nature, weakness, temporary zeal or temporary desires, it may be pardoned; yet for errors a punishment through trial is certainly given, so that that impurity may be removed and that weakness may be removed.

Then the scene of that defeat is presented in this way: "When you were fleeing up the slope, not turning to look at anyone, while the Messenger was calling out to you from behind you..." (Qur'an 3:153)

"Remember when you were running away, paying no heed to anyone, while the Messenger was calling you from behind." This is reminded so that this image is firmly engraved upon their sense of awareness, so that they feel shame, modesty and remorse in their place, and reflect upon the causes of the weakness, mutual dispute and disobedience that arose from them.

This verse portrays their physical movements and their psychological states in such few words that there is no parallel to it. In this picture it is clearly visible that they are climbing upward on the mountain while fleeing, that they have been overawed, that they are terrified and in severe agitation. No one looks at anyone else. No one answers another's call. The Messenger ﷺ was calling out so as to reassure them that he was alive, but they did not hear, because someone had given out the cry that Muhammad ﷺ had been killed, and because of this their hearts were shaken and their footing had given way. In short, it is a complete portrayal, but in a few words.

The outcome of this conduct was that by fleeing from Allah and leaving the Messenger of Allah ﷺ alone, and by the grief they caused him ﷺ, Allah the Exalted gave them much grief in return. They were regretting their deed, that they had left the Messenger of Allah ﷺ alone. The Prophet ﷺ was wounded, yet he remained steadfast while they had fled, "so that you would not grieve over what escaped you, nor over what afflicted you." For the experience they went through and the blows that fell upon the Prophet ﷺ were unbearable for them. Seeing him, they forgot their own distress, and the calamities became small in their eyes. "So He rewarded you with grief upon grief, so that you would not grieve over what escaped you or what befell you." (Qur'an 3:153) That is, at that time Allah repaid your conduct by giving you grief upon grief, so that in future you would learn that you should not be sorrowful over what slips from your hand or over whatever calamity descends upon you.

And Allah knows even the hidden matters. The reality of your deeds is well known to Him, and He is aware of the motive behind all your movements. "And Allah is All-Aware of what you do." (Qur'an 3:153)

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 154:

When the fear and panic of that defeat subsided and its confusion ended, a strange tranquillity descended upon the believers. The believers, who had returned to their Lord and gathered around the Prophet ﷺ, were overcome by a strange drowsiness. They attained an incomprehensible calm and were content. The description of this new, miraculous atmosphere of peace and tranquillity is extraordinarily striking. It is an atmosphere that is extremely clear, gentle and pleasant, and its melody and pleasant shade are depicted in these words:

ثُمَّ أَنْزَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ الْغَمِّ أَمَنَةً نُعَاسًا يَغْشَى طَائِفَةً مِنْكُمْ

﴿Then after distress He sent down upon you security, drowsiness overcoming a faction of you⦄

"After this distress, God again sent upon you a state of reassurance, such that they began to doze." This was an atmosphere through which the mercy of God was being manifested, and this special mercy descends upon His particular believing servants. This was a drowsiness, and when drowsiness comes upon fearful and anxious mujahideen, even for a moment, it has an enchanting effect upon their bodies. As soon as the drowsiness departs, they feel refreshed, as if they were a new creation. Tranquillity settles upon their hearts, and their bodies feel at rest. We cannot comprehend the reality, nature and mode of this drowsiness. I can only say that I myself have felt such a state in a condition of severe anxiety. I clearly felt that in it there was the dew of God's mercy, and so miraculous that our words are unable to describe it.

Tirmidhi, Nasa'i and Hakim narrated, through Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from Anas (رضي الله عنه), who related from Abu Talhah: "I raised my head on the day of Uhud and looked, and every person's head was bowed over his shield." Another narration from Abu Talhah is: "We were on the battlefield on the day of Uhud when a particular drowsiness overcame us. My sword would fall and I would pick it up, it would fall again and I would pick it up again."

One group was in this condition, while the other group was in a state of wavering faith. These were the people concerned only for their own lives, and they gave importance only to that. These people had not yet emerged from the concepts of jahiliyyah. They had not fully surrendered themselves to this movement, nor had they fully submitted to the decree of God. They were not content that the blow they had received was for the purpose of sifting among them; this had happened as a trial. It did not happen because God had handed His friends and supporters over to their enemies, nor had God issued a final decision that kufr, evil and falsehood had now achieved final victory and had gained complete control.

وَطَائِفَةٌ قَدْ أَهَمَّتْهُمْ أَنْفُسُهُمْ يَظُنُّونَ بِاللَّهِ غَيْرَ الْحَقِّ ظَنَّ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ يَقُولُونَ هَلْ لَنَا مِنَ الأمْرِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ

﴿But a group whose own selves had concerned them, thinking about God other than the truth, the thought of the jahiliyyah, saying, "Do we have any say in the matter?"⦄

"But another group, for whom everything of importance was only their own interest, began to make various ignorant assumptions about God, which were entirely contrary to the truth. Now these people say, 'Do we have any share in directing this affair?'"

The Islamic worldview teaches its adherents that their lives do not belong to them. They all belong to God, and when they set out for jihad in the way of God, they go out for God; they move for God and fight for God alone. In this act of jihad nothing is for their own selves. Then they surrender themselves to the decree of God, and they accept whatever circumstances the decree of God brings upon them, with complete submission and contentment, whatever may come.

As for those who give greater importance to their own selves, their thoughts and calculations revolve around themselves, their activity and all their arrangements are solely for themselves. These are people in whose hearts the reality of faith has not yet taken root. The second group mentioned here consisted of such people. The Qur'an considered it necessary to comment upon them. For this group, everything of importance was for their own selves. They were afflicted with grief and anxiety. The feeling was consuming them that they were wasting themselves and their abilities in a matter that was not clear to their minds. They thought that they had been compelled to take part in this battle against their will, that they had been thrown into it needlessly. Despite this, they had received this bitter blow, and they were paying a heavy price without cause: they were being killed, they were wounded, and as for their distress, there is no need to ask. These people are deprived of correct knowledge of God. They harbour suspicions about God like those of ignorant people, and the greatest of these suspicions was that God was squandering them in this battle, the arrangements of which had no place for them; they had merely been driven here so that they would die and be wounded. God neither protects them nor helps them; He has made them a morsel for the enemy. They ask, هَلْ لَنَا مِنَ الأمْرِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ ("Do we have any share in this affair?")

Included in their objection was also the fact that the plan drawn up by the leadership for this battle paid no heed to them. Perhaps this group's opinion was that the fighting should take place within Madinah and that going out to fight should be avoided; yet despite this, they had not returned with Abdullah ibn Ubayy. However, their hearts were not satisfied with this plan.

Before the discussion of their suspicions in this context is concluded, a brief reply is given in between, rejecting their objection. قُلْ إِنَّ الأمْرَ كُلَّهُ لِلَّهِ ("Say: Indeed, the whole affair belongs to God.") No one has any authority; neither their authority nor anyone else's authority exists. Earlier, God had already commanded His Prophet: لَيْسَ لَكَ مِنَ الأَمْرِ شَيْءٌ ("You have no share in the affair.") Therefore all the matters of this religion, its struggle in its cause, the establishment of its system, and the insertion of guidance into the hearts of people, are all for God. No human shares in these powers. The task of a human being is only to fulfil his duties and to meet the requirements of his pledge of faith. It is now solely God's task to determine what results this struggle produces and what He brings forth from it. At this moment God also exposes a hidden weakness within their hearts: يُخْفُونَ فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ مَا لا يُبْدُونَ لَكَ ("They conceal within themselves what they do not reveal to you.") Their question, "Do we have any share in the affair?", shows that in their conscious and subconscious minds was the notion that they had been thrown into a matter they had not entered of their own accord, and that because of the errors of leadership they had become a sacrificial lamb. Had they themselves drawn up the plan for this battle, it would not have ended this way. يَقُولُونَ لَوْ كَانَ لَنَا مِنَ الأمْرِ شَيْءٌ مَا قُتِلْنَا هَا هُنَا ("They say: If we had any share in the affair, we would not have been killed here.") Their real view is that, had they any share in the authority of leadership, they would not have been killed here.

This is a whisper that arises in hearts until they become pure and single-minded for the ideology. When such people suffer defeat at some occasion, when calamities befall them, when they must pay a price greater than their imagination and expectation, when they face unimaginably unpleasant outcomes, when that way of life has not firmly settled in their minds and hearts, and when they think that these calamities have fallen upon them merely because of the wrong policies of the leadership, and that had they themselves planned, there would have been great success: when people's mental state is such, then with this turbid perception such a person cannot think that behind all events lies the wisdom of God. He cannot think that behind all events lies the wisdom of God. They cannot think that this is a trial from God. In their view, in such a situation there is nothing but loss, and every kind of waste is simply waste.

To correct the thoughts and whispers of those who hold such notions, God places before them a very profound truth. That truth is the truth of death. Along with this, clarification is given about the wisdom hidden within trial. He says:

قُلْ لَوْ كُنْتُمْ فِي بُيُوتِكُمْ لَبَرَزَ الَّذِينَ كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقَتْلُ إِلَى مَضَاجِعِهِمْ وَلِيَبْتَلِيَ اللَّهُ مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمْ وَلِيُمَحِّصَ مَا فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ

﴿Say: Even if you had been in your houses, those decreed to be slain would have gone forth to their places of death. And this was so that God might test what is in your breasts and purge what is in your hearts. And God is Knowing of what is within the breasts.⦄ (3:154)

"Say to them: even if you had been in your homes, those for whom killing had been decreed would have gone out to their places of death. And this happened so that God might test what is in your breasts and sift out the impurity in your hearts; God knows well what is in the breasts."

Even if you had stayed in your homes and, responding to the call of Islamic leadership, not plunged into this battle, and had settled all matters by your own choice, then those among you for whom death had been written would have hurried out to their place of slaughter, because the time of death is fixed. It can neither advance nor be delayed. Every person has a place of death appointed for him, and every person will certainly be drawn to that place and will breathe his last there. When the hour of death draws near, that person will reach there on his own feet; he will come running. No one will drag him there, nor will anyone be the one who pushes him in that direction.

What a manner of expression this is: "to their place of rest." It is as though their place of slaughter is a soft bed upon which they are to rest. Their steps will become comfortably extended there. All people, in this world, are drawn towards their places of slaughter and their final resting places, and they are sometimes drawn to those places by motives that are incomprehensible to them; indeed, these motives are beyond their control. These motives are only within God's control, and He alone knows their outcomes. He has a particular disposal, and does whatever He wills. Therefore, if we are content with the resting place God has appointed, this will be to our benefit in spiritual peace, psychological tranquillity and the satisfaction of our conscience.

This is the decree of God, and the wisdom working behind it is: لِيَبْتَلِيَ اللَّهُ مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمْ وَلِيُمَحِّصَ مَا فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ ("And so that God might test what is in your breasts and purge what is in your hearts.")

There is no greater trial than that what is in the hearts be brought to light, and what lies at the bottom of the hearts rise to the surface. Impurity and hypocrisy are separated from it, and without any veneer or cover the true reality appears. This is a great trial for the things that are kept hidden in the treasury of the heart. The reality comes to the surface. This is the purification and clarification of hearts, such that no adulteration or impurity remains in them. In this way, beliefs become correct and appear in clear form, and no defect or adulteration remains in them.

وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ ("And God is Knowing of what is within the breasts.") Dhat al-sudur refers to the hidden secrets that lie at the bottom of hearts, that are present in the heart at all times, that are not separated from the heart and do not come into the light. God knows these secrets well. God makes these secrets manifest to people because people themselves are sometimes unaware of these hidden matters; that is, they lie in their subconscious, and certain events bring them to the surface.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 155:

Allah knows what was in their minds. They suffered defeat, and when they came face to face with the enemy in this battle, they turned and fled. They showed weakness and turned their backs. Why? Because they had disobeyed their commander. As a result, their souls were shaken. Through this opening, Satan entered their hearts and caused them to slip, and these people fell into error. He says:

﴿Indeed, those of you who turned away on the day the two hosts met, it was only Satan who caused them to slip because of some of what they had earned. And Allah has already pardoned them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.﴾

It may be that this refers to the archers, in whose hearts the greed for war booty stirred. Likewise, the thought also came into their hearts that perhaps the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would not give them their share. This was the matter that they earned through their weaknesses, and because of it Satan caused them to fall into error.

But, in its generality, it is a picture of the state of the human soul when a mistake occurs and is committed by it. It does not have control over itself. Its connection with Allah becomes weak. The balance of its personality is lost, and it no longer has control over itself. It falls prey to anxiety and whisperings. All of this happens because its connection with Allah is cut off, and it no longer has the assurance of Allah's good pleasure. This is the point at which Satan attacks. He enters the soul of the human being. Then he takes the reins of such a person in his hand, causes him to commit slip after slip, and this soul goes far away from the peaceful and firm court of Allah.

This is why the God-fearing people who fought alongside the prophets, when confronting the disbelievers, first turned to the weapon of seeking forgiveness (istighfar). For through istighfar, their attention turned towards Allah, their connection with Allah was strengthened by it, all anxiety and uncertainty was removed from their hearts, all whisperings were dispelled, and that door through which Satan could enter was closed. And this door always opens when the connection with Allah is broken, and the person comes out from His protection and refuge. When Satan enters through that opening, he makes their feet unsteady, and they begin to slip again and again, until he takes them far away from the refuge of Allah and leaves them wandering in a waterless desert.

Allah explains that His mercy has enveloped them, so Satan could not cut them off from Me. Therefore they were pardoned. Allah also introduces Himself to them, that He is Forgiving, Pardoning, and Forbearing. He does not cast out wrongdoers from His court, nor does He hasten to punish. When Allah knew that within them was the impulse to seek Allah and they wished to be joined to Him, and He knew that they did not want rebellion, nor did they want to escape, nor did they want to flee from the servitude of Allah, then He bestows His forgiveness upon them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 156:

Now the discussion of this theme concludes with an explanation of the reality of life and death, and it is shown how corrupt the views of the disbelievers and hypocrites are on this matter. The believers are called out and told to make their concept of life completely distinct from theirs. At the end, a different value of hardships and sacrifices is described. He says:

يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَقَالُوا لإخْوَانِهِمْ إِذَا ضَرَبُوا فِي الأرْضِ أَوْ كَانُوا غُزًّى لَوْ كَانُوا عِنْدَنَا مَا مَاتُوا وَمَا قُتِلُوا لِيَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ ذَلِكَ حَسْرَةً فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ وَاللَّهُ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ (156) وَلَئِنْ قُتِلْتُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَوْ مُتُّمْ لَمَغْفِرَةٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَحْمَةٌ خَيْرٌ مِمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ (157) وَلَئِنْ مُتُّمْ أَوْ قُتِلْتُمْ لإلَى اللَّهِ تُحْشَرُونَ (158)

"O you who believe! Do not be like those who disbelieve and say of their brothers, when they travel in the land or go out to fight: 'Had they stayed with us, they would not have died or been killed.' (Those are the sayings that Allah makes a cause of regret in their hearts.) It is Allah who gives life and causes death, and Allah sees what you do. And if you are killed in the way of Allah or you die, surely forgiveness from Allah and mercy are better than what they amass. And whether you die or are killed, it is to Allah that you will be gathered."

In the context of narrating the events of that battle, the connection of the verses is evident. These were the statements of the hypocrites of Madinah. These people had separated from the army of Islam at the very beginning of that battle. Likewise, the polytheists of Madinah also used to say such things. These people had not yet entered Islam, but ties of kinship existed between them and the Muslims. In the Battle of Uhud, those who were martyred became a topic for their hypocrite and polytheist relatives, who got the opportunity to create regret and despair in the hearts of their Muslim relatives. And these people repeatedly used the departure and killing of those who went to that battle to reopen fresh wounds among their relatives. There is no doubt that such statements and propaganda had very deep effects on the ranks of Islam, and these people created an atmosphere of despair and agitation. Therefore the Qur'an had to refute them here, in order to correct their false statements, their false beliefs and their false notions, in such a way that their own words turned back upon them.

One thing the disbelievers used to say was that had they been with us or had they returned, they would not have died. From this statement it becomes clear how great the difference is between a person who is a standard-bearer of an ideology and a person who has no belief at all. The outlook of both on the principles upon which life runs, in which there are both difficulties and ease, is very different. An ideologically committed person can well understand the cosmic laws of Allah in this universe. He is content with the decree and destiny of Allah. He knows well and affirms that he can only encounter what Allah has written, and that the pain destined for him cannot be averted, and the calamity not written for him cannot come. Therefore he does not wail and lament over a calamity, nor does he go beyond himself in joy. Neither does its effect fall upon his self, nor does that. He does not grieve over the fact that he did not say this or did not do that, so that he might have escaped such-and-such calamity or gained such-and-such benefit, when the matter has already been done and the time has passed. This is because the place for planning, destiny, proposals and opinions is the time when an event has not yet occurred, when some action and movement is yet to take place. When, after planning and consultation, he moves into action, then whatever results come out of it, he accepts them with great submission, contentment and peace. Yes, it is necessary that his movement conforms to the commands and prohibitions of Allah. He is certain that whatever happened happened according to Allah's destiny and His plan, exactly in accordance with His wisdom, and that it happened in the way it had to happen, although he himself supplied its causes through his movement and action. Thus there is a balance between the theory of action and acceptance of its results. It also creates a balance between reliance upon Allah and positive thinking. Because of it, every step of a person is correct and the conscience is at peace. As for those whose heart and mind are empty of this ideology and of the positive concept of life under it, they are always suspended in the air, always afflicted with anguish and worry. Their life passes in words such as "if only," "O that," and "alas."

Allah, while training the Muslim community in the light of the events of Uhud, in which calamities fell upon the Muslims like mountains, warns them in severe words lest their attitude become like that of those disbelievers who have no belief and no ideology, who remain constantly the prey of regrets. Whenever one of their relatives goes on a journey for trade and business and, by the decree of Allah, dies there, or at some time takes part in a battle and is killed, they say:

يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَقَالُوا لإخْوَانِهِمْ إِذَا ضَرَبُوا فِي الأرْضِ أَوْ كَانُوا غُزًّى لَوْ كَانُوا عِنْدَنَا مَا مَاتُوا وَمَا قُتِلُوا

"O you who believe! Do not be like those who disbelieve, who say of their brothers when they go out on journeys or take part in battle (and meet with some mishap there): 'Had they been with us, they would not have died or been killed.'" They say these things because their thinking about this universe is wrong. They do not understand that behind the events of this universe the hand of divine power is at work. They can only see as far as the apparent causes appear. They can only see those superficial circumstances in which an event occurred. This is simply because their connection is not with Allah, and they cannot see the hand of power that is operating and pervading this universe.

"That Allah may make it a cause of regret in their hearts..." Their feeling is that the one who sets out for trade or goes out to a battle and meets with an accident or is killed there, the real cause of it is apparently his departure, and this is a false feeling. Because of it they remain constantly drowned in regret and grief, wondering why they did not forbid them from that journey or that battle. Had they known that the true cause and real reason was that the person's time had arrived, that he had to reach his death, that destiny was calling him, and that the Sunnah of Allah regarding life and death had already begun its work, they would not have drowned in such regret and grief. They would have remained patient and composed in that trial, and in it they would have been content with the decree and would have returned to Allah, and they would have said: "And Allah gives life and causes death..." "And Allah sees what you do."

Now another truth comes under consideration. Does death or killing end life? Is life better than the reward that Allah will give? No. There are other values of life too; there are aspects that deserve consideration in the scale of Allah:

﴿And if you are killed in the way of Allah or die, forgiveness from Allah and mercy are better than what they accumulate.﴾ (157) ﴿And if you die or are killed, to Allah you will indeed be gathered.﴾

"If you are slain in the way of Allah, or die, the forgiveness and mercy of Allah that will come to your share are better than all those things which these people gather. And whether you die or are slain, in the end you will all be gathered and brought together to Allah."

In short, death and being killed in the way of Allah, under these conditions and restrictions, is far better than life. It is better than all the worldly interests and wealth and property that people are gathering day and night. It is better than the honour and respect that people strive for. This death is better because as a result one attains the mercy and forgiveness of Allah. In the revealing scale of Allah, this is better than all the things they gather. This forgiveness and mercy is what the believer truly seeks. And Allah, in this station of life and death, does not hand people over to personal superiority and human aims and heights of glory; rather, they are shown what is with Allah, their hearts are attached to the mercy of Allah, and the mercy of Allah is declared to be better and more precious than the wealth and property of the world. It is declared to be superior and more precious than all the possible aims of the world.

All people will return to Allah; all people will be raised up on the Day of Judgement and presented before Him. Whether they die on their beds, or die on a commercial journey on the surface of the earth, or are martyred during jihad fi sabilillah, they will indeed go to Allah. Their final outcome is that they must present themselves there. If there is any difference, it lies only in the viewpoint of people, their aims and their conduct. As for the actual practical outcome, there is no difference. At a fixed time, in a fixed place, according to the written decree which is unalterable, every person will certainly die. Thus he will return to Allah, and then at a fixed time on the Day of Resurrection he will be raised up on the field of gathering. There he will either be among those who receive the mercy and forgiveness of Allah, or he will go into the grip of the wrath and punishment of Allah. Therefore, the person who chooses a bad end for himself is the utmost fool, while he must die in any case.

Thus the reality of life and death settles in hearts. The lesson of Allah's decree is given, and thus the hearts of believers become content while observing the events of destiny flowing on. They become content with the wisdom working behind the veil of destiny. They prefer the reward of the Hereafter that lies in trials. With this, the important events of the Battle of Uhud end here, and the discussion on their related matters concludes.

Now the context gives birth to a new subject. The subject of this theme is the personality of the leader of the revolution. It is told about the personal qualities of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), about the reality of prophethood, and about the important role of the Prophet's person and the reality of prophethood in the life of the Muslim Ummah. It is told how much the Divine Being is merciful and generous to this Ummah. Along with this theme, some other threads are also linked: what is the divine method for organising the Muslim community, and on what foundation this organisation is established, that is, upon which principles it has been founded and upon which realities it is built. Also, what is the importance of this conception of life, and what is the importance of this divine methodology for organisation, and then what effect this methodology will have upon all of humanity?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 3, verse 159 (part 1 of 2):

The theme and central axis of this passage is the reality of prophethood and the person of the Prophet. The facts related to this axis are taken up in it. Here one sees that great principles are stated in small phrases. The mercy of Allah is embodied and presented in the form of the character and conduct of the Prophet (ﷺ). His noble person is presented as extremely kind, extremely compassionate, extremely gentle and extremely easy to approach. One sees people gathering around him like moths. A large number of people remain around him at all times. Then in this gathering it is clearly seen that the community whose system rests upon the principle of shura (consultation) is established upon it.

It is commanded that this community make decisions by mutual consultation, even though the results of decisions made through consultation may be bitter. Then, alongside the principle of shura, it is also seen that decisions are to be made through wisdom and consultation, and then acted upon. And this action should be decisive. And after shura and resolve, one should act with reliance (tawakkul) upon Allah. When the plan is prepared, shura has taken place on it, and then this decisive action and its implementation (Execution) begin, and every kind of arrangement for it is made, then the stage of reliance upon Allah (tawakkul 'ala Allah) comes, and then the power of Allah begins its work. Then the Muslims entrust their affair to Allah. This is because in all matters the true doer and the true disposer is only the Being of Allah. No one else can exercise true disposal. All results are in His hand.

Along with these matters, it is also commanded that misappropriation of spoils of war (khiyanah fi al-ghanimah) is a very great crime. It reveals greed and avarice. It creates disorder within the community.

In this passage it is explained that there is a great difference and distinction between one who works for the pleasure of Allah and one who is on the path of disobedience to Allah and His wrath. There is a difference in their values and priorities. There is a difference in their measures of gain and loss.

Finally, the People of Islam and the People of the World are told that the prophethood of the Prophet (ﷺ) is a great blessing for you and a magnificent favour upon you, and the ordinary spoils of war for which you run are nothing in comparison with this precious treasure. Moreover, the hardships that have befallen you are nothing in comparison with obtaining this great treasure. This great wealth demands great sacrifice.

This is an army of guidance and meanings, which is presented in a few phrases and verses, enclosing an ocean in a jar.

فَبِمَا رَحْمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ لِنْتَ لَهُمْ وَلَوْ كُنْتَ فَظًّا غَلِيظَ الْقَلْبِ لانْفَضُّوا مِنْ حَوْلِكَ فَاعْفُ عَنْهُمْ وَاسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ وَشَاوِرْهُمْ فِي الأمْرِ فَإِذَا عَزَمْتَ فَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُتَوَكِّلِينَ

"O Prophet, it is by a mercy from Allah that you are gentle towards them. Had you been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have scattered from around you. So pardon them, ask forgiveness for them, and consult them in the affair. Then when you have resolved, put your trust in Allah. Indeed Allah loves those who put their trust in Him."

Here the address is directed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). But this is said keeping in view some weaknesses of the Prophet's people: that at first they were very enthusiastic about going out of Madinah; after that, disunity arose in their ranks. A third of the whole army returned even before the battle. After that the archers disobeyed the command of the Messenger (ﷺ). They showed weakness upon seeing the spoils of war. Then, when the false news of the death of the Messenger (ﷺ) spread widely, these people became weak, turned back on their heels and accepted defeat. The Messenger (ﷺ) remained steadfast with a small number, wounds came upon wounds, and companions abandoned him. Then he called out from below, but they were fleeing and paid attention to no one. In this situation the address turns towards the Prophet (ﷺ). Allah consoles him, and the Muslims are given the awareness and sense of how great the favour of Allah upon them is. Both the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Muslims are turned towards this. This embodied noble character is a great blessing of Allah, that people gather around its axis. Thus the hidden feelings of mercy in the heart of the Prophet (ﷺ) are stirred, and he patiently forgives all their lapses. On the other hand, they come to realise how great a favour has been bestowed upon them through this compassionate and merciful Prophet. And the Messenger (ﷺ) is commanded to also seek forgiveness for them, and to continue consulting them as before, and lest, because of the unwanted results of the battle of Uhud that came out of consultation, he should stop such an important matter as mutual shura.

فَبِمَا رَحْمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ لِنْتَ لَهُمْ وَلَوْ كُنْتَ فَظًّا غَلِيظَ الْقَلْبِ لانْفَضُّوا مِنْ حَوْلِكَ……… "O Prophet, it is by a great mercy from Allah that you are very gentle towards them. Had you been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have scattered from around you."

This was the mercy of Allah which also encompassed the Messenger (ﷺ), and made him loving, compassionate and gentle towards them. And it was also a mercy for them, in that because of his gentleness he did not call them to account. Had you been hard-hearted and narrow-tempered, this assembly would have dispersed, and people's thoughts would not have been in harmony with you. Common people need a kindly court where they are treated with great indulgence, where they are welcomed with a cheerful face, where they receive love, where their mistakes, weaknesses and shortcomings are overlooked; where the leader is of so big a heart that he gives them everything but takes nothing from them; where the leader takes upon himself the difficulties of his followers but does not place excessive burdens upon them; and where followers always receive indulgence, consideration, a cheerful face, gentleness, love and approval. The heart of the Messenger of Allah was such a heart, and his conduct with people was exactly like this. He never became angry on account of his own person; he never showed narrowness of heart because of human weakness. He never reserved for himself any worldly benefit; rather, whatever he received, he distributed everything among them with open hands. In short, his patience, forbearance, sympathy, love and nobility always covered them. And whoever among them spent some days of life together with the Messenger (ﷺ) or merely saw him once, became his devotee. Therefore the Divine Being gave him a great, compassionate and generous personality. And all this was a mercy of Allah upon him (ﷺ), and from another aspect a blessing upon his ummah as well.

By reminding them of this favour, Allah tells the Prophet (ﷺ) the principle upon which the organisation of the community of the ummah was to be based in future, namely: فَاعْفُ عَنْهُمْ وَاسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ وَشَاوِرْهُمْ فِي الأمْرِ……… "So pardon them, ask forgiveness for them, and consult them in the affair." This is a definitive text (nass qat'i) and an emphatic one. "Consult them in the affair." Islam makes this principle obligatory in the system of government, even though the head of state in that system is Muhammad (ﷺ). This definitive text leaves no room for doubt that in the Islamic system of governance, shura is a foundational principle. Apart from this, the system of Islamic governance cannot be established at all. As for the question of what form shura should take, and how the purpose of shura is to be achieved, these are matters whose form and shape may vary. Shura may be established in different forms according to the conditions of each region. Any form through which the purposes of shura can be fulfilled is acceptable. It must not be a mere show. That form and shape through which the true objectives are achieved will be Islamic.

It is worth noting that when this verse was revealed, a council of shura had already been held, and the battle of Uhud had been fought in accordance with the majority decision of the shura, and bitter results came out of it. Because of the holding of this shura, the first loss was that disagreement arose in the Islamic ranks, and opinions differed. Some people thought that the Muslims should fight while taking refuge in Madinah: when the enemy attacked, they should be engaged within the narrow lanes. But in opposition to this, an enthusiastic group held the opinion that they should go out of Madinah and engage in battle in the open field. Because of these differing opinions, the army of Islam became divided, and Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul got the opportunity to withdraw with a third of the army. This happened when the enemy was standing at the door. It was a great calamity, and there was apparently a large crack in the Islamic ranks. Then, the military plan that was prepared as a result of this shura clearly proved not to be a secure war plan, even from the military point of view. This is because that plan differed from the defensive history of Madinah, as Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, expressing his opinion in that council, stated this historical fact: whenever they had fought inside Madinah, they had succeeded. And in the battle of the Confederates, the Muslims themselves, correcting the plan of the battle of Uhud, decided to fight inside Madinah, and they succeeded too. They dug a trench and did not go out to face the enemy. This was because the experience they had gained in the battle of Uhud required exactly this.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) himself was also aware that going out of Madinah to fight would have dangerous consequences. Indications had already come to him through true dreams (ru'ya sadiqah). He knew well that his dreams were absolutely true. He had already interpreted them to mean that someone from his family would be martyred, and that his companions too would attain martyrdom. Moreover, in interpreting his dreams, he had designated Madinah as a protected shield. In these circumstances he had the right to veto the decision of the council of shura, but he implemented that decision reluctantly (Execute), although the difficulties, sacrifices and losses hidden behind it were being seen by his prophetic insight. This was because the principle of shura was being laid down, the community was being trained, and these matters were more important than the temporary losses.

The right course would have been, at least after the battle of Uhud, to abandon the principle of shura, since because of that shura differences arose and disunity appeared in the Islamic ranks, and this disunity occurred in difficult circumstances, and after the battle, frightening results came to light. But Islam had to bring into being an ummah, to train it, to prepare it to lead all of humanity, and Allah knew well that the best training of a people, and making it guided, can be achieved only upon the principle of shura. And that it had to be prepared to bear the results of shura as well. Through it mistakes had to be allowed to occur, however great they might be, so that in future it could advance in the light of its experiences, however bitter the results might be, and be able to correct itself. And so that it could bear the good or bad consequences of its own opinions. For as long as a mistake does not occur, it cannot correct itself at all. If, as a result of some loss, a community comes into existence that is experienced, discerning and able to bear consequences, then those losses have no significance left. But if a people's losses and lapses are limited, yet it is deprived of experience, then that ummah will remain inexperienced in the same way that a child remains inexperienced. It is under supervision at every step. In such a state, like a child, that people can be protected from material losses, but neither can other material benefits be made available to it. Psychologically, that people suffers a loss; in spite of this its completion does not take place. Its training is deficient and it gains no experience of practical life. And its example is that of a child to whom nothing is given in hand.

Islam's policy was to produce a community that was experienced and mature. Its plan was to prepare this ummah for the guided leadership of humankind. Therefore it was necessary that this ummah become an adult community, and that in its practical life no helper be provided to save it from stumbling and falling, so that it might gain experience. And this experience was to be acquired during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and under his supervision. If, because of a far-sighted leadership, it had been appropriate that now there was no need for shura, and the training of the ummah was not necessary, and in dangerous events there was no need to consult with it and to follow its opinions, for example in stages such as the Battle of Uhud, because that was a decisive stage, when the Muslim ummah was a newly born community, surrounded by dangers from every side, with enemies lying in ambush on all four sides, then in such circumstances it would have been appropriate for the far-sighted leadership to make all decisions itself, and it had the right to do so. And in such circumstances there would have been no need for shura, since the conditions were dangerous. Moreover, at that time Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) was present and revelation was also coming, so in such circumstances the ummah could have been deprived of its right of shura. Especially in those circumstances, when all the bitter events at Uhud occurred precisely because of shura, although at that time this ummah was passing through an extremely dangerous and emergency situation, yet despite the blessed presence of the Messenger (ﷺ), despite the coming and continued coming of divine revelation, and despite the appearance of such bitter results of shura, and despite the existence of dangerous and emergency conditions, Allah did not abolish the right of shura. Whatever loss may occur, whatever discord and division may arise in the Islamic armies, whatever bitter results may appear, and whatever dangerous and emergency conditions may surround the newborn ummah around Madinah, all of these are necessary events compared with the great aim of bringing into action a mature and experienced ummah. The aim was that the ummah in practice be experienced, capable of digesting the consequences of good or bad opinions, and able to comprehend the outcomes of any opinion and action. This is the reason, and these are the reasons, why in such circumstances this verse was revealed: ﴿So pardon them, and ask forgiveness for them, and consult them in the matter……﴾ "Pardon them for their faults, pray for their forgiveness, and keep them as partners in consultation."

It was decided that even in the most dangerous circumstances this principle, the principle of consultation, must be maintained. And in circumstances like Uhud, and in circumstances after it, acting upon it would also be necessary. The purpose was that, for the future, no one should make an excuse, saying that since bad results may appear after consultation, therefore we abolish this principle. For example, the circumstances of Uhud are its best illustration: the enemy was knocking at the door, yet consultation also continued. Therefore a far-sighted ummah can come into being only when the principle of consultation is binding, and the far-sighted maturity of the whole nation is that precious goal for which small and large losses may be borne.

But the political picture and structure of the Islamic system cannot be complete until we reflect on the next part of this verse. It is evident that it is not necessary that the results of a consultative assembly always become a preferable and wise decision. Ultimately the decision will be that one matter is acted upon with reliance on Allah: ﴿And when you have resolved, then rely upon Allah……﴾ "And when a final decision has been made, rely upon Allah. Indeed, Allah loves those who rely upon Him."

The essence of shura is that various opinions come forward, and from the opinions presented in the assembly one is accepted. When a decision is made, the work of shura ends, and now the stage of implementation (Execution) begins. And for this critical stage great firm resolve and decisive action are needed. At this stage reliance upon Allah is needed. And the matter now goes to Allah; it is entrusted to the decree of Allah. Now it is the work of Allah's will to determine what decision and results He manifests. In the same way the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in his divinely guided manner, taught the lesson of shura to the ummah: he showed how opinions should be expressed, and how, after a decision, its consequences are to be borne, especially in dangerous circumstances. Likewise, the Messenger (ﷺ) gave a lesson regarding the implementation of the ummah's decisions and of a shura decision, and taught the manner of reliance upon Allah, and taught the method of surrendering oneself entirely to the decree of Allah. Yet he had a good understanding of how events would unfold; the course of events was within his knowledge. Nevertheless, he carried out the decision to fight outside Madinah. He entered the house and put on his armour and helmet. He knew well where they were going and what hardships and difficulties he and his Companions would face. Even when the enthusiastic people who were fighting outside gave counsel again and provided an opportunity for the decision to be changed, and by reading the blessed face of the Prophet (ﷺ) they perceived that their zeal had compelled the Messenger (ﷺ) to fight outside, although he did not wish it, and they returned the choice to him, saying that he could fight inside Madinah or outside, he did not take advantage of the opportunity to reconsider. Why? Because he wished to give them a lesson. He wanted to establish the example of the decisions of the shura (Parliament). He wished that once a decision was firm and final, then, instead of reconsidering again, it should be implemented, with reliance upon Allah, whatever happens, happens. He also wanted to show that a shura has one time: after a decision there should be no hesitation or wavering, and no decision should be remade again after fresh deliberation. For in this way nothing would remain final; decisions would keep changing, and if the example of repeated reconsideration were established, this process would never end. So there should be shura (Parliament), then a decision, then implementation, and reliance upon Allah, because Allah loves this. ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who rely upon Him.﴾

And the quality which Allah loves, and the people endowed with it whom Allah loves, it is the duty of the believers that this quality be found in them to the highest degree, and that they be greatly eager for it; indeed, it should be the distinguishing attribute of the believers. Reliance upon Allah and the surrender of oneself to Him is the balanced line of the Islamic outlook on life and the Islamic way of life. Now the matter is entrusted to the great reality of this universe: the reality that the final decision rests with Allah, and that it will be whatever He wills.

This was one of the great experiences of Uhud, and it was a great lesson. This lesson is a precious treasure for the Muslim ummah in every age and every era. It is not merely a matter of one period, but is for every period.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 3, verse 160:

To further impress upon the mind the reality of tawakkul (complete reliance upon Allah) and to establish and strengthen its principle, the next verse explains in some detail the reality that the true active power belongs to the Divine Being. Victory and success, as well as defeat and humiliation, are in His hand. Therefore, if you seek help, seek it from Him, and if you wish to be saved from defeat, humble yourselves before Him. Turn towards Him, rely upon Him, but only after complete preparation; be free from anxiety about the results, and leave the outcomes and consequences to Allah.

﴿If Allah helps you, no one can overcome you; and if He forsakes you, who is there that can help you after Him? So let the believers put their trust in Allah alone.﴾

Because of this, the concept of a believer becomes free from the idea that anything other than Allah can be sought. The thinking of a believer becomes directly attached to the One Who truly exercises control over this universe. Therefore, he withdraws from all those false gods and false means and does not seek their support or help. He relies on Allah alone for good outcomes, and expects from Him alone that He will set affairs on a good course and set them right by His wisdom. After this belief, whatever occurs as a result of the Divine decree, he accepts with great magnanimity. This is the balance of thought and outlook that human thought has found only under the shelter of Islam.

Following this, the discussion turns to prophethood and the special attributes of the Prophet, so that after this topic some instructions on trustworthiness and honesty may be given, for example that embezzlement and theft from the spoils of war (ghanimah) is a very reprehensible thing. And that whoever commits dishonesty in collective trusts will be held accountable for it, and every person will be given their due in full.

﴿It is not for a prophet to embezzle. And whoever embezzles will bring what he embezzled on the Day of Resurrection. Then every soul will be paid in full what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.﴾

"It is not the work of a prophet to commit dishonesty… and whoever commits dishonesty will come on the Day of Resurrection bearing his dishonesty, then every soul will receive full recompense for what it earned, and no one will be wronged."

The archers on the hill and the mountain pass of Uhud disobeyed the command and left their positions because they feared that, after the battle, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) might not give them any share. Likewise, after the Battle of Badr, some hypocrites spread propaganda that some items had disappeared from the spoils of war. And in this regard they were not even ashamed to avoid mentioning the name of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Therefore this verse brought this command and decisive ruling: that not even a prophet, including Muhammad, could ever do such a thing as moving something from the spoils of war here and there. That is, setting aside some item from the spoils of war, or giving a greater share to some soldiers, or in any way committing any kind of dishonesty.

﴿It is not for a prophet to embezzle…﴾ "It is not the work of a prophet to commit any dishonesty in the spoils of war."

This is contrary to his station. It is contrary to his disposition and the nature of prophethood. It is contrary to his character that he should do such a thing. In effect, the occurrence of this act from the person of prophethood is not even possible. Here, this negation is not a negation of permissibility or prohibition, because it is contrary to the trustworthiness, uprightness and pure nature and temperament of the Prophet that such a matter should occur from him. In some recitations the word is read as yughalla, that is, in the passive form, meaning that it is not permissible for dishonesty to be practised against the Prophet, and that his followers should not conceal anything from him. In this case the prohibition would be that his followers should not commit dishonesty against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and this recitation is more in harmony with the final part of the verse. The recitation of Hasan al-Basri (may Allah have mercy on him) was like this.

After this, those people are sternly warned that whoever commits dishonesty in the spoils of war or in other government property, this will be their end.

﴿…And whoever embezzles will bring what he embezzled on the Day of Resurrection…﴾ "And whoever commits dishonesty will come on the Day of Resurrection bearing his dishonesty; then every soul will receive full recompense for what it earned, and no one will be wronged."

Imam Ahmad, narrating through Sufyan, al-Zuhri, Urwah, and Abu Humayd al-Sa'idi, related that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appointed a man of the Azd tribe named Ibn Lutbiyyah as a collector of zakat. When he returned he said, "This is yours, and this was given to me as a gift." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then stood on the pulpit and delivered this address: "What is the matter with these collectors whom we appoint to tasks, and when they return they say, 'This is yours, and this was given to me as a gift'? Why did he not remain sitting in his father's or mother's house and wait to see whether a gift would be given to him or not? By Allah, in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, whoever takes anything from this property, on the Day of Resurrection he will bear it on his shoulder: if it is a camel, it will be bellowing; if it is a cow, it will be lowing; and if it is a sheep, it will be bleating." (Bukhari, Muslim)

Imam Ahmad also related with his chain from Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood among us one day and mentioned ghulul (theft from the spoils of war). He described it as a grave matter and a very great sin, and said: "On the Day of Resurrection, let me not find any one of you who comes with a camel on his shoulders, crying out, 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!', and I reply, 'I can do nothing for you with Allah; I had already conveyed the message to you fully.' Let me not find any one of you with a horse on his shoulders, neighing, who says, 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!', and I reply, 'I can do nothing for you with Allah; I had already conveyed to you fully.' And let me not find any one of you with a dumb animal on his shoulders who says, 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!', and I reply, 'I can do nothing for you with Allah; I had already conveyed to you fully.'" (Bukhari, Muslim; narrated by Abu Hayyan)

Imam Ahmad, with his chain, related from Hadrat Adi ibn Umairah al-Kindi that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O people, if any one of you is appointed as our agent and he steals from us a needle or more than that, he is a thief and he will bring it on the Day of Resurrection." Then a man of the Ansar, of dark complexion, stood up (Mujahid said that he was Sa'd ibn Ubadah; as if I can still see him now) and said, "O Messenger of Allah, I resign from my office; take over your work." He (ﷺ) said, "What has happened?" He said, "I have heard you say such and such, and I still say it: whoever we assign to a duty, let him bring whatever he gets, be it little or much. What he is given, let him take; and what is not given, let him refrain." (Muslim, Abu Dawud)

This verse and these traditions played a great role in the training of the Muslim community, until astonishing results emerged. A group came into being that was extremely trustworthy and honest, and so cautious regarding state property that its like is not found in human history, and in the whole of human history no such community was ever produced. It would happen that an ordinary Muslim would come across a very valuable item from the spoils of war which no one had seen, and he would bring it and hand it over to the commander. His own self could not lead him astray regarding it in any way, merely out of fear that on the Day of Resurrection he would meet the Prophet (ﷺ) in the condition mentioned above, and that he would be ashamed on the Day of Resurrection, about which the Prophet (ﷺ) had clearly warned them. In short, the life of the Muslims was such that concern for the Hereafter and fear of the Hereafter were a practical part of their lives and a part of their awareness, and this was the secret of their piety, fear of Allah, and extreme caution. The concept of the Hereafter was a living concept in their lives, not a dormant one. It was a promise that had been fulfilled; it was part of their certainty, in which there was no room for doubt or suspicion. They believed that everyone would be given full recompense and that no one would be wronged.

Ibn Jarir al-Tabari wrote in his history that when the Muslims camped at Mada'in, they gathered the spoils of war. A man came with a certain item and handed it to the treasurer. His companions said, "We have never seen such a valuable thing; the goods gathered by us are not as valuable as this item." So they asked him, "Have you taken anything from it?" He replied, "I have taken nothing, and by Allah, had it not been for Allah, I would not have brought it to you." Then the Muslims realised that this was an extraordinary person. The companions of the treasurer asked, "What is your identity?" He said, "I do not reveal my identity, lest you go about praising me, nor will I tell other people so that they go about praising my deed. I will praise only Allah and hope for His reward." They followed him, and when he reached his companions, they were told that he was Thabit ibn Abd Qays. (Tabari, vol. 4, p. 16)

In the time of Hadrat Umar, when the spoils of war were brought after the Battle of Qadisiyyah, among them was the crown of Kisra which he used to wear while sitting in his royal hall. It was extremely valuable. Hadrat Umar saw it and said that worthy are those soldiers who deposited it in the treasury, and said: "The people who brought this crown and gave it to their commander are, in truth, extremely trustworthy."

Such was the Islamic training of the Muslims; it appears so strange that its accounts seem like legends.

Now, after this discussion about the spoils of war and dishonesty within them, the Qur'an, in keeping with this context, mentions moral values.

﴿Can one who follows the pleasure of Allah be like one who has incurred the anger of Allah, and whose refuge is Hell, and what a wretched destination it is? They are of differing degrees in the sight of Allah, and Allah is Seeing of what they do.﴾

This is the far-reaching change under whose shadow those who are trained no longer regard the spoils of war as having any worth; even thinking about this world becomes trivial in their sight. The Qur'an is one of the lines of the method of training (manhaj tarbiyyah). These are wonderful impressions upon which this method trains human hearts. Their priorities themselves change; their horizons themselves change. Therefore they move forward toward the true goal of life, leaving aside the other fields.

﴿Is one who follows the pleasure of Allah like one who has incurred the wrath of Allah, and whose abode is Hell? And wretched is the destination.﴾

"Can it be that one who always walks on the pleasure of Allah would act like the one who has been enveloped in the wrath of Allah and whose final abode is Hell, which is the worst of abodes?"

These are the true values. This is the arena in which hope should lie. This is the field in which work should be done, and this is the field in which talk of gain or loss should take place. And how vast is the gulf between the person who seeks the pleasure of the Lord and succeeds in it, and the person who is on the path of wrath and has been overwhelmed by it, and has become deserving of Hell, which is indeed a very wretched abode.

This too is one station, and that too is another station, and between these two stations lies a vast gulf. "Hum darajatun 'indallah" ... "They are ranks in the sight of Allah." Each person reaches his station by merit. Therefore, in this matter there is neither injustice or excess toward anyone, nor unwarranted favouritism or partiality. "Wallahu basirun bima ya'malun" ... "And Allah is All-Seeing of what His servants do."

Now the passage turns to its main subject, the person of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It is explained that by making him a messenger, Allah has in fact bestowed a great favour upon the believers of Makkah, Madinah and the whole world. The believers should reflect upon this scheme of prophethood.

﴿Indeed, Allah conferred a favour upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger from among themselves, who recites to them His verses, purifies them, and teaches them the Book and wisdom, although before that they had been in clear error.﴾

"Indeed, Allah has bestowed a great favour upon the believers in raising among them a prophet from among themselves, who recites to them His verses, refines their lives, and teaches them the Book and wisdom, even though before this they were immersed in manifest misguidance."

The conclusion of this paragraph concerns the reality of Muhammadan prophethood. Here the personal status and rank of the Prophet (ﷺ) is described, this is presented as a great favour, and it is shown that he and his prophethood played an important role in the building and shaping of this ummah. It also mentions the education and training of this ummah, its leadership capacity, and its rise from manifest error to the lofty station of knowledge, wisdom, purification and cleanliness. All these matters contain diverse and profound Qur'anic sentiments that deserve reflection.
