These verses were initially revealed as a comment on the spoils of war: the greed for booty, the theft of some items, and being overly occupied with this trivial matter caused you to lose the battle of Uhud which you had been winning, and your victory turned into defeat. As a result, what you saw happened to the Muslim community. In this reference, the mention of the great office of prophethood and of this great favour, which is intended to make you feel, is very profound. Through it the Qur'an, in its particular manner, seeks to train the ummah. By mentioning this great office and explaining how great a favour it is, the intended impression for you is that all the spoils of war of the earth, all the wealth snatched from the whole globe, and all the goods and possessions of the world are nothing in comparison, have no importance and are not worth mentioning. In the presence of this great office and blessing, a Muslim feels shame even at mentioning these petty things; indeed, even thinking about them is a cause of embarrassment, let alone that any Muslim should take interest in them.

Then this thought-provoking indication is given at a time when the Muslims had suffered defeat, were afflicted with grief and sorrow, and precious lives had been lost in that battle. In such circumstances, by bringing forward the great work of the great office of prophethood, the aim is to remind them that they should also reflect upon the favours that came to them through this prophethood. This is a great favour which can be preferred over all other affairs of the world.

Then it is stated that, as a result of this great favour, you should also reflect upon the change that came about in you. The verses of Allah are being recited among you, your lives are being refined, you are being taught the Book, and then you are being made aware of wisdom, insight and technology. Although before this you had been immersed in clear misguidance.

﴿...who recites to them His verses, purifies them, and teaches them the Book and wisdom, although before that they had been in clear error.﴾

This verse shows that they had been transferred from one state to another through a revolution; one situation had changed and a completely new situation had come into being. One era had passed and a new era had arrived. Therefore the ummah is being given the awareness that this is a great revolution which is being brought about within this ummah purely through Allah's power, will, grace and favour. Then, through this ummah, the launching of this great revolution across the whole of human life began with the sending of the Muhammadan prophethood, which established this ummah and trained it. Therefore it is not appropriate for such a great revolutionary force to make decisions with petty things like spoils of war in view, or to lament excessively over small sacrifices, grief, defeat and breakdown. For these things are nothing in the path of this great revolution.

During the account of the Battle of Badr, these were a few indications concerning the importance and greatness of Muhammadan prophethood, which we have described here briefly. After this, it is appropriate that we shed light in detail on this Qur'anic verse, which is full of indications of wisdom and insight.

﴿Indeed, Allah conferred a favour upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger from among themselves...﴾ "Indeed, Allah has bestowed a great favour upon the believers in raising among them a prophet from among themselves..." This was a great favour of Allah, that He sent a messenger from among them. Then it was a second favour that the Messenger of the Noble Prophet (ﷺ) was also an Arab, from among them. The sending of a messenger by Allah to a people is in fact a pure favour and grace upon that people. It is a pure favour because there is no claim of entitlement on the part of that people to the sending of a messenger. If they had any claim, there would be some notable people for it; there is no group among people upon whom this kindness is being bestowed. It is purely the grace and favour of Allah that a messenger came among them, who recites to them the verses of Allah and conveys the words of Allah to them; and for this great bounty they had no cause or claim. This is purely the blessing of Allah.

This favour becomes greater and deeper from another aspect as well: this messenger is from among them, their own brother. The words "a messenger from among themselves" contain very profound indications. The connection between the believers and the Messenger is a connection of one soul with another soul. It is not a connection where an individual is bound to a people. It is not merely that he is one of them; rather a deeper and more exalted meaning is intended. Through faith they rise up and are connected with the Messenger, and purely through faith they reach that lofty station of honour and exaltation; and indeed this is a great favour upon the believers. Thus this favour is doubled: first, that a messenger was sent, and second, that this messenger is present among you, and they are with him, and this beloved bond is established between them.

After this, the practical effects of this favour appear: in their personalities, in their lives, and then in their history: "...who recites to them His verses, refines their lives, and teaches them the Book and wisdom..." Now the manifestation of this favour takes place on a broad and practical field. First, in the form of honouring them, this great favour appears: that He Himself, from His own side and according to His own plan, sent a messenger who addresses them through the word of Allah and recites to them the verses of Allah. If a human being were to reflect well upon this one favour of Allah alone, he would be overwhelmed with awe of Allah, would tremble, and would not be able to stand before Allah without immediately prostrating in gratitude.

If he thinks that Allah is showing him kindness, speaking with him, and introducing Himself to him so that the human being may know the reality of His divinity and His attributes; then that Lord addresses him, and addresses this humble servant of His, and the address concerns his life, answers his inner questions, discusses his actions and movements, and the matter is the programme in which the eternal life of this humble human being lies, and guidance is being spoken of, and this guidance is directed to the code in which lies the purity of his heart and the betterment of his conditions. Then he is given the good news that if he follows this programme, he will find a place in a vast paradise. Could there be any greater favour than this? Indeed, it is pure outpouring of generosity and grace, and pure bounty and gift.

Allah is the Rich King, and man is weak and needy. Yet this Rich King speaks with this weak and needy one. He showers favours upon him, invites him, and this Rich King repeatedly calls out to these poor ones and continually invites them to His generosity. This is a great kindness, a great favour, a great bounty and gift, which is selfless, and against it the full thanks cannot be rendered, nor can fidelity to His favour be achieved.

﴿...وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ...﴾ "...refines their lives..." It purifies, elevates, refines, and purifies their hearts, their concepts and their consciousness. It purifies their households, purifies their honour, and purifies their mutual relations. It purifies their individual lives, purifies their society, and purifies their intentions. It purifies them from the filth of shirk and idol-worship, purifies them from superstition and delusion, and from the customs and wrong servitudes that arise among them in life. And it purifies humans from the base conduct that is beneath the dignity of humanity. It purifies them from all the filth of the life of ignorance, and also from those things by which human consciousness and communal symbols become defiled, and by which the meanings, values and traditions of life become corrupted.

In truth, every jahiliyyah spreads some impurities in its environment. Likewise the Arab jahiliyyah also spread certain filths, and Islam was purifying them from all of these.

Some of the filth of the jahiliyyah is mentioned by Ja'far ibn Abi Talib when he was presenting Islam before the Negus, and he was presenting it before the representatives of Quraysh, who had come on a campaign against these emigrants, demanding that he hand them over to them. Ja'far (may Allah be pleased with him) said:

"O Noble King! We were a people immersed in jahiliyyah. We worshipped idols, ate carrion, committed all kinds of obscenity, severed all ties of kinship, mistreated the stranger, and the strong among us devoured the weak. This was our condition when Allah sent us a messenger from among us. We know his lineage well, we know well his truthfulness, his trustworthiness and his integrity, and his chastity is before us. He called us to Allah alone, that we should affirm His oneness and worship Him alone, and that we should cast off the stones and idols which we and our forefathers used to worship. He commanded us to speak the truth, to not betray trusts, to maintain ties of kinship, to take care of the rights of neighbours, to refrain from unlawful matters, not to kill; he forbade us from obscenity, forbade us from false speech, forbade us from consuming the property of orphans, and from slandering chaste women; and he commanded us to worship Allah alone, not to associate anything with Him, to establish prayer, to pay zakah and to fast."

And one of these filths is that which Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) mentioned, portraying according to the narration of Bukhari the sexual relations between men and women in the jahiliyyah: "In the jahiliyyah there were four forms of marriage prevalent. One was the marriage that is prevalent among us today: a man would propose for another's daughter, a dowry would be fixed, and then the marriage would take place. The second method was that when a man's wife became clean from her menstrual period, he would say: go to so-and-so and have relations with him. And he would not approach his wife until her pregnancy became evident, that is, from the seed of the man to whom he had sent her. And when the pregnancy became evident, then the husband would have sexual relations with her if he wished. This was done so that a good offspring would be produced from that man. This was called nikah al-istibda'. The third method was that fewer than ten men would gather and they would all have relations with one woman. Each would go to her, and when she conceived and gave birth, and some nights passed, she would summon them all. Every one of them had to come. They would come and gather at her place. She would say: you know your matter; now a child has been born, O so-and-so, this child is yours, and she would name whichever of them she wished, and the child would become his. And he could not refuse. The fourth form was that many men would go to one woman; this woman would not refuse anyone, whoever wished would go to her. When any of them became pregnant and gave birth, all these men would gather at her place, and physiognomists would be summoned. These physiognomists would attach the child to whichever of them they wished. He would take him, and he would be considered his son, and by law he could not deny him."

Now consider carefully whether any further commentary is needed on these brutal, degraded sexual customs. It is enough to think of a man who sends his wife to someone else in order to produce a good child, just as a she-camel, a mare or a female livestock is sent to bring forth a good offspring, so that the breed may be of the best.

As for the fourth form, which was prostitution, it is a form of prostitution in which the child is handed over to someone. They do not feel shame in it, nor do they refrain from it.

Then the third case is of the same kind, the one from which Islam purified the Arabs; and had Islam not come, they would have been sunk up to their ears in that filth.

In sexual relations, this filth was widespread among the Arabs simply because their view of women was extremely base. Abul Hasan Ali Nadwi writes in his book:

"In the age of jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic period of ignorance), women suffered immense oppression, and their rights were trampled. Their wealth was plundered, and they were deprived of inheritance. If a woman was divorced, or her husband died, she was not permitted to marry according to her own wishes. She was inherited like livestock and goods were inherited. It is narrated from Ibn Abbas: If a man's father died, he became the first claimant to his wife; if he wished, he would take her into his own marriage; if he wished, he would keep her confined until she paid him a ransom or died, so that he might take possession of all her property. Ata ibn Rabah says: The custom of the people of jahiliyyah was that when a man died and his wife remained, she would be held back until some child of hers reached maturity, and then she would be handed over to him."

Sudi said: In jahiliyyah, when a father or brother died, or a son died and left a widow behind, if some heir quickly threw a cloth over that widow, she became his; and he would marry her on the same former dower, or he would give her in marriage to someone else, but the right to her dower belonged to that man. And if a wife fled to her parental home as soon as her husband died, she was considered free. In jahiliyyah there was severe imbalance regarding women's rights: the husband could violate her rights, while she was unable to violate the husband's rights. Her dower was taken from her, and she was held back in order to harm her. The husband would treat her badly, turn away from her, and sometimes she would be left suspended. Among food and drink, some items were reserved for men and forbidden to women. A man was permitted to marry as many women as he wished.

Girls were regarded as so disgraceful that they were buried alive. Hashim ibn Adi, according to the narration of al-Maydani, wrote that burying daughters alive was a custom among all the tribes of Arabia; only, if one person did not practise it, ten would. When Islam came, the Arabs held various opinions and methods concerning burying alive. Some people, out of excessive zeal for honour, would bury their daughters alive and thereby conceal their shame. Some would bury girls with green eyes, or bury the black-skinned alive, or bury the leprous, or bury the lame, because they considered these attributes to be very ominous. And some would kill their children out of fear of poverty and hunger.

Sometimes they would kill or bury their daughters with great cruelty. For example, it would happen that the father was absent, travelling, or otherwise occupied, so he had no opportunity to bury the girl alive; she would grow up, and she would think that she was being killed. Some people have narrated their own stories which bring tears of blood. Some people would throw girls from the peak of a mountain.

Among these filths, one filth, and the greatest filth, was shirk. Then, in the base form of shirk, idol worship was common among the Arabs. Ustad Nadwi summarises this thus: "The Arabs were afflicted with the worst forms of idolatry and idol worship. Every tribe, indeed every valley, had an idol; indeed every family had an idol. Kalbi says: every household in Makkah had its own idol, which they worshipped. When someone set out on a journey, the last thing he did before leaving was to seek blessing from it, and when he returned home, the first thing he did was to worship it. The Arabs had become so extreme in worshipping idols that some had built temples for their idols; some had a single idol of their own. If someone could not build a temple and could not make his own idol, he would set up a stone in front of the Kaaba or in some other place, circumambulate it as he circumambulated the Kaaba, and such idols they called ansab. Within the Kaaba itself, although the Kaaba was built solely for the worship of Allah, three hundred and sixty idols were placed in its courtyard. Having gone beyond idol worship, they had gradually begun to worship stones. Imam Bukhari narrates from Abu Raja Utaridi, who said: We used to worship stones. If we found a good stone, we would leave the previous stone and take another. If we found no stone, we would take a clump of earth, bring a goat to milk it, and then circumambulate it. Kalbi says: If someone travelled and stopped at some place, he would take four stones; he would look to see which of them was the best, and take it as his lord, and make the other three into the three stones of a hearth. And when he left his stopping place, he would leave that stone behind too."

The Arabs, like other nations, also worshipped angels and jinn, and likewise they worshipped the stars. Thus they regarded the angels as daughters of Allah and made them intercessors with Him. They worshipped them and, through them, sought nearness (taqarrub) to Allah. Likewise, they had also made jinn partners with Allah. They believed in their power and influence, and indeed they worshipped them. Kalbi says that the Banu Mulayh clan of the tribe of Khuza'a worshipped jinn. Sa'id says that Himyar worshipped the sun, and Kinanah were worshippers of the moon. (See Madha Khasira al-Muslimun, Nadwi, p. 34)

From this initial picture of idolatry it can easily be understood how widespread the filth was in the hearts and minds, the concepts and the practical lives of the Arabs because of that idolatry. It also becomes clear what a tremendous revolution Islam brought about in Arab society, how greatly their lives were purified, how deeply their concepts were cleansed, and how thoroughly they were freed from moral and social filths; although these beliefs and these individual and collective filths were for them a kind of source of pride, and in their poetry, their fairs and their markets they would deliver long boastful speeches about them. For instance, wine-drinking, gambling, and small revenge-killings within tribes were, in their view, great moral virtues, and these people could not step outside their circle.

As for war, it was for them an extremely ordinary matter; bloodshed was their daily affair. Even a minor incident would become the cause of bloodshed. War broke out between the tribes of Bakr and Taghlib and continued for forty years. In that war, enormous bloodshed occurred. The war began thus: Kulayb, chief of Ma'ad, shot an arrow which struck the udder of the she-camel of Basus bint Munqidh; blood and milk mixed. Jassas ibn Murrah then killed Kulayb, and war broke out between the Bakr and Taghlib tribes. As Muhalhil, brother of Kulayb, said: "This war destroyed life, made mothers weep, and left children orphaned. Tears flowed without end, and so many were killed that they could not be buried." The War of Dahis was similar: Qays ibn Zuhayr's horse was named Dahis. In a wager race between Qays ibn Zuhayr and Hudhayfah ibn Badr, Dahis was ahead. A man belonging to the tribe of Asad placed an obstacle in front of it, and Hudhayfah went ahead. He struck the man on the face and thus entangled him, and the other horses went ahead. After that, fighting began, and retaliation followed retaliation. Tribes supported their members. People were killed, taken captive, and thousands of individuals perished."

From this it appears that in the life of the Arabs, great and lofty aims had no significance; if they had any lofty ideal, they would not have found time to occupy themselves with these base pursuits. Their life had no message, and no plan for the welfare of humanity was before them. In this world they had no lofty human programme, so that they would not have been occupied with these worthless and base pursuits of life. Nor did they have any worldview which would have restrained them from these collective blameworthy filths. If the divine worldview has not reached people, then what are their priorities? What is their concept of life? And what are their morals?

Jahiliyyah is, in any case, jahiliyyah; and the filths and wrongdoings of every jahiliyyah are different. In every time and place they have had their own opportunities. When people's hearts are empty of the divine worldview and divine thought no longer rules over them, when people are free from divine Shari'ah, then their life, which is based on a divine worldview, comes under the dominion of jahiliyyah, and they enter one of the various forms of jahiliyyah. In our own age, the jahiliyyah that has plunged humanity up to its ears in filth is, in its character, not much different from the ancient Arab jahiliyyah, nor is it different from the jahiliyyahs that were current across the world at that time and from which Islam delivered humanity.

Today the world lives in a great filth. Look at its journalism, look at its films, look at its fashion shows, look at its beauty contests, look at its dance halls, look at its baths, look at its institutions of publication and broadcasting; then look at naked flesh and provocative manners, look at its diseased suggestiveness in literature and the arts, and look at its base hints in the media of communication, and you will be certain that it is caught in and sick from a swamp of filth. Alongside this, the economy is gripped by a cruel usurious system. Inflation and the use of immoral means to accumulate and increase wealth are widespread. And under the shadow and cloak of the law, the masses are being plundered. Along with this, moral lawlessness has become so common that it engulfs every individual, every family and every system; indeed, its effects are being felt on every human society. Reflecting on all these matters makes it very easy to conclude that under this modern jahiliyyah humanity is advancing towards a deadly disease.

Humanity is devouring humanity. Its humanity is dissolving; it is chasing after the animal. Its breath is laboured. It has become devoted to things that are awakening animality. And man is descending to the world of animals; yet if you look at animals, they are purer than this man, because they are bound within the law of nature, and that law is so firm that it never slackens; nor do they become as filthy as man becomes when he is freed from the bonds of faith, worldview and ideological system, and returns to that jahiliyyah from which Allah has rescued him, and of which Allah, in this verse, points out and makes a special blessing of His.

"He purifies them and teaches them the Book and wisdom" ... "He teaches them the Book and wisdom." In this verse, those addressed were unlettered and ignorant. They could not write. In terms of reason and understanding, too, they were unlettered and ignorant; in no branch of knowledge did they have any understanding according to the global standards of knowledge and culture of that time, nor did they have any lofty aims in life that would hold global worth in any sphere of life. Yet suddenly the Islamic worldview came, and they became the teachers of the world. In the twinkling of an eye they became the wise ones of the world. They became possessors of an ideological system of life, which contained within it a complete system of thought, a system of society and an organisation of life; and it delivered all humanity in its own age from the jahiliyyah of that time. And today, too, in our age it will, God willing, deliver this modern humanity from modern jahiliyyah, because in our modern jahiliyyah are present all the elements of which the former jahiliyyah was composed: morally, socially, in terms of the goals of human life, and in terms of lofty purposes. Despite the great advances modern humanity has made in the fields of knowledge and understanding, and despite the record production it has shown in industry and the excellent conveniences of life it has provided, this humanity remains immersed in jahiliyyah.

"And indeed, before this, they were surely in manifest error." They were immersed in error in terms of beliefs and concepts. They were drowned in error in terms of the meanings and values of life, and they had lost their way in terms of aims and life's direction. In their customs and habits, in their order and discipline, in their social system and their moral system, they were misguided.

The Arabs who were the first addressees of this verse knew well, without any doubt or uncertainty, their past and their present; this past was well remembered by them. And the revolution that had emerged in their lives through Islam had taken place before their very eyes. They also knew that without the Islamic worldview, such a great revolution could not have occurred in their lives, the like of which is not found in the history of humanity.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 3, verse 164 (part 3 of 3):

They knew that it was Islam, and Islam alone, that had lifted them out of tribal customs, removed tribal preferences from their minds, and rescued them from the quagmire of tribal vengeance. And not merely so that they might become a great nation, but so that, suddenly, without any preliminary preparations and without any long-term plan, they would take the form of a nation leading humanity, one that was preparing a blueprint of life for mankind, preparing a methodology of life for it, and organizing its collective order, in a situation for which they had no precedent before them, and for which there was no example in the whole of human history.

With full insight they recognized the reality that it was Islam, and Islam alone, that had given them a national identity, given them a political existence, and given them an international standing. And, first and foremost, that it had bestowed upon them a human status, which elevated their humanity, their human dignity and the honour of humanity, and organized their entire system of life upon the foundation of the nobility of the human being. And this honour was bestowed upon them by Allah, as a gift and as a favour. Then they showered this honour of humanity upon the whole of humanity. They taught the whole of humanity how human beings are to be honoured: how, together with the honour of Allah, man is to be made the best of creation. And in bestowing this nobility upon man, before them there was no example either in the Arabian Peninsula or in any other region of the world. The discussion we have already had on the principle of consultation (shura) was one of the aspects of that system and of the nobility of humanity, in which they felt that this was an extraordinary blessing of Allah upon them.

They were fully aware that it was Islam, and Islam alone, that had given them a message, and that they were now presenting this message to the whole world; they were giving humanity a way of life, showing it a path for human life. And it is obvious that in this vast field of the human fraternity, if any nation can survive, it will be the one that possesses a message, that possesses a way of living, and that advances humanity through it.

This was Islam: its vision of the universe, its views on life, its collective and legal system for society, its distinctive organization of human life, and its ideal, positive and realistic system of living, under whose shade human beings attained prosperity. With these characteristics, Islam was a personal highway by means of which they advanced, and by which humanity recognized them, respected them, and entrusted them with the leadership of humanity.

Today or tomorrow, this highway is still theirs. Apart from it they have no other identity among the nations of the world. For them there is now only this path: that humanity should recognize them and honour them, or else they should abandon this message and return to a purposeless life, as they were before Islam, when no one knew them and no one acknowledged them.

The question is: if they do not wish to give humanity the message of the Islamic system of life, then what message do they wish to give the world? Do they wish to give the world something in arts, manners and science? In those fields the world has gone far ahead of them. In these secondary sciences and cultures, humanity has already been enriched beyond measure. It has no need of anything more, nor does it await that the Arabs will give it anything in these fields.

Do the Arabs wish to present to the world some marvel in the field of industry? Yet among the nations of the world industry has advanced to such an extent that before it the great and haughty have bowed; they have filled the markets with industrial products, and they have overshadowed (OverShade) the industrial production that exists among us. In this field, many nations are ahead of the Arabs, and in this field the reins of leadership are already in their hands.

Do the Arabs wish to give the world some philosophy of collective religion? Or do they wish to give the world some economic and organizational system that they have invented, the product of their own intellectual effort? The truth is that our present world is filled with these worldly philosophies, religions and ideologies, and it is under these worldly ideologies that humanity is passing through a condition of the greatest misery.

The question is: what gift do the Arabs wish to present to this humanity and to the nations of the world, by which they may become known among the community of nations, may gain distinction, and may be regarded as superior in this field?

I say that they have no message other than the message of Islam. This is the only system of life whose message they can give to this world. They have nothing other than this blessing of Allah, which He bestowed upon them, and by which He bestowed upon them honour. And one day, through this very message, they delivered the whole of humanity to salvation; and today, the field in which humanity is most bankrupt, and in which it is most in need, is this very message. It is about to fall into the pit of Hell. It is a victim of bewilderment, anguish and restlessness.

This is the only message that they once gave to humanity, and before which the whole of humanity bowed its head. Today, this is the message that the Arabs can give to humanity, and in it lies humanity's salvation, and in it lies the secret of its success.

Every nation has some message. Among all the great nations, each one has something. The greatest nation is the one whose message is great; a great nation is one that gives the greatest system. Then, in the world, it is regarded as unique by this system of life, and that system becomes its identity.

The Arabs possess this message. Indeed, it is their genuine message. The other nations are merely partners with them in the message of Islam. The question is: which devil is it that is depriving them of this great and precious treasure? Who is that devil? Recognize him.

It was a great and mighty blessing of Allah upon this ummah, because of this message, because of this Messenger, and because of his prophethood. Only the devil can turn them away from this great blessing and lead them astray, although Allah has commanded them to reject that devil and to stone him.

After this, in the account of the events of the Battle of Uhud, the discussion advances one step further. Further commentary is given and conclusions are drawn. Their astonishment is presented, which they expressed upon seeing the outcomes that emerged at Uhud. They regarded these events as unthinkable. Their thought was that they were Muslims, and yet they were defeated. From this it appeared that their conception of Islam was still very rudimentary. They had not yet passed through experiences and matured intellectually. They had not yet undergone practical training, so that they might deal with the actual situation and real events and comprehend the cosmic laws of nature of this world, according to which every person must conduct his practical life here. For this reason, Islam placed them on open battlefields and made it clear to them that whatever befell them was the necessary result of their own actions. The measures and initiatives they undertook had these natural results, in accordance with the Sunnah of Allah. But the Qur'an does not leave them at this point alone, because although this point is a reality, it is not the ultimate reality; rather, behind these causes and their natural consequences, the divine decree also operates. The Qur'an draws their attention to this as well, and behind these divine laws and natural principles the divine will also operates. Thus the Qur'an tells them the wisdom behind these events, and that Allah had intended good for them behind this arrangement of events. There was good in it for them, and benefit for the call for which they are striving. The purpose was to prepare them through this experience for the time to come, to purify their hearts, to cleanse their ranks, and to separate out the hypocrites who were exposed as a result of these events. Ultimately, all matters are in any case accomplished according to the will of Allah; they come to pass according to His decree and plan. Thus, through this commentary, their understanding and their consciousness are completed. Let us cast a glance at the very profound, deep and subtle expositions of the Holy Qur'an on this subject:

God has written upon Himself that He will help His friends, those who bear His banner and who hold firm faith and conviction in Him. But He has conditioned this promise upon a condition, namely that those who deserve God's help will be such when the reality of faith has firmly and well settled in their hearts. And they will be fulfilling the requirements of faith in their organisation and conduct. And whatever is within their scope and strength, they will have prepared. They will be striving to the extent of their capacity. This is the Sunnah of God (sunnat-ullah, the established way of God), and the Sunnah of God is not bound by special friendship with anyone, nor does it show favour to anyone. When the people of God have any shortcoming or deficiency in any of these matters, it is their duty to accept the consequences of their shortcomings. This is because merely being believers does not render the law of the divine Sunan (sunan-i-ilahiyyah) inoperative for them. Nor will the supreme order (namus-i-a'la) become void. They will truly be Muslims only when they put the divine Sunan into effect throughout their lives, and align their nature with the order of the cosmos.

But their being Muslims is not wasted either. It is not without effect. Their surrender before God, their raising of His banner, their resolve to obey Him and their adherence to His system of life, and similar matters, will certainly have the effect that God brings forth the aspect of good and blessing from their shortcomings and their errors. Although because of those errors they receive wounds, make sacrifices and suffer temporary defeat, He will increase their experience through those errors. In this way their belief will be purified. Their hearts will be cleansed. Their ranks will be refined, and thus in the end they will become deserving of the help that God has promised. The final outcome will be one of good and blessing. Muslims are not cast off from God's presence or His mercy and favour; rather, God bestows upon them further provision for the journey, even though along the way they may suffer hardships, face difficulties and be afflicted with grief and sorrow.

With this clarification, and in a decisive manner, God addresses the community of Muslims. In this questioning manner of theirs, and regarding their bewilderment and distress over the events that occurred, an answer is given, and it is explained what the immediate cause of these events was. It is also explained what far-reaching wisdom lay hidden within the divine decree. And the hypocrites are told that death has a fixed appointed time. Death is not averted by fear, nor is death postponed by not participating in jihad.

"And how is it that when a calamity struck you, though you had inflicted twice as much upon them, you said, 'From where has this come?' Say, 'It is from yourselves.' Indeed, God is over all things competent."

The calamities that befell the Muslims in the Battle of Uhud are before everyone. Seventy men were martyred, and there were the wounded, and further afflictions beyond these. It was a very bitter day for them. These afflictions were extremely heavy and unbearable for them. Their thought was that they were Muslims, striving in the way of God, while their opponents were enemies of God and polytheists; and the Muslims who were afflicted by this calamity had previously inflicted double that loss upon these enemies of Islam. This is an allusion to Badr, where they had inflicted losses upon the disbelievers, at a time when they stood upright by God's command. They were acting upon the orders of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), before they became led astray by seeing the spoils of war, and before thoughts arose in their hearts that do not accord with faith.

God reminds them of all these matters, and answers their bewildered question in this way: its direct cause was indeed their own actions. "Say, it is from yourselves..." (Say to them, "It is from yourselves.")

It was your own selves that became corrupted; you became divided and began to dispute with one another; and it was you who did not abide by the conditions of God and His Messenger. It was your own selves into which greed and avarice entered, and it was you who violated the explicit commands of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and sabotaged his military plan. Therefore, these consequences you have faced, which you regard as unexpected, and you say, "How did these circumstances come about?" the answer is that it happened because of you yourselves. The Sunnah of God has been applied to you. When you presented yourselves before that Sunnah, it applied fully to you. When a person presents himself before the Sunnah of God, that Sunnah applies to him completely. Whether the person is a Muslim or a polytheist, in this matter there will be no favour shown. Hence, the perfection of anyone's Islam should be that they adapt themselves to the Sunnah of God, and they should do this beforehand.

"Indeed, God is over all things competent." His power itself necessitates that He enforces His Sunnah. He establishes the operation of His order in this universe. All affairs proceed according to His power and will. And it is also a requirement of His power that His Sunnah, upon which He has run this universe, this life and the events of this life, is not rendered inoperative.

Along with this, keep in mind that behind all events stands the decree (taqdir) of Allah, and within it lies a wisdom known only to Allah. Every matter that occurs and every incident that takes place has the decree of Allah behind it. Behind every movement and every stillness there is the hand of divine decree, and behind every occurrence in this universe there is taqdir.

﴿Whatever befell you on the day the two hosts met, it was by the permission of Allah﴾ (Qur'an 3:166). This loss did not come about merely by chance, or by mischance on its own, nor did it come about aimlessly and in vain. This is because every movement within this universe conforms to a plan and to the power of God, and collectively there is wisdom behind these events, and collectively these events conform to the scheme of this entire universe. And despite this, they conform to the divine laws (sunan Ilahiyyah) operating within this universe and to those unalterable laws, which never deviate and never suspend, and which show no favour to anyone.

On the question of taqdir, the Islamic conception of life is so complete, comprehensive and balanced that no conception of life from the beginning of humanity until today can match it.

According to the Islamic conception of life, this universe has an unalterable law, and there are certain unbreakable divine laws. Behind these unalterable natural laws and inviolable divine laws, the will of Allah is at work, and the will of Allah is free, not confined by any constraint. And behind all of these, namely the divine laws and the divine will, stands the wise governance of Allah. All of these, in turn, proceed in accordance with the wise governance of Allah. It is the rule of the natural order (nāmūs), and everything operates within the divine laws; man too is subject to and governed by them. Within the sphere of these divine laws, man acts through his deliberate action, within his own sphere of choice. And whatever work he does according to his thought and his plans, these laws apply to those actions and affect them. But all of this happens in accordance with the taqdir and will of Allah, and alongside it, Allah's wisdom and planning also operate. In this system, human will, movement, thought and capacity for action are all a part of the divine laws. They are part of the natural order of the universe. Allah also carries out His work through these human actions, makes them effective, and all of this still occurs within the sphere of His power. None of these things lies outside the bounds of the laws of nature and the divine laws. Nor does any human movement or thought stand in contradiction to these laws or in opposition to them. Some people think that they stand in the other pan of the scale against the will of Allah. This situation is entirely impossible. The Islamic conception of life is not like that. Man is not a partner set against Allah, nor is he an enemy of Allah. When Allah bestowed upon man his existence, his thought, his will, and granted him his destiny, his planning, and his agency upon the earth, He did not place any contradiction between these human faculties and the divine laws, nor any opposition between them. These things were not contrary to the will of Allah, nor were all these matters outside the profound wisdom of Allah, which governs the decree of Allah. It was placed within the sunnah of Allah and the taqdir of Allah that man should exercise his planning, be active, and be effective in this universe. He should stand against the divine laws, they should apply to him, and under the sunnah of Allah in this world he should experience pleasure and pain, comfort and discomfort, happiness and misery, and through all his activities the taqdir of Allah should operate, within whose encompassing this entire universe lies, with perfect balance and harmony.

The events that occurred at Uhud were an example of the Islamic conception of life, that is, of what we have discussed regarding taqdir. Through these events Allah taught the Muslims what His sunnah is regarding victory and defeat. When they violated the sunnah of Allah and the condition He had set for victory, He afflicted them with the sufferings and calamities that befell them at Uhud. But the matter did not end there. Behind this opposition and grief, this taqdir was at work so that, as a result, Allah would separate the hypocrites from the ranks of the Muslims, purify the hearts of the believers, remove the impurities and defects in their conceptions, or remove the weakness and frailty in their character.

Outwardly they suffered grief and pain, but in its own place, for the believers, in terms of the future, this was good. Although this grief and pain was also exactly in accordance with the sunnah of Allah, it is one of the sunnahs of Allah that Muslims who accept the Islamic system of life and submit to it, and generally obey the Islamic system, will be supported and aided by Allah, and even their mistakes will, in the end, become a means of victory and a channel of good. Even though they may suffer grief and pain. Why? Because training takes place through grief, hardship and calamities, impurity is removed from the ranks of Islam, and thorough preparation is made for the next stage.

On this firm and clear stance the feet of the Muslims will be planted; their hearts will be at peace; there will be no wavering in them, no bewilderment and no anxiety. In this way they will acknowledge the taqdir of Allah and carry out their affairs in this universe in accordance with the divine laws. They will be certain that Allah is active in their own selves and in their environment, doing whatever He wills, and that they are instruments and means of the divine decree. Allah can use His instruments in whatever way He wishes; their correct decisions, their sound judgments, the effects of correct decisions and the consequences of wrong decisions, all of them, manifest from behind the veil of Allah's taqdir. Each carries some wisdom of His, and as long as they remain on this path of transformation, every stage will be nothing but good for them.

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 167:**

This verse refers to the position of Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and his companions. The address to them is ﴿Those who practised hypocrisy (nifaq)﴾. On this occasion, Allah exposed them, separated them from the ranks of the Muslims, and commented on their stance on that day: ﴿At that time they were nearer to disbelief than to faith﴾. He showed that in their protest they were not truthful when they said that there was no fighting taking place between the Muslims and the disbelievers today, and that this was why they were withdrawing. The real reason for their return was not this. Rather, ﴿they said with their mouths what was not in their hearts﴾. In their hearts was the disease of hypocrisy, and this hypocrisy did not bind them to a worldview. Instead, it gave greater importance to their personalities and their personal standing than to the worldview.

The chief of these people, Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, also objected that on the day of Uhud the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not accept his opinion. The background to this event is that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived in Madinah Tayyibah with the message of his prophethood, preparations were under way under the leadership of Abdullah ibn Ubayy to form a state, and a crown was being made for him. With the arrival of the Prophet (ﷺ), the position of leadership of the state was taken by the bearers of Islam. This fact pierced his heart like an arrow, and this is why he withdrew on the day of Uhud. Since the enemy was at the gates of Madinah, these people turned back and rejected the words of the true believer. This true believer was Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Haram. He was calling them: ﴿Come, fight in the way of Allah, or at least defend﴾. Their reply, their argument and their reasoning was that in their view there was no fighting. Had there been any real fighting, they would certainly have gone. Their position was refuted in this way: ﴿And Allah knows best what they conceal﴾.

In this way, they regard their lagging behind and turning back as wise and beneficial, and they regard obedience to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as harmful and damaging. Even more serious is that they corrupt the clear and pure concept of life in Islam, because according to the Islamic concept of life, the time of each person's death is fixed. The reality of life and death is connected with the decree of Allah. Therefore Allah deems it necessary here to refute their wrong ideas. Their concept is immediately and clearly refuted, which on one side scatters the threads and fibres of the plot they had prepared, and on the other side makes the Islamic concept of life free from every kind of ambiguity and vagueness. He says: ﴿Say: Then avert death from yourselves, if you are truthful﴾.

Death comes to the warrior just as it comes to those who sit at home; it comes to the brave as well as to the coward. No guard can avert it, nor any precautionary measure. Neither cowardice nor absence from jihad can ward it off. This situation is self-evident, and there is no room for doubt about it. This is the real situation which the Holy Qur'an itself presents against them. Thus their despicable plot is rejected. By keeping the truth in its place, it is established. The hearts of the Muslims become content and firm. They are filled with tranquillity, peace and the savour of certainty.

The human mind cannot help but notice in this manner of narrating the events of Uhud that the account of the turning back of Abdullah ibn Ubayy and his companions has been placed very late, although this event took place in the early stage of that battle, and he had withdrawn from the very beginning of the engagement. Instead of mentioning it at the beginning, it has been placed at the end. Why?

This delay was made because it also expresses a particular style from the educational method of the Holy Qur'an. The purpose was that before commenting on this incident, all the foundational concepts which form the basic principles of the Islamic system of life should be stated. When all those sentiments had settled in the minds of the Muslims, and genuine standards had been established for the values of the Muslims, then at the end the Qur'an pointed to those who had adopted hypocrisy. Their character and activities were exposed. Criticism of those people came at a time when the minds of the Muslims were ready for it and were able to understand where their ideas and concepts deviated, what their weaknesses were, and how faulty their standards were. It also showed how the ideas, concepts and criteria of good and evil in the heart and mind of a believer should be, and that the deeds of an individual or a people should be assessed according to those standards. Then, when deeds and persons are presented to the believer, he, in the light of a illuminated disposition, a faith-based sensitivity and a faith-based store of wisdom, immediately passes judgement on what is inferior and what is better, who is righteous and who is wicked.

This is a particular feature of the Qur'anic style of expression. Abdullah ibn Ubayy had, up to that time, been the leading chief of his people, as we have mentioned above. He became enraged because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had not accepted his opinion. This was because the Prophet (ﷺ) had to establish the principle of consultation, and then implement whatever matter was decided, even if it was wrong, since the inclination of the people towards a different opinion had become apparent. Because of this man's turning away, great disorder arose within the ranks of the Muslims, and their ideas were shaken. Then the importance of his opinion became even clearer when the defeat occurred and people began to feel regret and sorrow, and the thought came to their hearts that they should have acted on his advice. For the Islamic method, it was necessary to present his opinion and his action as relatively neglected and unimportant, and not to begin the account of the battle with that incident, even though it had occurred first. By delaying the mention of this incident so much, and then narrating it while attaching the label of hypocrisy to that group, by using the passive and unspecified form for them, by not mentioning the leader of that group, and by addressing them as ﴿those who practised hypocrisy﴾, the purpose is simply to diminish their importance, and for this matter to apply in principle to all those who commit such acts, so that the matter takes on a general principle, just as it was given the character of a general principle at the beginning of the discourse.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 168:

After establishing tranquillity in the hearts of the Muslims, and after settling their hearts and consciences upon the divine laws (sunan Ilahiyyah) that operate and prevail throughout this universe, and after informing them that all affairs occur in accordance with Allah's decree, and after explaining that behind Allah's decree stands Allah's wisdom and planning at work, and after impressing upon the mind that death has an appointed time, that its moment is already fixed, that refraining from battle cannot postpone it, that taking part in battle cannot bring it forward, and after explaining that no guard can protect a person from death and no measure can hold it back, now in the context of the discourse another reality is taken up. This reality is great in itself, and its effects are also extremely great.

What is this reality? It is that those who are killed in the way of Allah are not dead; rather, they are alive. They are the special guests of their Lord. Their life, after death, is not severed from the life of the Islamic community; they are not unconcerned with the events that follow; they are themselves affected by those events, and they are also an effective factor within those events. And what is life made of? Influence and impression are indeed life itself.

Here, a connection is established between the life of the martyrs of the Battle of Uhud and the events and occurrences that took place after their martyrdom. Immediately after this, the account of the community of believers is presented, those who responded to the call of Allah and of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) even though they were covered in wounds. They set out and pursued the Quraysh. Although the Quraysh had already departed, there remained the fear that they might attack Madinah again. This group paid no heed to the rumour spread by people that the Quraysh were gathering once more. They placed their trust in the Divine Being, and through this exploit they gave their faith the form of reality.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 169:

After establishing correct concepts of destiny and the appointed time of death in the hearts and minds of the believers, and after refuting the restlessness, doubts and regrets that the hypocrites were creating within the ranks of Islam, Allah the Exalted considered it appropriate to create greater tranquility and complete contentment in the hearts of the people of faith. The hypocrites were constantly propagating that if you are so resourceful, then prevent your own death when it comes. But after the faith and certainty created in the preceding verses and this conclusive reply, Allah willed that greater assurance be created in their hearts regarding the future of the martyrs. Those martyrs who were killed in the way of Allah (and those are indeed martyrs who are killed in the way of Allah), and whose aims are these same objectives, with no other aim associated with these objectives. Such martyrs who were killed in the way of Allah are in reality ever-living. They possess those distinctions which living people possess. For example, they are given provision from their Lord, and beyond provision they enjoy the bounty of Allah, and they are very happy with that bounty. Then they are given reports about the affairs of the believers for which they gave their lives. The complete events are related to them. After them, the events that befall their brothers are presented before them. And all these distinctions are those possessed by living people, such as equipment, good news, attention, and impact and influence. All these are attributes of living people. Therefore their separation through death is not a cause for regret. They are alive, their connection with the living is established, and in addition to this, there is further bounty: they are immersed in the grace of Allah. This grace is separate from their provision and their rank and station. Therefore the distinction that people make between the martyrs and the brothers who remain after them has in reality no substance. Thus the difference that exists in people's minds between the world of life and the world after death has no bearing in the case of the martyrs. From the standpoint of the believers there is no difference, because their affair is with Allah here and with Allah there.

After this truth is established in the mind, the manner of thinking about the events of this world changes. This truth transforms human thinking. A completely new outlook arises within a believer about this universe. From the perspective of a believer, the movement of this universe has continuity within itself; it is never cut off. Thus when a person dies, his life does not end; rather, a veil is drawn between life before death and life after death.

This is a new viewpoint on life and death. It brings a great revolution in a Muslim's consciousness. A Muslim receives both life and death with a particular viewpoint.

﴿وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ قُتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَمْوَاتًا ۚ بَلْ أَحْيَاءٌ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ يُرْزَقُونَ﴾ "And do not think of those who have been killed in the way of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for."

This verse is a definitive text regarding the fact that those who were killed in the way of Allah, who sacrificed their lives and disappeared from the sight of people, it is prohibited to call them dead or to consider them so. And this verse is also definitive in affirming that they are alive and are being provided for by their Lord. After this prohibition and affirmation, this verse mentions those distinctions of life and mentions their being provided for.

In this transient world we do not gain correct knowledge of the life of the martyrs. Indeed, some characteristics of the life of these martyrs are mentioned in some ahadith, but this verse revealed through wahy from Allah, may He be glorified, is sufficient and adequate for us in this matter. This is because Allah is All-Knowing and All-Aware, and Allah alone is the guarantor that He changes the concepts about life and death, regarding how far there is duality and separation between them and how much unity and connection there is. And only Allah can tell that matters are not exactly as they apparently appear to us or as we are able to perceive them. When we fix in our minds the meanings of unrestricted and absolute realities, this does not mean that these concepts are ultimate concepts and that we have fully comprehended the realities after death. Therefore it is better for us to wait only for the explanation of the Divine Being regarding what Allah has said, and to be content with that.

The martyrs are those who apparently are killed. Apparently their life is separated from them and they too are separated from life, as it appears to us. But since they are killed in the way of Allah, and are killed having abandoned all worldly aims, leaving aside even the small worldly purposes, their souls are joined with Allah. Therefore they sacrifice their souls in the way of Allah. And they thus appear to be killed. So Allah, who is the Truthful Informant, informs us that they are not dead, and He forbids us from calling them dead even with the tongue. And He further emphasizes that they are alive. They are regularly given provision, and they receive the provision of Allah in the same way that living people receive it. And in the same manner, Allah informs us of some other of their special characteristics, for example:

"Rejoicing in what Allah has given them of His bounty..." — they are pleased and delighted with what Allah has bestowed upon them from His grace. That is, they receive the provision that comes from Allah with great joy, because they fully realize that this is a special favour of Allah. This special favour is for them a proof of Allah's good pleasure, since they were slain in His cause. What greater cause for joy could there be for them than to receive the provision of Allah with the awareness that He is also pleased with them?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 171:

After this, the distinguishing feature is that their hearts are occupied with, and take an interest in, the circumstances of those who are still living in this world, and they are very content regarding the outcome of those who remain alive. This is because they have come to know that Allah is pleased with them too.

﴿يَسْتَبْشِرُونَ بِنِعْمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَفَضْلٍ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾

"And they rejoice in a blessing from Allah and a bounty, and that Allah does not waste the reward of the believers."

And they are content that the believers who have remained behind them in the world, and have not yet reached them, also have no occasion for grief or fear. They rejoice and exult in the favour and bounty of Allah, and they have come to know that Allah does not waste the reward of the believers.

They have not cut off from their brothers who have not yet arrived and who have separated from them. They are alive, they are with them, and they are very pleased with what will be given to those who come after them in this world and in the Hereafter. They rejoice because there is no occasion for grief or fear for those who are coming either. They are living a high-level life with their Lord, and from this they have come to know that those who are coming will also enjoy good things, because boundless grace and generosity is being showered upon them. This is precisely the relationship Allah has with the truthful believers: He does not waste their reward.

The question is: what is that distinctive feature of life which the martyrs in the way of Allah do not lack? And what is it that distinguishes them from the believers who are yet to come? And what room is there, after their departure, for regret, loss, desolation and sorrow? That is, what occasion is there for the left-behind to grieve, when it is a moment of great joy? This is a moment of pleasure and love, that a person has separated from us and reached Allah, and while departing, is also joined with us.

If death is in the way of Allah, then it is not death, and according to the awareness of the mujahideen themselves, it is not death. For those who have remained behind too, it is not death; rather it is an expansion of the field of life, an expansion of its awareness, an expansion of its forms. This life of the martyr extends beyond the boundaries of life. Likewise, the manifestations of this life change. This life emerges from the narrowness of the world and enters a vast field. Before it there are not those veils and barriers which exist in our minds. It is as though life passes from one form and shape into another form and shape: one life ends and another begins.

The new meaning which this verse gives to life, or the meaning which this and other similar verses of the Quran give to the life of the martyrs, had the effect that the steps of the noble mujahideen were constantly moving forward in seeking martyrdom. An example of this is the models we gave at the beginning of the account of the Battle of Uhud.

After the statement of this truth, and this great truth, that what has been prepared by Allah for the believers, the martyrs are rejoicing over it, Allah here clarifies who the believers are, who they are, and what their relationship is with their Lord.

These were the people whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called out on the second morning after the Battle of Uhud, saying: "Set out; the bitter engagement is not yet over." Their condition was such that blood was still flowing from their wounds. They had only just escaped the jaws of death the day before, having fought with everything they had. The horrors of the previous day's battle had not yet left their minds. The bitterness of defeat was still in their mouths, and the intensity of their pain had not yet subsided. Furthermore, they had just offered up the precious lives of their kinsfolk the day before, and, above all, the majority of them were severely wounded.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had called them, and only them, and this call, and the response of the people to it, was an act containing profound indications and great realities, and deep wisdom lay hidden within it.

It is possible that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wished that the last word of the believers in that battle, and their final awareness, should not be that they had suffered a defeat, had been beaten, and were lying in their wounds groaning. For this reason, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) instructed them to shake off the dust from their clothes and to pursue the Quraysh, following them so that it would settle in their minds that this had been a trial, an experience, and not the final decision of that battle. And that, after this, the strength of the Muslims remained intact, that the enemy was still weak, that this had been a single occasion in which they were suddenly defeated, and that "we will take revenge for it, if we remove weakness and disunity and submit to the command of Allah and His Messenger."

It was also possible that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wished to remove from the minds of the Quraysh the notion that they were entering Makkah with victory banners flying. Therefore, he pursued them in that battle together with those who had taken part in it. By this, he intended to make the Quraysh understand that they had not yet broken the strength of the Muslims, and that the capacity for pursuit or for another battle still remained among them. As the narrations in the biography (sirah) report, these two objectives were fulfilled by that pursuit.

Perhaps the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wished to make the Muslims and the whole world feel that a new reality had emerged in this world, and that this new reality, which now stands established after its emergence, is that the real capital of this new movement is its creed. This is its goal and its purpose, it has no other aim in life, and it has no other priority in its life besides this. Muslims live for this way of life alone, so beyond this way of life they have no other desire in their souls, and they are ready to sacrifice everything for it.

At that time, on this earth, this was an entirely new thing. Therefore it was necessary that the whole world should know it, and that the Muslims themselves should become aware of it, that this new ideology had now been established and is now an indelible reality on this earth. And there could be no greater manifestation of this reality than that, after suffering such wounds at Uhud, the self-sacrificing servants of Islam should set out with their open wounds in pursuit of a dominant force. Their step was a clear, bright and utterly frightening one. In it was found a bright example of trust in Allah (tawakkul). And people were frightening those devoted warriors, saying that the Quraysh were gathering again, just as the representatives of Abu Sufyan had conveyed this to them, and the hypocrites too presented the Quraysh's plan in a frightening manner, that they were about to do so.

﴿Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the injury had befallen them; for those among them who did good and guarded themselves there is a great reward.﴾ ……… [They are] those to whom people said: "The people have gathered against you, so fear them." But this increased their faith, and they replied: "Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs."

In this frightening situation, this pursuit was in fact a declaration that revolution, this great revolution, had now become a reality on this earth. Thus these were the aspects which are clearly visible from this wise step of the Messenger (ﷺ). From some narrations of the sirah we learn about the circumstances of those people who, despite being shattered by their wounds, responded to the call of the Messenger (ﷺ).

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 3, verse 173:

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrates from Abdullah ibn Jarihah, from Abu al-Sa'ib, that one of the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a man from the Banu Abd al-Ashhal, who had taken part in Uhud, related: "We participated with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Uhud. I was there, and my brother was there. We both returned wounded. The muezzin of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ announced: 'Come out, we are to pursue the enemy.' I said to my brother, or my brother said to me: 'Will the battle with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ be missed by us? We have no mount, and we are both severely wounded.' Both of us went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. My wound was slightly less than my brother's. Whenever he became weak, I would support him from behind, until we reached the destination with the Muslims."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq says that the Battle of Uhud took place on Saturday, the 15th of Shawwal. On the next day, the 16th of Shawwal, the muezzin of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave the call to prayer and ordered that the enemy be pursued. The muezzin also announced that only those who had participated in the battle of the previous day would go with them. The companion Jabir ibn Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Haram said that his father had left him in charge of his sisters. He had seven sisters. His father said to him: "My son, it is neither proper for me nor for you that you should leave these seven women and go out for jihad. And it is not possible for me to grant you the honour of jihad with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So stay with your sisters." Only then did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ grant him permission, and he went out with him.

When this great truth was proclaimed, great and unparalleled events of this kind came to pass. A revolution occurred in the mental world of the people. Holy souls were produced who were trained to regard Allah alone as their Protector and Helper. They were content with the Divine Being alone and considered the Divine Being sufficient. They remembered the Divine Being alone, and when the harshest of circumstances came upon them, their faith became even firmer; and when people frightened them with difficulties, their response was: ﴿Hasbunallahu wa ni'mal-wakil﴾ "Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verses 174–175:

And what will be the outcome? It is what Allah has decreed for those who rely (upon Him) (mutawakkilin), who become sincerely devoted to Allah and for whom Allah alone is sufficient.

﴿So they returned with a blessing from Allah and grace, no harm touched them, and they followed the pleasure of Allah; and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty.﴾

"They returned with the blessing and grace of Allah. No harm touched them, and they were given the honour of following the pleasure of Allah. Allah is the Possessor of great bounty."

They escaped from difficulties and returned without any hardship. They returned with the pleasure of Allah, and they returned with success and joy. ﴿With a blessing from Allah and grace……﴾ Here Allah again draws their attention to the first cause of generosity and forgiveness, namely that the primary cause is the blessing of Allah and His grace. And there is also an intention in this to indicate that the position of the Companions (ṣaḥābah) (may Allah be pleased with them) was praiseworthy, because their stance was that they were seeking only the grace of Allah and His blessing. The source of all blessings is this: that the grace of Allah descends, and their position was such that it was a rain of divine grace. ﴿And Allah is the Possessor of great bounty……﴾ "And Allah is the Possessor of great grace." In this way, Allah records this in His eternal Book, portrays them in His speech, and presents their stance; and the speech of Allah is that speech with which this whole universe is in harmony. In short, their stance is most noble and their portrait is most beautiful.

When a person reflects upon this stance and this scene of theirs, he realises that within a single night the outlook of these people was completely transformed. They became mature, they became harmonious with one another, and they settled firmly where they stood with contentment. The mist and dirt were removed from their thoughts, and their situation became entirely new. The turmoil and wavering that existed in their ideas and within their ranks yesterday now have no trace. Only one night had passed, yet their stance had changed like the difference between earth and sky. A great difference and a journey of miles was covered in an instant. This bitter experience did its work within their souls. This incident shook them thoroughly, as a result of which all the dust was shaken off their thoughts, their hearts were awakened anew, their steps became firm, and their hearts were filled once again with unwavering resolve. It is entirely correct to say that within this trial too there lay hidden the grace of Allah.

At the end of this paragraph, the cause of the present anxiety and fear of that time is also explained. It is stated that it is Satan who instills the fear and awe of his friends in your hearts. He presents his friends in the garb of awe and majesty. Therefore the believers should be thoroughly alert to this trick of Satan, and should adopt measures to render his deception ineffective. Hence they should not fear the people of Quraysh, for at that time they were the companions of Satan. Instead of being afraid of friends, they should fear Allah, for He alone is the all-powerful, the absolute Sovereign and the Compeller, and He alone deserves to be feared.

﴿"Now you have come to know that it was Satan who was frightening you of his friends without cause. So from now on do not fear people; fear Me, if you are truly believers."﴾

Satan presents his friends greatly magnified and inflated. He presents them in garments in which they appear strong and powerful. He instils in hearts the awe that Satan's companions can turn everything in their favour, that their hands are long, that they can bestow benefit and also inflict harm, so that Satan may through this means keep fulfilling his needs and aims, and spread evil and corruption in the world through these friends. And he bows people before his friends to such an extent that they obey them unconditionally. No one can deny anything before them, no one can criticise them, and no one even dares to restrain them from such evil and corruption.

Satan's policy is to present falsehood greatly inflated and swollen, such that it appears powerful, capable, overpowering, compelling, and holding a firm grip. It has no real standing, yet no one stands against it, and no force exists that could prevail over it. Satan's interest is to keep the situation in this condition. Under the cover of fear and awe, and in an atmosphere of intimidation and seizure, the friends of Satan carry out all their activities in the world. They make the good appear evil and the evil appear good. They spread evil, corruption and misguidance. They silence the voice of truth, guidance and justice, without anyone challenging them, standing before them, or being able to remove them from positions of leadership. In short, the believers do not even dare to criticise the falsehood they promote, nor dare to clarify or establish the truth which they wish to erase.

Satan is extremely cunning, deceitful and treacherous. He comes in the guise of his friends, and he terrifies with them those who do not take precautions against satanic whisperings. This is why Allah here strips him bare, and he is so exposed that no garment of his deception remains upon his body. The believers come to know the reality of Satan well; they grasp the truth of his whisperings and his deceit, so that they may be cautious of him. They should not fear his friends nor be overawed by them. For the believer who places complete trust in the Divine Being, Satan is very weak in comparison, because the source of his strength is Allah. The only force that a person should fear is that which has the power to bring benefit and harm, and the power to bring benefit and harm belongs to Allah alone. The believer fears only Allah. When all believers become those who fear Allah alone, they become stronger than all powers, and then no worldly power can stand against them, neither satanic power nor the power of Satan's friends.

﴿"So do not fear them, but fear Me, if you are believers."﴾

Now the final conclusion and essence of this discussion is presented. Addressing the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) by way of consolation and comfort, it is said that he should not be distressed and should not grieve over the fact that these people of disbelief and atheism are hastening towards it so swiftly, and are so eager in their disbelief as if they are competing in a race. It is said: consider their conduct, what harm does it cause to Allah? It is in fact a calamity for themselves. Allah has decreed this calamity in their destiny. Allah knew well what they would do and which acts of disbelief they would commit. Therefore, before that, He decided: "Very well, you will be deprived in the Hereafter." So He left them to their own condition, and they continued advancing swiftly towards disbelief. The path of guidance was clear before them, but they used their power of discernment and adopted the path of disbelief. Therefore they were left to their own condition, and they were given further respite to accumulate sins as much as possible. This respite was granted to them in terms of time, and also in the form of prosperity. Thus this respite and prosperity, for them, are in effect, as a reward, a calamity and a trial. This section of verses concludes with the wisdom behind all these events: why the believers were put to trial, and why the people of disbelief are being granted such respite. It is so that the pure may be distinguished from the impure and separated from them. This purification and cleansing takes place only through trial and tribulation, for the message of the Messenger can be known only through trial, since the unseen is known only to Allah, and people do not know it. Therefore Allah deemed it appropriate that, through a suitable mode of action, the unseen should be made manifest to the believers, that the believers should come to know the condition of hearts, that the pure should be separated from the impure elements, and that those who believe in Allah should come forward clearly and definitively upon the field.
