This respite was granted to them in terms of time, and also in the form of prosperity. Thus this respite and prosperity, for them, are in effect, as a reward, a calamity and a trial. This section of verses concludes with the wisdom behind all these events: why the believers were put to trial, and why the people of disbelief are being granted such respite. It is so that the pure may be distinguished from the impure and separated from them. This purification and cleansing takes place only through trial and tribulation, for the message of the Messenger can be known only through trial, since the unseen is known only to Allah, and people do not know it. Therefore Allah deemed it appropriate that, through a suitable mode of action, the unseen should be made manifest to the believers, that the believers should come to know the condition of hearts, that the pure should be separated from the impure elements, and that those who believe in Allah should come forward clearly and definitively upon the field.

This is the excellent conclusion to the events of the Battle of Uhud. In that battle, calamities rained down upon the Muslims, and the disbelievers achieved victory and dominance. In the struggle between truth and falsehood, a doubt always arises, and it always pricks the hearts of the people of truth. Sometimes the desire for success rises in their hearts: in the struggle between truth and falsehood, truth should always prevail, and if truth is defeated somewhere, as at Uhud, and falsehood and disbelief gain victory and triumph, then why does this happen?

This is a false doubt, and it keeps arising in hearts, and the human desire for success keeps pressing upon it continually. Why does this happen, O Lord? Why is truth defeated and falsehood victorious? The people of truth are afflicted with calamities while the people of falsehood are saved and succeed. Why is it not that whenever truth and falsehood clash, truth is granted victory and returns with dominance and spoils? Do truth and reality not deserve to be granted victory? And why does falsehood have this strength and this awe, that in its collision with truth it achieves such successes that they cause trials among the people of truth and make their hearts waver?

These questions were practically raised when, on the day of Uhud, the believers asked in great astonishment and confusion: ﴿Anna hadha?﴾ "How has this happened?" Therefore, in this final conclusion, its final answer is given. The last and decisive word is spoken, and Allah, the Exalted, provides peace to troubled hearts, and from this aspect, whatever great misgiving finds its way into hearts is cleared away. The Sunnah of Allah is explained. Under the Sunnah of Allah, His decrees are explained, and then the broader plan and wisdom behind all these Sunan and decrees are also disclosed. This wisdom existed in the past, exists today, and will exist in the future, and it will occur in every place where there is a struggle between truth and falsehood and results like Uhud emerge.

The departure of falsehood from any battle in the world victorious, its swelling with pride for a time, and its appearing powerful is not a proof that Allah has simply given it free rein, or that it has become so strong that it can no longer be overcome, or that falsehood will remain harmful to truth forever. This can never be so.

Likewise, the defeat of truth in a battle and its emergence afflicted by calamities, or truth being weakened in some era, does not mean that Allah is doing any injustice to it, or that Allah has forgotten truth, or that He has left falsehood free to uproot truth from its roots and destroy it.

It can never be so. Rather, it is the profound wisdom and planning of Allah that is carrying out its work everywhere. Sometimes the demand of wisdom is that falsehood be given respite so that it reaches its final limit; it displays all its evil consequences, places unbearable burdens upon people, and eventually becomes deserving of the harshest assault. Then truth is put to trial so that a distinction is made between truth and falsehood, between the good and the wicked, and those who remain steadfast in these trials receive a great reward and become deserving of a distinguished station. In its reality, this situation is a gain for truth and a loss for falsehood. Where this gain is increasing to the greatest extent, that loss is also increasing to the greatest extent.

﴿And let not those who disbelieve think that Our giving them respite is good for themselves. We only give them respite so that they may increase in sin, and for them is a humiliating punishment.﴾

"O Prophet, let not the activities of those who are exerting great effort in the path of disbelief grieve you. They will not be able to harm Allah in any way. Allah's will is that He should not give them any share in the Hereafter, and eventually they are to receive a severe punishment."

This is consolation for the Prophet (ﷺ), through which the sadness of his heart caused by these events is removed. He was greatly distressed that those who serve disbelief are rushing headlong into disbelief. They are advancing with extreme speed, as though a goal has been set for them and they must attain it.

These are words and an expression through which the true psychological state of these people is portrayed. Often it is seen that some people are zealous in disbelief. They make falsehood, evil, and disobedience to Allah their ideal, as though they must reach a goal in opposition to it. Therefore such people advance with great strength, great boldness, and great speed; sometimes it appears as though someone is pushing them from behind, saying "Go forward," or someone is calling to them from ahead, "Hurry, this is your reward."

Your sadness and grief were for this creation of Allah. You looked at them with longing, seeing that these people, with their sleeves rolled up, were rushing swiftly toward the fire, and you did not have the power to stop them by force. These people do not even lend an ear to Allah's repeated warnings. Then you were also distressed that these people, who are rushing headlong toward Hell with their sleeves rolled up, are not only afflicting themselves but, along with that, are also becoming a cause of grief, sorrow, and pain for the Muslims. These people are also causing pain to the Islamic call and are blocking its spread among the masses, because the general Arab population was watching what the outcome of the struggle between Madinah and Makkah would be, so that they too might join the ranks whose future is bright. When the Quraysh became Muslim and submitted, all people entered the religion of Allah in multitudes. There is no doubt that this situation had an effect upon the heart of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Therefore it became necessary for Allah, the Exalted, to reassure the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He was consoled, and the sadness of his heart was removed.

﴿And let not those who hasten toward disbelief grieve you. Indeed, they will never harm Allah at all.﴾

"O Prophet, let not the activities of those who today are exerting great effort in the path of disbelief grieve you. They will not be able to harm Allah in any way." These weak servants cannot be such that they could cause harm to Allah. And this point needs no explanation: it is Allah's will that the ideological war remain ideological, and that the confrontation with the polytheists remain in its place, and that it be His own war and His own confrontation. Therefore the burden of this responsibility is lifted from the shoulders of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Likewise, the Muslims are also not under obligation to be bound to change people's beliefs. Those who show zeal in disbelief are in reality fighting a war against Allah, and in this war with Allah they can never achieve success, because they are extremely weak in comparison to that Divine Being. Therefore they cannot cause any ultimate harm to the Islamic call. And from this, the conclusion automatically follows that they also cannot cause harm to those bearers of the Islamic call whom they consider defeated at present, no matter how much speed they show and no matter how much torment they inflict upon the people of the call.

Now the question arises: why has Allah given them this free rein to advance successfully and to be unable to contain themselves because of their dominance, even though they are Allah's direct enemies? Because Allah has prepared for them an extremely evil and extremely humiliating end.

﴿Allah intends not to give them any share in the Hereafter.﴾ Allah wills that He should not give them any share in the Hereafter. Allah wishes that they should exhaust all their capital here, and that they should be carrying all their sins, and that in the Hereafter they should become deserving of all punishment, and that they should reach their final destination by rushing swiftly forward in the path of disbelief. Because ﴿for them is a great punishment.﴾

And why has Allah decided upon this shameful end for these people? Because they, by their own will, bought disbelief in exchange for faith, and thereby made themselves deserving of it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 177:

﴿Indeed, those who exchange faith for disbelief will never harm Allah at all, and for them is a painful punishment.﴾ ... Those who abandoned faith and became buyers of disbelief are certainly not harming Allah in any way. For them there is a painful punishment prepared.

Faith was within their reach. The proofs of faith are scattered throughout this entire universe. Within human nature itself and within the self there are proofs of faith. Within the marvellous design of the human body, within its complete harmony, within the human nature placed in it, then within the harmony between human nature and this physical existence, then within the innate awareness of its Creator and Fashioner that has been deposited in it, and then within the best psychological and natural disposition of that awareness, there are proofs upon proofs. Besides these proofs, the call of the Messengers has also remained present and still is. This call exists in its natural state, which human nature accepts. Within this nature and this call of the Messengers there is a beautiful harmony, and this call possesses complete capacity for the needs of people and for their lives.

Yes, faith was fully present before them; it was within their grasp. They, and they alone, left the path of faith and purchased the path of disbelief. And they did this knowingly and deliberately. Therefore they became deserving that Allah leave them in the state where they rush headlong on the path of disbelief, so that they spend their entire life's capital on that path, and no share of reward in the Hereafter remains for them. And this is the reason that they are not capable of causing any harm to Allah. This is because they have become utterly misguided, and no even slight measure of truth remains with them. Allah has not sent down any proof or any power in favour of misguidance. Therefore, in its reality, falsehood has no strength. Hence they can never cause any harm to the people of truth and to the Islamic call. For even if they have any power, it is very weak and feeble, even though they may puff themselves up and display it, and even though the Muslims may temporarily suffer grief and distress due to some defeat.

﴿And for them is a painful punishment.﴾ ... This will be so distressing that its very conception cannot be imagined, and such grief and anguish they cannot inflict upon the Muslims in this world.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 3, verse 178:

"And let not those who disbelieve think that Our giving them respite is good for them. We give them respite only that they may increase in sin. And for them is a humiliating punishment."

Here the discussion arrives at the point that had been causing unease in some hearts. Some hearts were asking this question, and the disquiet that some people's souls were feeling was this: they saw that some enemies of Allah and some enemies of the truth were being given respite, and were not caught in the grip of the punishment of Allah. Apparently they eat and drink well, they enjoy strength, rule, wealth and status, and they themselves are being afflicted by trial, while they also spread mischief in the world around them. And those believers whose faith is weak hold improper notions and ideas about Allah, like those of the Age of Ignorance. They thought that perhaps Allah is pleased with falsehood, evil, rejection of the truth, disbelief and transgression, God forbid. Therefore He grants them respite and loosens the rope for them. They also supposed that Allah does not intervene in the battle between truth and falsehood, so they leave falsehood free to let go of the truth, and Allah does nothing to support and help it; or they think that perhaps falsehood is itself the truth. Had this not been so, Allah would not have let it flourish, grow and prevail. Or they thought that falsehood's right is that it should prevail over the truth, and the position of the Arabian Peninsula should remain thus, and that there is no supremacy for truth; otherwise why would Allah leave the people of falsehood, oppressors, rebels and mischief-makers in such a way that they remain active in falsehood, hasten towards disbelief, remain bewildered in transgression, and think that they have become firmly established and that now no force can stand before them.

All these were false thoughts. The thinking about Allah was bad. The matter was not so, therefore Allah Himself warns the people of disbelief that they should by no means suppose such a thing. The fact that the grip of Allah's seizure does not encircle you, although they are rushing ahead in disbelief, and that what is given to them of abundant enjoyment in this world, from which they derive pleasure and advance further in misguidance, is not so; rather, the reason is that it is a further trial for them. This is Allah's firm plan, and it is a severe test for them that their rope has been left loose.

"Let not those who disbelieve think that Our giving them respite is good for them. We give them respite only that they may increase in sin. And for them is a humiliating punishment."

If they were deserving that Allah should remove them from these blessings and place them in a trial that would open their eyes, Allah would certainly place them in such a trial. But the reality is that Allah does not desire any good for them, because they have bought disbelief in exchange for faith. Then they are advancing quickly in the field of disbelief and striving in it. Therefore now they are not deserving that Allah should awaken them from this heedlessness and slumber and place them in trial. It is better for them to remain immersed in the intoxication of divine blessings and the pride of power and rule. Therefore "for them is a humiliating punishment." It is a punishment that causes humiliation, and in contrast to it, the believers will have elevated station, rank and blessings.

From this it becomes clear that trial is also a blessing from Allah, and this blessing is bestowed only upon the person for whom Allah has intended good and success. If trial falls upon the friends of Allah, then some good is hidden in it for them, even though the trial may initially have come because of their own actions and as a result of their own deeds. In any case, some hidden wisdom is at work in it, some extremely subtle plan, and the grace and kindness of Allah upon His friends is intended.

Thus hearts settle in their place, the human self becomes content, and the clear and straightforward realities of Islam become part of the Muslims' conception.

It was the requirement of Allah's wisdom, and a great good from Allah upon the Muslims, that He sifted them and separated them from the hypocrites who had infiltrated their ranks, and their coming had various causes. They had not come because they had any love or interest in Islam, but they had infiltrated the Islamic ranks due to various circumstances. Therefore Allah put the Muslims to trial at Uhud, and this trial also came upon them because of their own thinking and some of their actions; yet the wisdom in it was that the khabith (the impure) and the tayyib (the pure) would be distinguished within the ranks of the mujahideen of the path of truth.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 3, verse 179 (part 1 of 3):

Here this verse decisively settles that it is not the majesty of Allah, nor the demand of His divinity, nor the established way of His universe, that He should leave the hypocrites hidden within the ranks of the Muslims in this manner. The condition is that the hypocrites merely make claims of faith, display Islam, and remain hidden within the Islamic ranks, while their hearts are devoid of the freshness of faith and the spirit of Islam is entirely absent from them. Allah has raised this ummah so that it may play a great role in this universe. It should rise up with a great system of life's knowledge and bring into being a unique situation on this earth. A new system should come into existence. The demand of this mission and this great objective was that it should hold fast to this objective firmly, with complete single-mindedness, complete purity and complete discernment, and that there should be no disorder or weakness within its ranks, and no weakness in its foundations. In brief, the demand of these aims was that this ummah should be as great as its objective is great, the objective and target to which it must arrive in this universe. And the lofty station of the Hereafter has, in any case, been prepared by Allah for them.

All these matters demand that the Islamic ranks remain awake at all times, so that corrupt elements may be expelled from them. It should keep such pressure upon its workers that whatever brick is unbaked will settle on the very first day. And they should remain under constant light, so that inner weaknesses and evil thoughts within the conscience may continue to be purified. This is why Allah also assisted them in cleansing their ranks. It was not befitting the majesty of Allah to leave such impure people within the ranks of His friends.

Moreover, it is not Allah's way to give people direct knowledge of unseen matters, because knowledge of the unseen belongs only to Allah. By their nature, with which they were created, human beings are not capable of perceiving unseen information. The machinery of the human body that has been created within them has not been fashioned according to a plan that would enable it to perceive unseen matters, except that Allah grants someone a certain measure of it. And this too happens under special wisdom, namely to the extent that it is necessary for the purposes of their vicegerency on earth. For the purpose of man's duty of vicegerency on earth, there is no need at all for knowledge of the unseen. If Allah were to open the doors of unseen knowledge upon this existing human machinery, this machinery would be destroyed, because it is not at all prepared to receive the knowledge of the unseen. Man needs only as much knowledge of the unseen as is related to the joining of his soul with his Creator and the uniting of his existence with the existence of the universe. The least harm of being informed of the unseen would be that he would stop moving his hands and feet, would constantly think about the consequences that are yet to occur, and would be unable even to think of any kind of progress on this earth.

This is why it was not befitting Allah's majesty to inform people of the knowledge of the unseen, nor was it in accordance with the wisdom and plan by which He runs this earth.

The question is: how then does Allah separate the evil from the good? And how does His way and His majesty operate in this process of purification? How does He sift it and set it apart? How does He remove dust and haze? How does He, by separating the hypocrites, purify the Islamic ranks, so that Muslims may fulfil on this earth the role for which they have been raised as an ummah?

﴿But Allah chooses of His messengers whom He wills﴾: Allah separates the genuine from the counterfeit in this way: He sent the messengers, some believed in them, and some denied them. The fulfilment of the requirements of prophethood was ordained through the institution of jihad, and within jihad people were put into trials and tested. Through all these measures the majesty of Allah becomes manifest. Thus Allah's sunnah operates, and thus the genuine is separated from the counterfeit. Hearts are purified, souls become pure, and what is in Allah's decree becomes apparent.

In this way a part of Allah's wisdom is unveiled. This wisdom manifests in life as reality, and it takes root upon the earth on a firm foundation, openly, like a shining star... Keeping in view this reality, which is luminous, which is clear, which is simple and comprehensible, Allah now turns to the believers and gives them counsel that they should create genuine faith within their own selves, and then fulfil the requirements of that genuine faith, and they are told that there is a great bounty awaiting them in the Hereafter.

﴿So believe in Allah and His messengers. And if you believe and become God-fearing, you will have a great reward﴾. After the narration of the events of Uhud and the subsequent commentary and criticism of those events, this is the excellent guidance and counsel given to the believers.

Regarding the battle of Uhud, the Qur'an has made comments in which certain very important and great truths are pointed out. It is not possible to enumerate all these truths and give complete details of them here, but it is appropriate to indicate those among these truths that are more general, comprehensive and more evident, so that all the events that occurred in this battle may be inferred from these indications, as the Qur'an has presented them as lessons.

1. This battle and this lengthy commentary upon it have fully explained one fundamental truth: what the essential nature of this religion is, which in reality is a system of life for mankind, and how it operates within human lives. This is a most foundational, simple and comprehensible truth, yet it is often entirely overlooked or not comprehended from the outset, and because of forgetting it and failing to understand it, gross errors are committed in understanding this religion. Not only is there error in grasping the reality of this religion, but there is also error in understanding this history, and in understanding the role it has played, or plays, or will play in human life, there is also a most gross error.

Some among us expect that the religion of Islam, which is Allah's prescribed system for human life, should work miraculously. In this expectation, no regard is given to its human nature, its natural power, or the material circumstances existing at any given time, whatever stage of progress people may be in, and whatever society and environment they may be in.

When these people see that Islam does not work in this miraculous and magical manner, but rather that Islam works in accordance with human power, and that the limited human capacity and man's fundamental basic condition work together, then at times man and the circumstances of the time are clearly influenced by the Islamic system, or both together influence people's response to Islam. At times the effects of both are against Islam. As a result, people sit down heavy like mud. Greed, pleasure and lust become so important in their eyes that they stand as a barrier in the way of accepting Islam's message, and people do not walk in the Islamic direction. When such people see such a situation, they fall into disappointment, and this situation runs contrary to their expectations, because this religion comes from Allah... And at times they begin to doubt whether this religion is in fact a complete system of life for people, and going further still, some people doubt the very truth of this religion.

The root of these errors in thought and action lies in just one mistake: such people have not understood the very nature of this religion, nor its method, or they have understood this reality and then forgotten it.

The truth is that this religion is a methodology for human life, and its establishment within human life has been made dependent upon purely human striving, and this striving has been confined within human power. The commencement of acting upon this religion is made from the point where a person stands at a certain stage of the progress of his material life; this religion takes them from where it finds them and carries them forward, and brings them to their final destination. All of this is done within the limits of human power and capacity. And it advances them as far as their power and capacity extend, and as far as they can reach and have the ability to reach.

In this work its distinguishing feature is that it does not neglect this work for a single moment. It does not neglect any plan. It does not neglect any initiative. It works in accordance with human nature, working within the limits of human power. It works in accordance with the degree of material development a person has attained, and along with that it takes him to the point he has not yet reached, a point that humanity has never reached in any of the eras of all the systems of life devised by man in human history. Islam has demonstrated these achievements in practice whenever it has been implemented, even for a short time, and it will continue to do so in the future, provided effort is made for its implementation.

But the truth is that the error began because of not understanding the nature of this religion, or understanding it and then forgetting it, as we have done. We began to await a miraculous and magical revolution for the implementation of the religion, which is not suited to the human condition, which changes human nature, and which changes the nature of Islam. This method does not fit its true nature. It is also contrary to its capacity and its inclinations, and contrary to the material conditions of man.

Is Islam not from Allah? Is it not sent down by a power capable of everything, which no power can overpower? Then why has the establishment of Islam been made dependent upon the limits of human power, and why has it been made to require human striving? Why does it not happen that people work for it and it always prevails? Why are Islamic people not always successful? Why do human carnal desires, temperament and material circumstances overcome them, and why does it happen at times that the people of truth suffer a crushing defeat, although they are the people of truth?

All these questions, as we have stated, are genuine questions, and they arise because we have not understood the true nature of this religion, although its nature and its method are most simple; or we have understood them and forgotten them.

It is a reality that Allah is Absolutely Powerful, and He can also change human nature, whether He changes it through this religion or adopts some other method for it. He was also capable of creating mankind from the beginning upon a different nature. But His will was that He create man upon his present nature. And Allah chose to make man one who possesses will, and that he should have within him the capacity to accept guidance and misguidance. His will also was that guidance be made dependent upon human striving, upon man's seeking of guidance, and upon his receptive capacity. Then Allah's will decreed that human nature should always continue to function, and that it could not be erased in any form, nor changed, nor rendered inoperative; and His will was also that the Islamic system of life be established upon this earth through human striving, and be established within the limits of human power and capacity. And it was also a part of the divine will that man receives exactly what he strives for according to his capacity, in accordance with the day and night of his life, and within the framework of the circumstances actually present.

It is not the right of any human being to ask why Allah willed it thus. As long as man is a servant and God is the Deity, because man does not possess complete knowledge of the system of this universe, nor is there any possibility of man ever attaining that knowledge. Nor can man obtain knowledge of what the demands of the universal system are with respect to each existent in this universe, and what wisdom lies behind the planning and formation of man's present nature. Therefore, in such matters a sincere Muslim cannot even pose the question "why?" I think that even a serious atheist cannot ask "why?" The believer cannot ask it because he should be very reverent in the presence of the Divine, since his heart knows the reality of the Divine Being and His attributes, and he also knows that this is not the field of human perception. And the disbeliever does not ask it because he does not acknowledge God at all. If he had true knowledge of the Divine Being, he would acknowledge His essence and attributes, and would know the requirements of divinity.

Yes, some people who are not serious and are morally degraded ask such questions. They are neither serious and sincere Muslims, nor serious and sincere disbelievers. Therefore, it is not necessary to be very interested in this question, nor should it be taken seriously.

Sometimes an ignorant person asks about the Divine Being. Such an ignorant person's question should not be answered directly. Only the reality of Allah's divinity should be explained to him: if he grasps it, he is a believer, and if he cannot grasp it, he is a disbeliever. With such an ignorant person, the matter ends there. Otherwise, this person would be engaging in argument for the sake of argument.

The fact is that none of Allah's creatures has the right to raise the question of why Allah created human beings with this present nature. Why does this nature keep functioning, and why can it not be erased, changed, or suspended? And then, why did Allah make the establishment of the Islamic system of life dependent on human struggle, and make struggle within human capacity a requirement?

It is every person's duty to understand this reality. Let him see how human nature functions within the human environment. Then let him study human history in this natural manner. In this way, he will understand the real causes of historical events, and secondly, he will also know how the course of history can be turned.

This system of life which we call Islam, as it was presented by Hazrat Muhammad (ﷺ), cannot be established and put into effect in this earth, among these people, merely on the basis that it has been revealed by Allah. Nor can it be enforced merely through "preaching" and "explanation." Nor can it be enforced in the manner that Allah enforces the laws of nature and the principles of creation, which He has set in motion for the revolution of the heavens, the movement of the stars, and the natural consequences that follow natural causes. Rather, the method prescribed for it is that a human community should rise to carry it, which first believes in it firmly, then itself acts upon it fully, and makes it its life's duty and objective according to its capacity. Then this community should strive for the transmission of this faith into the hearts of others and the establishment of this system in their lives, and strive to such an extent that it exerts its full strength in this cause. It should wage jihad against human weaknesses, it should wage jihad against human desires, and it should wage jihad against the ignorance of its own self and the ignorance of other souls. It should wage jihad against those who, because of human weaknesses, carnal desires and ignorance, stand blocking the path of this system of life, and it should establish this system of life to the extent that human temperament and capacity can bear it. It should take people from the level at which they actually stand in terms of their development. It should not ignore the real circumstances of people's lives. Likewise, it should not ignore the demands of people's real conditions, and should run this system in accordance with those conditions and demands. This community of people should first gain victory over its own self, and then at times it gains victory over the people of its environment, and at times it may be that it suffers defeat at the hands of its own self and the people of its environment. This should be in accordance with its struggle, in accordance with the practical methods that this community adopted, or to the extent that it was granted the capacity to adopt them. Then for this community, before everything, before every struggle, and before every means and method, a second fundamental element is also necessary: how sincere this community is to this objective, and how far it is implementing it within its own self. And how close its relationship is with Allah, the Revealer of this system? How much confidence does it have in Him, and how much reliance and trust does it place in Him?

This is the true reality of this religion, this is its method of enforcement, and this is the plan of its movement. And this is precisely what Allah wishes to make clear to the Muslim community. The entire summary of the accounts of the Battle of Uhud and the comments made upon those events is exactly this.

Now, at the occasion of Uhud, when the Islamic community fell somewhat short in giving practical shape within themselves to complete Islam, which at that time included the commands of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and fell short in taking certain practical measures at certain positions, and when it failed to grasp this great foundational reality mentioned above, and thought that "we will certainly be successful, because this religion and this system is from Allah," and on this basis it ignored its own measures and plans, then Allah afflicted it with defeat, so that it might also taste the bitter experiences. Accordingly, after that experience, the Qur'an sought to remove their misunderstanding through its commentary.

﴿Or when a calamity struck you, though you had inflicted twice as much (on the enemy), did you say, "How is this?" Say, "It is from yourselves." Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.﴾

As has been stated earlier in the context, Allah does not leave the believers at this stage, but connects them to the decree of Allah which operates behind these causes and consequences, and Allah tells them that behind this trial lies Allah's will that He desires good for them; as for the trial itself, it comes upon them because of their own actions and apparent causes.

The decision that the establishment of the Islamic system of life has been left to human struggle, and that it is affected by the human measures they take regarding it, contains a great good for human beings, because the Islamic system of life desires reform instead of corruption, and does not desire to suspend it. It desires the reform of human nature in such a way that it awakens it and brings it to moderation. This is because faith in any heart cannot become complete and perfect unless that person confronts people in the context of Islam. He will carry out this jihad first through preaching and explanation. After that, he will carry out jihad with his hand, when the opposing force of Islam is forcibly blocking the path of guidance. In this matter, a period of trial may also come upon this believer in which he must exercise patience, bear hardships, suffer defeat, and remain steadfast upon it. If victory is granted, he must remain serious, because at the time of victory, patience and seriousness are more difficult than at the time of defeat, until the hearts are purified, the crude element is shed from the ranks, the community is set upon its correct path, ascends along its straight way upward, and in all this activity remains trusting in Allah.

Understand well that as long as the Muslim heart does not struggle and wage jihad against people in matters of faith, it will be extremely difficult for the reality of faith to settle in their hearts. This is because before contending and struggling with people, he must have struggled with his own self. And after this jihad, there will open before him horizons of faith that could never have opened before him as long as he sat idle, accustomed to living a peaceful life, compromising with everyone and getting along in every situation. When he begins jihad, he will see realities among people, and some realities of life will become clear to him that could never have become clear to him until he began striving in the way of Allah. As a result of this jihad in the way of Allah, his self, his consciousness, his ideas, his habits, his temperament, his impressions, and his capacity to accept truth will reach a level to which he could never have reached without it. In short, this hard and bitter experience of jihad transforms a person into pure gold.

Likewise, within a Muslim community too, the reality of faith cannot become complete and firm until it passes through experience, testing, and trial, and until each of its members knows the reality of his own strength, until that individual knows his objective. Similarly, this community too must know all of the bricks of which it is made: how much weight each brick can bear, and how closely those bricks are bound together at the time of difficulty and collision.

This was the wisdom which Allah wished to make the Muslim community understand, and this wisdom was explained to it in the training course given to it on the field of Uhud. And after that, in the comment made on the events of Uhud in this surah, this same wisdom was also explained to it, when after mentioning the apparent causes of defeat, Allah said: "The harm that befell you on the day the two armies met was by Allah's permission, and so that He might know the believers and know the hypocrites." And elsewhere He said: "Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in now, until He separates the wicked from the good." And after that, Allah refers them to His wisdom and decree, that is, the decree and wisdom behind those causes. Thus He turns them toward this great reality and truth of faith, which cannot be completed until it settles within the human soul. He says: "If a wound has touched you, a similar wound has already touched the enemy. These are the days of alternation which We turn among people, so that Allah may know those who believe, and take witnesses from among you. And Allah does not love the wrongdoers. And He wished to purify the believers through trial and to destroy the disbelievers."

So this is now Allah's decree, His planning, and His wisdom, operating behind these causes, operating behind these events. And it is the true effective agent behind all these persons and all their movements. And this is the complete, comprehensive, and all-encompassing concept of Islam. And this concept settles into the human mind as a result of these events. And the comment made on these events also contains clear indications toward it.

2. Through the events of this battle and these comments, another reality becomes clear. That is, considering the human self, human nature, the temperament of human struggle, and all these matters, the possibilities of achieving the obligation of establishing the religion... The truth is that the human self is not perfect, and in its real state it is not perfect; yet along with this it is also a reality that it is capable of development and progress, and in this field it can reach the heights of advancement and perfection that have been set as its limit.

Let us examine one human community, which exists before us in its real form. This community is in the form of the group of the Companions, concerning which the Holy Qur'an says: "You are the best community brought forth for mankind..." These Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were the best community. They were the soul of all humanity and the salt of the earth. But regarding the study of this community of Companions presented in this surah: "Those of you who turned away on the day the two hosts met, it was Satan who caused them to slip because of some of their deeds. Allah has forgiven them." And concerning some other Companions: "But when you showed weakness and disputed in the matter, and when that which you loved was shown to you, you disobeyed the command of your leader, because some of you desired the world and some desired the Hereafter." "And indeed Allah has pardoned you..." Concerning them the Qur'an says: "When two groups among you were about to lose heart, though Allah was their helper, and upon Allah let the believers put their trust." Some of these same persons were defeated, and they were exposed, and concerning their rout Allah Himself says:

"When you were fleeing without turning back to anyone, and the Messenger was calling you from behind. Then Allah repaid you with grief upon grief, so that you would not grieve over what escaped you or what befell you."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 3, verse 179 (part 3 of 3):

The participants of the Battle of Badr were all believers and Muslims. But this was the early period of Islam, when the community was still being trained and formed. Yet they were serious and sincere in adopting the Islamic way of life (nazariya-e-hayat). They had entrusted their entire affair to Allah. They were content with Allah's guidance. They had bowed their heads before this system of life.

That is why Allah did not cast them away from the abode of His mercy. He showed them mercy and pardoned them, and He commanded the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) also to pardon them and to seek forgiveness for them. And Allah also commanded the Messenger (ﷺ) that he must certainly consult them. Despite their mistakes, and despite the loss suffered at Uhud as a result of that consultation, Allah let them taste the consequences of their own affairs and actions, and placed them in such a harsh and bitter trial. Yet, despite these mistakes, He did not throw them out of the ranks of Islam, nor did He issue the verdict: "Go, you are not fit for this task, since experience has proven that weaknesses appeared in you and you committed errors." Rather, Islam accepted their mistakes and weaknesses. By placing them in this trial, their training was carried out. After that, by commenting further on their mistakes, further training was given. And after that, by admonition and giving instructions, further training was given. And this admonition and this exhortation was also delivered in an extremely compassionate manner, with forgiveness and forbearance, just as an elder trains his children. They are burned by fire so that they may know that fire burns, and so that they may become alert.

Allah exposed their weakness to them and also made them aware of the hidden thoughts of their hearts. Not so that they would be put to shame, or humiliated, or regarded as contemptible, or so that they would be compelled and burdened with what they cannot bear, but so that their hands would be held, they would be guided, self-confidence would be instilled in them, they would not regard themselves as worthless, and they would never despair, as long as they hold firmly to the strong rope of Allah.

After this training they returned to their true station. They reached their final destination, and that spirit arose in them which they had at the beginning of the battle of Uhud. Today only one night has passed since the defeat and the wounding, and they are setting out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in pursuit. Today there was neither fear in their hearts nor hesitation. Today they were not paying any heed to the words of those who were frightening them with these words:

الَّذِينَ قَالَ لَهُمُ النَّاسُ إِنَّ النَّاسَ قَدْ جَمَعُوا لَكُمْ فَاخْشَوْهُمْ فَزَادَهُمْ إِيمَانًا وَقَالُوا حَسْبُنَا اللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ

"Those to whom people said: 'Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them.' But this increased them in faith, and they said: 'Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.'"

And after this, as the members of the community grew up and matured, their situation also changed, and their accountability began to be carried out in the manner in which it is carried out for adults and mature individuals. But at the beginning, their training was the same as the training of children. Whoever reads the account of the Battle of Tabuk (in Surah Al-Bara'ah) will find that a few individuals remained behind from that expedition. The Messenger (ﷺ) held them to a severe accountability. This was a very harsh accountability. From this, a clear difference will be seen between the policy at Uhud and the policy at Tabuk, because by then the community had advanced far in terms of training. But when these very people were at Uhud, they were dealt with gently, because at the time of Tabuk they were in the final stage of training. Yet, despite this, they were human beings. Even so, human weakness remained in them, a mistake occurred, but within them there was acknowledgment of the mistake and a readiness to repent, and in the end forgiveness was granted.

In short, in Islamic life the humanity of a human being has always been kept in view. It is not changed, it is not suspended, and no burden is placed on him beyond his capacity, although the Islamic system of life raises him in this world to the lofty station that is destined for him.

This approach of Islam is very important from the perspective that it always endows a person with the ray of hope, so that he continues striving for perfection and moves forward. But under the shade of the Islamic system of life, this community reached the lofty station, having begun its journey from the fallen state in which it lay when Islam came. Along the way, lapses continued to occur, because the path was arduous, and that community was, after all, a human community that had risen from an extremely backward society immersed in jahiliyyah, backward in every respect, as we presented examples of when explaining the verses. The effect of this policy of Islam is that it fills humanity with the hope of reaching that lofty station, even if the present conditions of a society are worse than bad. Then, by raising the ummah from that backward society, Islam brings about such progress that its like is not found in the entire history of humanity until today. This example has not yet been repeated, although it was not a miraculous revolution that cannot be repeated, but rather a revolution that took place under Islamic life, that came about as a result of human struggle, within the limits of human capacity. Even today this revolution can be brought about by that same human power, and indeed an even greater revolution is possible.

In short, Islamic life takes society from where it is and from the level of material progress it has already reached. Then it advances it further, as it did with the jahiliyyah-stricken, backward society of the Arabs, which was at the most elementary stages, extremely lowly. And within an extremely short period, which was less than a quarter of a century, Islam carried that society to the pinnacle of perfection.

But for this, one essential condition is required: that a human society hand over its reins to this system, believe in it, and bow its head before it. It must make it the principle of its life, make it the emblem of its movement, and walk alongside it on this long and arduous journey.
