**Lesson 28: At a Glance**

With this, the account of the Battle of Uhud comes to an end. But the struggle of the Muslim community against the enemies of Islam, who were spread across the surrounding region, had not yet ended. The Jews in particular had launched debates and disputes, sought to create doubt and unrest, plotted conspiracies, and looked for opportunities to strike from ambush. Most of the discussions in this surah revolve around this confrontation and are spread across it.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had expelled the tribe of Banu Qaynuqa from the outskirts of Medina, because after the Battle of Badr they had become seriously alarmed and had begun to plot. They started provoking the Muslims and openly broke the covenants that had been made with them. These covenants had been concluded with them immediately after the Prophet (ﷺ) migrated to Medina, at a time when most of the Aws and Khazraj had embraced Islam, and an Islamic state had been established in Medina. But around Medina, Banu al-Nadir and Banu Qurayza were still present. Besides them, there were the Jews of Khaybar and other Jews of the Arabian Peninsula. All of these people were in correspondence with one another, gathering armies, forging ties with the hypocrites of Medina, maintaining links with the disbelievers around Medina, and with the polytheists of Makkah. Against the Muslims, they had initiated an unending chain of conspiracies.

Allah says: "Say to those who disbelieve: 'You will be overcome and gathered into Hell, and what a wretched resting place it is.' There was a sign for you in the two hosts that met: one fighting in the way of Allah, and the other disbelieving, who saw them with their own eyes as twice their number. Yet Allah supports with His victory whom He wills. Indeed, in that is a lesson for those who have insight."

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conveyed to them this warning from Allah, which had been revealed because all the activities they were displaying in those days were known to Allah, and because of the hostility visible from them, and since after Badr they had been continually engaged in conspiracies, they rejected this warning in a very wicked and contemptuous manner. They said: "Muhammad, do not let yourself be deceived by pride. You have indeed killed some of the people of Quraysh. Those people were inexperienced; they did not know how war is fought. By Allah, if you ever fight us, you will come to know that we are something. Surely you will not find people like us." After this reply, they took part in conspiracies. This surah reports some aspects of their conspiracies. Eventually they broke the covenant they had made with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger (ﷺ) besieged them, and they became ready to surrender to his judgment. The Messenger (ﷺ) expelled them from Medina and sent them to Adhruʿat.

Only two groups of Jews remained in Medina: Banu Qurayza and Banu al-Nadir. Although they outwardly kept the covenant, secretly they too were engaged in conspiracies, deceit, treachery, mischief-making, and spreading rumours. In short, they began doing all the things that the Jews have skilfully done throughout their history. The Book of Allah has recorded this in full detail, and the inhabitants of the whole earth have been warned about them: that they are a cursed people on this earth.

In this lesson, some of the sayings and deeds of the Children of Israel are taken up. It becomes clear that they had gone so far as to show disrespect even in the presence of the Lord, the Mighty. Mistreating the Muslims was no matter at all to them. They would evade fulfilling their financial obligations under the Mithaq-e-Madina (Charter of Medina), which they had concluded themselves with the Prophet (ﷺ). They used to say: "Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich."

In this lesson, one also finds the frivolous arguments that the Jews used to put forward against the call to Islam whenever it was presented to them. All of these arguments were false, and historically they had no basis. For example, they were violating the covenant they had made with Allah. That covenant was that they would explain the commands of Allah and the truth, and would never conceal them. They had broken this covenant, cast it behind their backs, and in exchange gained worldly benefits. They killed their prophets unjustly, although those prophets had shown them miracles beyond the ordinary, as they had demanded. Moreover, those prophets had come with clear proofs, yet these Jews rejected them.

Because of the mention of these shameful sayings and deeds of the Jews, and the expression of their insolence towards the prophets and in the presence of the Lord, the Jews living around Medina became enemies of this newly formed Muslim community. Also in this lesson it is explained how greatly the Muslims were being harmed by the conspiracies and persecutions of the Jews and the polytheists. Mentioning these matters was extremely necessary here for the training of the Muslim community, so that they would be informed with insight about their surroundings, and would know who the people living around them are. This was so that the believers would understand well the conditions of the land in which they were working, and what difficulties lay in their path, where snares had been laid beneath the ground, and what trials were prepared for them on this path. The conspiracies that the Jews were carrying out against the Muslims in Medina were not less dangerous than the hostilities that the polytheists of Makkah were showing towards the Muslims. It is likely that most of the conspiracies against the Muslims throughout the entire history of Islam have been carried out by the Jews. They have always been dangerous for the Muslims.

In this impactful lesson, guidance on this subject is given repeatedly. The Muslims are told which values are lasting and which values are perishable, because worldly life is only for a limited time. Every soul shall taste death one day. The true reward will be received in the Hereafter, and the real gain and loss will be known there. Whoever is saved from the Fire there and admitted into Paradise has, in effect, succeeded. The world is full of goods which at every moment can deceive a person. Our wealth and our lives are a trust from Allah in our hands. You will continue to face hurt from the People of the Book and the polytheists. Only patience, fear of Allah, and steadfastness upon Islam can save you from the Fire, and in this way you can also be protected from these conspiracies.

The guidance given to the first community of Medina is fresh guidance for us today as well, and it will remain guidance for us tomorrow. Those who wish to re-establish Islam, and those who want to establish an Islamic way of life, will see with their own eyes that their enemies have the same character as the enemies of Medina. These enemies are the same polytheists and the godless among the People of the Book. Today the Jews have come in the form of global Zionism. The Christians are present in the form of the global cross, and in the form of global communism. Even today, the Islamic movement is told that the obstacles in its path, and the snares laid out, require the same sacrifices, the same persecutions, and the same trials. But keep your gaze fixed on the Hereafter. You will have to bear losses of wealth and life, but, like the first Islamic community, you too must remember that same lesson. "Eventually every person must die, and you will all receive your full reward on the Day of Resurrection. The one who truly succeeds is the one who is saved from the Fire of Hell there and is admitted into Paradise. As for this world, it is merely a deceptive enjoyment… O Muslims! You will surely be tested in your wealth and your lives, and you will hear many hurtful words from the People of the Book and the polytheists. If you remain patient and conscious of Allah in all these circumstances, that is indeed a matter of great resolve."

In short, the Qur'an is the same Qur'an that it always was, and its status is the same: it is a book containing lasting guidance for this Ummah. It is the guide and the leader of this Ummah, and it is a trustworthy commander for it. But its enemies are also the same enemies that they always were, and the path of revolution is also the same path it always was.

Regarding the first verse of this group of verses, there is no report specifying who the "misers" are, what this blameworthy act of miserliness is, against whom the warning is directed, and what their end will be on the Day of Judgment. However, given the place where this verse occurs, it appears that it relates to the verses that follow, which concern the Jews. This is because it was these Jews who said that Allah is poor and they are rich, and it was these same people who said that Allah had promised them not to believe in any messenger until he brought them a sacrifice that fire would consume.

The fact is that this verse concerns the Jews, who at that time were being called upon to fulfil the financial obligations they were bound to under the Mithaq-e-Madina. They were also being invited to accept the call of the Final Prophet and to spend in the way of Allah.

Accordingly, this threatening warning was revealed, and after it the Jews' stubborn and obstinate arguments, which they presented as reasons for not believing in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), were refuted. In these arguments they adopted an extremely insolent tone, and in truth this disrespect was directed at their own Lord. Along with the threatening warning to the Jews, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is consoled: it is true that these Jews are denying you, but the peoples to whom earlier messengers were sent treated those messengers even more harshly than they treat you. Among those messengers were the prophets of the Children of Israel, who came to them with clear proofs, and they also showed them miracles as they were demanded, as is well known in the history of the Children of Israel.

The meaning of this verse is general. It may refer to the Jews, who used to be stingy with the financial obligations imposed on them under the Mithaq-e-Madina, and it also includes others who do not spend from what they have and are miserly. They think that this miserliness is good for them, because their wealth is thereby preserved, and spending would cause that wealth to go away.

This verse forbids them from such false reckoning. It declares that whatever they hoard will become a collar around their necks on the Day of Resurrection, and that this collar will be made of fire from the front. This is a most terrifying warning. The manner of expression is such that it presents miserliness in an extremely ugly form. It is said that Allah has blessed these people with His bounty, and yet they still act miserly. They are not being miserly with their own personal wealth; rather, they are being miserly with what Allah has given. When they came into this world, they had nothing in their hands, nor did their fellow tribesmen have anything. Then Allah showed them His favour and gave them everything. When Allah demanded that they give Him a portion of what He had given them, they forgot the favour and generosity of Allah and were miserly even in returning a small part. They began to imagine that this hoarding would be beneficial to them, although it is in fact extremely harmful to them, indeed a shameful kind of harm. This is because they will certainly leave this world. They will leave this wealth and riches behind for those who come after them, and ultimately Allah is the inheritor. For "to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth." So this gold and accumulated wealth remain only for a very short time. After that, all of it returns to Allah. And what is recorded in their account is only what they spent in the way of Allah, spent seeking His pleasure. They will receive its full reward, and only in this way can they be saved from the fiery collar.

After this, severe criticism is directed at the Jews who had wealth in their hands. This wealth had been given to them by Allah, yet they began to consider themselves self-sufficient and independent of Allah, thinking that they had no need for any reward or recompense from Him, nor any need for the multiplied reward that Allah gives to those who spend in His way, and which He calls His bounty, and describes as a loan from those people. But these people answered in a base manner, as a contemptible person would, saying: "What need does Allah have to ask us for our wealth as a loan, and then multiply it for us?" Yet Allah Himself forbids usury and declares multiplied, compounding increases to be unlawful. Their statement is a mere play of words, from which it is clear that they are extremely vile, disrespectful and insolent people.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 181:

The worst thoughts about the Being of Allah are also recorded in the distorted books of the Jews. But the statement that the Qur'an has quoted from them is an extremely base conception of the Divine Being. ……………"We shall record what they say." So that they may be held to account. Their words will not simply dissolve into the air, nor will they be dismissed as nonsensical and frivolous talk. Along with the description of this insolence of theirs, a portion of their past misdeeds is also mentioned here. These are the sins that their people committed in the past. These earlier sins are entered into their account because their nature remains the same. They were disobedient and sinful in the same way.

﴿وَقَتْلَهُمُ الأَنْبِيَاءَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ﴾ ……………"And their killing of the prophets without right." ……The history of the Children of Israel has preserved the events of this abominable act of killing the prophets, and their last such exploit was the plot to kill Hadrat Masih (peace be upon him). Even now they believe that they had Hadrat Masih (peace be upon him) hanged, and they take pride in this great crime.

﴿وَنَقُولُ ذُوقُوا عَذَابَ الْحَرِيقِ﴾ ……………"We will say: Taste the punishment of the burning." The word ḥarīq, meaning burning, is used so that the terror of this punishment may be brought before the eyes, and so that it may come to mind that at the time of receiving this punishment the flames of fire will have blazed up, and they will be carrying out their task in a frightful manner. There will be a terrifying fervour in the fire. This is because their act is equally abominable: killing the prophets, killing them without any justification, and then the statement they make, which is also extremely base, that Allah is poor and they are rich.

That is because of what your own hands have sent ahead. It is the recompense of your own deeds, a full requital in which there is neither injustice nor any harshness.

And Allah is not ever unjust to His servants. Here, by using the word "ʿabīd" (servants, slaves) for the people, the true position of man has been made clear: in relation to Allah he is a slave of slaves. Yet even so, he behaves with such impertinence in the court of Allah, and though he is a servant and a slave, he says that Allah is poor and we are rich. How great is this audacity, and along with it, a heinous deed such as the killing of the prophets.

These people who say that Allah is poor and we are rich are the same ones who killed the prophets. Behold their further exploit: they say, "We do not believe in Muhammad (ﷺ) because Allah Himself has commanded us not to believe in any messenger until he brings us a sacrifice which fire comes down from the unseen realm and consumes miraculously." Just as some of the prophets of the Children of Israel were given such a miracle. And since Muhammad (ﷺ) has not shown a miracle of this kind, and since they have already made a covenant with Allah, they cannot believe in him.

Here the Qur'an answers their claim with historical references: the prophets they killed had shown miracles, and those were miracles that they themselves had demanded.

﴿Those who say, "Indeed, Allah has taken our covenant that we should not believe in any messenger until he brings us an offering which fire devours." Say, "There have already come to you messengers before me with clear proofs and with what you speak of. Then why did you kill them, if you are truthful?"﴾

This was a very forceful argumentative reply (الزامی جواب, ilzami jawab, a reply that silences the opponent by turning their own position against them). It showed that they were lying, that they twisted the matter, that they insisted upon disbelief, and that they displayed arrogance and invented falsehoods against Allah.

At this point the direction of the discourse turns toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He is consoled and comforted, and the attitude of these opponents is made bearable for him, since they have treated countless messengers in exactly this way throughout their history.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 3, verse 184:

﴿And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], then the messengers before you were denied as well, who came with clear proofs, the scriptures, and the illuminating Book.﴾ These people, if they deny you, then many messengers were denied before you, who came bringing clear signs, scriptures, and books that give light.

So the Prophet ﷺ is not the first messenger whom the People of the Book, the Jews, have denied. The Children of Israel throughout their entire history have always denied the messengers, although those messengers came to them with sound proofs. They presented miracles. They presented scriptures containing divine guidance, namely the Zabur... And they also presented the illuminating Book, such as the Torah and the Gospel. In short, this has been the method of the messengers and their messages. And on this path there are hardship and trials, and this is the only way.

The reality that this worldly life is limited, temporary, and bound to a fixed term must fully settle into the human soul, and its end is inevitable. Good people die here and bad people depart here. Those who take part in jihad die, and those who sit at home also die. Those who are exalted because of their convictions die, as do those who never endure humiliation, and the cowards die too, who want to live at any price. Those whose aspirations are lofty and whose aims are pure depart, and so do the self-seekers, whose attention is set on the petty things of the world.

All die. Kullu nafsin dha'iqatul-maut ("Every soul shall taste death"). This cup must be raised to everyone's lips, and one day everyone must bid farewell to this life. In this respect there is no distinction between one person and another. The cup of death comes before each in turn, and every person drinks from it. If there is a difference, it lies in another dimension: the difference is only in values, and the difference is in the outcome.

Wa innama tuwaffawna ujurakum yawmal-qiyamah. Faman zuhzina 'anin-nari wa udkhilal-jannata faqad faz ("And you will be paid your full rewards on the Day of Resurrection. So whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has indeed triumphed.")

This is the difference between one death and another death. This outcome is what distinguishes one person from another. This is the value that remains, and for which striving and effort are necessary, and it is the bad outcome from which one should be concerned night and day to be saved.

Faman zuhzina 'anin-nari wa udkhilal-jannata faqad faz ("Whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise is indeed successful.") The word zuhzih, by its very sound, reveals its meaning. It brings before the eyes a picture of a situation, and it has a particular quality. It is as if the Fire has a pull, so that whoever comes near it is drawn into it and enters its domain. Therefore such a person needs someone to free him gradually from this pull so that he comes out of the sphere of its attraction. Thus, whoever is made possible to be pulled away from that sphere, removed from the magnetic pull of the Fire, and admitted into Paradise, is in effect successful.

This is a clear portrayal, a living scene. It has movement and tug-of-war, and in reality the situation is exactly this. Does the Fire have a pull? Does sin not have an attraction and a pleasure? Does the human soul not need a guide who gradually draws it away from the sphere of the Fire's pull? Yes, certainly it does, and this is what saves it from the Fire. Does a person, despite continuous efforts, not always remain at fault in action, unless Allah's grace and mercy are upon him? Indeed, it is the grace of the Lord that drives him away from the Fire. Divine favour gradually draws him out of the sphere of the Fire.

Wa ma al-hayatud-dunya illa mata'ul-ghurur ("And the enjoyment of this worldly life is nothing but the delusive enjoyment.") The provision of this world is, after all, provision, but it is not real provision. It is not the provision of wakefulness and alertness. It is a provision that deceives. A person, falling into its deception, takes it to be a possession. It is a provision that produces deceit and delusion. As for the provision that is based on truth and is real, and for which one should truly strive, it is the provision of the Hereafter and the success of the Hereafter, which is that a person is turned away from the Fire.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 3, verse 186:

When this reality takes root in a person, and when the human self lets go of its craving to live by its own calculations, because every soul must in any case taste death, and likewise when it removes the deceptive goods of this world from the list of its priorities, then Allah speaks to the believers, telling them that trials of wealth and of life are coming to them. And only then are they prepared for those sacrifices.

﴿You will surely be tested in your possessions and in your selves, and you will certainly hear much hurtful talk from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate partners with Allah. But if you endure patiently and guard yourselves (in piety), then that is indeed among the matters requiring firm resolve.﴾

"O Muslims, you will certainly be tested in your wealth and in your lives, and you will hear many painful words from the People of the Book and from the polytheists. If you remain steadfast in patience and in the path of God-consciousness amid all these circumstances, that is a matter of great resolve."

It is the way (sunnah) of beliefs, ideologies, da'wah (call) and movements that trials, trials of life and trials of wealth, are necessary in them, and the human self must confront them with steadfastness, patience and resolve. This is because it is the path to Paradise, and Paradise is attained only when one abstains from disliked deeds; Paradise is surrounded by hardships, and Hellfire is surrounded by desires of the self.

This is the only way in which a community rising up with a da'wah can be established. Only in this way can the duties of da'wah be fulfilled. This is the method of training such a community, and only by this method can its hidden powers, its powers of goodness, and its powers of patience and steadfastness be awakened. This method is that obligations be fulfilled in practice, that people's real standing be known, and that the reality of life be kept in mind, namely what its true nature is. This is the only way by which firm people gather around a da'wah. It is such people who carry a da'wah forward, bear the difficulties that come in its way with patience, and it is upon such people that one can rely.

The worth of any da'wah is held by such people, who regard it as important, and the more difficulties they bear in its path, the dearer it becomes to them. Therefore they will never neglect it, whatever the circumstances.

Trial has been designated as the sunnah of every da'wah because through it both the caller and the da'wah become strong. Confrontation itself awakens the hidden powers within a person, nurtures them, gathers them together, and then directs them onto one path. Any modern da'wah should make use of these hidden powers, awaken them, so that its roots become firm and it holds deep roots within society. Then, ideologically, it should be fresh and deeply embedded in human nature.

The bearers of da'wah should know well the reality of their own selves, and should carry jihad fi sabilillah (struggle in the way of Allah) and its life together. They should know what the reality of the human self is and what hidden powers lie within it. They should know how a community and a society are formed. They should know where and in what ways the struggle will take place between the principles of their da'wah and their own carnal desires, and then how the struggle of this da'wah with all people will unfold. Then they should know through which doors Satan enters the human self, where the slippery places lie on the path, and where the swamps of misguidance are.

One benefit of this continuous struggle is that its opponents also begin to reflect upon it. They think that those who make so many sacrifices must surely have some good in it, some secret in it. These people bear such hardships on this path, and they remain firmly fixed upon their position. There comes a point at which the hearts of the opponents melt, they are broken, and at last they enter the movement group after group.

In sum, this is the sunnah of da'wah. The difficult circumstances that come upon this da'wah are circumstances in which bitter tug-of-war persists, in which the schemes of enemies are confronted, and in which one must constantly bear hardships while keeping hope in the mercy of Allah. All of these tasks can be carried out only by those who are very solid people and who are possessed of great resolve.

﴿And if you endure patiently and guard yourselves in piety, then that is among the matters requiring firm resolve.﴾

The Islamic community of Medina expected that it would face immense difficulties on its path. It was anticipating harassment, calamity and hardships, whether in life or in wealth. These would come from the People of the Book who lived around Medina, or from the hostile polytheists who were in Mecca. But these hardships would certainly come upon their path. It would never accept defeat... This community was also certain that it would have to die one day, that the true reward would be what it received in the Hereafter, that the successful one would be the one who was distanced from the Fire and admitted into Paradise, and that the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion. The Medinan community stood on such firm foundations, on open ground, and it was walking on that highway which surely leads to the intended destination. This firm and solid ground remains available even now to the bearers of the Islamic da'wah, and this open and straight highway lies before every human being. The old enemies of this da'wah are its enemies even today. Despite the passing of centuries, these enemies have not changed. Until today they remain engaged in conspiracies against it, although centuries have passed, the Qur'an is the same Qur'an, and its message is the same as it was.

Yes, it is true that the styles of trial and affliction change in every age, and new means of propaganda against this movement appear. New methods of harming it also keep arising. Its reputation is damaged, the fundamental elements of its concepts are distorted, their importance is diminished, and false impressions about the aims of the da'wah are spread. But in this matter the single principle is:

﴿You will surely be tested in your possessions and in your selves, and you will certainly hear much hurtful talk from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate partners with Allah.﴾

"O Muslims, you will certainly be tested in your wealth and in your lives, and you will hear many painful words from the People of the Book and from the polytheists."

In this surah a large part of the schemes of the People of the Book has been unmasked. It is full of examples of their propaganda and of their spreading of doubts. Sometimes doubts are raised about the original da'wah and its principles themselves. Sometimes doubts are spread against the bearers and workers of this da'wah. The style and form of this work change in every age, and after modern means and publication, its methods have changed greatly. And all this work is being carried on continuously against the ideological mission of Islam. Moreover, its first target is the Islamic community and its leadership. But the framework that Allah has given in the verse mentioned above, this work is still going on within it today and in the temperament that Allah has made it. And the indications Allah has given about the enemies, their methods are the same even today.

The guidance that Allah has given in this verse is a treasure for the Islamic movement in every age, whenever it rises with this call, and whenever it rises with the aim of establishing an Islamic system in any part of this earth. Whenever this work begins, the means of mischief and conspiracy will begin to move against it, the doors of the most modern propaganda means will open, its aims will be twisted and presented in a distorted colour, and efforts will be made to scatter its ranks. And this verse will come before the movement, from the Qur'an, as guidance and as opening the eyes of the Islamic movement. It will warn the callers about the temperament of this movement, and explain its method. It will also place before the movement the temperament of its opponents, who are on the road alongside it. This verse will fill the heart of the Islamic movement with tranquillity, and will make the difficulties it faces on this path easy to bear. And when these wolves tear its flesh from every side, when the means of publication bark around it from all directions, when trials come upon it from everywhere and it faces the mischief-making, this movement will remain content and continue on its own path, and all these signposts will be clearly visible to it.

For this reason it was warned in advance of trial, harassment, mischief and false propaganda. It was told that it would hear much because of this da'wah, and this was told so that the movement would have firm certainty from the beginning that patience and God-consciousness are its provision for the journey. Through them all schemes and all propaganda come to an end; in their presence the force and intensity of harassment and trial itself diminish, and the movement proceeds toward its target, moving forward, full of hope, with great resolve, and with patience and God-consciousness as its provision for the road.

After this, the address turns to criticism of the People of the Book. Their false position is exposed. It is explained that when the Scripture was given to them, a covenant was taken from them that they would do such and such, but they cast it behind their backs, and they betrayed what had been entrusted to them as a trust. They are asked:

This surah takes up many of the words and deeds of the People of the Book, especially the Jews. Among the most prominent characteristics mentioned about them is that they used to conceal the truth even though they knew well that it was the truth. Then they would mix the truth with falsehood, and in this way they would pave the way for their propaganda. Thus they spread doubts about the meaning of the religion. They raise objections against the soundness of Islam. They also deny that Islam and the earlier religions share common foundations. Islam confirms the earlier religions, and the earlier religions confirm Islam. They had the Torah in their possession, in which the truthfulness of Hadrat Muhammad (ﷺ) was recorded, and they knew it. They also knew that the Holy Qur'an had come from the same source from which the Torah was revealed.

Now, the position they are adopting is extremely inappropriate for them, because Allah the Exalted has commanded them that they would convey the Book and would not conceal what is in it; they would explain it and explain it before all people. They would neither conceal it nor keep it secret. But they cast aside this clear covenant of Allah. The manner of expression in this verse is extremely effective. It contains, in addition to the religious act, a physical movement as well, namely, throwing something behind the back. ﴿So they cast it behind their backs﴾ ... and they committed this shameful act. Why? ﴿And sold it for a small price﴾ ...

They did this for the sake of the worldly interests of this world. They did this for the personal interests of the religious leaders of the Jews and for the protection of their nationhood. And all of this is only a small price, even if they were to gain control over the entire world for the whole duration of time. Even this would be a small price in comparison to the covenant of Allah. And if they had kept in view the reward that was with Allah for them, it would indeed have appeared to them as a small price. ﴿How wretched is what they are trading for!﴾

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verses 188–189:

In Sahih al-Bukhari, it is narrated from Ibn Abbas (رضي الله عنهما) that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked the Jews about something. They concealed it and gave him a wrong answer. They left, giving the impression that they had told the Messenger (ﷺ) what he had asked, and they were pleased with themselves, both because they had been deemed worthy of praise by the Messenger (ﷺ) and because they had concealed the real matter. Then this verse was revealed:

﴿Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have brought, and love to be praised for what they have not done, will be secure from punishment. For them is a painful torment.﴾

In another narration, Imam Bukhari has related from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that among the hypocrites there were people who, whenever the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out for jihad, would always remain behind, and they would be very pleased at staying behind, because it was contrary to the wish of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned, these people would present excuses and swear oaths, and they would love to be praised for what they had not done. Then this verse was revealed: ﴿Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have brought, and love to be praised for what they have not done...﴾

The real fact is that it is not a definite matter as to which event a verse was revealed about. Such narrations sometimes describe a situation in which the Messenger (ﷺ) cited a verse as evidence. The narrator may have the misunderstanding that perhaps the verse has just been revealed, or, if a verse applies to some event, the narrator says that this verse is its fulfilment and that it was revealed concerning it. Therefore, no definite statement can be made about these two narrations either.

As for the first narration, it is in harmony with the context, because the discussion concerns the People of the Book. It refers to the claim of the People of the Book that they would not conceal the Book given to them and the trust they hold, but would declare it to the people. They were concealing it and, by way of deceit and trickery, were presenting something else, and then they also expected that they would be praised for this lie and fabrication.

If the second narration is correct, the context still contains a reference to the hypocrites, and this verse is also linked with those verses. In short, these are examples of the people who existed in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Such people are found in every movement even today. They are people who cannot fulfil the demands of their ideals and their obligations, nor can they bear the consequences, nor fulfil the responsibilities of the ideology. They sit behind in the struggle. When those who struggle are defeated and suffer humiliation, these people raise their heads and speak with a sneer and a curled nose, giving the impression that they are very wise, opportunity-aware and self-respecting. And when the mujahideen achieve victory and gain benefits, our such companions move forward and show that they were supporters of that plan and that they too had a hand in that victory. These people love to be praised for deeds they did not do.

This is the example of those people among humanity who are timid and make grand claims. The Qur'an draws the portrait of these people within a few lines, and their features become very clearly visible. Then, clothing them in words, the Qur'an preserves these features as a permanent record, so that those who come before this mirror may see their own face. This is the style of the Qur'an.

Concerning such people, Allah instructs His Messenger (ﷺ) with emphasis that there is no way for them to be saved in the Hereafter.

﴿So do not think that they are secure from punishment.﴾ ﴿And for them is a painful punishment.﴾ And this threat of a painful punishment is from Allah, who is the Owner of the heavens and the earth, and who has power over everything. So what way of escape then remains, and when can salvation be attained? ﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is Competent over all things.﴾

Lesson No. 29 at a Glance

This surah, with all the lessons and discourses it contains, has reached its final lesson. This surah addresses a large number of the fundamental elements of the Islamic worldview. These elements have been established by removing every kind of ambiguity and confusion, and by engaging in debate with the People of the Book and in discussion with the polytheists. Throughout this entire surah, the nature of the Islamic system of life and its demands with regard to life and property are explained. The Muslim community is taught how it should discharge these duties, how it should conduct itself in times of hardship and trial, how it will come through the trials of prosperity, and how it will carry out the great duties and obligations of the Islamic ideology, both those relating to the self and those relating to wealth. These were the themes that formed the axis of this entire surah, and we explained them in our commentary Fi Zilal al-Quran on Parts Three and Four.

Now this final lesson is a kind of final blow, or final blows. These concluding blows are perfectly suited to the theme of this surah. And this final blow is in complete harmony with the earlier blows, both in its subject matter and in its manner of expression.

Within it, a very profound truth is stated: that this universe is an open book. It contains countless proofs and signs of faith and certainty. From this universe, one can well perceive the Being who is governing it with great wisdom. It makes clear that beyond this worldly life there is an otherworldly life, and that the reckoning, accountability and recompense of this life will take place there. Who can read these proofs, who can grasp these signs and indications, who can comprehend this wisdom, and who can hear the voice of this universe? Only those who are ulu al-albab (people of understanding), who are men of intellect and insight, can do so. Those who do not pass heedlessly over this open book, and who do not close their eyes to these manifest verses and signs.

This truth, in relation to the universe, is one of the fundamental elements of the Islamic worldview, and there is a deep connection between it and human nature. There is a profound inner harmony between human nature and the nature of the cosmos. The universe points, from one aspect, to the existence of its Creator. And from another aspect, it reveals that great law (al-namus al-akbar) which operates within it and animates it, with purpose, profound wisdom, and intention and will. The understanding and comprehension of this great law is very important from the standpoint of what attitude a human being adopts regarding this universe and its Creator, the Lord of all worlds. In truth, this universe is an important treasury and source of Islamic ideas about this present world. After this, in this lesson, the acceptance of the humble supplication of people of intellect and knowledge of the cosmos is mentioned. These are the people who continually study this open book of the universe, and reflect upon the proofs that the universe presents. And they also contemplate the purposes that the universe indicates. And along with the acceptance of supplication, what guidance is given? That continuous action, ceaseless struggle, patience, love, and the fulfilment of the demands of faith are in truth the gifts that are bestowed upon those who read the open book of the universe with fear of God. And then, at the end, the position of the disbelievers is belittled, even though they have an abundance of worldly provisions. These are nothing; the true wealth is that which will be received in the Hereafter. The believers should speak of this.

In this surah, a detailed discussion was made about the People of the Book and their stance against Muslims. In this final lesson, mention is also made of some good individuals among the People of the Book. And their reward in the Hereafter and their quality of humble submission (khushu') are specifically mentioned. In connection with this, mention had been made of those among the believers who study this open book of the universe, and who also supplicated with the quality of khushu' and inclining to God (inabah). And they regarded it as most shameful to sell the verses of God for a paltry price, as some People of the Book used to do, and as has already been mentioned in this surah. After this, the conclusion of the entire surah comes, and in it a summary of the guidance of this entire surah is given. And the Muslim community is told that this is the summary of their life. This is the summary of their duties and programme. And their success lies within it.

O you who believe! Be patient, outdo others in patience, be steadfast on the frontiers, and fear Allah, that you may be successful. (Qur'an 3:200)

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (*Fi Zilal al-Quran*, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 191:

In the creation of the heavens and the earth, and in the alternation of night and day, what signs and indications are there? When these people of understanding (ulul-albab) reflect on the heavens and the earth, what signs do they find? When they consider the night and its alternation, what do they see? Then they begin to remember Allah, standing, sitting, and lying on their sides. And the question is how the outcome of their reflection becomes so closely linked with the remembrance of Allah that they immediately remember Him standing, sitting, and lying on their sides. And then how do they conclude this remembrance with humble submission and a heartfelt, burning supplication? They say: "Our Lord, You did not create this without purpose. Glory be to You; so protect us from the punishment of the Fire." (Our Lord, You did not create all this in vain or without purpose. You are free from such futility. So save us from the punishment of the Fire.)

The Qur'an here paints a living and moving picture of those who reflect soundly upon this universe and perceive its influences. They then turn their attention to these perceptions and influences, and before their eyes, whatever happens day and night throughout this entire universe, they respond to it with "Labbayk" (here I am).

The Qur'an repeatedly calls human thought and vision to observation and emphatically commands them to study this open book, whose pages are turned by night and day themselves. On every page appears one of the signs of the Creator's power. It stirs in the sound nature an intense eagerness to recognize a truth that is inscribed within the pages of this book. This truth lies at the foundation of this universe. It inclines one to accept the demands of the Creator of this universe. And it invites one to turn to the One who placed this law in the universe. Love of the Creator is born in the heart, together with fear and awe of Him.

Then, who are these ulul-albab? They are people of sound intellect who study the signs of the book of the universe with open eyes. They do not cover their eyes with veils, nor do they close the windows of their reflection, contemplation and pondering. In this way, through their hearts, while standing, sitting and lying on their sides, they turn toward Allah. Thus their eyes are opened, their means of perception are unlocked, and they grasp the great law and the reality of the universe that Allah has placed within it. They attain the purpose of the existence of this universe. The real causes of its creation become known to them, and they understand the elements of nature's composition and the system of its sustenance. They obtain all these secrets through the inspiration that comes through the connection between these laws of nature and the human heart.

The scene of the heavens and the earth, the spectacle of the change of night and day, and the sights of the orbits of the planets are such sights that, if we open our eyes and look, with our hearts functioning and our perception working well, and see them with the vision with which a person sees a scene for the first time, and if we remove from our sensibility the notion of having become accustomed to these scenes, and cleanse our senses of the effects of repetition, then they will be capable of stirring our feelings. An earthquake will occur in our consciousness, and we will clearly realize that the harmony created in this system, with such precise attention, is impossible without a wise hand. Behind this system works a wise intellect. Behind this system works a law which cannot be violated. And all this cannot be deception or fraud. It cannot be mere chance, nor can this system be a mere illusion of sight.

It is also no small earthquake for our consciousness that this earth revolves around the sun and on its own axis, and from this arise the two scenes of day and night; that attraction works among these heavenly bodies and has held each body in its place. Or there is some other system. Such theories, based on principles we have established, will sometimes be correct and sometimes wrong. Whatever the case, in every case this wonder of the universe remains a wonder. And it appears that there is a great system which holds these gigantic planets and bodies together. With extreme precision, they neither break apart nor collide with one another. Whatever names astronomers among humankind may give to this, it is in any case a sign of the system of nature, a proof of truth, and the truth is manifest through the rotation of days and the movement of the heavens.

What the Qur'an has depicted here clearly, it has recorded with great precision, down to every part of the effects that the scenes of the rotation of the heavens and celestial bodies, and the constant alternation of night and day, leave on the consciousness and thought of the ulul-albab and people of understanding. It is a kind of impactful picture. Upon seeing it, the heart adopts a very correct system and method in dealing with this universe. These scenes speak in their own language, and these hearts come into harmony with the nature of the universe, unite with its reality, and accept the signals and influences of the universe. In this way, the book of the universe becomes, for a believer who has reached Allah, a book of knowledge and recognition, which Allah has composed.

The first effect of this study of the universe on human consciousness is that it turns the person toward the remembrance of Allah and His worship. Those who study it remember Allah standing, sitting, and turning on their sides. While they reflect on the creation of the earth and the heavens, and while they are also studying the alternation of night and day, these reflections become worship. And thus these observations become the remembrance of Allah. In this way, according to this conception of humanity and the conception of the universe, two truths are established.

The first truth is that reflecting on Allah's creation, observing it, studying Allah's open book, and studying the creative hand of Allah, as well as the study of the movement of the universe and the turning of its pages, is in reality the fundamental and essential worship. And it is a remembrance of Allah which is truly the real remembrance of Allah. If cosmic sciences, which deal with the organization and formation of this universe, and the study of the laws and customs that operate within this universe, and the study of the powers and treasures gathered within this universe, and the knowledge of the secrets and mysteries of this universe, are combined with the remembrance and recollection of the Creator of this universe, and if through this study an awareness of Allah's exalted majesty is produced, and an awareness of Allah's grace and mercy is awakened, then all this activity becomes the worship of the Creator of this universe, and takes on the form of prayer. Through this knowledge, life can be set right and firmly established on the straight path, and the whole human population can turn toward Allah. But it is regrettable that our materialistic and disbelieving tendency has created a conceptual gap between this universe and the Creator of the universe. They have created a contradiction between the laws of creation and eternal, everlasting reality. The result is that knowledge, which was the most beautiful gift of Allah to humanity, has itself become a curse for humanity, pursuing human beings and transforming human life into hell. Human life is being spent in anguish, spiritual emptiness, and dissatisfaction, as if a tyrannical and overpowering ghost were pursuing a person.

The second truth is that the signs of Allah in this universe, in their inspired form, are revealed only to the person whose heart is occupied with the remembrance of Allah and the worship of Allah. And those who remember Allah standing, sitting and lying on their sides are in reality the very people who reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth, and who ponder on the constant coming of night and day. It is these people upon whom great realities are disclosed, which are wrapped within the creation of the heavens and the earths and within the system of the alternation of night and day. Only those who become the confidants of these secrets then reach the Islamic life, which is the guarantor of salvation in the Hereafter, well-being in this world, and goodness and righteousness. As for those who are content only with the apparent worldly life, and who discover some of the created things of this universe but have no connection with the Islamic system of life, these people are concerned with the ruin of their entire life. They subject their lives to breaking and disintegration, and they use these created secrets and mysteries for destruction. In this way they make their lives an unbearable hell, subjecting themselves to a kind of anguish in which breath is choked. And in the Hereafter they will return to the wrath of Allah and His punishment.

In short, these two truths are necessarily linked with one another. The surah has made both of them its subject of discussion, which are mentioned here for the people of understanding, for the time of their study of the universe and for the establishment of their connection with Allah. And this is the time of reflection and remembrance in which inner purity is attained, the soul becomes clear, the doors of perception open, the capacity to receive guidance increases, and the person becomes ready for acceptance, impression and reception.

This time of studying the universe is a time of the worship of Allah. In this respect, it is a time of reception from Allah and of union from the servant's side. Therefore, at this time the capacity to perceive the universe and the cosmic signs is also greater. At this time, mere reflection on this universe, its system of the rotation of night and day, and the system of the earth and the heavens, inspires the human mind that a great reality lies hidden within this universe, and that this universe is not purposeless, nor is it a mere illusion of sight. This time is also the time of union with Allah, and of direct recognition of Allah.

"Our Lord, You did not create this in vain. Glory be to You..." ("Our Lord, You did not create all this without purpose. Glory be to You, so save us from the punishment of the Fire.") You did not create this universe in vain. Rather, it was created so that it would be true, so that truth would be the means of its establishment, truth would be its law, and truth would be its essence.

The truth is that this universe has a reality. It is not "nothingness," as some philosophies say, that it is mere nothingness. Being real, it moves according to a law, so it does not function according to anarchy. It is advancing toward a purpose, so it does not operate by chance. In short, in its existence, its motion and its purposes, it functions under the control of a great truth. And no falsehood can mix with it.

This is the first dose which is given to the hearts of people of knowledge and understanding when they reflect on the system of the creation of the earth and heavens and the system of the rotation of night and day. Through this dose they are made aware of worship of Allah, remembrance of Allah, and union with the Essence. Through this dose, a true impression of the truth that is at work in the design of this universe is imprinted on the veil of their perception. When these people of understanding reach this truth, they immediately begin to glorify and exalt Allah, and the result of this interpretation of theirs is: "Our Lord, You did not create this in vain..." ("O our Lord, You did not create this universe in vain.")

After this, this psychological thought advances further. Some further cosmic feelings and inspirations come forward: "So protect us from the punishment of the Fire (191). Our Lord, whoever You cause to enter the Fire, You have indeed disgraced him, and the wrongdoers will have no helpers." ("Save us from the Fire. Whoever You admit into the Fire, You have indeed brought to utter disgrace, and for the wrongdoers there will be no helpers.") ... The question is: what logical connection exists between the perception of the truth that is within the heavens and the earth and within the alternation of the night and day, and this supplicatory tremor of consciousness, such that the one who perceives begins to supplicate with the utmost fear of Allah, the utmost humility, and the utmost concentration?

When people of understanding perceive this truth which works beneath the surface of this universe, then for them the meaning of this perception is that within this universe there is a destiny, there is a plan, a wisdom is at work within it, and it has a purpose of creation. That behind the lives of people, in those stars, a truth and justice are at work. Therefore, whatever deeds and actions people perform here must be reckoned on some day. There must be a requital of deeds, and on the basis of this requital there must necessarily be another world in which truth, justice, reward and punishment are realized.

In short, the truths that appear within the supplication of people of understanding are the self-evident logic of nature, whose links connect to one another so swiftly that their consciousness acquires the awareness of fire and hell in a single leap. And immediately they raise their hands in supplication: "O Allah, protect us from it." This is the first thing that comes into their hearts. And this coming is the logical result of the perception that they attain regarding the truth hidden within this universe. In terms of its state, this supplication is extremely long, full of humble submission, comes from a heart in extreme agitation, with a body trembling in the extreme, and with complete concentration. It rises from the heart of a believer. And in terms of its words, it is a sweet melody, whose rhythms are harmonious and which carries within it the burning intensity of melodies. It is in beautiful words.

Consider first the intellectual world of these people of knowledge and understanding, and the first tremor that passes through it. They turn wholly toward their Lord, so that He may save them from the punishment of the Fire. Reflect on their words: "Our Lord, indeed whomever You cause to enter the Fire, You have truly disgraced him" (﴿رَبَّنَا إِنَّكَ مَنْ تُدْخِلِ النَّارَ فَقَدْ أَخْزَيْتَهُ﴾), "and for the wrongdoers there will be no helpers" (﴿وَمَا لِلظَّالِمِينَ مِنْ أَنْصَارٍ﴾).

This supplication shows that their fear was of the punishment of the Fire, and even more so of the disgrace that befalls the people of the Fire. This agitation in their intellectual world arose from the shame and humiliation that will be the lot of the people of the Fire. Thus this fear overtook them merely because they were seized by modesty before Allah. In this way, they are more sensitive to feeling shame before Allah than to being branded by fire. This fear and trembling also reveals their awareness that none can help anyone against Allah, and therefore a wrongdoer will have no supporter or helper.

Now this humble supplication moves a step further:

﴿Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith, "Believe in your Lord," so we have believed. Our Lord, forgive us our sins, remove from us our misdeeds, and cause us to die among the righteous.﴾

"Master! We heard a caller who called to faith and said, 'Obey your Lord.' We accepted his call. So, O our Lord, forgive us the transgressions we have committed, remove the evils that are within us, and make our end among the righteous."

People of understanding have open hearts; whatever is inspired in them, they answer with "Here I am" (labbayk). Their sense becomes even keener, and now their gaze falls upon their shortcomings, failings, sins and acts of disobedience. Immediately they seek forgiveness for their sins from their Lord; they become ready to expiate their sins, and they express the desire that their death be among the category of the righteous.

The imprint of this supplication in this passage is in harmony with the themes of this entire surah. The whole surah carries the color of the purification of character and of seeking forgiveness from disobedience to Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ). Throughout this surah there is the atmosphere of a full-fledged war against carnal desires and sins and misdeeds. And this is the war upon which the success of every battlefield engagement depends: until victory is attained in this war of moral purification, no external battle against the enemies of Allah and the enemies of faith can be won. And throughout this surah these themes are presented, which are interconnected, harmonious, complementary, mutually adjacent, and carry similar effects.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 194:

The supplication concludes with turning towards Allah and hoping for His grace. It expresses confidence and certainty that with Allah every promise is fulfilled. ﴿Our Lord, and grant us what You promised us through Your messengers, and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not break the promise.﴾

Here, in the form of supplication, the demand is made that the promises which Your messengers conveyed to us from You, and about which we are certain that Your promise is never broken, be fulfilled. These people hope that on the Day of Resurrection they will not be humiliated. This is the state of their faith, which is the first jolt in the world of their thoughts: their hearts are filled with hope that they will not be disgraced. They bring this at the beginning of the supplication as well as at its end. From this it becomes known how sensitive these people of understanding have become, how tender their hearts have become, and how pure they have become. The fear of Allah and the shame of disobedience fill their hearts.

In terms of its overall subject, this supplication is an expression of complete acceptance and complete readiness, arising from their contemplation of the natural world, which was inspired into their hearts through the study of the order of the universe.

It is fitting that we reflect once more on this supplication, and it is also necessary to look at its artistic beauty and its appropriate style of expression.

In every surah of the Holy Quran, a fixed rhyme (qafiyah) has been adopted for its verses. The Quran does not adopt the rhyme and fawasil pattern found in poetry, where letter matches letter. Rather, their melody and rise and fall are mutually similar. For example, the words baseer, hakeem, mubeen and mureeb have similar sound effects. Or, for example, the words al-bab, absar, al-nar and qarar have identical sound effects, or, for example, words like khufya, shaqiya, shariya, though not poetic rhyme, have a similar sonic rhythm. Of these, the first type of rhyme occurs mostly in occasions of forceful speech, where the style is narrative... The second type of rhyme occurs on occasions of supplication, and the third type is brought for accounts and the narration of events.

In Surah Al-Imran the first type of rhyme is found, and it deviates from this in only two places: at the beginning, where there is a supplication, and then in these final verses, where there is again a supplication.

This style is a completely new and unique style which the Quran has adopted for particular expressions. The style adopted for supplication gives the supplication a soft voice and a plaintive tone. The words carry a sweetness, which is most fitting for presenting one's request with humility.

There is another artistic feature found in these verses. In the universe, the scene of the creation of the heavens and the earth and the sequence of the night and day, which were presented for human reflection, it was fitting that the supplication should be one in which humility and submission are accompanied by a pleasing voice. Its melodies are long, and the rise and fall of its voice is very profound. Thus the inspirations and effects of that scene are long-lasting, and their profound impact falls upon the nerves of hearing and imagination, and then this impression passes into the conscience. For the vocal movements of these words also contain great humility, sweetness, pleasantness, attentiveness and God-consciousness. Just as the wording of that scene is long, so too are its melodies. Through this, the true purpose and aim of the Quran's expressions are fulfilled, and along with it the real new excellences of the Quran also come to light.

Just as this supplication is long, so too is the answer to this supplication long:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 3, verse 195:

This is a detailed answer to a supplication. Its style is also lengthy, and it is entirely in keeping with the style of the Holy Quran: in accordance with the demands of the situation and the positions of both parties, from both the psychological and the conscious perspectives.

Now we come to the subject matter of the answer to the supplication and the acceptance of prayer that comes from Allah. What aspects of the Islamic system of life does this answer reveal, what is the temperament of this system, what are its constituent elements, and what method does this system adopt for the training of human beings, and what are its characteristics?

Those men of understanding who reflected upon the creation of the heavens and the earth, who contemplated the alternation of night and day, and who derived proofs and signs from this book of the universe which lies open; their nature accepted these proofs and signs of truth, and after that they turned towards their Lord. They made a long supplication, full of humility and submission, steeped in longing and yearning. And after that, the answer to their supplication came immediately from their Lord, the Merciful and Generous, because their supplication was extremely sincere and was full of love… Now see what the answer to the supplication is.

This answer contains the acceptance of the supplication, and in it guidance is given towards the fundamental constituent elements of the Islamic way of life. And its duties are described: "So their Lord answered them: 'I will not let go to waste the work of any worker among you, whether male or female; you are of one another.'"

In reply, their Lord said: "I do not waste the deed of any of you, whether male or female; you are all of one another's kind."

Reflection and contemplation alone are not sufficient for you. Humility, submission and a supplication full of longing are not sufficient either. Merely turning towards Allah and seeking forgiveness for sins is not sufficient, and merely seeking salvation in the Hereafter is not sufficient. Rather, action is necessary. Positive action is needed. And this positive action is the result of that reflection and that turning towards Allah, of that readiness and that feeling which will be expressed in that heartfelt supplication. It requires that a person be prepared for positive action, action which Islam regards as worship in the same way that Islam regards reflection and contemplation as worship. Just as Islam regards remembrance and thought, fear and seeking forgiveness, and hopeful turning towards Allah as worship, so too it regards that action as worship, the action which Islam describes as the fruit of all acts of worship. And this fruit will be accepted from all: whether men perform this action or women perform it, there is no condition of sex or gender attached to this action, because men and women are completely equal in humanity. They are parts of one another and descendants of one another, and they are equal on the scale of the Day of Judgment.

After this, the details of these actions are given. It is explained what duties relating to life and property the Islamic outlook on life imposes. Moreover, through the mention of these actions it also becomes known what the temperament of this system of life is, and what the ground is upon which this system is built. And what the nature of its method of operation is, and what obstacles and thorns it has, and that there is an urgent need to overcome these difficulties, and a need to pick these thorns one by one, and what preparations are needed to plant a pure tree in this earth. Then, what measures are needed to give it firm establishment upon this earth, no matter how great the sacrifices that must be given and no matter how many difficulties must be faced.

"So those who emigrated, and were driven out from their homes, and suffered harm in My way, and fought and were killed, I will surely remit their evil deeds from them, and I will surely admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, as a reward from Allah. And with Allah is the best reward."

Those who first were addressed by this Quran and called to reflection had exactly these features. These were the people who emigrated from Makkah; these were the people who were expelled from their homes solely because of their way of life, and they had no other fault. These were the people who fought for that outlook and were killed. But these features must belong to all those who rise up with the call of Islam, whenever anyone rises and wherever anyone rises. The same features will be found in those who grow up within jahiliyyah (the state of ignorance before Islam), whatever that jahiliyyah may be… those who grow up in the land of the enemy, whatever that enemy may be, and whatever that land may be… those who exist among enemy peoples, whatever that people may be; and when their patience is brimming over, while the enemies' worldly ambitions, their greed and their base desires stand in their way; and when they are few in number and are being made targets of persecution. And these conditions were at the very beginning, when they were the oppressed. After that, this pure plant gained some strength, and in every place it gains strength in the same way, and it gains strength despite these persecutions. It gains strength despite emigration and exile. After that, this strength stands on its own feet; power of resistance arises within it, and then it is able to defend itself. At this stage, fighting and armed struggle begin again. This difficult, bitter and arduous struggle is in fact what becomes the expiation of sins, and it also becomes the cause of reward in this world and the Hereafter.

This is the method of action, this is the divine method of action. For the way of life for which Allah has laid down this method, the means of human struggle will be employed to implement it practically in human life; in accordance with this method and in accordance with the measure of jihad which the believers and the mujahidin in the cause of Allah perform, purely seeking His pleasure.

This is the temperament of this system of life; these are its constituent elements and these are its duties; this is the training method of this approach, this is its manner of guidance and instruction: that, passing through the intuitive stage of reflection upon this universe, it moves a person to positive action. And this action conforms to those ideological impressions, and in this way this system of life is established.

After this, in the answer to the supplication, attention is drawn to the markets full of goods in the land of the disbelievers, who are the enemies and disobedient ones of the Islamic system of life. It is pointed out that a Muslim gives to this merchandise only the weight that it truly deserves for this world, and does not make it a trial for himself, nor does he give it the opportunity to become a trial for the people of faith. Because the people of faith are making enormous sacrifices; they are being guided, they are being driven out of their homes and they are being killed; therefore the goods of the world should not become a trial for them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah Al-Imran, verses 196–198:

"O Prophet! Let not the movements of the disbelievers through the lands deceive you. It is but a brief enjoyment; then their abode will be Hell, and what an evil resting place it is. But for those who fear their Lord there are gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever, as a welcome from Allah. And what is with Allah is best for the righteous."

The movement of people through the lands, their travels and tours, is a sign that they are wealthy and have means. It is also a sign of their status and political power. These are phenomena that can unsettle the believers. They may feel a pang in their hearts. Ordinary people naturally feel as though they are suffering difficult economic conditions and deprivation. They are being persecuted, they are struggling continuously, they have been exiled and are striving for betterment. Every kind of hardship and frightening circumstance is befalling them, while the enemies of Islam and the upholders of falsehood are being raised in luxury and comfort. This situation, on the one hand, afflicts the heedless common masses with inner anguish, when they see that truth and the people of truth are in difficulty while falsehood and the people of falsehood prosper, indeed live in luxury. And on the other hand, this situation creates pride and self-confidence in the hearts of those misguided ones and the people of falsehood themselves, and they become further misguided, and advance further in mischief, rebellion and error. Therefore this verse came: "O Prophet! Let not the movements of the disbelieving people through the lands deceive you. It is only a brief enjoyment of a few days' life; then they will go to Hell, which is the worst resting place." ……… It is a small provision, which passes away and departs. And their eternal abode is Hell, which is a very evil place. And in comparison with this small, passing and perishing provision, what is there? There are gardens, in them is everlasting life, and honour from Allah." "Gardens beneath which rivers flow." "……… "Abiding therein forever." …… "This is a welcome for them." …… "What is with Allah is far better for the righteous."

There is no doubt that if we place this portion on one side of a scale and the other portion on the other side, then what is with Allah is far better for the righteous people. And no heart will harbour doubt that those who adopt the path of piety in their lives, their scale will be heavier than those who adopted disbelief. And likewise no person of sound intellect will hesitate in this matter that he should choose the portion that thinkers choose for themselves.

Here Allah does not make any promise to the Muslims in the field of education and training and in the establishment of the fundamental values of the Islamic conception of life that He will grant them help. He does not promise that I will subdue and overpower your enemies and give them to you, nor does He promise that you will be granted establishment and firm foothold in the earth, nor does He promise any other of the things of this worldly life, as Allah has promised in some other places, that He makes it binding upon Himself to help His friends against the enemies of Islam.

Here Allah promises only one thing: what is with Allah. In the Islamic call, the true reward is this, and this is the distinguishing feature of this call. Detachment from every goal and every purpose, indifference to every aim, to the extent that one becomes free even from the desire that one's way of life should prevail, that the word of Allah should be exalted, and that the enemies of Allah should be subdued and overpowered. In short, Allah's will is that the believers become detached even from this aim, entrust their affairs to Allah, and that their hearts become pure even from wishing these aims for themselves, although these are not merely their own desire.

The belief that one must give one's life, be faithful, and discharge one's duty, and nothing more, without any worldly purpose or greed, without seeking that victory, dominion, establishment in the land, and eminence be attained in the world, and that everything be awaited in the Hereafter.

After this, victory also comes, establishment in the land is also granted, and Islam is also given eminence in the world. But all these matters are not included in the pledge (bay'ah). These matters are not part of the bargain. In this bargain, the believers have not to receive any part of the price in this world. Here there is only the discharge of duty, fulfilment of the covenant, giving of one's life, and bearing of hardships.

The call and the pledge for the call in Makkah Mukarramah continued on this principle. This very bargain was being made there. But Allah had not yet granted the Muslims victory, dominion and eminence. There Allah had not yet entrusted them with the keys of authority in the earth, nor had the office of leadership of humanity been handed over to them. Yes, when they became sincere according to this standard and began to keep their covenant according to this standard, then they received everything.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi says: Abdullah ibn Rawahah (may Allah be pleased with him) said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night of 'Aqabah (on the night when the representatives of the Aws and Khazraj pledged allegiance, and it was decided that the Prophet (ﷺ) would migrate to Madinah). He submitted: "O Messenger of Allah, stipulate whatever conditions you wish for your Lord and for yourself." He (ﷺ) said: "For my Lord, I stipulate that you worship Him and associate nothing with Him. And for myself, I stipulate that you protect me in the same way you protect your own lives and property." They said: "Then what will we get?" He (ﷺ) replied: "Only Paradise." They all said: "In this bargain we have profited greatly. We neither return this bargain, nor demand its cancellation from the other party."

This was the matter: Paradise, only Paradise. There was no promise to them that they would receive victory, honour, unity, strength, establishment in the land, leadership, wealth, riches or any other thing. Although all these things were in fact given to them, yet these things were outside the bargain. ……… Despite this, their view was that they had succeeded in this bargain, and that they neither seek a retraction nor express such a desire to the other party. They made a clear bargain. The deal took place between two parties pledging allegiance. The matter ended, the agreement was made, and after that there was no haggling in it.

Thus Allah trained that community concerning which Allah's decision was that the keys of authority over this earth would be entrusted to them, the reins of power would be in their hands, and this leadership was entrusted to them when they became free of every kind of greed, when they threw away every kind of desire, and when they restrained every kind of carnal desire. To the extent that they abandoned even their natural desires regarding the Islamic revolution. They suppressed even the desire for the establishment of the Islamic system. And they stopped thinking about the success of the way of life for which they were giving their lives. Because no person or group capable of bearing the responsibilities of this great leadership can have any desire within the self, or any selfishness within the self, unless they have fully entered Islam.
