He submitted: "O Messenger of Allah, stipulate whatever conditions you wish for your Lord and for yourself." He (ﷺ) said: "For my Lord, I stipulate that you worship Him and associate nothing with Him. And for myself, I stipulate that you protect me in the same way you protect your own lives and property." They said: "Then what will we get?" He (ﷺ) replied: "Only Paradise." They all said: "In this bargain we have profited greatly. We neither return this bargain, nor demand its cancellation from the other party."

This was the matter: Paradise, only Paradise. There was no promise to them that they would receive victory, honour, unity, strength, establishment in the land, leadership, wealth, riches or any other thing. Although all these things were in fact given to them, yet these things were outside the bargain. ……… Despite this, their view was that they had succeeded in this bargain, and that they neither seek a retraction nor express such a desire to the other party. They made a clear bargain. The deal took place between two parties pledging allegiance. The matter ended, the agreement was made, and after that there was no haggling in it.

Thus Allah trained that community concerning which Allah's decision was that the keys of authority over this earth would be entrusted to them, the reins of power would be in their hands, and this leadership was entrusted to them when they became free of every kind of greed, when they threw away every kind of desire, and when they restrained every kind of carnal desire. To the extent that they abandoned even their natural desires regarding the Islamic revolution. They suppressed even the desire for the establishment of the Islamic system. And they stopped thinking about the success of the way of life for which they were giving their lives. Because no person or group capable of bearing the responsibilities of this great leadership can have any desire within the self, or any selfishness within the self, unless they have fully entered Islam.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 3, verse 199:

Before the surah's themes come to an end, the direction of address turns once more toward the People of the Book, and it is said that among the People of the Book there are some who hold sound belief like the believers. These people have joined the caravan of faith and are travelling along with it. Therefore, their reward will also be the same as the reward of the people of faith.

This is the concluding address to the People of the Book. Earlier, in a large part of this surah, the sects of the People of the Book and their various positions were discussed. Here it is shown that in this exhibition of the highest examples of faith, and in this scene of supplication and its acceptance, there are also some among the People of the Book whose examples are worthy of being displayed in this showcase, because some among the People of the Book have set out upon the right path. They have reached the right destination. They have believed in all the scriptures (the present and the earlier ones). They do not distinguish between Allah and His command in terms of obedience. They also do not make any distinction among the messengers of Allah. They believed in the book revealed to them, and they also believe in the book revealed to the Muslims. This is indeed the distinctive feature of the Islamic way of life: it looks upon the caravan of faith with the eyes of closeness and love. Its view is that it is one single line of belief that is connected with the Divine Being. It regards the Islamic way of life as a unity and views it from a comprehensive perspective.

Here, among the important characteristics of the believers among the People of the Book that are being shown, the most significant is their quality of humility and submissiveness (khushu' wa khudu'), and their quality that they do not accept the paltry worldly gain (thaman qalil) in exchange for the verses of Allah. These attributes are mentioned so that they may be separated and distinguished from the ranks of the other People of the Book, among whom both of these weaknesses existed. That is, they were arrogant and also shameless. They concealed the verses and also distorted them, and they did this for an extremely base purpose. The same promise of reward that is made to the people of faith is made to them, and this reward will be paid promptly, without any delay or procrastination. ﴿Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning﴾ ……………(Allah does not delay in settling accounts.)

This is the final stroke. From the Lord of the heavens, those who have believed are called. In it, the difficulties of this path are presented in their most concise essence and summary, and the responsibilities and conditions of the road are mentioned.

This call from the higher realm is for the people of faith, and it comes by that attributive name which has bound them to the Divine Being. It is the Being who places these responsibilities upon these believers, who makes them fit for this call, who trains them to bear responsibilities, and who makes them honoured on this earth in the same way as they have been honoured in the heavens. يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا……………(O you who have believed……)

And what is the call for? Be patient, show courage, always be ready to confront the enemy, and always keep the fear of Allah before you………Throughout this entire surah, patience and taqwa (God-consciousness) are repeatedly enjoined. They are mentioned separately and also together. Furthermore, throughout this surah there is an invitation: bear the hardships in the way of truth, strive, confront conspiracies, and do not give heed to those who call towards defeat and speak words that break resolve. Here, at the end of this surah, this theme is repeated, and patience and perseverance (musabarah) are called for. Urging readiness at all times in the way of Allah and adopting fear of Allah is the best conclusion here.

Patience is the best provision for this path, the path of the Islamic call, because it is a long and laborious road. It is full of difficulties and strewn with thorns. Trials are everywhere. There are always occasions for injury and for the sacrifice of life. And every occasion is one that requires patience: patience over human desires, patience over the appetites of the self, patience over every kind of greed and longing, patience over one's own weakness and deficiency, patience over the deviation of their temperament, patience over the hastiness and despondency of the self, patience over the desires of people, patience over the weakness and frailty of people, patience over the ignorance and ill thinking of people, patience over the deviation of their temperament, patience over their arrogance and pride, patience over their deceptions, patience over the pride of falsehood, patience over the filth of disbelief, patience over the flourishing of evil, patience over the dominance of lust, patience over the fire of pride and haughtiness, patience over the scarcity of helpers, patience over the scarcity of supporters, patience over the length of the road, patience at times of anguish and restlessness over satanic whisperings, and patience over the bitterness of jihad; and patience over all these psychological impressions and varied emotional states………such as grief and sorrow, rage and anger, constriction and suffocation of the heart, at times loss of trust in goodness and despair of reforming human nature, and so on………At times sorrow, weariness and fatigue arise, and a cloud of despair settles upon a person. In such circumstances, only patience helps. Then, when victory is attained and a person gains power over retaliation, patience is again needed at that time. Then, at times, material comforts are obtained, and humility and sober-mindedness must be maintained over them, without arrogance, without inclination toward revenge, and without exceeding limits in retribution………Then, in both prosperity and adversity, to remain attached to Allah, to bow the head before His decrees, and to entrust all one's affairs to Him with complete tranquillity, complete confidence and great humility.

Patience in all these matters, and patience in other similar matters, are the stages which the one travelling the path of truth encounters throughout its long journey. Such difficulties and such circumstances arise which cannot be expressed in words, because the difficulties cannot be articulated in language. The meaning of these hardships cannot be contained within words. Only the one upon whom those meanings have passed, and who has undergone the hardships of this path, can comprehend this meaning. He has tasted those impressions, and he has himself passed through those bitter experiences.

Those who had believed had themselves tasted the bitterness of most of the aspects of the difficulties mentioned above. Therefore they understood this call well. They understood well the meaning of patience, to which they were being urged to hold fast.

Now, what is musabarah after patience? It is the form of mufa'alah of sabr. That is, be in mutual contest in patience. In all the matters mentioned above, [it means] musabarah with the enemies of Islam, who wish to cut the patience of the believers with their sword. That is, musabarah with the aforementioned sentiments, or musabarah with the enemies. Therefore, in the long journey of jihad, their patience must not come to an end; rather, until their last breath they should display more patience than their enemies. They should be more patient than those enemies who are hidden within hearts, and likewise against the mischief-making enemies. It is thus a contest of patience between the believers and their enemies, to see who goes ahead in this field. It is commanded: contest patience with patience, contest defence with defence, contest striving with striving, contest persistence with persistence; and the final contest will be that the believers are foremost in the contest. If falsehood insists upon its ideology, endures, and proceeds along its path, then truth is more deserving that it be more insistent, more enduring, and more striving in its own path.

And what is ribat? Stationing guards at the places of jihad, being on watch, establishing posts at the dangerous points of the enemy's attacks. The Islamic community always kept watch on the enemy; it never slept, because its enemies had never made peace with it. Since it undertook the burden of the Islamic call and presented this call to people, it has remained on the battlefield and in a state of war. In no place and in no age has it been free from the obligation of ribat in jihad, and until the Last Age and the Day of Resurrection this position will remain so.

The Islamic call presents to people a realistic system of life: a system that is established within their conscience as well, that rules over their wealth, that governs all the affairs of their lives, that governs their economy, and that is a just and straight system. But it is the law of the world that evil does not tolerate such a just, equitable, and straight system founded upon good with equanimity. No falsehood loves goodness, justice and uprightness, and no tyranny tolerates justice, equality and nobility. Therefore, against the call of Islam, the people of evil, the people of falsehood and oppressors rise up. All filthy and self-interested people rise against Islam, so that they may continue to use people for their own interests. Tyrants and arrogant people also rise against Islam, because they are not prepared to give up oppression and domination. And against it, all immoral people and those who adopt a path of waywardness rise up, because they cannot abandon their moral waywardness and lustfulness. Therefore, continuous jihad against all of them is very necessary, and patience and musabarah against them is an individual obligation (fard 'ain). Hence there is need for continuous vigilance and Islamic security guards, lest some force suddenly attack the Muslim Ummah, whereas such forces lie in wait against it in every land and every generation.

This is the temperament of this call, its method and its policy. Its policy is not that it should exceed limits, but its policy certainly is that it should establish on this earth a stable system of life and a healthy method. Yet against the Islamic call there always rises up some force that dislikes that method and that system. Then this force comes forward with its full strength in its path and goes about practising every kind of deception. It rejoices at every harm done to the Islamic call, and it continuously drives people to struggle against the Islamic call with hand, heart and tongue. Therefore it is also the duty of the Islamic movement to plunge into this struggle with all its duties and obligations, and it is its duty to remain awake at all times and never be heedless.

But in all these tasks, it must necessarily have tied to its waist the weapon of God-fearing (taqwa). For taqwa is an alert sentinel who sits at the door of the heart. It does not let the heart become heedless; it does not let it become weak; it does not let it transgress limits; and it does not let it stray from the straight path.

And the sense of the need for this alert sentinel of taqwa can be felt only by the one who has seen the hardships of this path, who has confronted the pressure of conflicting inclinations and of many successive impressions, amid different circumstances and different moments.

In this surah, this was the final stroke upon the strings of the lute, in which countless plectrums of this kind were used. And these strokes were all laid upon those strings which relate to the obligations and duties imposed in the way of the Islamic call. That is why, at the end, the verdict is given that if you seek all-encompassing success and complete revolution, then it is necessary to fulfil these duties in the best manner. لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ……………(so that you may attain success.)
